NOP.description: No Operation - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 1 byte in the instruction stream for alignment.

ENTR.description: Enter (MOV bp, sp) - Creates a new stack frame by moving the value of the stack pointer register to the base pointer register.

LEAV.description: Leave (MOV sp, bp) - Destroys the current stack frame by moving the value of the base pointer register to the stack pointer register.

CMP.description: Compare - Compares(subtracts) the values of two source registers and sets the flags accordingly.

JMP.description: Jump near - Unconditionally jumps to the specified 2 byte address.

JMPR.description: Jump Register - Unconditionally jumps to the address contained in the source register.

JMPFAR.description: Jump far - Unconditionally jumps to the specified 4 byte address.

CALL.description: Call near - Calls the subroutine at the specified 2 byte address.

CALLR.description: Call Register - Calls the subroutine at the address contained in the source register.

RET.description: Return - Returns from the current subroutine.

IMM.description: Load Immediate - Loads the 4 byte immediate value into the destination register.

IMMB.description: Load Immediate Byte - Loads the 1 byte immediate value into the destination register.

IMMBSX.description: Load Immediate Byte with Sign Extension - Loads the 1 byte immediate value into the destination register with sign extension.

LEA.description: Load Effective Address - Loads the effective address calculated by adding the signed 1 byte offset to the value in the source register into the destination register.

LEASC.description: Load Effective Address with Scale - Loads the effective address calculated by adding the signed 1 byte offset to the value in the source register plus the value in the second source register multiplied by the scale factor into the destination register. (Effective Address = SR1 + (SR2 * SCL) + OF8)

CLI.description: Clear Interrupt Flag - Disables maskable hardware interrupts by clearing the interrupt flag in the flags register.

STI.description: Set Interrupt Flag - Enables maskable hardware interrupts by setting the interrupt flag in the flags register.

COPYIP.description: Copy Instruction Pointer - Copies the current value of the instruction pointer into the destination register.

NOP2.description: No Operation 2 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 2 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP3.description: No Operation 3 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 3 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP4.description: No Operation 4 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 4 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP5.description: No Operation 5 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 5 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP6.description: No Operation 6 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 6 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP7.description: No Operation 7 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 7 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP8.description: No Operation 8 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 8 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP9.description: No Operation 9 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 9 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP10.description: No Operation 10 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 10 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP11.description: No Operation 11 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 11 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP12.description: No Operation 12 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 12 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP13.description: No Operation 13 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 13 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP14.description: No Operation 14 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 14 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

NOP15.description: No Operation 15 - Does nothing for one instruction cycle, or occupies 15 bytes in the instruction stream for alignment.

PUSH ra.description: Push ra - Pushes the value of ra onto the stack.

POP ra.description: Pop ra - Pops the value on the stack to ra.

PUSH rb.description: Push rb - Pushes the value of rb onto the stack.

POP rb.description: Pop rb - Pops the value on the stack to rb.

PUSH rc.description: Push rc - Pushes the value of rc onto the stack.

POP rc.description: Pop rc - Pops the value on the stack to rc.

PUSH rd.description: Push rd - Pushes the value of rd onto the stack.

POP rd.description: Pop rd - Pops the value on the stack to rd.

PUSH ri.description: Push ri - Pushes the value of ri onto the stack.

POP ri.description: Pop ri - Pops the value on the stack to ri.

PUSH bp.description: Push bp - Pushes the value of bp onto the stack.

POP bp.description: Pop bp - Pops the value on the stack to bp.

PUSHIMMB.description: Push Immediate - Pushes the 1 byte immediate value onto the stack.

ADDSP.description: Add Stack Pointer - Adds the 1 byte immediate value to the stack pointer and stores the result in the stack pointer register.

SUBSP.description: Subtract Stack Pointer - Subtracts the 1 byte immediate value from the stack pointer and stores the result in the stack pointer register.

PUSHIMMDW.description: Push Immediate - Pushes the 4 byte immediate value onto the stack.

PUSHIMMW.description: Push Word Immediate - Pushes the 2 byte immediate value onto the stack.

PUSH.description: Push - Pushes the value of the source register onto the stack.

POP.description: Pop - Pops the value on the stack to the destination register.

PUSHF.description: Push Flags - Pushes the value of the flags register onto the stack.

POPF.description: Pop Flags - Pops the value on the stack to the flags register.

PUSHIP.description: Push Instruction Pointer - Pushes the value of the instruction pointer onto the stack.

LDSTVAL.description: Load Stack Value - Loads a value from the stack at an offset from the stack pointer into the destination register. (Offset is a signed 1 byte value.) (x86: MOV reg, [SP + offset])

STSTVAL.description: Store Stack Value - Stores a value from the source register into the stack at an offset from the stack pointer. (Offset is a signed 1 byte value.) (x86: MOV [SP + offset], reg)

LDSTVALOW.description: Load Stack Value - Loads a value from the stack at an offset from the stack pointer into the destination register. (Offset is a signed 2 byte value.) (x86: MOV reg, [SP + offset])

STSTVALOW.description: Store Stack Value - Stores a value from the source register into the stack at an offset from the stack pointer. (Offset is a signed 2 byte value.) (x86: MOV [SP + offset], reg)

PUSHTR.description: Push triple register - Pushes the values of three source registers onto the stack in order: SR1, SR2, SR3.

POPTR.description: Pop triple register - Pops the top three values from the stack into the destination registers in order: SR1, SR2, SR3.

ADD.description: Add - Adds the values of two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

SUB.description: Subtract - Subtracts the value of the second source register from the first source register and stores the result in the destination register.

INC.description: Increment - Increases the value in the source register by 1 and stores the result in the destination register.

DEC.description: Decrement - Decreases the value in the source register by 1 and stores the result in the destination register.

NEG.description: Negate - Negates the value in the source register (two's complement) and stores the result in the destination register.

ABS.description: Absolute Value - Computes the absolute value of the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

INC rc.description: Increment rc - Increases the value in the rc register by 1.

DEC rc.description: Decrement rc - Decreases the value in the rc register by 1.

ADDIB.description: Add Immediate Byte - Adds the 1 byte immediate value to the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

SUBIB.description: Subtract Immediate Byte - Subtracts the 1 byte immediate value from the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

ADDIDW.description: Add Immediate Double Word - Adds the 4 byte immediate value to the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

SUBIDW.description: Subtract Immediate Double Word - Subtracts the 4 byte immediate value from the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

MUL.description: Multiply - Multiplies the values of two source registers and stores the lower 32 bits of the result in the destination register, and the upper 32 bits in a SR3 register.

DIV.description: Divide - Divides the value in the source register by the value in the second source register and stores the quotient in the destination register and the remainder in a SR3 register.

SMUL.description: Signed Multiply - Multiplies the signed values of two source registers and stores the lower 32 bits of the result in the destination register, and the upper 32 bits in a SR3 register.

SDIV.description: Signed Divide - Divides the signed value in the source register by the signed value in the second source register and stores the quotient in the destination register and the remainder in a SR3 register.

RANDOM.description: Random Number Generator - Generates a random number and stores it in the RD register.

XOR.description: Exclusive OR - Performs a bitwise exclusive OR operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

AND.description: AND - Performs a bitwise AND operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

OR.description: OR - Performs a bitwise OR operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

NOT.description: NOT - Performs a bitwise NOT operation on the value in the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

XNOR.description: Exclusive NOR - Performs a bitwise exclusive NOR operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

NAND.description: NAND - Performs a bitwise NAND operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

NOR.description: NOR - Performs a bitwise NOR operation between the values in the two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

XORI.description: Exclusive OR Immediate - Performs a bitwise exclusive OR operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

ANDI.description: AND Immediate - Performs a bitwise AND operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

ORI.description: OR Immediate - Performs a bitwise OR operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

XNORI.description: Exclusive NOR Immediate - Performs a bitwise exclusive NOR operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

NANDI.description: NAND Immediate - Performs a bitwise NAND operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

NORI.description: NOR Immediate - Performs a bitwise NOR operation between the value in the source register and the 1 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

SHL.description: Shift Left - Shifts the bits in the source register to the left by the number of positions specified in the immediate value, filling the least significant bits with zeros, and stores the result in the destination register.

SHR.description: Shift Right - Shifts the bits in the source register to the right by the number of positions specified in the immediate value, filling the most significant bits with zeros, and stores the result in the destination register.

ROL.description: Rotate Left - Rotates the bits in the source register to the left by the number of positions specified in the immediate value, wrapping the bits around, and stores the result in the destination register.

ROR.description: Rotate Right - Rotates the bits in the source register to the right by the number of positions specified in the immediate value, wrapping the bits around, and stores the result in the destination register.

SAR.description: Shift Arithmetic Right - Shifts the bits in the source register to the right by the number of positions specified in the immediate value, preserving the sign bit (most significant bit), and stores the result in the destination register.
SAR.encoding_notes: Relocated from v1 opcode 0x5B, which collided with COPYIP; SAR is 0x5D in v2 and COPYIP keeps 0x5B.

BTLE.description: Big endian to little endian - Converts the value in the source register from big-endian to little-endian format and stores the result in the destination register.

BTBE.description: Little endian to big endian - Converts the value in the source register from little-endian to big-endian format and stores the result in the destination register.

XCHG.description: Exchange - Swaps the values between the destination and source registers.

SHLR.description: Shift Half Left - Shifts the bits in the source register to the left, filling the least significant bits with zeros, and stores the result in the destination register. The maximum shift amount is 32.

SHRR.description: Shift Half Right - Shifts the bits in the source register to the right, filling the most significant bits with zeros, and stores the result in the destination register. The maximum shift amount is 32.

SARR.description: Shift Arithmetic Left - Shifts the bits in the source register to the left, preserving the sign bit (most significant bit), and stores the result in the destination register. The maximum shift amount is 32.

ROLR.description: Rotate Left - Rotates the bits in the source register to the left, wrapping the bits around, and stores the result in the destination register. The maximum rotate amount is 32.

RORR.description: Rotate Right - Rotates the bits in the source register to the right, wrapping the bits around, and stores the result in the destination register. The maximum rotate amount is 32.

XORIDW.description: Exclusive OR Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise exclusive OR operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

ANDIDW.description: AND Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise AND operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

ORIDW.description: OR Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise OR operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

XNORIDW.description: Exclusive NOR Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise exclusive NOR operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

NANDIDW.description: NAND Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise NAND operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

NORIDW.description: NOR Immediate Double Word - Performs a bitwise NOR operation between the value in the source register and the 4 byte immediate value, storing the result in the destination register.

MOV.description: Move - Copies the value of the source register to the destination register.

CLR ra.description: Clear ra - Sets the value of the ra register to zero.

JZ.description: Jump if Zero - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the zero flag (ZF) is set.

JC.description: Jump if Carry - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the carry flag (CF) is set.

JO.description: Jump if Overflow - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the overflow flag (OF) is set.

JN.description: Jump if Negative - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the negative flag (NF) is set.

JNZ.description: Jump if Not Zero - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the zero flag (ZF) is not set.

JNC.description: Jump if Not Carry - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the carry flag (CF) is not set.

JNO.description: Jump if Not Overflow - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the overflow flag (OF) is not set.

JNN.description: Jump if Not Negative - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the negative flag (NF) is not set.

JL.description: Jump if Less - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the signed comparison indicates the first value is less than the second. (NF != OF)

JGE.description: Jump if Greater or Equal - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the signed comparison indicates the first value is greater than or equal to the second. (NF == OF)

JA.description: Jump if Above - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is above the second. (CF == 0 && ZF == 0)

JBE.description: Jump if Below or Equal - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is below or equal to the second. (CF == 1 || ZF == 1)

JLE.description: Jump if Less or Equal - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the signed comparison indicates the first value is less than or equal to the second. (ZF == 1 || NF != OF)

JAG.description: Jump if Above or Greater - Jumps to the current 2 byte address plus the specified 2 byte offset (signed) if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is above and the signed comparison indicates the first value is greater than the second. (CF == 0 && ZF == 0 && NF == OF)

MOVZ.description: Move if Zero - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the zero flag (ZF) is set.

MOVC.description: Move if Carry - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the carry flag (CF) is set.

MOVO.description: Move if Overflow - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the overflow flag (OF) is set.

MOVN.description: Move if Negative - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the negative flag (NF) is set.

MOVNZ.description: Move if Not Zero - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the zero flag (ZF) is not set.

MOVNC.description: Move if Not Carry - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the carry flag (CF) is not set.

MOVNO.description: Move if Not Overflow - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the overflow flag (OF) is not set.

MOVNN.description: Move if Not Negative - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the negative flag (NF) is not set.

MOVL.description: Move if Less - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the signed comparison indicates the first value is less than the second. (NF != OF)

MOVGE.description: Move if Greater or Equal - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the signed comparison indicates the first value is greater than or equal to the second. (NF == OF)

MOVA.description: Move if Above - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is above the second. (CF == 0 && ZF == 0)

MOVBE.description: Move if Below or Equal - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is below or equal to the second. (CF == 1 || ZF == 1)

MOVLE.description: Move if Less or Equal - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the signed comparison indicates the first value is less than or equal to the second. (ZF == 1 || NF != OF)

MOVAG.description: Move if Above or Greater - Moves the value from the source register to the destination register if the unsigned comparison indicates the first value is above and the signed comparison indicates the first value is greater than the second. (CF == 0 && ZF == 0 && NF == OF)

IN.description: Input - Reads a byte from the specified port into the ri register.

OUT.description: Output - Writes the value in the ri register to the specified port.

LD.description: Load - Loads the value in the source register + the 1 byte offset as a signed value into the destination register. (DRG = [SR1 + OF8])

ST.description: Store - Stores the value in the source register into the destination register + the 1 byte offset as a signed value. (DRG = [SR1 + OF8])

LDOFIP.description: Load Offset from Instruction Pointer - Loads the value at the current instruction pointer plus the 2 byte offset (signed) into the destination register. (DRG = [IP + O16])

STOFIP.description: Store Offset from Instruction Pointer - Stores the value in the source register into the current instruction pointer plus the 2 byte offset (signed). ( [IP + O16] = SR1 )

SYSCALL.description: System Call - Triggers a system call interrupt to request services from the operating system.

SYSRET.description: System Return - Returns from a system call interrupt back to user mode.

HALT.description: Halt - Halts the processor until the next external interrupt is received.

LDIDT.description: Load IDT - Loads the IDT register to rb. (LD rb, [IDT])

MODIDT.description: Modify IDT - Reads the address in IDT register, adds the 1 byte offset (unsigned) to it as the address and writes the new address to that location. (LD [IDT + OF8], A32)

SETIDT.description: Set IDT - Writes the address in A32 to the IDT register. (ST [IDT], A32)

MOVCTRL.description: Move Control - Copies the value of the source register to the destination register. (DRC = SR1)

COPCTRL.description: Copy from Coprocessor - Copies the value from the coprocessor source register to the general-purpose destination register. (DRG = COP SRC)

BRK.description: Breakpoint - Triggers a breakpoint interrupt to request services from the operating system.

INT.description: Interrupt - Triggers an interrupt to request services from the operating system.

IRET.description: Interrupt Return - Returns from an interrupt back to the previous mode.

BT.description: BT - Bit Test - Copies bit (SR2 mod 8*2^ESZ) of DRG into ZF and leaves DRG unchanged; ESZ 0, 1 and 2 select a byte, word or dword bit base and ESZ 3 raises #UDI.

BTS.description: BTS - Bit Test And Set - Copies bit (SR2 mod 8*2^ESZ) of DRG into ZF and then sets that bit in DRG, so the operation is a read-modify-write on the destination register; ESZ 3 raises #UDI.

BTR.description: BTR - Bit Test And Reset - Copies bit (SR2 mod 8*2^ESZ) of DRG into ZF and then clears that bit in DRG, so the operation is a read-modify-write on the destination register; ESZ 3 raises #UDI.

BTC.description: BTC - Bit Test And Complement - Copies bit (SR2 mod 8*2^ESZ) of DRG into ZF and then inverts that bit in DRG, so the operation is a read-modify-write on the destination register; ESZ 3 raises #UDI.

BTI.description: BTI - Bit Test Immediate - Copies bit (IM8 mod 32) of the full 32-bit DRG into ZF and leaves DRG unchanged; the immediate forms always address the dword bit base.

BTSI.description: BTSI - Bit Test And Set Immediate - Copies bit (IM8 mod 32) of the full 32-bit DRG into ZF and then sets that bit in DRG; the immediate forms always address the dword bit base.
BTSI.pseudo_semantics: i <- IM8 & 31 ; ZF <- (DRG >> i) & 1 ; DRG <- DRG | (1 << i)

BTRI.description: BTRI - Bit Test And Reset Immediate - Copies bit (IM8 mod 32) of the full 32-bit DRG into ZF and then clears that bit in DRG; the immediate forms always address the dword bit base.

BTCI.description: BTCI - Bit Test And Complement Immediate - Copies bit (IM8 mod 32) of the full 32-bit DRG into ZF and then inverts that bit in DRG; the immediate forms always address the dword bit base.
BTCI.pseudo_semantics: i <- IM8 & 31 ; ZF <- (DRG >> i) & 1 ; DRG <- DRG ^ (1 << i)

BSF.description: BSF - Bit Scan Forward - Writes into DRG the index of the lowest set bit of the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 and sets ZF when that field is zero, in which case DRG is written with zero so the result is always defined.
BSF.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; ZF <- (v == 0) ; DRG <- v ? ctz(v) : 0

BSR.description: BSR - Bit Scan Reverse - Writes into DRG the index of the highest set bit of the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 and sets ZF when that field is zero, in which case DRG is written with zero; this is the floor of log2 for nonzero input.
BSR.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; ZF <- (v == 0) ; DRG <- v ? (31 - clz32(v)) : 0

POPCNT.description: POPCNT - Population Count - Counts the one bits in the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 into DRG and sets ZF when that count is zero, that is when the source field is zero.
POPCNT.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; n <- popcount(SR1 & lowmask(w)) ; ZF <- (n == 0) ; DRG <- n

CLZ.description: CLZ - Count Leading Zeros - Counts the leading zero bits of the 8*2^ESZ bit field of SR1 into DRG, giving the full field width when the field is zero, and sets ZF when the field is zero.
CLZ.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; ZF <- (v == 0) ; DRG <- (v == 0) ? w : (w - bitlen(v))

CTZ.description: CTZ - Count Trailing Zeros - Counts the trailing zero bits of the 8*2^ESZ bit field of SR1 into DRG, giving the full field width when the field is zero, and sets ZF when the field is zero.
CTZ.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; ZF <- (v == 0) ; DRG <- (v == 0) ? w : ctz(v)

PARCNT.description: PARCNT - Parity Count - Writes the parity of the one bit count of the 8*2^ESZ bit field of SR1 into DRG and PF, where one means an odd number of one bits, and sets ZF when the source field is zero.
PARCNT.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; p <- popcount(v) & 1 ; PF <- p ; ZF <- (v == 0) ; DRG <- p

BREV.description: BREV - Bit Reverse - Reverses the bit order of the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 and zero-extends the reversed field into DRG; no flags are written.

SHLD.description: SHLD - Shift Left Double - Shifts the 64-bit value DRG:SR1 left by (SR2 mod 32) bits, keeps the high half in DRG, writes CF with the last bit shifted out of DRG, and sets ZF and NF from the result; a count of zero changes neither DRG nor CF and OF is left unchanged.

SHRD.description: SHRD - Shift Right Double - Shifts the 64-bit value DRG:SR1 right by (SR2 mod 32) bits, keeps the low half in DRG, writes CF with the last bit shifted out of DRG, and sets ZF and NF from the result; a count of zero changes neither DRG nor CF and OF is left unchanged.

SHLX.description: SHLX - Shift Left Without Flags - Shifts SR1 left by (SR2 mod 32) bits into DRG and leaves every flag unchanged, so the shift can be scheduled between two flag-producing operations.

SHRX.description: SHRX - Shift Right Without Flags - Shifts SR1 right logically by (SR2 mod 32) bits into DRG and leaves every flag unchanged, so the shift can be scheduled between two flag-producing operations.

SARX.description: SARX - Shift Arithmetic Right Without Flags - Shifts SR1 right keeping its sign bit by (SR2 mod 32) bits into DRG and leaves every flag unchanged.

ROLX.description: ROLX - Rotate Left Without Flags - Rotates SR1 left by (SR2 mod 32) bits into DRG and leaves every flag unchanged; a count of zero copies SR1.

RORX.description: RORX - Rotate Right Without Flags - Rotates SR1 right by (SR2 mod 32) bits into DRG and leaves every flag unchanged; a count of zero copies SR1.

PEXT.description: PEXT - Parallel Bit Extract - Gathers into the low bits of DRG the bits of SR1 whose positions hold a one in the mask SR2, in increasing position order, zeroes the remaining bits of DRG and sets ZF when DRG is zero.

PDEP.description: PDEP - Parallel Bit Deposit - Scatters the low bits of SR1 into the bit positions of DRG where the mask SR2 holds a one, in increasing position order, and sets ZF when DRG is zero.

BZHI.description: BZHI - Zero High Bits - Clears every bit of SR1 at or above the index SR2[7:0] and writes the result to DRG; an index of 32 or more copies SR1 unchanged with CF set, a smaller index clears CF, and ZF describes the result.
BZHI.pseudo_semantics: n <- SR2[7:0] ; if n > 31 then (DRG <- SR1 ; CF <- 1) else (DRG <- SR1 & lowmask(n) ; CF <- 0) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0)

MASKLSB.description: MASKLSB - Low Mask - Builds in DRG a mask of SR2[7:0] low order one bits within the 8*2^ESZ bit operand width, saturating at the width, and sets ZF when the mask is zero.
MASKLSB.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; n <- SR2[7:0] ; DRG <- (n >= w) ? lowmask(w) : lowmask(n) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0)

BEXT.description: BEXT - Bit Field Extract - Extracts MO+1 bits of SR1 starting at bit IM8 and 31 into the low bits of DRG and zero-extends, so MO 0 extracts one bit, MO 15 extracts sixteen bits and positions beyond bit 31 read as zero.
BEXT.pseudo_semantics: o <- IM8 & 31 ; n <- MO + 1 ; DRG <- zext((SR1 >> o) & lowmask(n), 32)

BINS.description: BINS - Bit Field Insert - Replaces the MO+1 bits of DRG that start at bit IM8 and 31 with the low MO+1 bits of SR1 and leaves every other bit of DRG unchanged, so DRG is read before it is written; field bits that would land above bit 31 are discarded.
BINS.pseudo_semantics: o <- IM8 & 31 ; n <- MO + 1 ; m <- lowmask(n) << o ; DRG <- (DRG & ~m) | ((SR1 & lowmask(n)) << o)

BEXTS.description: BEXTS - Sign Extended Bit Field Extract - Extracts MO+1 bits of SR1 starting at bit IM8 and 31 and sign-extends that field to the full 32 bits of DRG, which is the signed counterpart of BEXT.
BEXTS.pseudo_semantics: o <- IM8 & 31 ; n <- MO + 1 ; DRG <- sign_extend((SR1 >> o) & lowmask(n), n)

BEXTD.description: BEXTD - Bit Field Extract Dynamic - Extracts the field of SR1 that starts at bit SR2[4:0] and is SR2[12:8]+1 bits wide into the low bits of DRG with zero extension, which is the register-driven form of BEXT.
BEXTD.pseudo_semantics: o <- SR2[4:0] ; n <- SR2[12:8] + 1 ; DRG <- zext((SR1 >> o) & lowmask(n), 32)

BINSD.description: BINSD - Bit Field Insert Dynamic - Replaces in DRG the field that starts at bit SR2[4:0] and is SR2[12:8]+1 bits wide with the low bits of SR1 and leaves all other bits of DRG unchanged; field bits that would land above bit 31 are discarded.
BINSD.pseudo_semantics: o <- SR2[4:0] ; n <- SR2[12:8] + 1 ; m <- lowmask(n) << o ; DRG <- (DRG & ~m) | ((SR1 & lowmask(n)) << o)

GRAYE.description: GRAYE - Gray Encode - Converts the 8*2^ESZ bit value of SR1 to reflected Gray code in DRG by exclusive-oring it with itself shifted right by one and zero-extending the field; no flags are written.
GRAYE.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; DRG <- zext(v ^ (v >> 1), 32)

GRAYD.description: GRAYD - Gray Decode - Converts the 8*2^ESZ bit reflected Gray code of SR1 back to binary in DRG, where bit i of the result is the exclusive-or of the source bits from i to the top of the field; no flags are written.
GRAYD.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; g <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; DRG <- zext(gray_to_binary(g, w), 32)

MULH.description: MULH - Multiply High Unsigned - Multiplies the unsigned 32-bit SR1 and SR2 and writes the upper half of the 64-bit product to DRG while the low half is discarded; ZF and NF describe the high half. v1 MUL delivers the same product but forces the high half into SR3.
MULH.pseudo_semantics: p <- zext(SR1, 32) * zext(SR2, 32) ; DRG <- wrap32(p >> 32) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MULHS.description: MULHS - Multiply High Signed - Multiplies SR1 and SR2 as signed 32-bit values and writes the upper half of the signed 64-bit product to DRG; ZF and NF describe the high half. v1 SMUL is the only signed product and always writes the low half to the destination.
MULHS.pseudo_semantics: p <- sign_extend(SR1, 32) * sign_extend(SR2, 32) ; DRG <- wrap32(p >> 32) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MULX.description: MULX - Multiply Extended - Multiplies the unsigned 8*2^ESZ bit values of SR2 and SR3 and writes the low 32 bits of the product to DRG and the high 32 bits to SR1, so one 8x8, 16x16 or 32x32 product produces a full width pair; ZF and NF describe DRG.

MULI.description: MULI - Multiply Immediate - Multiplies SR1 by IM8, extended by sign when MO[0]=0 and by zero when MO[0]=1, writes the low 32 bits to DRG, sets CF and OF when the exact product does not fit in 32 bits under the selected signedness and sets ZF and NF from DRG.
MULI.pseudo_semantics: m <- MO[0] ? zext(IM8, 32) : sign_extend(IM8, 32) ; p <- MO[0] ? (zext(SR1, 32) * m) : (sign_extend(SR1, 32) * sign_extend(m, 32)) ; DRG <- wrap32(p) ; CF <- MO[0] ? ((p >> 32) != 0) : (sign_extend(DRG, 32) != p) ; OF <- CF ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MADD.description: MADD - Multiply Accumulate - Adds the signed product of SR1 and SR2 to DRG, writes the low 32 bits back to DRG and sets OF when the 32-bit accumulator overflowed; ZF and NF describe the new DRG.
MADD.pseudo_semantics: p <- sign_extend(SR1, 32) * sign_extend(SR2, 32) ; s <- sign_extend(DRG, 32) + p ; DRG <- wrap32(s) ; OF <- (sign_extend(DRG, 32) != s) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MSUB.description: MSUB - Multiply Subtract - Subtracts the signed product of SR1 and SR2 from DRG, writes the low 32 bits back to DRG and sets OF when the 32-bit accumulator overflowed; ZF and NF describe the new DRG.
MSUB.pseudo_semantics: p <- sign_extend(SR1, 32) * sign_extend(SR2, 32) ; s <- sign_extend(DRG, 32) - p ; DRG <- wrap32(s) ; OF <- (sign_extend(DRG, 32) != s) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MADDU.description: MADDU - Multiply Accumulate Unsigned - Adds the unsigned product of SR1 and SR2 to DRG, writes the low 32 bits back to DRG and sets OF when the 32-bit accumulator wrapped; ZF and NF describe the new DRG.
MADDU.pseudo_semantics: p <- zext(SR1, 32) * zext(SR2, 32) ; s <- zext(DRG, 32) + p ; DRG <- wrap32(s) ; OF <- (s > 0xFFFFFFFF) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MSUBU.description: MSUBU - Multiply Subtract Unsigned - Subtracts the unsigned product of SR1 and SR2 from DRG, writes the low 32 bits back to DRG and sets OF when the unsigned accumulator went below zero; ZF and NF describe the new DRG.
MSUBU.pseudo_semantics: p <- zext(SR1, 32) * zext(SR2, 32) ; s <- zext(DRG, 32) - p ; DRG <- wrap32(s) ; OF <- (s < 0) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

DIVMOD.description: DIVMOD - Divide With Remainder - Divides the unsigned SR1 by SR2, writes the quotient to DRG and the remainder back into SR1, raises #DIV when SR2 is zero and sets ZF and NF from the quotient; unlike v1 DIV the remainder stays in the dividend register instead of a third encoded register.
DIVMOD.pseudo_semantics: #DIV if SR2 == 0 ; d <- zext(SR1, 32) ; DRG <- wrap32(d / zext(SR2, 32)) ; SR1 <- wrap32(d % zext(SR2, 32)) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

REM.description: REM - Remainder Unsigned - Writes into DRG the remainder of the unsigned SR1 divided by SR2, raises #DIV when SR2 is zero and sets ZF and NF from the remainder.
REM.pseudo_semantics: #DIV if SR2 == 0 ; DRG <- wrap32(zext(SR1, 32) % zext(SR2, 32)) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

REMS.description: REMS - Remainder Signed - Writes into DRG the signed remainder of SR1 divided by SR2, whose sign follows the dividend, raises #DIV when SR2 is zero and sets ZF and NF from the remainder.
REMS.pseudo_semantics: #DIV if SR2 == 0 ; DRG <- wrap32(srem(sign_extend(SR1, 32), sign_extend(SR2, 32))) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

DIVI.description: DIVI - Divide Immediate - Divides SR1 by IM8, extended by sign when MO[0]=0 and by zero when MO[0]=1, writes the truncated signed quotient to DRG, raises #DIV when the divisor is zero and sets ZF and NF from the quotient.
DIVI.pseudo_semantics: d <- MO[0] ? zext(IM8, 32) : sign_extend(IM8, 32) ; #DIV if d == 0 ; DRG <- wrap32(sdiv(sign_extend(SR1, 32), d)) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

ADDC.description: ADDC - Add With Carry - Adds SR1, SR2 and the incoming CF into DRG and writes ZF, CF, OF and NF, so a multi-word addition chains one ADDC per word starting from the carry of the previous word.

SUBC.description: SUBC - Subtract With Borrow - Subtracts SR2 and the incoming CF from SR1 into DRG and writes ZF, CF, OF and NF, so a multi-word subtraction chains one SUBC per word starting from the borrow of the previous word.

ADCX.description: ADCX - Add With Carry Chain - Adds SR1, the incoming CF and the low 8*2^ESZ bits of DRG, writes only that field of DRG and CF, and leaves ZF, OF, NF, AF and PF untouched, so ADCX and ADOX can run two independent carry chains over the same data.
ADCX.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; m <- lowmask(w) ; s <- (DRG & m) + (SR1 & m) + CF ; DRG <- (DRG & ~m) | (s & m) ; CF <- (s >> w) & 1

ADOX.description: ADOX - Add With Overflow Chain - Adds SR1, the incoming OF and the low 8*2^ESZ bits of DRG, writes only that field of DRG and OF, and leaves ZF, CF, NF, AF and PF untouched, giving a second carry chain that runs alongside ADCX.
ADOX.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; m <- lowmask(w) ; s <- (DRG & m) + (SR1 & m) + OF ; DRG <- (DRG & ~m) | (s & m) ; OF <- (s >> w) & 1

MAXS.description: MAXS - Maximum Signed - Writes the larger of SR1 and SR2 compared as signed 32-bit values into DRG and sets ZF and NF from the result; equal operands write SR1.
MAXS.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- (sign_extend(SR1, 32) >= sign_extend(SR2, 32)) ? SR1 : SR2 ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MINS.description: MINS - Minimum Signed - Writes the smaller of SR1 and SR2 compared as signed 32-bit values into DRG and sets ZF and NF from the result; equal operands write SR1.
MINS.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- (sign_extend(SR1, 32) <= sign_extend(SR2, 32)) ? SR1 : SR2 ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MAXU.description: MAXU - Maximum Unsigned - Writes the larger of SR1 and SR2 compared as unsigned 32-bit values into DRG and sets ZF and NF from the result; equal operands write SR1.
MAXU.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- (SR1 >= SR2) ? SR1 : SR2 ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MINU.description: MINU - Minimum Unsigned - Writes the smaller of SR1 and SR2 compared as unsigned 32-bit values into DRG and sets ZF and NF from the result; equal operands write SR1.
MINU.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- (SR1 <= SR2) ? SR1 : SR2 ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

ABSDIFF.description: ABSDIFF - Absolute Difference - Writes into DRG the absolute value of the unsigned difference of SR1 and SR2 and sets CF when SR1 was below SR2, so the sign of the difference survives in CF; ZF and NF describe the result.
ABSDIFF.pseudo_semantics: CF <- (SR1 < SR2) ; DRG <- CF ? (SR2 - SR1) : (SR1 - SR2) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

AVG.description: AVG - Average Unsigned - Writes into DRG the floor of the unsigned average of SR1 and SR2 computed without an intermediate overflow, and sets ZF and NF from the result.

SATADD.description: SATADD - Saturating Add Signed - Adds SR1 and SR2 as signed values, saturates the 32-bit sum to 0x7FFFFFFF or 0x80000000 into DRG, sets VF when saturation happened and sets ZF and NF from the result.

SATSUB.description: SATSUB - Saturating Subtract Signed - Subtracts SR2 from SR1 as signed values, saturates the 32-bit difference to 0x7FFFFFFF or 0x80000000 into DRG, sets VF when saturation happened and sets ZF and NF from the result.

SATADDU.description: SATADDU - Saturating Add Unsigned - Adds SR1 and SR2 as unsigned values, saturates the sum at 0xFFFFFFFF into DRG, sets VF when saturation happened and sets ZF and NF from the result.
SATADDU.pseudo_semantics: s <- zext(SR1, 32) + zext(SR2, 32) ; DRG <- (s > 0xFFFFFFFF) ? 0xFFFFFFFF : s ; VF <- (s > 0xFFFFFFFF) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

SATSUBU.description: SATSUBU - Saturating Subtract Unsigned - Subtracts SR2 from SR1 as unsigned values, saturates the difference at zero into DRG, sets VF when the unsigned difference would have gone below zero and sets ZF and NF from the result.

CLAMP.description: CLAMP - Clamp To Range Signed - Clamps SR1 into the signed range whose lower bound is the incoming DRG and whose upper bound is SR2, writes the clamped value back to DRG and sets VF when SR1 was outside the range; DRG is read before it is written.
CLAMP.pseudo_semantics: r <- (sign_extend(SR1, 32) < sign_extend(DRG, 32)) ? DRG : ((sign_extend(SR2, 32) < sign_extend(SR1, 32)) ? SR2 : SR1) ; VF <- (r != SR1) ; DRG <- r ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

CLAMPU.description: CLAMPU - Clamp To Range Unsigned - Clamps SR1 into the unsigned range whose lower bound is the incoming DRG and whose upper bound is SR2, writes the clamped value back to DRG and sets VF when SR1 was outside the range; DRG is read before it is written.
CLAMPU.pseudo_semantics: r <- (SR1 < DRG) ? DRG : ((SR2 < SR1) ? SR2 : SR1) ; VF <- (r != SR1) ; DRG <- r ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

ISQRT.description: ISQRT - Integer Square Root - Writes into DRG the floor of the square root of the unsigned 8*2^ESZ bit field of SR1 and sets ZF when the result is zero; the operation never faults on data and raises #UDI only for a reserved ESZ.
ISQRT.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; v <- SR1 & lowmask(w) ; DRG <- isqrt(v) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0)

SEXT.description: SEXT - Sign Extend - Sign-extends the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 into DRG, where ESZ 0, 1 and 2 select byte, word and dword source widths and ESZ 3 raises #UDI; no flags are written.

ZEXT.description: ZEXT - Zero Extend - Zero-extends the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 into DRG, where ESZ 0, 1 and 2 select byte, word and dword source widths and ESZ 3 raises #UDI; no flags are written.

TRUNC.description: TRUNC - Truncate With Loss Detect - Keeps the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 in DRG, zeroes every higher bit and sets VF when any discarded bit was one; ESZ 3 raises #UDI.
TRUNC.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; VF <- (SR1 >> w) != 0 ; DRG <- SR1 & lowmask(w)

BSWAP.description: BSWAP - Byte Swap - Reverses the byte order of the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1, with ESZ 0 an identity, ESZ 1 a halfword swap and ESZ 2 a dword swap, and zero-extends the result into DRG; no flags are written.

CVTSZ.description: CVTSZ - Convert Size - Converts the low 8*2^ESZ bits of SR1 to the width selected by MO[1:0] (0=BYTE, 1=WORD, 2=DWORD), extending by sign when MO[2]=1 and by zero otherwise, clamping when MO[3]=1 and wrapping when MO[3]=0, then zero-extends into DRG and sets VF when the conversion was inexact.
CVTSZ.pseudo_semantics: s <- 8 << ESZ ; d <- 8 << MO[1:0] ; t <- (MO[2] ? sign_extend(SR1[s-1:0], 32) : zext(SR1[s-1:0], 32)) ; r <- (MO[3] ? clamp_to(t, d) : wrap_to(t, d)) ; VF <- (r != t) ; DRG <- zext(r, 32)

SATCAST.description: SATCAST - Saturating Cast - Clamps SR1 into the 8*2^ESZ bit destination field, with MO[0]=0 for signed clamping and MO[0]=1 for unsigned clamping, MO[1]=1 preserving the upper bits of DRG while MO[1]=0 zeroes them, and MO[2]=1 replacing clamping with plain truncation; VF is set whenever the written field cannot carry the full source value.
SATCAST.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; p <- MO[2] ? (SR1 & lowmask(w)) : (MO[0] ? clamp_unsigned(SR1, w) : clamp_signed(SR1, w)) ; VF <- MO[2] ? ((SR1 & ~lowmask(w)) != 0) : (MO[0] ? (SR1 > lowmask(w)) : (sign_extend(SR1, 32) != sign_extend(p, w))) ; DRG <- MO[1] ? ((DRG & ~lowmask(w)) | p) : p

PACK.description: PACK - Pack Two Lanes - Packs SR1 into the low lane and SR2 into the high lane of DRG, where MO[1:0] selects BYTE lanes (0) or WORD lanes (1) and MO[3:2] selects signed saturation (0), unsigned saturation (1) or truncation (2); VF is set when a lane lost information, that is when the source value did not fit the lane under the selected mode, and bits above the packed field of DRG are zeroed.
PACK.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << MO[1:0] ; md <- MO[3:2] ; lo <- pack_lane(SR1, w, md) ; hi <- pack_lane(SR2, w, md) ; VF <- pack_lost(SR1, w, md) | pack_lost(SR2, w, md) ; DRG <- (hi << w) | lo

MOVS.description: MOVS - Move String - Copies the 8*2^ESZ bit element at the source pointer ri to the destination pointer rd and then steps both pointers by 1, 2 or 4 bytes, upward when DF is zero and downward when DF is one; under the REP prefix the move repeats rc times.
MOVS.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; e <- [ri] ; [rd] <- e ; ri <- ri + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0

CMPS.description: CMPS - Compare String - Subtracts the 8*2^ESZ bit element at rd from the element at ri, sets ZF, CF, OF and NF from that comparison and steps both pointers according to DF; under REP the comparison repeats rc times and stops early once the elements differ.
CMPS.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; a <- [ri] ; b <- [rd] ; ZF <- (a == b) ; CF <- (a < b) ; NF <- wrap32(a - b)[31] ; OF <- (a[sz*8-1] != b[sz*8-1]) & (wrap32(a - b)[sz*8-1] != a[sz*8-1]) ; ri <- ri + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0 or ZF == 0

SCAS.description: SCAS - Compare String Accumulator - Subtracts the 8*2^ESZ bit element at rd from the accumulator ra, sets ZF, CF, OF and NF from that comparison and steps rd according to DF; under REP the scan repeats rc times and stops early once the elements are equal.
SCAS.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; a <- ra ; b <- [rd] ; ZF <- (a == b) ; CF <- (a < b) ; NF <- wrap32(a - b)[31] ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0 or ZF == 1

STOS.description: STOS - Store String - Writes the low 8*2^ESZ bits of the accumulator ra to the element at rd and steps rd according to DF; under the REP prefix the store repeats rc times, which is the canonical block fill idiom.
STOS.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; [rd] <- ra[sz*8-1:0] ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0

LODS.description: LODS - Load String - Loads the 8*2^ESZ bit element at ri into the accumulator ra with zero extension and steps ri according to DF; under the REP prefix the load repeats rc times.
LODS.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; ra <- zext([ri], 32) ; ri <- ri + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0

MOVSN.description: MOVSN - Move String Non Temporal - Identical to MOVS but the destination store is issued as a non temporal streaming write that does not allocate in the L1 data cache; a MEMO prefix CH field selects the eviction hint and REP repeats the move rc times.
MOVSN.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; e <- [ri] ; nontemporal_store([rd], e) ; ri <- ri + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0

STOSN.description: STOSN - Store String Non Temporal - Identical to STOS but the store is issued as a non temporal streaming write that does not allocate in the L1 data cache; a MEMO prefix CH field selects the eviction hint and REP repeats the store rc times.
STOSN.pseudo_semantics: sz <- 1 << ESZ ; nontemporal_store([rd], ra[sz*8-1:0]) ; rd <- rd + (DF ? -sz : sz) ; if REP then repeat until rc == 0

ADDBCD.description: ADDBCD - Add Packed BCD - Adds SR1 and SR2 as eight packed BCD digits with two digits per byte, writes the decimal sum to DRG, sets CF on the carry out of the most significant digit, AF on the carry out of the least significant digit and VF when an input digit was not a valid BCD digit; NF mirrors bit 31 of the result.
ADDBCD.pseudo_semantics: r <- bcd_add(SR1, SR2) ; DRG <- r.sum ; CF <- r.carry_out ; AF <- r.carry_low ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) | bcd_invalid(SR2) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

SUBBCD.description: SUBBCD - Subtract Packed BCD - Subtracts SR2 from SR1 as eight packed BCD digits, writes the difference to DRG, sets CF on the borrow out of the most significant digit, AF on the borrow out of the least significant digit and VF when an input digit was not valid; NF mirrors bit 31 of the result.
SUBBCD.pseudo_semantics: r <- bcd_sub(SR1, SR2) ; DRG <- r.diff ; CF <- r.borrow_out ; AF <- r.borrow_low ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) | bcd_invalid(SR2) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

CMPBCD.description: CMPBCD - Compare Packed BCD - Subtracts SR2 from SR1 as packed BCD digits only to produce flags: ZF when the numbers are equal, CF when SR1 is the smaller, AF from the least significant digit, NF from bit 31 of the digitwise difference and VF when an input digit was not valid; DRG is not written.
CMPBCD.pseudo_semantics: r <- bcd_sub(SR1, SR2) ; ZF <- (r.diff == 0) ; CF <- r.borrow_out ; AF <- r.borrow_low ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) | bcd_invalid(SR2) ; NF <- r.diff[31]

NEGBCD.description: NEGBCD - Negate Packed BCD - Writes into DRG the ten's complement of the eight digit packed BCD value in SR1 when MO[0]=0 and its nine's complement, that is 99999999 minus SR1 digit by digit, when MO[0]=1; CF is set when SR1 was nonzero and VF when an input digit was not valid.
NEGBCD.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- MO[0] ? bcd_nines(SR1) : bcd_neg(SR1) ; CF <- (SR1 != 0) ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

BCDSHL.description: BCDSHL - Decimal Shift Left - Multiplies the packed BCD value in SR1 by ten MO[2:0] times, which shifts it left by whole decimal digits, writes the low eight digits to DRG and sets VF when a nonzero digit was shifted out of the most significant position.
BCDSHL.pseudo_semantics: n <- MO[2:0] ; r <- SR1 ; VF <- 0 ; repeat n times (VF <- VF | (r[31:28] != 0) ; r <- (r << 4) & 0xFFFFFFFF) ; DRG <- r ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

BCDSHR.description: BCDSHR - Decimal Shift Right - Divides the packed BCD value in SR1 by ten MO[2:0] times, which shifts it right by whole decimal digits with the vacated high digits filled with zero, and sets VF when a nonzero digit was shifted out of the least significant position.
BCDSHR.pseudo_semantics: n <- MO[2:0] ; r <- SR1 ; VF <- 0 ; repeat n times (VF <- VF | ((r & 0xF) != 0) ; r <- r >> 4) ; DRG <- r ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

MULBCD.description: MULBCD - Multiply Packed BCD - Multiplies SR1 and SR2 as unsigned eight digit packed BCD values, writes the low eight decimal digits of the product to DRG and sets CF when the exact product needs more than eight digits; VF marks an input digit that was not valid.
MULBCD.pseudo_semantics: a <- bcd_value(SR1) ; b <- bcd_value(SR2) ; p <- a * b ; DRG <- bin_to_bcd(p % 100000000) ; CF <- (p > 99999999) ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) | bcd_invalid(SR2) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

DIVBCD.description: DIVBCD - Divide Packed BCD - Divides the unsigned packed BCD value in SR1 by SR2, writes the BCD quotient to DRG and the BCD remainder back into SR1 following the DIVMOD register convention, raises #DIV when SR2 is zero or not valid BCD and sets VF when SR1 was not valid BCD.
DIVBCD.pseudo_semantics: #DIV if (SR2 == 0) | bcd_invalid(SR2) ; a <- bcd_value(SR1) ; b <- bcd_value(SR2) ; DRG <- bin_to_bcd(a / b) ; SR1 <- bin_to_bcd(a % b) ; VF <- bcd_invalid(SR1) ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

BCD2BIN.description: BCD2BIN - BCD To Binary - Converts the eight digit packed BCD value in SR1 to a binary 32-bit value in DRG; MO[0]=0 rejects invalid input digits by writing zero and setting VF, while MO[0]=1 treats an invalid digit as zero and converts the remaining digits.
BCD2BIN.pseudo_semantics: bad <- bcd_invalid(SR1) ; DRG <- (bad & !MO[0]) ? 0 : bcd_to_bin_masked(SR1) ; VF <- bad ; ZF <- (DRG == 0) ; NF <- DRG[31]

BIN2BCD.description: BIN2BCD - Binary To BCD - Converts the binary value in SR1 to eight packed BCD digits in DRG; MO[0]=0 saturates values above 99999999 to 99999999 and MO[0]=1 takes them modulo 10^8, and VF is set in both cases when SR1 exceeded eight digits.

JCND.description: JCND - Conditional Jump Relative - Jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 16-bit offset O16 when the condition selected by CC holds; the offset base is the address of the branch itself, matching v1 JZ and JMP, and a not-taken branch falls through.
JCND.pseudo_semantics: if cond(CC) then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(O16, 16)

JCNDL.description: JCNDL - Conditional Jump Relative Long - Jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32 when the condition selected by CC holds, giving a conditional branch that can reach anywhere in the 32-bit address space.
JCNDL.pseudo_semantics: if cond(CC) then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(O32, 32)

JMPREL.description: JMPREL - Jump Relative Short - Unconditionally jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 8-bit offset OF8, which is the densest branch form at two bytes and carries no SOP nibble so the encoding stays minimal.

JMPRELL.description: JMPRELL - Jump Relative Long - Unconditionally jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32; the format holds only O32, because a SOP nibble would break the even-nibble alignment and cost a sixth byte.

CALLREL.description: CALLREL - Call Relative - Pushes the address of the following instruction, which is this instruction's address plus five, and jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32.

LOOP.description: LOOP - Loop - Decrements DRG by one without writing any flag and jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 8-bit offset OF8 while DRG is still nonzero; the counter is an explicit register so no hidden register is read.
LOOP.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(OF8, 8)

LOOPZ.description: LOOPZ - Loop While Zero - Decrements DRG by one without writing any flag and jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 8-bit offset OF8 while DRG is nonzero and ZF is set, so a comparison placed before the loop survives.
LOOPZ.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 and ZF == 1 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(OF8, 8)

LOOPNZ.description: LOOPNZ - Loop While Not Zero - Decrements DRG by one without writing any flag and jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 8-bit offset OF8 while DRG is nonzero and ZF is clear, so a comparison placed before the loop survives.
LOOPNZ.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 and ZF == 0 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(OF8, 8)

LOOPL.description: LOOPL - Loop Long - Same as LOOP but jumps to this instruction's address plus the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32, which allows a loop body larger than the 8-bit short form can address.
LOOPL.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(O32, 32)

LOOPZL.description: LOOPZL - Loop Long While Zero - Same as LOOPZ but jumps with the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32, combining the long loop range with the ZF test.
LOOPZL.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 and ZF == 1 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(O32, 32)

LOOPNZL.description: LOOPNZL - Loop Long While Not Zero - Same as LOOPNZ but jumps with the sign-extended 32-bit offset O32, combining the long loop range with the ZF test.
LOOPNZL.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- DRG - 1 ; if DRG != 0 and ZF == 0 then IP <- addr(this) + sign_extend(O32, 32)

JTABLE.description: JTABLE - Jump Through Table - Reads a target address from the dispatch table entry at SR1 plus (SR2 and 255) times the entry size and jumps to it; MO[0]=0 selects 16-bit zero-extended entries and MO[0]=1 selects 32-bit entries, and a bad table address raises #MAV or #PGF.
JTABLE.pseudo_semantics: idx <- SR2 & 255 ; a <- SR1 + idx * (MO[0] ? 4 : 2) ; t <- MO[0] ? mem32[a] : zext(mem16[a], 32) ; IP <- t

CALLTAB.description: CALLTAB - Call Through Table - Pushes the address of the following instruction, which is this instruction's address plus three, and then jumps through the dispatch table entry at SR1 plus (SR2 and 255) times the entry size; MO[0] selects 16-bit or 32-bit entries.
CALLTAB.pseudo_semantics: push(addr(this) + 3) ; idx <- SR2 & 255 ; a <- SR1 + idx * (MO[0] ? 4 : 2) ; t <- MO[0] ? mem32[a] : zext(mem16[a], 32) ; IP <- t

RETFAR.description: RETFAR - Return Far - Pops the 32-bit return address from the top of the stack into IP and then discards MO more 32-bit stack words, so a callee can return and clean up to fifteen argument words in a single two-byte instruction.
RETFAR.pseudo_semantics: t <- mem32[sp] ; sp <- sp + 4 ; IP <- t ; sp <- sp + 4 * MO

SETCC.description: SETCC - Set Field On Condition - Writes the value 1 into the low 8*2^ESZ bit field of DRG when the condition selected by CC holds and the value 0 into that same field otherwise, leaving the other bits of DRG unchanged; ESZ 2 writes the whole register.

CMOVCC.description: CMOVCC - Conditional Move - Copies SR1 into DRG when the condition selected by CC holds and leaves DRG unchanged otherwise; the move always covers the full 32-bit register and the flags are only read.

CMPCC.description: CMPCC - Compare And Set Condition - Subtracts the low 8*2^ESZ bit fields of SR2 from SR1 into ZF, CF, OF, NF and AF and then writes 1 into DRG when the condition selected by CC holds for that comparison and 0 otherwise, fusing a compare with predicate materialisation.

TSTCC.description: TSTCC - Test And Set Condition - Ands the low 8*2^ESZ bit fields of SR1 and SR2 into ZF and NF, clears CF and OF, and then writes 1 into DRG when the condition selected by CC holds for that logical test and 0 otherwise; SR1 and SR2 are not modified.
TSTCC.pseudo_semantics: w <- 8 << ESZ ; m <- lowmask(w) ; r <- (SR1 & SR2) & m ; ZF <- (r == 0) ; NF <- r[w-1] ; CF <- 0 ; OF <- 0 ; DRG <- cond(CC) ? 1 : 0

FADD.description: FADD - Floating Add - Adds the FPF-format operands SF1 and SF2 with RM rounding and writes DFR; a NaN operand propagates the quieted payload of the first NaN, denormal operands take part in the operation exactly, and SF1 + (-SF1) produces +0 except under RM where it produces -0.
FADD.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, SF1 + SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2)

FSUB.description: FSUB - Floating Subtract - Subtracts SF2 from SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; infinities of equal sign set FLV, the sign of a zero difference follows the RM rule, and NaN inputs propagate a quieted payload.
FSUB.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, SF1 - SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | (isInf(SF1) & isInf(SF2) & sameSign)

FMUL.description: FMUL - Floating Multiply - Multiplies SF1 by SF2 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; a zero times infinity sets FLV, the sign of a zero product is the XOR of the operand signs, and denormal inputs and outputs are computed exactly.
FMUL.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, SF1 * SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | ((SF1 == 0) & isInf(SF2)) | ((SF2 == 0) & isInf(SF1))

FDIV.description: FDIV - Floating Divide - Divides SF1 by SF2 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; a finite non-zero dividend over zero yields an infinity with the XOR sign and sets FLO, 0/0 and inf/inf set FLV, and the result is correctly rounded once.
FDIV.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, SF1 / SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow | ((SF1 != 0) & isInf(SF2)); FLV <- ((SF1 == 0) & (SF2 == 0)) | (isInf(SF1) & isInf(SF2)) | isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2)

FMIN.description: FMIN - Floating Minimum - Writes the smaller of SF1 and SF2 to DFR using minNum semantics: one NaN operand yields the other operand, two NaNs yield the quieted payload of SF1, and -0 orders below +0 so that negation of the maximum matches the minimum.
FMIN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- minNum(SF1, SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) & isNaN(SF2)

FMAX.description: FMAX - Floating Maximum - Writes the larger of SF1 and SF2 to DFR using maxNum semantics: one NaN operand yields the other operand, two NaNs yield the quieted payload of SF1, and +0 orders above -0 so that max(x,y) == -min(-x,-y).
FMAX.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- maxNum(SF1, SF2); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) & isNaN(SF2)

FSQRT.description: FSQRT - Floating Square Root - Computes the square root of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; sqrt(-0) is -0, a negative non-zero operand sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and an exactness loss sets FLO.
FSQRT.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, sqrt(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- (SF1 < 0)

FRECIP.description: FRECIP - Floating Reciprocal - Computes 1/SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; the reciprocal of a zero is an infinity with the same sign and sets FLO, the reciprocal of an infinity is a zero, and a denormal input produces an overflowed reciprocal detected by FLO.
FRECIP.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, 1 / SF1); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | ((SF1 == 0) & !isNaN(SF1)); FLV <- isNaN(SF1)

FRECIPSQRT.description: FRECIPSQRT - Floating Reciprocal Square Root - Computes 1/sqrt(SF1) in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; a negative operand or a negative zero sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and 1/sqrt(+0) yields +infinity with FLO set.
FRECIPSQRT.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, 1 / sqrt(abs(SF1))); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | (SF1 == 0); FLV <- (SF1 < 0) | (SF1 == -0) | isNaN(SF1)

FROUND.description: FROUND - Floating Round To Integral - Rounds SF1 to an integral value in the same FPF format with RM into DFR; the sign of a zero result follows the input so that FROUND(-0.4) is -0 in RN, an infinity or NaN passes through unchanged, and FLV marks a NaN pass-through.
FROUND.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- roundToIntegral_fpf(RM, SF1); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)

FMADD.description: FMADD - Fused Multiply-Add - Computes SF1 * SF2 + SF3 with a single rounding in the FPF format and writes DFR; the product is formed exactly before the addition so that a denormal intermediate is not flushed, and the negated forms FNMSUB/FNMADD are not equivalent to FMADD under RM because only one rounding occurs.
FMADD.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RN, SF1 * SF2 + SF3); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | isNaN(SF3) | ((SF1 == 0) & isInf(SF2)) | ((SF2 == 0) & isInf(SF1))

FMSUB.description: FMSUB - Fused Multiply-Subtract - Computes SF1 * SF2 - SF3 with a single rounding in the FPF format into DFR; the exactness and NaN-propagation rules are those of FMADD, and the general rounding mode is RN with the FMT prefix able to override it.
FMSUB.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RN, SF1 * SF2 - SF3); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | isNaN(SF3)

FNMADD.description: FNMADD - Fused Negated Multiply-Add - Computes -(SF1 * SF2) + SF3 with a single rounding in the FPF format into DFR; the sign of the exact product is inverted before the addition, so a zero product yields +0 rather than the sign of the operand XOR.
FNMADD.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RN, -(SF1 * SF2) + SF3); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | isNaN(SF3)

FNMSUB.description: FNMSUB - Fused Negated Multiply-Subtract - Computes -(SF1 * SF2) - SF3 with a single rounding in the FPF format into DFR; it is the exact-negation form of FMADD and keeps the FNMSUB/FMADD identity only when both roundings are exact.
FNMSUB.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RN, -(SF1 * SF2) - SF3); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | isNaN(SF3)

FABS.description: FABS - Floating Absolute Value - Clears the sign bit of the FPF-format operand SF1 and writes DFR; this is a bit operation, so a NaN payload is preserved unchanged, -0 becomes +0, and no FP flag is modified or clearable by the FMT prefix.

FNEG.description: FNEG - Floating Negate - Inverts the sign bit of the FPF-format operand SF1 into DFR; the significand and any NaN payload are untouched, +0 becomes -0, and no flag is modified because negation is not an arithmetic operation.

FCOPYSIG.description: FCOPYSIG - Floating Copy Sign - Writes DFR with the magnitude taken from SF1 and the sign taken from SF2, both read in the FPF format; the payload of a NaN in SF1 survives intact, so FCOPYSIG can build a negative NaN from a positive one.

FSEL.description: FSEL - Floating Select - Writes SF1 to DFR when the condition selector CC holds and SF2 when it does not; the condition is evaluated on the integer flags and the FP flags FLZ/FLO/FLV, a NaN operand is selected like any other bit pattern, and no exception is ever raised.
FSEL.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- if cond(CC, FLZ, FLO, FLV, ZF, CF, OF, NF) then SF1 else SF2

FCMP.description: FCMP - Floating Compare Quiet - Orders the FPF-format operands SF1 and SF2 and sets FLZ when they are equal, FLO when SF1 is less than SF2 and FLV when either operand is a NaN; a signalling NaN operand is quieted without trapping and -0 compares equal to +0.
FCMP.pseudo_semantics: FLZ <- (SF1 == SF2); FLO <- (SF1 < SF2); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2)

FCMPU.description: FCMPU - Floating Compare Unordered - Signalling form of FCMP: any NaN operand, quiet or signalling, sets FLV and raises the FP invalid exception before the flags are written; for non-NaN operands it sets FLZ on equality and FLO when SF1 is less than SF2.
FCMPU.pseudo_semantics: if isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) then FLV <- 1, trap(#FLV) else FLZ <- (SF1 == SF2); FLO <- (SF1 < SF2); FLV <- 0

FCLASS.description: FCLASS - Floating Classify - Classifies the FPF-format operand SF1 and writes a one-hot class mask to the GPR DRG: bit0 -inf, bit1 negative normal, bit2 negative denormal, bit3 -0, bit4 +0, bit5 positive denormal, bit6 positive normal, bit7 +inf, bit8 signalling NaN, bit9 quiet NaN.

FTOSI.description: FTOSI - Float To Signed Integer - Converts the FPF-format operand SF1 to a 32-bit signed integer in DRG using RM rounding; a NaN or a value outside the signed 32-bit range sets FLV and writes the indefinite value 0x80000000, and any inexact conversion sets FLO.
FTOSI.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- wrap32(roundint(RM, SF1)); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | outOfRange; FLO <- inexact

FTOUI.description: FTOUI - Float To Unsigned Integer - Converts the FPF-format operand SF1 to a 32-bit unsigned integer in DRG using RM rounding; a negative value other than -0, a NaN or a value above 2^32-1 sets FLV and writes 0, and an inexact conversion sets FLO.
FTOUI.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- wrap32(roundint_unsigned(RM, SF1)); FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | (SF1 < 0) | (SF1 > 2^32-1); FLO <- inexact

SITOF.description: SITOF - Signed Integer To Float - Converts the 32-bit signed integer in the GPR SR1 to the FPF format in DFR using RM rounding; the conversion is exact when SR1 is representable in 24 significand bits, otherwise it rounds once and sets FLO, and a zero input sets FLZ and produces +0.
SITOF.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, sign_extend(SR1, 32)); FLZ <- (SR1 == 0); FLO <- inexact

UITOF.description: UITOF - Unsigned Integer To Float - Converts the 32-bit unsigned integer in the GPR SR1 to the FPF format in DFR using RM rounding; values above 2^24 round once and set FLO, and only SR1 equal to zero sets FLZ and produces +0.
UITOF.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, zero_extend(SR1, 32)); FLZ <- (SR1 == 0); FLO <- inexact

FMOV.description: FMOV - Floating Move - Copies the FPF-format FP register SF1 to DFR without any conversion, rounding or NaN quieting; all 32 FP registers are reachable through REX and no flag is modified.

FMOVG.description: FMOVG - Floating Move General - Moves data across the FP and integer register files: with MO=0 the FPR DFR receives the bit pattern of the GPR DRG placed in the FPF field width, with MO=1 the GPR DRG receives the low 32 bits of the FPR DFR bit pattern; the move is a pure bitcast with no rounding.
FMOVG.pseudo_semantics: if MO == 0 then DFR <- bits_fpf(DRG) else DRG <- low32(bits_u64(DFR)); no flags

FLOAD.description: FLOAD - Floating Load - Loads one value of the FPF format from the effective address SR1 + sign_extend(O16) into DFR; an F16 load is zero-extended into the 64-bit register, an unaligned address raises #AC, and a translation miss raises #PGF.

FSTORE.description: FSTORE - Floating Store - Stores the FPF-format value held in DFR to the effective address SR1 + sign_extend(O16); the store width is 2, 4 or 8 bytes from FPF, an unaligned address raises #AC and a translation miss raises #PGF.

FLDEXP.description: FLDEXP - Floating Load Exponent - Returns SF1 scaled by 2 raised to the truncated integer value of SF2, written to DFR in the FPF format; the operation is exact because it only adjusts the exponent, denormals and infinities in SF1 behave correctly, and a NaN exponent yields the default quiet NaN.
FLDEXP.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- scaleExp_fpf(SF1, trunc(SF2)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF2)

FSCALE.description: FSCALE - Floating Scale - Multiplies SF1 by 2 raised to the floor of SF2 and writes DFR in the FPF format; unlike FLDEXP the exponent is floored, so a fractional or negative scaling exponent can step down one power of two, and the sign of a zero SF1 is preserved.
FSCALE.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- scaleExp_fpf(SF1, floor(SF2)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF2)

FCVT.description: FCVT - Floating Convert Precision - Converts SF1 from the source format named by MO (0=F16, 1=BF16, 2=F32, 3=F64) into the destination FPF format in DFR using RM; narrowing rounds once, widening is exact, a NaN is propagated in the destination payload width, and BF16 conversion rounds to nearest even.
FCVT.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- convert(MO -> FPF, RM, SF1); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLV <- invalid_format | isNaN_incompatible; FLO <- overflow | inexact

FRMSTATE.description: FRMSTATE - Floating Rounding Mode State - Reads and writes the FP control state: DRG receives the previous rounding mode in bits 3:0 and the previous exception mask in bits 11:4, the RM field becomes the architectural default rounding mode and SR1 becomes the default exception mask; the FP flags are not touched.
FRMSTATE.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- {FRM_state}; FRM_state <- {RM, SR1_im8}; no FP flag change

VSETVL.description: VSETVL - Vector Set Vector Length - Sets the active vector length: DRG receives the previous length in elements, the new length becomes SR1 interpreted through MO (0 = element count, 1 = byte count, 2 = vtype bitfield) clamped to VLMAX for the current ESZ, and the VLE status flag is set when the accepted length exceeds 256 bits.
VSETVL.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- VL_prev; VLMAX <- 256 / (8 << ESZ); VL <- min(zext(SR1), VLMAX) per MO; VLE <- (VL * (8 << ESZ)) > 256

VGETVL.description: VGETVL - Vector Get Vector Length - Writes the current vector length in elements to the GPR DRG with the VLE status flag mirrored in bit 31; no vector register is read and no flag is modified, so the instruction is safe in any privilege state.

VZERO.description: VZERO - Vector Zero Register - Writes binary zero to all 256 bits of the vector register VDG, including lanes beyond VL and lanes disabled by the active mask; no other register is touched and no flag is modified.

VCLEAR.description: VCLEAR - Vector Clear State - Zeroes a whole vector file in one architectural operation: MO bit 0 clears v0-v31, MO bit 1 clears the writable mask registers k1-k7 and MO=3 clears both; the active length VL and the VLE flag are unchanged and k0 is not affected because it is the hardwired all-ones mask.
VCLEAR.pseudo_semantics: if MO & 1 then v[0..31] <- 0; if MO & 2 then k[1..7] <- 0; k0 stays hardwired all ones; VL and VLE unchanged

VLDR.description: VLDR - Vector Load - Loads VL elements of size ESZ from consecutive addresses starting at SR1 + sign_extend(O16) into VDG, lane i coming from base + i*sizeof(ESZ); lanes past VL are zeroed, an unaligned access raises #AC and a translation miss raises #PGF as a precise fault that leaves VDG unchanged.
VLDR.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- [SR1 + sign_extend(O16,16) + i*(8 << ESZ)]:ESZ; lanes past VL <- 0

VSTR.description: VSTR - Vector Store - Stores the VL active lanes of size ESZ from VDG to consecutive addresses starting at SR1 + sign_extend(O16); inactive lanes are not written so tail lanes never modify memory, and the fault model matches VLDR with the first failing lane address in the fault address register.
VSTR.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: [SR1 + sign_extend(O16,16) + i*(8 << ESZ)]:ESZ <- lanes(VDG)[i]

VLDRS.description: VLDRS - Vector Load Strided - Loads VL elements of size ESZ into VDG with a byte stride of zero_extend(SR2) scaled by the MO multiplier (0 = x1, 1 = x2, 2 = x4, 3 = x8), so lane i comes from SR1 + i*stride*scale; a stride of zero replicates the element at SR1 across every active lane and the tail is zeroed.
VLDRS.pseudo_semantics: stride <- zext(SR2) << MO[1:0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- [SR1 + i*stride]:ESZ; lanes past VL <- 0

VSTRS.description: VSTRS - Vector Store Strided - Stores the active lanes of VDG with the byte stride taken from SR2 and scaled by MO in the same encoding as VLDRS; a zero stride repeatedly stores the same element and inactive lanes generate no memory traffic.
VSTRS.pseudo_semantics: stride <- zext(SR2) << MO[1:0]; for i in 0..VL-1: [SR1 + i*stride]:ESZ <- lanes(VDG)[i]

VLDRX.description: VLDRX - Vector Load Indexed - Gathers VL elements of size ESZ into VDG, taking lane i from SR1 + sign_extend(lanes(VF1)[i]) where VF1 holds byte offsets and MO selects the offset element width (0 = 32-bit, 1 = 64-bit); any fault is precise, so the destination is either fully written or left unchanged.
VLDRX.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- [SR1 + sign_extend(lanes(VF1)[i],32)]:ESZ; lanes past VL <- 0

VSTRX.description: VSTRX - Vector Store Indexed - Scatters the active lanes of VDG to SR1 + sign_extend(lanes(VF1)[i]) with the offset width selected by MO exactly as in VLDRX; inactive lanes perform no store, which makes scatter safe for masked-off and tail lanes.

VLDREP.description: VLDREP - Vector Load Replicate - Reads one element of size ESZ from [SR1] and replicates it into every lane of VDG from lane 0 through VL-1; MO=0 broadcasts an ESZ element and MO=1 broadcasts a 64-bit element into the whole 256-bit register, and the replicated value is neither sign- nor zero-extended.
VLDREP.pseudo_semantics: e <- [SR1]:ESZ; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- e; lanes past VL <- 0

VLOADM.description: VLOADM - Vector Load Masked - Loads elements of size ESZ from SR1 + i*sizeof(ESZ) into VDG only for the lanes whose bit is set in the mask register KM1; the load is fault-suppressing so a disabled lane never touches memory, mask-cleared lanes are zeroed; naming k0 as the mask reads all ones for the active mask length, so a VLOADM through k0 is exactly a unit-stride VLDR.
VLOADM.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: if KM1[i] then lanes(VDG)[i] <- [SR1 + i*(8 << ESZ)]:ESZ else lanes(VDG)[i] <- 0

VSTOREM.description: VSTOREM - Vector Store Masked - Stores the lanes of VDG selected by mask register KM1 to SR1 + i*sizeof(ESZ); lanes cleared in KM1 or beyond VL produce no memory access, and a store whose mask is empty retires without generating any traffic; naming k0 as the mask reads all ones, so a VSTOREM through k0 is exactly a unit-stride VSTR.
VSTOREM.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: if KM1[i] then [SR1 + i*(8 << ESZ)]:ESZ <- lanes(VDG)[i]

VADD.description: VADD - Vector Add - Adds the ESZ-size lanes of VF1 and VF2 and writes VDG; MO[3:2] = 0 keeps the wrapping low half of the exact sum while MO[3:2] = 1 forces signed saturation and MO[3:2] = 2 unsigned saturation, with VF recording that some lane clamped. MO[1:0] selects the signed or unsigned lane interpretation and MO[3:2] selects wrap, signed-saturate or unsigned-saturate overflow. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VADD.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- sat_or_wrap(MO, lanes(VF1)[i] + lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); VF <- any_saturated; lanes past VL <- 0

VSUB.description: VSUB - Vector Subtract - Subtracts the ESZ lanes of VF2 from the matching lanes of VF1 into VDG with the overflow behaviour selected by MO[3:2] (0 = wrap, 1 = signed saturate, 2 = unsigned saturate); VF is set when any lane clamped and cleared when none did. MO[1:0] selects the signed or unsigned lane interpretation and MO[3:2] selects wrap, signed-saturate or unsigned-saturate overflow. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSUB.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- sat_or_wrap(MO, lanes(VF1)[i] - lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); VF <- any_saturated; lanes past VL <- 0

VMUL.description: VMUL - Vector Multiply - Multiplies the ESZ lanes of VF1 by the matching lanes of VF2 and writes VDG; MO[3:2] = 0 keeps the low half of the exact double-width product, MO[3:2] = 1 keeps the high half (the widening multiply form), and MO[1:0] selects the signed or unsigned interpretation of the product. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VMUL.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: p <- 2*ESZ-wide product of lanes(VF1)[i] and lanes(VF2)[i]; lanes(VDG)[i] <- half(p, MO[3:2]); lanes past VL <- 0

VDIV.description: VDIV - Vector Integer Divide - Divides each ESZ lane of VF1 by the matching lane of VF2 and writes the truncated quotient to VDG; a zero divisor leaves the destination lane unchanged and sets VF, and MO[1:0] selects the signed or unsigned rule, including the signed overflow case that saturates to the most negative value. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VDIV.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: if lanes(VF2)[i] == 0 then VF <- 1 else lanes(VDG)[i] <- trunc_div(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i]); lanes past VL <- 0

VMIN.description: VMIN - Vector Minimum - Writes the smaller of the matching ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 to VDG with the signed or unsigned ordering selected by MO[1:0]; the operation is exact, sets no flag and is bit-for-bit the dual of VMAX. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VMIN.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- min(MO[1:0], lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i]); lanes past VL <- 0

VMAX.description: VMAX - Vector Maximum - Writes the larger of the matching ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 to VDG with the signed or unsigned ordering selected by MO[1:0]; VMAX is the exact dual of VMIN and modifies no flag. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VMAX.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- max(MO[1:0], lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i]); lanes past VL <- 0
