VAVG.description: VAVG - Vector Average - Computes the rounding average (VF1 + VF2 + r) >> 1 of the matching ESZ lanes without intermediate overflow, with r = 1 when MO[1:0] = 0 and r = 0 when MO[1:0] = 1; this sum-preserving average needs no widened intermediate and is intended for pixel blending. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VAVG.pseudo_semantics: r <- (MO[1:0] == 0); for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- (zext(lanes(VF1)[i]) + zext(lanes(VF2)[i]) + r) >> 1; lanes past VL <- 0

VADDSAT.description: VADDSAT - Vector Add Saturating - Adds the ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 and clamps each result to the representable range of the lane, using signed saturation when MO[1:0] = 0 and unsigned saturation when MO[1:0] = 1; VF is set when at least one lane clamped and cleared otherwise. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VADDSAT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- clamp(MO[1:0], lanes(VF1)[i] + lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); VF <- any_lane_clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VSUBSAT.description: VSUBSAT - Vector Subtract Saturating - Subtracts the ESZ lanes of VF2 from VF1 and clamps to the lane range, flooring at zero for unsigned lanes and at the minimum signed value for signed lanes; VF reports whether any lane clamped. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSUBSAT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- clamp(MO[1:0], lanes(VF1)[i] - lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); VF <- any_lane_clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VDOT.description: VDOT - Vector Dot Product - Multiplies the matching ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 and accumulates adjacent product pairs into double-width lanes that are added to the running accumulator in VDG; MO=0 accumulates in 2*ESZ and MO=1 accumulates in ESZ with saturation, and VF reports accumulator overflow. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VDOT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-2 step 2: acc <- lanes(VDG)[i/2] + lanes(VF1)[i]*lanes(VF2)[i] + lanes(VF1)[i+1]*lanes(VF2)[i+1]; lanes(VDG)[i/2] <- acc; VF <- saturated; lanes past VL <- 0

VMADD.description: VMADD - Vector Multiply-Add - Computes VF1[lane] * VF2[lane] + VF3[lane] per ESZ lane and writes VDG; the product is formed at double width before the add so that exactly one wrap is applied, and VF reports that some lane's exact result did not fit the ESZ lane. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VMADD.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- wrap(lanes(VF1)[i]*lanes(VF2)[i] + lanes(VF3)[i], ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VMSUB.description: VMSUB - Vector Multiply-Subtract - Computes VF3[lane] - VF1[lane] * VF2[lane] per ESZ lane into VDG; the accumulator is the third source so a reduction loop can keep its running sum in place, and VF reports that some lane's exact result did not fit the ESZ lane. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VMSUB.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- wrap(lanes(VF3)[i] - lanes(VF1)[i]*lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VFMA.description: VFMA - Vector Fused Multiply-Add - Computes VF1[lane] * VF2[lane] + VF3[lane] as a fused floating-point operation in the lane format named by the FMT prefix (F16, BF16, F32 or F64) with one IEEE-754 rounding per lane; NaN lanes propagate a quieted payload, denormal lanes are consumed exactly, and FLZ/FLO/FLV summarise zero, overflow and invalid across all written lanes. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VFMA.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- fma_fpf(FMT.FPF, FMT.RM, lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i], lanes(VF3)[i]); FLZ/FLO/FLV <- or over lanes; lanes past VL <- 0

VFMS.description: VFMS - Vector Fused Multiply-Subtract - Computes VF1[lane] * VF2[lane] - VF3[lane] as one fused floating-point operation per lane in the format and rounding named by the FMT prefix; the fused form differs from a separate multiply and subtract because the product is never rounded before the subtraction. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VFMS.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- fms_fpf(FMT.FPF, FMT.RM, lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i], lanes(VF3)[i]); FLZ/FLO/FLV <- or over lanes; lanes past VL <- 0

VABSD.description: VABSD - Vector Absolute Difference - Writes |VF1[lane] - VF2[lane]| to VDG per ESZ lane; the signed form widens internally so the magnitude never overflows, MO[1:0] = 1 selects the unsigned difference, and VF is set when MO[3:2] = 1 requested saturation and a lane clamped. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VABSD.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: d <- abs(sext(lanes(VF1)[i]) - sext(lanes(VF2)[i])); lanes(VDG)[i] <- sat(MO, d, ESZ); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VNEG.description: VNEG - Vector Negate - Writes the two's-complement negation of each ESZ lane of VF1 to VDG; negating the most negative lane wraps to itself unless MO[3:2] = 1 requests signed saturation, in which case it clamps and sets VF, and MO[1:0] = 1 selects a bit-wise not instead of the arithmetic negation. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VNEG.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- neg_or_not(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], ESZ); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VAND.description: VAND - Vector Bitwise And - Computes the bit-wise AND of the full 256-bit registers VF1 and VF2 into VDG; ESZ is ignored because the operation does not interpret lanes, and MO is reserved and must be encoded as zero. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VAND.pseudo_semantics: v[VDG] <- v[VF1] & v[VF2]; lanes past VL <- 0

VOR.description: VOR - Vector Bitwise Or - Computes the bit-wise inclusive OR of the full 256-bit registers VF1 and VF2 into VDG; ESZ is ignored, MO is reserved and must be zero, and no flag is modified. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VOR.pseudo_semantics: v[VDG] <- v[VF1] | v[VF2]; lanes past VL <- 0

VXOR.description: VXOR - Vector Bitwise Exclusive Or - Computes the bit-wise XOR of the full 256-bit registers VF1 and VF2 into VDG; XOR with operands naming the same register is the architectural way to zero a vector without a dedicated clear, which VZERO also provides. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VXOR.pseudo_semantics: v[VDG] <- v[VF1] ^ v[VF2]; lanes past VL <- 0

VXNOR.description: VXNOR - Vector Bitwise Exclusive Nor - Computes the bit-wise complement of the XOR of VF1 and VF2 into VDG; it is the negated equality primitive used for byte-wise compare loops and it modifies no flag. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).

VNOT.description: VNOT - Vector Bitwise Not - Writes the one's complement of the full 256-bit register VF1 to VDG; ESZ is ignored, MO is reserved and must be zero, and the tail lanes beyond VL are zeroed rather than complemented. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).

VSHL.description: VSHL - Vector Shift Left - Shifts every ESZ lane of VF1 left by the single count held in lane 0 of VF2; a count at or above the lane width produces zero, MO[3:2] = 1 requests saturation into the lane with VF set on any clamped bit, and the per-lane variable form is VSHLV. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSHL.pseudo_semantics: sh <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- shl_or_sat(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], sh, ESZ); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VSHR.description: VSHR - Vector Shift Right Logical - Shifts every ESZ lane of VF1 right by the single count held in lane 0 of VF2, filling with zeros; a count at or above the lane width produces zero and no flag is modified, while arithmetic shifting is VSAR. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSHR.pseudo_semantics: sh <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- shr_logical(lanes(VF1)[i], sh, ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VSAR.description: VSAR - Vector Shift Arithmetic Right - Shifts every ESZ lane of VF1 right by the single count in lane 0 of VF2 and replicates the sign bit into the vacated positions; a count at or above the lane width produces the sign fill (all ones for negative lanes, zero otherwise). Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSAR.pseudo_semantics: sh <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- sar(lanes(VF1)[i], sh, ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VSHLV.description: VSHLV - Vector Variable Shift - Shifts each ESZ lane of VF1 by the count held in the matching lane of VF2, so different lanes shift by different amounts in one instruction; MO[1:0] = 0 selects a left shift, 1 a logical right shift and 2 an arithmetic right shift, and counts at or above the lane width clear the lane for logical shifts. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSHLV.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- vshift(MO[1:0], lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i], ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VNARROW.description: VNARROW - Vector Narrow Shift - Shifts each double-width lane pair of VF1 right by the count in lane 0 of VF2 and saturates the result into the half-width lane of VDG, so a 2*ESZ intermediate becomes an ESZ element; MO[1:0] selects signed or unsigned saturation and VF is set when any lane clamped. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VNARROW.pseudo_semantics: sh <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- sat(MO, signed_wide(lanes(VF1)[2i], lanes(VF1)[2i+1]) >> sh, ESZ); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VCMP.description: VCMP - Vector Compare Into Mask - Compares the ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 with the condition selector CC (the architectural condition table where 0 EQ, 1 NE, 2 CS/LO, 3 CC/HS, 4 MI, 5 PL, 6 VS, 7 VC, 8 LT, 9 GE, 10 LE, 11 GT, 12 HI, 13 LS, 14 AL, 15 NV) and writes one predicate bit per lane to KDG; MO does not exist in this form, so signedness is selected by choosing the signed (LT..GT) or unsigned (LO..HI) condition, and lanes past VL clear their predicate bit. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VCMP.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: KDG[i] <- cond(CC, lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i]); KDG[i] <- 0 for i >= VL

VTEST.description: VTEST - Vector Test Lanes - Tests the ESZ lanes of VF1 and VF2 and writes one predicate bit per lane to KDG: MO=0 records lanes where the AND is non-zero, MO=1 where VF1 == VF2, MO=2 where both lanes are negative in two's complement and MO=3 where VF1 has any bit set outside VF2; no arithmetic exception is possible and lanes past VL write zero. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VTEST.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: KDG[i] <- test(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], lanes(VF2)[i]); KDG[i] <- 0 for i >= VL

VFIND.description: VFIND - Vector Find First Set - Scans the mask register KM1 for the lowest set predicate bit and writes its lane index to DRG, with CF set when no bit is set and ZF set when bit zero is the first hit; MO=1 instead scans from the highest lane (find last), and the index is reported in the granularity given by ESZ; naming k0 as the mask reads all ones, so the reported index is always lane 0.
VFIND.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- index_of_first_set(KM1) per MO; CF <- none_set; ZF <- (DRG == 0)

KAND.description: KAND - Mask And - Computes the bit-wise AND of the source mask registers KM1 and KM2 and writes it to KDG; predicate bits above the active mask length are cleared; naming k0 as a source reads all ones for the active mask length, so KAND with k0 leaves the other operand unchanged, and a write to k0 through KDG is discarded because k0 is hardwired.
KAND.pseudo_semantics: k[KDG] <- k[KM1] & k[KM2]; bits above masklen <- 0

KOR.description: KOR - Mask Or - Computes the bit-wise OR of the source mask registers KM1 and KM2 and writes it to KDG; predicate bits above the active mask length are cleared, so a mask built by KOR is never wider than the current vector length allows; a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.
KOR.pseudo_semantics: k[KDG] <- k[KM1] | k[KM2]; bits above masklen <- 0

KXOR.description: KXOR - Mask Exclusive Or - Computes the bit-wise XOR of the source mask registers KM1 and KM2 and writes it to KDG; XOR of a mask register with itself yields an empty mask, which combined with the zeroing mask policy is how a program forces all lanes off; a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.
KXOR.pseudo_semantics: k[KDG] <- k[KM1] ^ k[KM2]; bits above masklen <- 0

KNOT.description: KNOT - Mask Not - Writes the one's complement of the source mask register KM1 into KDG; the trailing 0x0 nibble is a reserved field that must be encoded as zero, predicate bits above the active mask length are cleared rather than complemented, and a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.

KMOV.description: KMOV - Mask Move - Copies the source mask register KM1 into the destination mask register KDG; the trailing 0x0 nibble is a reserved field that must be encoded as zero, the mask register is 32 bits wide with one bit per 8-bit lane at VLEN=256, predicate bits above the active mask length read as zero and are written as zero, k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask so naming it as KM1 reads all ones, and a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.

KTEST.description: KTEST - Mask Test - Compares the mask registers KM1 and KM2 and updates the integer flags without writing any register: ZF is set when (KM1 & KM2) is zero and CF is set when (KM1 & ~KM2) is zero, so the pair of flags distinguishes disjoint, subset and equal mask pairs; naming k0 reads all ones, so KTEST with k0 as KM1 reports ZF when KM2 is empty and CF when KM2 is all ones over the active mask length.

KUNPCK.description: KUNPCK - Mask Unpack - Interleaves the predicate bits of the mask registers KM1 and KM2 into KDG: bit i of KM1 goes to KDG bit 2i and bit i of KM2 goes to KDG bit 2i+1, which is the widening step that builds the alternate-lane mask of a 16-lane element group out of two narrower masks; a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.
KUNPCK.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..masklen-1: k[KDG][2i] <- k[KM1][i]; k[KDG][2i+1] <- k[KM2][i]

VPOPC.description: VPOPC - Vector Population Count Of Mask - Counts the set predicate bits of the source mask register KM1 and writes the count to the GPR DRG, with ZF set when the count is zero; predicate bits above the active mask length are not counted; naming k0 as the source therefore returns the active mask length itself.

KMOVG.description: KMOVG - Mask Move General - Moves data between a mask register and a GPR: with MO=0 the low 32 bits of the GPR DRG become KDG, and with MO=1 the 32-bit mask register KM1 is zero-extended into the GPR DRG; bits above the active mask length are cleared on the way into a mask register; naming k0 as KM1 reads all ones and a write to k0 through KDG is discarded.
KMOVG.pseudo_semantics: if MO == 0 then k[KDG] <- DRG[31:0] else DRG <- zext(k[KM1], 32)

VSHUF.description: VSHUF - Vector Shuffle - Builds VDG by selecting elements from the concatenation of VF1 and VF2 under the per-lane control held in VF3: each ESZ lane of VF3 supplies an element index whose low bit chooses the source register and whose remaining bits choose the element, which makes VSHUF the interchange primitive for 2x2 and 4x4 block transposes. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSHUF.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: idx <- lanes(VF3)[i]; lanes(VDG)[i] <- (idx & 1) ? lanes(VF2)[idx >> 1] : lanes(VF1)[idx >> 1]; lanes past VL <- 0

VSWIZ.description: VSWIZ - Vector Swizzle - Permutes whole 64-bit blocks of VF1 under the control bytes in VF3 and then merges the result with VF2 block by block according to the high control bit of each block; the swizzle never leaves the register file and is used for byte-order and matrix-row rearrangements inside one vector. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSWIZ.pseudo_semantics: for b in 0..VL/8-1: ctl <- byte(VF3, b); lanes(VDG)[b] <- (ctl & 0x80) ? lanes(VF2)[b] : block64(VF1)[ctl & 7]; lanes past VL <- 0

VPERM.description: VPERM - Vector Permute - Performs a full lane crossbar: element i of VDG is taken from element (VF3[i] mod VL) of the bank selected by the low bit of VF2 lane i, so any element can reach any lane in one instruction; indices beyond VL wrap modulo VL as an architectural guarantee rather than raising an exception. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VPERM.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: j <- lanes(VF3)[i] mod VL; lanes(VDG)[i] <- (lanes(VF2)[i] & 1) ? lanes(VF2)[j] : lanes(VF1)[j]; lanes past VL <- 0

VSLIDE.description: VSLIDE - Vector Slide - Concatenates VF1 (low half) with VF2 (high half) and slides the 2*VL element window down by the amount in lane 0 of VF3, keeping the newest VL elements in VDG; a slide of zero returns VF1 unchanged and a slide of VL returns VF2, which is how a sliding window moves between vectors. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSLIDE.pseudo_semantics: s <- lanes(VF3)[0] mod (2*VL); for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- element(i + s) of concat(VF1, VF2); lanes past VL <- 0

VBLEND.description: VBLEND - Vector Blend - Selects lanes from VF1 and VF2 under the per-lane control of VF3, taking VF2 where the control lane has its most significant bit set and VF1 otherwise; blend is the data-dependent counterpart of mask predication and needs no mask register. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VBLEND.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- (lanes(VF3)[i] >> (8*ESZ-1)) ? lanes(VF2)[i] : lanes(VF1)[i]; lanes past VL <- 0

VTBL.description: VTBL - Vector Table Lookup - Looks up each lane of the index vector VF3 in the table formed by the 2*VL elements of VF1 and VF2; an index in the VF1 range reads VF1, an index in the VF2 range reads VF2, and an out-of-range index yields the matching lane of VF3 as the fallback instead of raising an exception. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VTBL.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: idx <- lanes(VF3)[i]; lanes(VDG)[i] <- (idx < VL) ? lanes(VF1)[idx] : ((idx < 2*VL) ? lanes(VF2)[idx-VL] : lanes(VF3)[i]); lanes past VL <- 0

VREDSUM.description: VREDSUM - Vector Reduce Sum - Sums the active ESZ lanes of VF1 into lane 0 of VDG starting from the scalar seed in lane 0 of VF2; the reduction is a horizontal tree so the latency is logarithmic in VL, the remaining lanes of VDG are zeroed, and VF reports accumulator overflow when MO[3:2] requests saturation.
VREDSUM.pseudo_semantics: acc <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: acc <- acc + lanes(VF1)[i]; lanes(VDG)[0] <- sat(MO, acc); lanes(VDG)[1..VL-1] <- 0

VREDMIN.description: VREDMIN - Vector Reduce Minimum - Finds the smallest of the active ESZ lanes of VF1 and combines it with the scalar seed in lane 0 of VF2, writing the result to lane 0 of VDG with the other lanes zeroed; MO[1:0] selects signed or unsigned ordering.
VREDMIN.pseudo_semantics: acc <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: acc <- min(MO[1:0], acc, lanes(VF1)[i]); lanes(VDG)[0] <- acc; lanes(VDG)[1..VL-1] <- 0

VREDMAX.description: VREDMAX - Vector Reduce Maximum - Finds the largest of the active ESZ lanes of VF1 and combines it with the seed in lane 0 of VF2, writing the result to lane 0 of VDG; the scan is a horizontal tree and MO[1:0] selects signed or unsigned ordering.
VREDMAX.pseudo_semantics: acc <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: acc <- max(MO[1:0], acc, lanes(VF1)[i]); lanes(VDG)[0] <- acc; lanes(VDG)[1..VL-1] <- 0

VREDAND.description: VREDAND - Vector Reduce And - ANDs the active ESZ lanes of VF1 together with the seed in lane 0 of VF2 and writes the reduction to lane 0 of VDG; the usual seed is all ones, and the instruction is the primitive behind vector all-ones and all-zero tests.
VREDAND.pseudo_semantics: acc <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: acc <- acc & lanes(VF1)[i]; lanes(VDG)[0] <- acc; lanes(VDG)[1..VL-1] <- 0

VSCAN.description: VSCAN - Vector Prefix Scan - Computes the inclusive running sum of the ESZ lanes of VF1 with the seed from lane 0 of VF2 and writes every partial result to the matching lane of VDG; MO=0 scans upward from lane 0 and MO=1 scans downward, and this is the vectorised prefix sum that feeds compaction loops. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSCAN.pseudo_semantics: acc <- lanes(VF2)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: acc <- acc + lanes(VF1)[i]; lanes(VDG)[i] <- acc; lanes past VL <- 0

VEXTRACT.description: VEXTRACT - Vector Extract Lane - Writes the ESZ element selected by the IM8 lane index from the vector register VF1 into the GPR DRG; the element is zero-extended to 32 bits, an index beyond VL-1 reads zero rather than faulting, and a QWORD lane is truncated to its low 32 bits.

VINSERT.description: VINSERT - Vector Insert Lane - Copies VF1 to VDG and replaces the ESZ element selected by the IM8 lane index with the GPR SR1 zero-extended to the lane width; every other lane is copied unchanged and an index beyond VL-1 leaves the destination vector identical to the source. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VINSERT.pseudo_semantics: v[VDG] <- v[VF1]; if IM8 < VL then lanes(VDG)[IM8] <- zext(SR1, ESZ)

VBROADCAST.description: VBROADCAST - Vector Broadcast - Replicates the element held in lane 0 of the vector register VF1 into every lane of VDG; the element size is ESZ, the copy is a pure data move with no sign or zero extension, and the tail lanes beyond VL are zeroed. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VBROADCAST.pseudo_semantics: e <- lanes(VF1)[0]; for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- e; lanes past VL <- 0

VCVT.description: VCVT - Vector Convert - Converts every lane between integer and floating-point element formats: MO=0 converts signed integers to floating point, MO=1 converts floating point to signed integers with the FMT rounding mode, MO=2 converts between two FP formats and MO=3 converts unsigned integers to floating point; ESZ is the destination element size, the source size comes from the OPSZ prefix, and FLZ/FLO/FLV summarise zero, inexact and invalid lanes. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VCVT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- convert(MO, FMT.FPF, ESZ, lanes(VF1)[i]); FLZ/FLO/FLV <- or over lanes; lanes past VL <- 0

VZEXT.description: VZEXT - Vector Zero Extend - Widens each ESZ lane of VF1 into a double-width lane of VDG by zero extension, so only the low half of the active lanes is consumed and the destination active lane count is VL/2; the extension loses no information and modifies no flag. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VZEXT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..(VL/2)-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- zext(lanes(VF1)[i], 2*ESZ); lanes past VL/2 <- 0

VSEXT.description: VSEXT - Vector Sign Extend - Widens each ESZ lane of VF1 into a double-width lane of VDG by sign extension, so an 8-bit lane becomes a 16-bit lane and so on; negative lanes keep their value and the remaining destination lanes are zeroed. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSEXT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..(VL/2)-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- sext(lanes(VF1)[i], 2*ESZ); lanes past VL/2 <- 0

VTRUNC.description: VTRUNC - Vector Truncate Saturating - Narrows each double-width lane pair of VF1 into an ESZ lane of VDG: MO[3:2] = 0 keeps the low half without saturation and MO[3:2] = 1 saturates into the destination range first, with MO[1:0] selecting signed or unsigned interpretation and VF reporting any clamped lane. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VTRUNC.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- narrow(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], 2*ESZ, ESZ); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VSAT.description: VSAT - Vector Saturate - Clamps each ESZ lane of VF1 into the representable range of a narrower destination element width selected by MO[1:0] (0 = 8, 1 = 16, 2 = 32, 3 = 64 bits) with signed clamping unless MO[3] = 1 requests unsigned clamping; VF is set when any lane clamped and cleared when the input already fit. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VSAT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- clamp_width(MO, lanes(VF1)[i], 8 << MO[1:0]); VF <- clamped; lanes past VL <- 0

VROUND.description: VROUND - Vector Round To Integral - Rounds each floating-point lane of VF1 to an integral value in the same format using the rounding mode from the FMT prefix and writes VDG; the sign of a zero result follows the input, and FLZ/FLO/FLV report zero, overflow and NaN lanes for the whole vector. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VROUND.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- roundToIntegral_fpf(FMT.FPF, FMT.RM, lanes(VF1)[i]); FLZ/FLO/FLV <- or over lanes; lanes past VL <- 0

VCNT.description: VCNT - Vector Population Count - Counts the set bits of each ESZ lane of VF1 and writes the count as the matching lane of VDG; the count never exceeds the lane width so it always fits the same lane size, and no flag is modified. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VCNT.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- popcount(lanes(VF1)[i]); lanes past VL <- 0

VCLZ.description: VCLZ - Vector Count Leading Zeros - Counts the leading zero bits of each ESZ lane of VF1 and writes the count into the matching lane of VDG with the same lane width; an all-zero lane returns the full lane width and no flag is modified. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VCLZ.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- clz(lanes(VF1)[i], ESZ); lanes past VL <- 0

VBYTEREV.description: VBYTEREV - Vector Byte Reverse - Reverses the byte order inside each ESZ lane of VF1 into the matching lane of VDG; MO=0 reverses all ESZ bytes, MO=1 reverses only within each half-lane, and MO=2 swaps the two halves of the register as 128-bit blocks for endianness conversion of mixed data. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VBYTEREV.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..VL-1: lanes(VDG)[i] <- byterev(lanes(VF1)[i], MO); lanes past VL <- 0

VCOMPRESS.description: VCOMPRESS - Vector Compress - Packs the ESZ lanes of VF1 whose predicate bit is set in KM1 down to the lowest lanes of VDG in ascending lane order and fills the remaining lanes with zero; this is the compaction half of a streaming filter loop; lanes disabled by the mask are never read, and naming k0 selects every active lane, which makes VCOMPRESS through k0 an identity move.
VCOMPRESS.pseudo_semantics: j <- 0; for i in 0..VL-1: if KM1[i] then lanes(VDG)[j] <- lanes(VF1)[i], j <- j+1; lanes(VDG)[j..VL-1] <- 0

VEXPAND.description: VEXPAND - Vector Expand - The inverse of VCOMPRESS: consumes the ESZ lanes of VF1 in order and writes them into the lane positions of VDG whose predicate bit is set in KM1, leaving every other lane zero, so the low popcount(KM1) lanes of VF1 are read and no more; naming k0 selects all active lanes, which makes VEXPAND through k0 an identity move. Lanes past VL and mask-cleared lanes are zeroed (tail-undisturbed off, zeroing mask policy by default).
VEXPAND.pseudo_semantics: j <- 0; for i in 0..VL-1: if KM1[i] then lanes(VDG)[i] <- lanes(VF1)[j], j <- j+1 else lanes(VDG)[i] <- 0

VSTATE.description: VSTATE - Vector State Save Restore - Saves or restores the whole vector state: with MO=0 the whole state is written to the buffer at SR1 as a 1064-byte record and DRG receives that byte count, composed of 32 vector registers x 32 bytes = 1024 bytes, then the eight 32-bit mask registers = 32 bytes at offsets 1024..1055, then 8 bytes at offsets 1056..1063 holding VL as a 32-bit little-endian element count at 1056..1059 followed by a 32-bit word at 1060..1063 whose bit 0 is VLE and whose remaining bits are reserved zero, and the k0 word of the mask area reads as all ones on save and is ignored on restore because k0 is hardwired; with MO=1 the state is reloaded from SR1 with SR2 giving the record length and a short record raises #GP before any register is written.

AESENC.description: AESENC - AES Encrypt Round - Performs one AES encryption round on the 128-bit state held in the low half of VDG using the round key in VF1 and the AddRoundKey input in VF2: SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns and AddRoundKey in that order, with the upper 128 bits of the destination zeroed. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

AESDEC.description: AESDEC - AES Decrypt Round - Performs one equivalent-inverse AES round on the 128-bit state in the low half of VDG with the round key in VF1 and the AddRoundKey input in VF2: InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, InvMixColumns and AddRoundKey, with the upper half zeroed. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

AESENCLAST.description: AESENCLAST - AES Encrypt Last Round - Performs the final AES encryption round, which omits MixColumns: SubBytes, ShiftRows and AddRoundKey with the round key in VF1 and the input in VF2; this is the only round form that produces a ciphertext compatible with FIPS-197. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

AESDECLAST.description: AESDECLAST - AES Decrypt Last Round - Performs the final equivalent-inverse AES round without InvMixColumns: InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes and AddRoundKey with the round key in VF1 and the input in VF2; paired with AESIMC on the key schedule it decrypts a FIPS-197 ciphertext. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

AESIMC.description: AESIMC - AES Inverse Mix Columns - Applies the InvMixColumns transform to the 128-bit round key held in the low half of VF1 and writes it to VDG, which is the key-schedule step that turns an encryption round key into an equivalent decryption round key; VF2 is ignored and should name the same register as VF1. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

AESKEYGEN.description: AESKEYGEN - AES Key Schedule Step - Produces round key IM8 of an AES key schedule from the previous two round keys in VF1 and VDG: RotWord, SubWord, the round constant for round IM8 and the word-wise XOR are applied, with MO=0 selecting the encryption direction and MO=1 the decryption direction through InvMixColumns; the result overwrites VDG and the whole instruction executes in the CIU so no key bit is exposed to software except through the register. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
AESKEYGEN.pseudo_semantics: VDG[127:0] <- keyScheduleStep(MO, VF1[127:0], VDG[127:0], IM8); VDG[255:128] <- 0

SHA1RNDS4.description: SHA1RNDS4 - SHA-1 Four Rounds - Executes four SHA-1 rounds with the round function selected by the low two bits of IM8 (0 = f0, 1 = f1, 2 = f2, 3 = f3) on the state in VDG using the message words packed in VF1 and VF2, adding the message and the constant before the rotate so one instruction advances four of the eighty rounds. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
SHA1RNDS4.pseudo_semantics: for r in 0..3: VDG[127:0] <- sha1round(IM8 & 3, VDG[127:0], word(VF1, VF2, r)); VDG[255:128] <- 0

SHA1MSG1.description: SHA1MSG1 - SHA-1 Message Schedule 1 - Computes the first half of the SHA-1 message expansion: the four words in VF2 are XORed with the words in VF1 and with the words shifted by one position, producing the intermediate schedule words that SHA1MSG2 completes into the next message block. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

SHA1MSG2.description: SHA1MSG2 - SHA-1 Message Schedule 2 - Completes the SHA-1 message expansion: it XORs the intermediate words produced by SHA1MSG1 in VF2 with the words in VF1 after a rotate-by-one of the four-word group, yielding the next four W[t] values with the wrap-around that makes the schedule a feedback shift register. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

SHA256RNDS2.description: SHA256RNDS2 - SHA-256 Two Rounds - Executes two SHA-256 compression rounds on the state pair held in VDG using the round keys packed in VF1 and the message words plus round constants in VF2; the state pair is rotated inside the register so that two consecutive invocations advance four rounds without extra shuffling. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
SHA256RNDS2.pseudo_semantics: for r in 0..1: VDG <- sha256round(VDG, word(VF1, VF2, r)); VDG[255:128] <- 0

SHA256MSG1.description: SHA256MSG1 - SHA-256 Message Schedule 1 - Computes the sigma0 part of the SHA-256 message expansion over the four words of VF1 with the words of VF2 and writes the partially expanded schedule to VDG; the sigma1 term and the addition are added by SHA256MSG2. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

SHA256MSG2.description: SHA256MSG2 - SHA-256 Message Schedule 2 - Completes the SHA-256 message expansion by adding the sigma1 term and the two older schedule words held in VF2 to the partial words of VF1, producing four new W[t] values in VDG that feed SHA256RNDS2. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

SHA512RNDS2.description: SHA512RNDS2 - SHA-512 Two Rounds - Executes two 64-bit SHA-512 compression rounds on the eight-word state in VDG using the round keys in VF1 and the message words and constants in VF2, with the state pair rotated inside the register between invocations; the wider word size makes the latency roughly double that of SHA256RNDS2. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
SHA512RNDS2.pseudo_semantics: for r in 0..1: VDG <- sha512round(VDG, qword(VF1, VF2, r)); VDG[255:128] <- 0

CLMUL.description: CLMUL - Carry-Less Multiply - Multiplies two 64-bit polynomials taken from the low quadwords of VF1 and VF2 without carry propagation into a 128-bit result in VDG, which is the primitive behind GCM authentication and CRC folding; the upper half of the destination is zeroed and the operation is constant-time. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.

GF2P8MUL.description: GF2P8MUL - GF(2^8) Multiply - Multiplies each byte of VF1 by the matching byte of VF2 in the finite field GF(2^8) modulo the AES polynomial x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1 and writes 32 product bytes to VDG; all 256 bytes of the vector are processed and no flag is modified. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
GF2P8MUL.pseudo_semantics: for b in 0..31: VDG.byte[b] <- gfmul(VF1.byte[b], VF2.byte[b]); no flags

GF2P8AFFINE.description: GF2P8AFFINE - GF(2^8) Affine Transform - Applies the 8x8 bit-matrix affine transformation selected by the immediate IM8 to every byte of VF1 and adds the constant byte, writing the result to VDG; MO=0 applies the transform used by SubBytes and MO=1 applies the inverse matrix used by InvSubBytes, so the AES S-box is built as GF2P8MUL followed by this instruction. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
GF2P8AFFINE.pseudo_semantics: for b in 0..31: VDG.byte[b] <- affine8(IM8, MO, VF1.byte[b]); no flags

CRC32.description: CRC32 - CRC-32 Accumulate - Folds the value of SR1 into the running CRC held in DRG using the IEEE 802.3 reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320; ESZ selects the number of source bytes folded (0 = 1 byte, 1 = 2, 2 = 4, 3 = 8) and the updated CRC is written back to DRG without touching any flag.
CRC32.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..(1 << ESZ)-1: crc <- (crc >> 8) ^ table[(crc ^ byte(SR1, k)) & 0xFF]; DRG <- crc

CRC32C.description: CRC32C - CRC-32C Accumulate - Folds the value of SR1 into the running CRC in DRG using the Castagnoli polynomial 0x82F63B78 used by iSCSI and SCTP; ESZ selects the folded byte count exactly as in CRC32, and the two instructions share the same accumulator register so a driver can implement either polynomial with one loop. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
CRC32C.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..(1 << ESZ)-1: crc <- (crc >> 8) ^ tableC[(crc ^ byte(SR1, k)) & 0xFF]; DRG <- crc

RDRAND.description: RDRAND - Read Random Number - Returns a hardware-generated random value in DRG and sets CF when the value is valid; ESZ selects the output width (0 = 8, 1 = 16, 2 = 32, 3 = 64 bits with the high half in DRG+1) and MO=1 requests that the instruction retry internally until a valid value is produced instead of reporting CF clear.
RDRAND.pseudo_semantics: if entropy_valid() then DRG <- random(8 << ESZ), CF <- 1 else CF <- 0 when MO == 0; DRG unchanged when CF == 0

RDSEED.description: RDSEED - Read Seed - Returns a value taken directly from the conditioned entropy source in DRG and sets CF on success; unlike RDRAND the value is suitable for seeding a deterministic random bit generator, and a CF-clear result means the entropy pool was not ready rather than that a number was not produced.
RDSEED.pseudo_semantics: if seed_ready() then DRG <- entropy(8 << ESZ), CF <- 1 else CF <- 0; DRG unchanged when CF == 0

SECCMP.description: SECCMP - Secure Compare - Compares the SR1 and SR2 register blocks of 8*(1 << ESZ) bytes and sets ZF when they are equal, accumulating the difference without any early exit so that the latency and the memory access pattern are independent of where the first differing byte lies; MO selects whether the comparison is byte-wise or word-wise. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
SECCMP.pseudo_semantics: d <- 0; for k in 0..n-1: d <- d | (byte(SR1,k) ^ byte(SR2,k)); ZF <- (d == 0)

KEYGEN.description: KEYGEN - Key Generate - Derives a key from the platform root secret into the key slot whose handle is DRG, using SR1 as the key-derivation context and SR2 as the caller-supplied nonce, with ESZ selecting the key length (1, 2, 4 or 8 blocks of 128 bits); the instruction requires mode L7, never returns the root secret to software, and raises #SEC when the slot is already occupied or the caller lacks the platform key.
KEYGEN.pseudo_semantics: if mode < L7 then #SEC; slot[DRG] <- kdf(root_secret, SR1, SR2, 16 << ESZ); key bits never visible to general registers

KEYLOAD.description: KEYLOAD - Key Load - Imports the key material held in the register block based at SR1 with length SR2 into the key slot named by DRG, after which crypto instructions may reference the slot without the key ever appearing in a general register again; it requires mode L3 and raises #SEC when the slot is protected by a higher privilege.
KEYLOAD.pseudo_semantics: if mode < L3 then #SEC; slot[DRG] <- [SR1..SR1+(16 << ESZ)-1]; zeroize the source block when MO == 1

KEYZERO.description: KEYZERO - Key Zeroize - Destroys the key material in the slot named by DRG by overwriting it with zeros and then with a random pattern, so that a subsequent use of the handle raises #SEC; ESZ selects how many slots are cleared starting at DRG and MO=1 also zeroizes any live cipher context that was bound to the slot.
KEYZERO.pseudo_semantics: if mode < L3 then #SEC; for s in 0..(1 << ESZ)-1: slot[DRG+s] <- 0 then slot[DRG+s] <- random(); invalidate bound contexts when MO == 1

MONT.description: MONT - Montgomery Multiply - Computes SR1 * SR2 * R^-1 mod N for the modulus held in the register block based at DRG, where the block width in 32-bit words is 3*(1 << ESZ) covering A, B and N and R = 2^(32*words); the result replaces the block at DRG and is used to build RSA and Diffie-Hellman exponentiation loops that never need a general division. The operation is constant-time with respect to the data and key operands and modifies no flag unless stated.
MONT.pseudo_semantics: w <- 3*(1 << ESZ) words; R <- 2^(32*w/3); DRG[0..w/3-1] <- montmul(SR1 block, SR2 block, N block at DRG[2w/3..]) * R^-1 mod N

SHA3ABS.description: SHA3ABS - SHA-3 Absorb - Absorbs the three 32-bit message words SR1, SR2 and SR3 into the SHA-3 sponge context whose 1600-bit state is selected by the handle in DRG, applying the Keccak-f[1600] permutation whenever the rate boundary is crossed; ESZ selects the digest size (0 = SHA3-224, 1 = SHA3-256, 2 = SHA3-384, 3 = SHA3-512) and MO carries the domain-separation suffix, so no software padding is required.
SHA3ABS.pseudo_semantics: ctx <- handle(DRG); absorb(ctx, ESZ, MO, SR1, SR2, SR3); if rate_reached(ctx) then keccakf1600(ctx.state)
SHA3ABS.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory CIU.EN prefix byte 0xFD selects the ciu decode space and is not counted in length.

SHA3FIN.description: SHA3FIN - SHA-3 Finalize - Pads and finalizes the sponge context selected by the handle in DRG and squeezes four consecutive digest words into the register block based at SR1, with SR2 selecting the starting word index and SR3 = 0 requesting the final padded block while SR3 = 1 requests a mid-stream squeeze; ESZ must match the digest size used by SHA3ABS.
SHA3FIN.pseudo_semantics: ctx <- handle(DRG); pad(ctx, ESZ); for k in 0..3: GPR[SR1+k] <- squeezeWord(ctx, SR2+k); if SR3 == 1 then keccakf1600(ctx.state)
SHA3FIN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory CIU.EN prefix byte 0xFD selects the ciu decode space and is not counted in length.

KECCAKF.description: KECCAKF - Keccak-f Permutation - Applies the full 24-round Keccak-f[1600] permutation to the sponge state selected by the handle in DRG, optionally XORing the three words SR1, SR2 and SR3 into the first three lanes when MO bit 0 is set; this exposes the raw permutation so that SHAKE, cSHAKE, KMAC and TupleHash can be built without new opcodes.
KECCAKF.pseudo_semantics: ctx <- handle(DRG); if MO & 1 then ctx.lane[0..2] <- ctx.lane[0..2] ^ (SR1, SR2, SR3); 24 rounds of theta, rho, pi, chi, iota on ctx.state
KECCAKF.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory CIU.EN prefix byte 0xFD selects the ciu decode space and is not counted in length.

POLY1305.description: POLY1305 - Poly1305 Block Update - Folds the 128-bit message block formed by the 64-bit pair SR1 and SR2 into the Poly1305 accumulator of the context selected by the handle in DRG, computing acc = ((acc + m + 2^128) * r) mod 2^130-5 with the clamp already applied to r at key load, and SR3 = 0 means the block is complete while SR3 = 1 marks it as the final partial block.
POLY1305.pseudo_semantics: ctx <- handle(DRG); m <- (SR2 << 64) | SR1 | (2^128 if SR3 == 0); ctx.acc <- ((ctx.acc + m) * ctx.r) mod (2^130 - 5)
POLY1305.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory CIU.EN prefix byte 0xFD selects the ciu decode space and is not counted in length.

CHACHA.description: CHACHA - ChaCha Block Function - Produces one ChaCha keystream block from the key and nonce held in the context selected by the handle in DRG, using the block counter in SR1 and writing four consecutive keystream words into the register block based at SR2; SR3 selects the round count (0 = 8, 1 = 12, 2 = 20 rounds) and the output is the pre-XOR keystream so the caller applies the message XOR itself.
CHACHA.pseudo_semantics: ctx <- handle(DRG); st <- chachaInit(ctx.key, ctx.nonce, SR1); for rounds in 0..(roundsOf(SR3)/2)-1: quarterRounds(st); for k in 0..3: GPR[SR2+k] <- st[k] + initial[k]
CHACHA.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory CIU.EN prefix byte 0xFD selects the ciu decode space and is not counted in length.

FSIN.description: FSIN - Big-Math Sine - Computes the sine of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; argument reduction uses a 2^-128 accurate representation of 2*pi so large arguments stay accurate, a NaN or infinite argument sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and a denormal argument returns the argument itself. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FSIN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, sin(reduce_fpf(SF1))); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)
FSIN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FCOS.description: FCOS - Big-Math Cosine - Computes the cosine of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; the same 2^-128 accurate argument reduction as FSIN is used, cos is evaluated as an even function so cos(-x) equals cos(x) exactly, and a NaN or infinite argument sets FLV. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FCOS.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, cos(reduce_fpf(SF1))); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)
FCOS.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FTAN.description: FTAN - Big-Math Tangent - Computes the tangent of SF1 as sin/cos under the common argument reduction, with RM rounding into DFR; an argument very close to an odd multiple of pi/2 overflows and sets FLO, so callers that must handle the pole test the reduced magnitude first. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FTAN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, tan(reduce_fpf(SF1))); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | overflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)
FTAN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FASIN.description: FASIN - Big-Math Arc Sine - Computes the principal arc sine of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR, returning a result in [-pi/2, +pi/2]; an argument outside [-1, +1] sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and asin(x) for a tiny x returns x unchanged with only FLZ affected. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FASIN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, asin(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- (|SF1| > 1) | isNaN(SF1)
FASIN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FACOS.description: FACOS - Big-Math Arc Cosine - Computes the principal arc cosine of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR, returning a result in [0, pi]; an argument outside [-1, +1] sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and FACOS(1) returns an exact +0 with FLZ set. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FACOS.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, acos(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- (|SF1| > 1) | isNaN(SF1)
FACOS.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FATAN.description: FATAN - Big-Math Arc Tangent - Computes the principal arc tangent of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR, returning a result in (-pi/2, +pi/2); an infinite argument returns the exact limit representable in the format, and the sign of a zero argument is preserved so FATAN(-0) is -0. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FATAN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, atan(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1)
FATAN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FATAN2.description: FATAN2 - Big-Math Arc Tangent Two - Computes the four-quadrant arc tangent atan2(SF1, SF2) with SF1 as ordinate and SF2 as abscissa, writing the result in (-pi, +pi] to DFR with RM rounding; both-zero arguments resolve from the operand signs so atan2(-0, -0) is -pi, and a NaN operand propagates a quieted payload while setting FLV. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FATAN2.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, atan2(SF1, SF2)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2)
FATAN2.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FEXP.description: FEXP - Big-Math Exponential - Computes e raised to SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; an argument above the overflow threshold yields +infinity with FLO, one below the underflow threshold yields +0 with FLO, and an argument of -infinity yields +0 without setting FLV. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FEXP.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, exp(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow | inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1)
FEXP.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FLN.description: FLN - Big-Math Natural Logarithm - Computes the natural logarithm of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; FLN(1) returns an exact +0 with FLZ set, a zero argument returns -infinity with FLO set, a negative argument sets FLV and returns the default quiet NaN, and the logarithm of a denormal is computed exactly. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FLN.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, ln(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | (SF1 == 0); FLV <- (SF1 < 0) | isNaN(SF1)
FLN.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FLOG2.description: FLOG2 - Big-Math Binary Logarithm - Computes the base-2 logarithm of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; powers of two produce exact integer results, so a range-reduction or scaling loop can use FLOG2 to size a normalization step without an inexactness penalty. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FLOG2.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, log2(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | (SF1 == 0); FLV <- (SF1 < 0) | isNaN(SF1)
FLOG2.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FLOG10.description: FLOG10 - Big-Math Decimal Logarithm - Computes the base-10 logarithm of SF1 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; FLN, FLOG2 and FLOG10 share one reduction pipeline, so their accuracy classes and their treatment of zero, negative and NaN arguments are identical. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FLOG10.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, log10(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | (SF1 == 0); FLV <- (SF1 < 0) | isNaN(SF1)
FLOG10.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FPOW.description: FPOW - Big-Math Power - Raises SF1 to the power SF2 in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR, computed internally as exp2(SF2 * log2(SF1)); a negative base is accepted only when SF2 is an exact integer, and the special cases 0^0 = 1, 0^negative = +infinity with FLO and infinity^0 = 1 are architectural. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FPOW.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, pow(SF1, SF2)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- overflow | underflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2) | ((SF1 < 0) & !isInteger(SF2))
FPOW.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FSINH.description: FSINH - Big-Math Hyperbolic Sine - Computes sinh(SF1) in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; the odd symmetry is exact so sinh(-x) is -sinh(x) bit for bit, a large argument overflows to infinity with FLO, and a tiny argument is returned unchanged to avoid a cancellation loss. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FSINH.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, sinh(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | overflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)
FSINH.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FCOSH.description: FCOSH - Big-Math Hyperbolic Cosine - Computes cosh(SF1) in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; the function is even, cosh(0) is exactly 1, a large argument overflows to +infinity with FLO, and the result is never negative so no sign restoration step is needed. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FCOSH.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, cosh(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | overflow; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1)
FCOSH.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FTANH.description: FTANH - Big-Math Hyperbolic Tangent - Computes tanh(SF1) in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR; the result approaches +1 or -1 for large arguments without reaching it, a tiny argument is returned unchanged, and an infinite argument yields the exact +1 or -1 with FLZ clear. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FTANH.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, tanh(SF1)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1)
FTANH.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

FHYPOT.description: FHYPOT - Big-Math Hypotenuse - Computes sqrt(SF1*SF1 + SF2*SF2) in the FPF format with RM rounding into DFR without intermediate overflow or underflow, because both operands are prescaled by their common exponent; an infinity operand returns infinity even when the other operand is a NaN. MO selects the accuracy class (0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp) and FPF/RM fix the result format and rounding, so the result is deterministic for a given class.
FHYPOT.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, hypot(SF1, SF2)); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact; FLV <- isNaN(SF1) | isNaN(SF2); FLV suppressed when isInf(SF1) | isInf(SF2)
FHYPOT.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BMUL.description: BMUL - Big Multiply - Multiplies the block at SR1 by the block at SR2 and writes the double-width product to the block at DRG, which must be twice as wide as the source blocks; the schoolbook carry chain runs from the least significant word upward, CF reports a carry out of the final word and OF reports that the high half was not merely a sign extension. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant. The operation covers the whole block and writes no other flag.
BMUL.pseudo_semantics: T <- 0; for i in 0..n-1: for j in 0..n-1: T[i+j] <- T[i+j] + a[i]*b[j] with carry propagation; block[DRG] <- T; CF <- carry out of word 2n-1
BMUL.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BADD.description: BADD - Big Add - Adds the block at SR1 to the block at SR2 word by word with full carry propagation and writes the sum to DRG; with MO[3:2] = 1 the incoming CF is added as a carry-in and the carry out of the most significant word becomes the new CF, which is what makes a multi-precision addition loop possible. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BADD.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BSUB.description: BSUB - Big Subtract - Subtracts the block at SR2 from the block at SR1 with borrow propagation and writes the difference to DRG; with MO[3:2] = 1 the incoming CF acts as a borrow-in and the borrow out of the most significant word becomes CF, so a comparison and a subtraction can share one pass. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BSUB.pseudo_semantics: b <- (MO[3:2] == 1) ? CF : 0; for k in 0..n-1: d <- a[k] - b[k] - b; r[k] <- wrap32(d); b <- (d < 0); block[DRG] <- r; CF <- b; ZF <- (r == 0)
BSUB.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BDIV.description: BDIV - Big Divide - Divides the double-width block at SR1 by the block at SR2 using Knuth algorithm D and writes the quotient to DRG, leaving the remainder in the SR2 block, which the instruction therefore consumes and overwrites; a zero divisor raises #DIV before any register is written, and MO[3:2] = 1 writes the remainder to DRG instead of the quotient. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BDIV.pseudo_semantics: if block[SR2] == 0 then #DIV; (q, rem) <- divmod(block[SR1], block[SR2]); block[SR2] <- rem; block[DRG] <- (MO[3:2] == 1) ? rem : q; ZF <- (block[DRG] == 0)
BDIV.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BMOD.description: BMOD - Big Modulo - Computes the remainder of the block at SR1 divided by the block at SR2 and leaves it in DRG without keeping the quotient, so a modular-exponentiation loop can preserve the modulus block; a zero modulus raises #DIV, and with MO[1:0] = 1 a negative dividend yields a remainder carrying the sign of the divisor. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BMOD.pseudo_semantics: if block[SR2] == 0 then #DIV; block[DRG] <- block[SR1] mod block[SR2] per MO[1:0]; ZF <- (block[DRG] == 0)
BMOD.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BSHL.description: BSHL - Big Shift Left - Shifts the whole block at SR1 left by the bit count held in SR2 and writes the result to DRG; the shift crosses word boundaries so the block moves as one integer, bits shifted beyond the most significant word are lost, and a count at or above the block width clears the block. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BSHL.pseudo_semantics: sh <- zext(SR2) mod (32*n); for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- wordShl(a, k, sh); block[DRG] <- r
BSHL.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BSHR.description: BSHR - Big Shift Right - Shifts the whole block at SR1 right by the bit count held in SR2 and writes the result to DRG, filling with zeros in the logical form and replicating the sign word when MO[1:0] = 1; a count at or above the block width produces zero for logical shifts and the sign fill for arithmetic shifts. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BSHR.pseudo_semantics: sh <- zext(SR2) mod (32*n); for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- wordShr(a, k, sh, MO[1:0]); block[DRG] <- r
BSHR.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BAND.description: BAND - Big And - Computes the bit-wise AND of the blocks at SR1 and SR2 and writes it to DRG; the operation is applied to every word independently, so it is the mask operation that clears the high words of a partial-width bignum without a separate compare. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. The operation covers the whole block and writes no other flag.
BAND.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- a[k] & b[k]; block[DRG] <- r
BAND.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BOR.description: BOR - Big Or - Computes the bit-wise inclusive OR of the blocks at SR1 and SR2 into DRG; it is the counterpart of BAND and is typically used to inject marker bits into the top word of a bignum before a compare. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. The operation covers the whole block and writes no other flag.
BOR.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- a[k] | b[k]; block[DRG] <- r
BOR.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BXOR.description: BXOR - Big Exclusive Or - Computes the bit-wise XOR of the blocks at SR1 and SR2 into DRG; XOR with the same block twice restores the original value, which makes it usable as a block-wide operation in cryptographic masking code. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. The operation covers the whole block and writes no other flag.
BXOR.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- a[k] ^ b[k]; block[DRG] <- r
BXOR.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BNOT.description: BNOT - Big Not - Writes the one's complement of every word of the block at SR1 to the block at DRG; the two trailing 0x0 nibbles are reserved fields that must be encoded as zero, and the result equals the two's-complement negation minus one. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BNOT.pseudo_semantics: for k in 0..n-1: r[k] <- ~a[k]; block[DRG] <- r
BNOT.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

BCMP.description: BCMP - Big Compare - Compares the blocks at SR1 and SR2 from the most significant word downward and sets ZF when they are equal, CF when SR1 is below SR2 and NF from the sign of the difference; MO[1:0] = 1 compares as two's-complement signed values rather than as unsigned magnitudes, and no register is written. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register. MO[1:0] selects unsigned magnitude or two's-complement signed interpretation and MO[3:2] selects the plain, carry-aware, truncated or extended variant.
BCMP.pseudo_semantics: for k in n-1..0: if a[k] != b[k] then r <- sign_of(a[k] - b[k]), break; r <- 0; ZF <- (r == 0); CF <- (a < b) per MO[1:0]; NF <- (r < 0)
BCMP.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

B2D.description: B2D - Big To Double - Converts the integer block at SR1 into the floating-point format FPF with RM rounding and writes DFR; a 512-bit magnitude keeps only the leading 53 bits of significand so the value rounds once with FLO set when it was inexact, an exponent overflow yields an infinity with FLO, and a zero block yields +0 with FLZ. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register.
B2D.pseudo_semantics: DFR <- round_fpf(RM, block[SR1]); FLZ <- (DFR == +-0); FLO <- inexact | overflow; FLV <- 0
B2D.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

D2B.description: D2B - Double To Big - Converts the floating-point operand SF1 into the integer block at DRG using RM rounding, producing a two's-complement value that fills the whole block; a NaN or an infinity sets FLV and leaves the block unchanged, and discarding fractional bits sets FLO. Operands are GPR blocks named by their base register, 2 << ESZ words wide (2, 4, 8 or 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register and word k in register base+k; a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 is the architectural zero register.
D2B.pseudo_semantics: if isNaN(SF1) | isInf(SF1) then FLV <- 1 else block[DRG] <- roundint(RM, SF1) as 32*n-bit twos-complement; FLO <- inexact
D2B.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

MMUL.description: MMUL - Matrix Multiply - Multiplies the NxN matrix block based at VF1 by the NxN matrix block based at VF2, adds the NxN accumulator block based at VF3 and writes the NxN product block to the register block based at VDG; N comes from ESZ (0 = 2x2, 1 = 4x4, 2 = 8x8) and each element's multiply-accumulate is exact for the OPSZ element width, so integer matrices never round. Operands are vector-register blocks in the BMU matrix buffer: a matrix of order N (N = 2, 4 or 8 from ESZ) occupies N consecutive vector registers, one 256-bit row per register, and the element width comes from the OPSZ prefix (32-bit by default).
MMUL.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..N-1: for j in 0..N-1: acc <- C[i][j]; for k in 0..N-1: acc <- acc + A[i][k]*B[k][j]; VD[i][j] <- acc
MMUL.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

MVEC.description: MVEC - Matrix Vector Multiply - Multiplies the NxN matrix block based at VF1 by the vector VF2 and writes the N-element result vector to VDG; MO=0 is a plain product, MO=1 transposes the matrix first for a column-major layout, MO=2 accumulates into VDG and MO=3 accumulates with the transposed layout, which covers the usual graphics transform cases. Operands are vector-register blocks in the BMU matrix buffer: a matrix of order N (N = 2, 4 or 8 from ESZ) occupies N consecutive vector registers, one 256-bit row per register, and the element width comes from the OPSZ prefix (32-bit by default).
MVEC.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..N-1: acc <- (MO >= 2) ? VD[i] : 0; for k in 0..N-1: acc <- acc + ((MO & 1) ? A[k][i] : A[i][k]) * v[k]; VD[i] <- acc
MVEC.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

MTRANS.description: MTRANS - Matrix Transpose - Transposes the NxN matrix block based at VF1 into the block based at VDG with N taken from ESZ; MO selects the exchange granularity (0 = single elements, 1 = 2x2 element blocks, 2 = 4x4 element blocks), so one instruction serves both a plain transpose and the in-place block transforms of a fast matrix multiply. Operands are vector-register blocks in the BMU matrix buffer: a matrix of order N (N = 2, 4 or 8 from ESZ) occupies N consecutive vector registers, one 256-bit row per register, and the element width comes from the OPSZ prefix (32-bit by default).
MTRANS.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..N-1: for j in 0..N-1: VD[j][i] <- (MO == 0) ? A[i][j] : blockTranspose(A, i, j, 1 << MO)
MTRANS.encoding_notes: Encoded size is length+1 bytes: the mandatory BMU.EN prefix byte 0xF6 selects the bmu decode space and is not counted in length.

LDP.description: LDP - Load Pair - Loads two elements of width 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] into DRG and DRG+1, zero-extending each to 32 bits; no flags are modified.
LDP.pseudo_semantics: ea <- SR1 + sign_extend(OF8); DRG <- zext([ea], 8*(1<<ESZ)); DRG+1 <- zext([ea + (1<<ESZ)], 8*(1<<ESZ))
LDP.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI.

STP.description: STP - Store Pair - Stores DRG and DRG+1 as two elements of width 1<<ESZ bytes at [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)]; no flags are modified.
STP.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI.

LDM.description: LDM - Load Multiple - Loads SR2+1 consecutive elements of width 1<<ESZ bytes starting at [SR1] into DRG..DRG+SR2; the base register is not modified and no flags change.
LDM.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI.

STM.description: STM - Store Multiple - Stores SR2+1 consecutive elements of width 1<<ESZ bytes from DRG..DRG+SR2 to [SR1]; the base register is not modified and no flags change.
STM.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI.

LDX.description: LDX - Load Indexed - Loads the 32-bit word at [SR1 + (SR2 << SCL)] into DRG with SCL 0..3 selecting a shift of 0..3 bits; SCL 4..15 raise #UDI and no flags change.
LDX.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SCL 0..3 encode a shift of 0..3 bits; SCL 4..15 raise #UDI.

STX.description: STX - Store Indexed - Stores DRG as a 32-bit word to [SR1 + (SR2 << SCL)] with SCL 0..3 selecting a shift of 0..3 bits; SCL 4..15 raise #UDI.
STX.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SCL 0..3 encode a shift of 0..3 bits; SCL 4..15 raise #UDI.

LDSX.description: LDSX - Load Sign-Extended - Loads 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] and sign-extends them to 32 bits in DRG; no flags are modified.
LDSX.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI.

LDZX.description: LDZX - Load Zero-Extended - Loads 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] and zero-extends them to 32 bits in DRG; no flags are modified.
LDZX.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI. LDZX is the zero-extending counterpart of the v1 LD, which sign-extends.

PREFETCH.description: PREFETCH - Prefetch for Read - Hints the cache hierarchy to fetch the line containing [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] with hint CH; it never faults and changes no architectural state.
PREFETCH.pseudo_semantics: prefetch_read(SR1 + sign_extend(OF8), CH); no architectural change
PREFETCH.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. CH is a cache/eviction hint: 0=T0 1=T1 2=T2 3=non-temporal 4=last-level-only, 5..15 reserved and ignored.

PREFETCHW.description: PREFETCHW - Prefetch for Write - Hints the cache hierarchy to fetch the line containing [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] in exclusive state with hint CH; it never faults.
PREFETCHW.pseudo_semantics: prefetch_write(SR1 + sign_extend(OF8), CH); no architectural change
PREFETCHW.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. CH uses the same table as PREFETCH.

CLZERO.description: CLZERO - Cache Line Zero - Writes zeros to the whole 32-byte line containing SR1 + sign_extend(OF8) with hint CH using non-allocating stores; no flags are modified.
CLZERO.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. The address is aligned down to the 32-byte line size; CH selects the fill policy of the zeroed line.

CACHECTL.description: CACHECTL - Cache Control - Performs the cache maintenance operation selected by MO on the line containing [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)], or on the whole data cache for MO 4..5; MO 6..15 raise #UDI.
CACHECTL.pseudo_semantics: if MO in 0..3: cache_line_op(MO, SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)) else if MO in 4..5: cache_all_op(MO) else #UDI
CACHECTL.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO: 0=icache-invalidate-line 1=dcache-clean-line 2=dcache-invalidate-line 3=clean-and-invalidate-line 4=dcache-writeback-all 5=dcache-invalidate-all; 6..15 raise #UDI. For MO 4..5 the address operand is ignored.

LDNT.description: LDNT - Non-Temporal Load - Loads 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] into DRG with a streaming hint: the line is not allocated for reuse and no flags change.
LDNT.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI. The accessed line is marked non-temporal so it is evicted first.

STNT.description: STNT - Non-Temporal Store - Stores the low 1<<ESZ bytes of DRG to [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] through a write-combining, non-allocating path; no flags are modified.
STNT.pseudo_semantics: ea <- SR1 + sign_extend(OF8); [ea] <- DRG[8*(1<<ESZ)-1:0]; store_path <- write_combining
STNT.encoding_notes: ESZ selects the element width in bytes as 1<<ESZ (0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD); ESZ 4..15 raise #UDI. Stores combine in a write-combining buffer; they are weakly ordered until MFENCE.
