LDLK.description: LDLK - Load-Linked - Loads 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1], zero-extends them into DRG and arms the local exclusive monitor for that address; ordering class MO applies and no flags change.
LDLK.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

STLK.description: STLK - Store-Conditional - Stores the low 1<<ESZ bytes of DRG to [SR1] only while the exclusive monitor still covers that address, with ordering class MO taken from the instruction, sets ZF on success and clears ZF on failure.
STLK.pseudo_semantics: if monitor_holds(SR1, 1<<ESZ) then [SR1] <- DRG[8*(1<<ESZ)-1:0]; ZF <- 1 else ZF <- 0; monitor <- invalid
STLK.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. STLK consumes and clears the monitor armed by LDLK.

CAS.description: CAS - Compare and Swap - Reads the ESZ-sized value at [SR1]; if it equals the low ESZ bytes of DRG it stores SR2 and sets ZF, otherwise it loads the observed value into DRG and clears ZF, and the whole operation is ordered by MO.
CAS.pseudo_semantics: old <- [SR1]; if lowbytes(old, ESZ) == lowbytes(DRG, ESZ) then [SR1] <- lowbytes(SR2, ESZ); ZF <- 1 else DRG <- zext(old); ZF <- 0
CAS.encoding_notes: The two 0x0 nibbles are reserved and must decode as zero; the second one pads the three-register layout to a byte boundary. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

CLREX.description: CLREX - Clear Exclusive - Invalidates the local exclusive monitor so that a following STLK reports failure in ZF; no other architectural state changes.
CLREX.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. CLREX is the explicit exit from an LDLK/STLK sequence, for example on the failure path of a retry loop.

AMOSWAP.description: AMOSWAP - Atomic Swap - Atomically replaces the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with the low ESZ bytes of DRG and discards the previous memory value; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOSWAP.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. AMOSWAP discards the previous memory value; use AMOFSWAP when the old value is needed.

AMOADD.description: AMOADD - Atomic Add - Atomically adds the ESZ-sized value in DRG to the value at [SR1] and stores the wrapped sum back; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOADD.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- wrap(old + DRG, 8*(1<<ESZ)); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOADD.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^(8*(1<<ESZ)).

AMOSUB.description: AMOSUB - Atomic Subtract - Atomically subtracts the ESZ-sized value in DRG from the value at [SR1] and stores the wrapped difference back; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOSUB.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- wrap(old - DRG, 8*(1<<ESZ)); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOSUB.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. Arithmetic wraps modulo 2^(8*(1<<ESZ)).

AMOAND.description: AMOAND - Atomic And - Atomically ANDs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG and stores the result back; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOAND.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old AND DRG; discard(old); order(MO)
AMOAND.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOOR.description: AMOOR - Atomic Or - Atomically ORs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG and stores the result back; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOOR.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old OR DRG; discard(old); order(MO)
AMOOR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOXOR.description: AMOXOR - Atomic Xor - Atomically XORs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG and stores the result back; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOXOR.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old XOR DRG; discard(old); order(MO)
AMOXOR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOMIN.description: AMOMIN - Atomic Minimum Signed - Atomically replaces the signed ESZ-sized value at [SR1] when DRG is smaller, otherwise leaves it unchanged; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOMIN.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- min_signed(old, DRG); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOMIN.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. The comparison is signed.

AMOMAX.description: AMOMAX - Atomic Maximum Signed - Atomically replaces the signed ESZ-sized value at [SR1] when DRG is larger, otherwise leaves it unchanged; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOMAX.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- max_signed(old, DRG); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOMAX.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. The comparison is signed.

AMOMINU.description: AMOMINU - Atomic Minimum Unsigned - Atomically replaces the unsigned ESZ-sized value at [SR1] when DRG is smaller, otherwise leaves it unchanged; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOMINU.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- min_unsigned(old, DRG); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOMINU.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. The comparison is unsigned.

AMOMAXU.description: AMOMAXU - Atomic Maximum Unsigned - Atomically replaces the unsigned ESZ-sized value at [SR1] when DRG is larger, otherwise leaves it unchanged; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOMAXU.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- max_unsigned(old, DRG); discard(old); order(MO)
AMOMAXU.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. The comparison is unsigned.

AMOFADD.description: AMOFADD - Atomic Fetch-Add - Atomically adds DRG to the ESZ-sized value at [SR1], stores the wrapped sum back and returns the previous memory value in DRG; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOFADD.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- wrap(old + DRG, 8*(1<<ESZ)); DRG <- zext(old, 8*(1<<ESZ)); order(MO)
AMOFADD.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised. The fetch forms return the pre-operation value in DRG, which makes them the building block for lock-free counters and stacks.

AMOFAND.description: AMOFAND - Atomic Fetch-And - Atomically ANDs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG, stores the result back and returns the previous memory value in DRG; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOFAND.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old AND DRG; DRG <- zext(old); order(MO)
AMOFAND.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOFOR.description: AMOFOR - Atomic Fetch-Or - Atomically ORs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG, stores the result back and returns the previous memory value in DRG; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOFOR.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old OR DRG; DRG <- zext(old); order(MO)
AMOFOR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOFXOR.description: AMOFXOR - Atomic Fetch-Xor - Atomically XORs the ESZ-sized value at [SR1] with DRG, stores the result back and returns the previous memory value in DRG; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOFXOR.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- old XOR DRG; DRG <- zext(old); order(MO)
AMOFXOR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

AMOFSWAP.description: AMOFSWAP - Atomic Fetch-Swap - Atomically exchanges DRG with the ESZ-sized value at [SR1]: the memory operand receives DRG and DRG receives the previous memory value; ordering class MO applies and no flags are modified.
AMOFSWAP.pseudo_semantics: atomic: old <- [SR1]; [SR1] <- DRG[8*(1<<ESZ)-1:0]; DRG <- zext(old); order(MO)
AMOFSWAP.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO is the ordering class: 0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST (5..15 reserved and raise #UDI); the MEMO prefix may strengthen but never weaken it. The address operand is exactly [SR1]: atomics take no displacement, and SR1 must be naturally aligned for 1<<ESZ or #AC is raised.

MFENCE.description: MFENCE - Full Memory Fence - Orders every load and store issued before it against every memory operation issued after it, with strength SPB over the domains selected by the IM8 mask; no flags change.
MFENCE.pseudo_semantics: wait_until(visible(all prior loads and stores)); barrier(class=SPB, domain=IM8)
MFENCE.encoding_notes: SPB: 0=light 1=standard 2=strong 3=sequentially consistent. IM8 is a domain mask: bit0 loads bit1 stores bit2 instruction fetches bit3 device/MMIO; IM8=0 means all domains; SPB 4..15 raise #UDI.

LFENCE.description: LFENCE - Load Fence - Orders all loads issued before it against all later loads and stores without draining stores; strength SPB and the IM8 domain mask apply as for MFENCE.
LFENCE.encoding_notes: SPB and IM8 use the same tables as MFENCE; LFENCE is also the canonical speculation barrier for load-dependent gadgets; SPB 4..15 raise #UDI.

SFENCE.description: SFENCE - Store Fence - Orders all stores issued before it against all later stores and loads, making them visible in program order; strength SPB and the IM8 domain mask apply.
SFENCE.encoding_notes: SPB and IM8 use the same tables as MFENCE; SFENCE is required before publishing a data structure and after non-temporal stores; SPB 4..15 raise #UDI.

XBEGIN.description: XBEGIN - Begin Transaction - Takes a checkpoint of architectural state and starts a speculative transaction whose fallback address is IP + length + sign_extend(O16); MO supplies transaction attributes.
XBEGIN.pseudo_semantics: TXE <- 1; checkpoint(state); fallback <- IP + 4 + sign_extend(O16); if already in a transaction then abort(code=1)
XBEGIN.encoding_notes: MO: bit0=read-only transaction hint bit1=suspendable bit2=retry-on-conflict bit3=nested allowed; unused bits must be zero. O16 is the signed fallback offset measured from the end of XBEGIN. Transactions are gated by the TXE status flag: XBEGIN sets it, XEND/XABORT clear it, and a #BP/#GP/#PGF while TXE=1 triggers a hardware abort instead of a trap.

XEND.description: XEND - End Transaction - Commits the buffered writes of the current transaction atomically and clears TXE; executing XEND with TXE=0 raises #GP.
XEND.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Transactions are gated by the TXE status flag: XBEGIN sets it, XEND/XABORT clear it, and a #BP/#GP/#PGF while TXE=1 triggers a hardware abort instead of a trap. XEND is the commit point: buffered writes become visible atomically.

XABORT.description: XABORT - Abort Transaction - Discards all buffered writes with the software abort code IM8, clears TXE and transfers control to the fallback address recorded by XBEGIN; #GP when TXE=0.
XABORT.pseudo_semantics: if TXE == 0 then #GP; discard(buffered); abort_code <- IM8; TXE <- 0; IP <- fallback
XABORT.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Transactions are gated by the TXE status flag: XBEGIN sets it, XEND/XABORT clear it, and a #BP/#GP/#PGF while TXE=1 triggers a hardware abort instead of a trap. The abort code is software defined and is reported to the fallback path.

XTEST.description: XTEST - Test Transaction - Sets ZF to 1 when the thread is inside a transaction and to 0 otherwise; no other flag is modified and no transaction is started.
XTEST.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Transactions are gated by the TXE status flag: XBEGIN sets it, XEND/XABORT clear it, and a #BP/#GP/#PGF while TXE=1 triggers a hardware abort instead of a trap. XTEST never starts a transaction, so a fallback path can probe TXE safely.

XSUSPEND.description: XSUSPEND - Suspend Transaction - Suspends speculative execution of the current transaction for up to O16 cycles so a conflicting writer can make progress; ZF reports whether the suspension completed.
XSUSPEND.pseudo_semantics: if TXE == 0 then #GP; suspend(speculation, timeout=O16); ZF <- suspended
XSUSPEND.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Transactions are gated by the TXE status flag: XBEGIN sets it, XEND/XABORT clear it, and a #BP/#GP/#PGF while TXE=1 triggers a hardware abort instead of a trap. O16 is a timeout hint in core cycles; 0 suspends until a conflict or an interrupt arrives.

RDCR.description: RDCR - Read Control Register - Copies the control register selected by CR into DRG; reads of control registers the implementation leaves unimplemented raise #GP and no flags change.
RDCR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. CR selects cr0-cr15; the v2 control set is cr4 vector, cr5 security, cr6 protection keys, cr7 performance, cr8 virtualization, cr9 TLB, cr10 debug, cr11 shadow stack, cr12 cache, cr13 transaction, cr14 feature and cr15 revision control.

WRCR.description: WRCR - Write Control Register - Copies SR1 into the control register selected by CR, then serializes the pipeline and flushes the TLB or cache state the new control bits invalidate.
WRCR.pseudo_semantics: CR[CR] <- SR1; serialize(); flush_dependent_state(); no flags changed
WRCR.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. WRCR is a serializing instruction: it drains the pipeline and flushes the structures whose behaviour the written bits change.

RDMSR.description: RDMSR - Read Model-Specific Register - Copies the low 32 bits of the model-specific register selected by MSI into DRG; unimplemented indices raise #GP and no flags change.
RDMSR.encoding_notes: MSI indexes the 64 model-specific registers defined by the v2 register model; unimplemented indices raise #GP.

WRMSR.description: WRMSR - Write Model-Specific Register - Writes SR1 into the low 32 bits of the model-specific register selected by MSI, serializes the pipeline and invalidates the state that register controls.
WRMSR.pseudo_semantics: MSR[MSI][31:0] <- SR1; serialize(); invalidate(MSR[MSI].dependent); no flags changed
WRMSR.encoding_notes: WRMSR is serializing and may raise #GP when the written value is reserved for the selected register.

RDTSC.description: RDTSC - Read Time-Stamp Counter - Writes the 64-bit time-stamp counter to DRG (low word) and DRG+1 (high word); the counter is monotonic and keeps counting in low-power states.
RDTSC.encoding_notes: Reading the counter at L0 can be disabled by the TSD control bit in cr14, which turns the instruction into #GP.

RDTSCP.description: RDTSCP - Read Time-Stamp Counter and Id - Writes the 64-bit time-stamp counter to DRG/DRG+1 and the virtual processor id to SR1 after ordering all prior loads against the read.
RDTSCP.pseudo_semantics: wait_until(prior_loads_ordered); DRG <- TSC[31:0]; DRG+1 <- TSC[63:32]; SR1 <- VPID
RDTSCP.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. RDTSCP does not wait for older stores, so a fence is still required to time a store-to-load round trip.

RDPMU.description: RDPMU - Read Performance Counter - Copies the 32-bit performance counter pmc[SR2] into DRG; the counter counts the event that PMUCTL assigned to it and never counts itself.
RDPMU.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SR2 selects pmc0-pmc7; cr7 gates L0 reads and raises #GP when the counter is marked hypervisor-only.

PMUCTL.description: PMUCTL - Performance Counter Control - Applies operation MO to counter SR1 with argument SR2, for example start, stop, reset or select event; unknown MO codes raise #UDI and no flags change.
PMUCTL.pseudo_semantics: case MO of 0: start(PMC[SR1]); 1: stop(PMC[SR1]); 2: reset(PMC[SR1]); 3: select_event(PMC[SR1], SR2); 4: freeze_all(); 5: enable_overflow(PMC[SR1]); 6..15: #UDI
PMUCTL.encoding_notes: MO: 0=start 1=stop 2=reset 3=select event from SR2 4=freeze all 5=enable overflow interrupt; MO 6..15 raise #UDI. SR1 selects pmc0-pmc7.

INVLPG.description: INVLPG - Invalidate Page - Invalidates the TLB entry that translates the linear address SR1 + sign_extend(OF8), keeping global entries unless the global-flush bit in cr9 is set.
INVLPG.encoding_notes: Entries marked global survive unless cr9 bit0 asks for a global flush as well; the address is first formed by the normal paging rules, without faulting.

INVTLB.description: INVTLB - Invalidate TLB - Invalidates translation entries according to MO (all, by address-space identifier in SEG, global only, or everything including global); MO 4..15 raise #UDI.
INVTLB.pseudo_semantics: case MO of 0: flush_all(); 1: flush_asid(SEG); 2: flush_global(); 3: flush_all(including_global); 4..15: #UDI
INVTLB.encoding_notes: MO: 0=all entries 1=entries of the ASID in SEG 2=global entries only 3=all entries including global; MO 4..15 raise #UDI. SEG is the 16-bit address-space identifier.

INVEPT.description: INVEPT - Invalidate Extended Page Mappings - Drops cached guest-physical to host-physical translations selected by MO for the extended-page-table context in SEG; MO 4..15 raise #UDI.
INVEPT.pseudo_semantics: if VME == 1 then #GP; case MO of 0..3: flush_ept(MO, SEG); 4..15: #UDI
INVEPT.encoding_notes: MO: 0=the single mapping cached for SEG 1=every mapping of the EPTP index SEG 2=all guest mappings 3=all mappings including global; MO 4..15 raise #UDI. Requires VME=0.

ICACHEINV.description: ICACHEINV - Invalidate Instruction Cache - Invalidates the instruction-cache line containing SR1 + sign_extend(OF8) and flushes the pipeline so following fetches observe newly written code.
ICACHEINV.encoding_notes: ICACHEINV is required after a store that modifies code; the decoder refetches the line and the pipeline is flushed.

CLWBI.description: CLWBI - Clean and Write Back Line - Writes the dirty data-cache line containing SR1 + sign_extend(OF8) back to memory and invalidates the cached copy, so the next read refetches it.
CLWBI.encoding_notes: CLWBI is a clean-and-invalidate, not a pure writeback: the line leaves the cache in the invalid state.

SYSENT.description: SYSENT - System Entry - Saves IP and flags on the system stack, loads the handler entry from SYSENT_BASE plus IM8*4, switches to mode L3 and clears IF; unimplemented IM8 values raise #GP.
SYSENT.pseudo_semantics: push(IP); push(flags); IP <- SYSENT_BASE + IM8*4; level <- L3; IF <- 0
SYSENT.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SYSENT is the fast system-entry path used instead of the v1 INT gate sequence; IRET remains the matching return for interrupt frames.

SYSEXI.description: SYSEXI - System Exit - Restores the flags, IP and privilege level saved by the most recent SYSENT and returns to the interrupted context; #GP when no such frame exists.
SYSEXI.pseudo_semantics: if sysent_frame_pending == 0 then #GP; flags <- pop(); IP <- pop(); level <- saved_level
SYSEXI.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SYSEXI is the exact inverse of SYSENT and raises #GP when no system-entry frame is pending on the SYS stack.

CPUID.description: CPUID - Cpu Identification - Takes the leaf number in DRG and the subleaf in SR1, then returns four feature words in DRG, DRG+1, DRG+2 and DRG+3; the leaf index is destroyed.
CPUID.pseudo_semantics: (DRG, DRG+1, DRG+2, DRG+3) <- feature_words(leaf = DRG, subleaf = SR1)
CPUID.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Values returned for unknown leaves are all zero except DRG, which holds the highest implemented basic leaf, so software can probe the leaf space.

READREV.description: READREV - Read Architecture Revision - Writes the packed revision word into DRG: major in b[31:24], minor in b[23:16], stepping in b[15:8] and vendor id in b[7:0].
READREV.encoding_notes: Vendor id 0x01 identifies the reference Hayneko implementation; major 2 minor 0 stepping 0 describes v2.0.0.

SETMODE.description: SETMODE - Set Privilege Mode - Requests the privilege level encoded in MO; the request succeeds only when the level is reachable from the current one and permitted by the capability mask, otherwise #GP.
SETMODE.pseudo_semantics: if reachable(MO, current_level) && capability_mask[MO] then level <- MO else #GP
SETMODE.encoding_notes: MO encodes the target level 0..7 directly; MO values 8..15 are not encodable because the field is 4 bits wide. Entering a level requires the corresponding capability bit in the capability mask.

GETMODE.description: GETMODE - Get Privilege Mode - Writes the current privilege level into bits 2:0 of DRG and the current capability mask into bits 31:16; no flags change.
GETMODE.encoding_notes: GETMODE is the cheap probe used by libraries that must branch on privilege without faulting.

WRFLAGS.description: WRFLAGS - Write Flags - Replaces the architected flag word from SR1, masking privileged fields according to the current privilege level; the written value is observable by RDFLAGS.
WRFLAGS.pseudo_semantics: mask <- writable_mask(level); flags <- (flags AND NOT mask) OR (SR1 AND mask)
WRFLAGS.encoding_notes: Privileged fields (IF, TF, RF, AC) can only be changed at L3 or above; lower levels get an implicit mask and never a fault.

RDFLAGS.description: RDFLAGS - Read Flags - Writes the architected flag word into DRG with the bit assignment of the flags section, so software can save and restore flags without touching the stack.
RDFLAGS.pseudo_semantics: DRG <- flags_word(ZF, CF, OF, NF, DF, IF, TF, RF, AC)
RDFLAGS.encoding_notes: RDFLAGS is the read side of WRFLAGS and uses the same bit assignment as PUSHF and POPF.

VMENTER.description: VMENTER - Virtual Machine Enter - Loads guest architectural state from the control block addressed by DRG, sets VME and switches to virtual-machine mode L6; executing it with VME=1 raises #GP.
VMENTER.pseudo_semantics: if VME == 1 then #GP; load_guest(DRG); VME <- 1; level <- L6
VMENTER.encoding_notes: The descriptor passed in DRG has the same layout as the v2 VMCS-equivalent control block read by VMREAD and VMWRITE at field offsets.

VMEXIT.description: VMEXIT - Virtual Machine Exit - Saves guest state to the active control block, writes the exit reason code into DRG, clears VME and returns the CPU to hypervisor mode L5; requires VME=1.
VMEXIT.pseudo_semantics: if VME == 0 then #GP; save_guest(); DRG <- exit_reason; VME <- 0; level <- L5
VMEXIT.encoding_notes: Hardware-initiated exits re-use this save sequence and write the reason table entry into the control block; the DRG form is the guest-initiated exit request.

VMRUN.description: VMRUN - Virtual Machine Run - Launches or resumes the virtual processor identified by DRG and stays in virtual-machine mode until an exit occurs, then writes the exit reason back into DRG.
VMRUN.pseudo_semantics: if VME == 1 then #GP; run_vcpu(DRG) until exit; DRG <- exit_reason
VMRUN.encoding_notes: VMRUN is the long-running form: it returns to the next instruction only after an exit, so the hypervisor loop is VMRUN plus a dispatch on the reason.

VMREAD.description: VMREAD - Virtual Machine Read Field - Copies the virtual-machine control field selected by the low 10 bits of SR2 into DRG; unimplemented field encodings raise #GP.
VMREAD.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Only the low 10 bits of SR2 select the field, so a 32-bit field identifier can be passed in a register and ignored above bit 9.

VMWRITE.description: VMWRITE - Virtual Machine Write Field - Writes SR1 into the virtual-machine control field selected by the low 10 bits of SR2 and invalidates the cached state that field controls.
VMWRITE.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. Writing control fields that affect cached translations also invalidates the affected extended-page mappings.

VMCALL.description: VMCALL - Virtual Machine Call - Raises virtualization exception #VC (vector 14) to the hypervisor with the hypercall number IM8 and its arguments in SR1, SR2, SR3 and r0.
VMCALL.pseudo_semantics: raise(#VC, vector = 14, reason = hypercall, number = IM8)
VMCALL.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. VMCALL is the guest side of the hypercall ABI; arguments follow the v2 syscall convention in SR1, SR2, SR3 and r0, and the result returns in r0.

VMFUNC.description: VMFUNC - Virtual Machine Function - Invokes the hypervisor service selected by MO and IM8 inside the current context without a world switch; CF reports whether the service completed.
VMFUNC.encoding_notes: MO is the service class (0=TLB management 1=interrupt injection 2=state query 3=tracing) and IM8 is the sub-function; unimplemented pairs leave CF=1.

VMLOAD.description: VMLOAD - Virtual Machine Load State - Loads the guest register and control state from the control block at [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] without entering virtual-machine mode.
VMLOAD.encoding_notes: VMLOAD and VMSTORE are the pair used for context migration and for debugging a guest image without executing it.

VMSTORE.description: VMSTORE - Virtual Machine Store State - Stores the current guest register and control state to the control block at [SR1 + sign_extend(OF8)] for migration or inspection.
VMSTORE.encoding_notes: VMSTORE writes exactly the bytes VMLOAD reads, so a saved image is freely reloadable.

MAP.description: MAP - Map Page - Installs the translation of the page containing linear address SR1 to physical base SR2 with the size class and rights encoded in MO, then drops the cached translations of that page.
MAP.pseudo_semantics: pte(SR1) <- {pa = SR2 & size_mask(MO), rights = MO[7:4], present = 1}; invalidate_translation(SR1)
MAP.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO bits 3:0 select the size class (0=4 KiB 1=64 KiB 2=2 MiB 3=1 GiB) and bits 7:4 carry the write, user, execute and global rights; the physical base in SR2 must be aligned to the size class.

UNMAP.description: UNMAP - Unmap Page - Clears the translation of the page containing linear address SR1 with the size class from MO, invalidates its cached translations and marks the entry not present.
UNMAP.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. MO uses the same size-class table as MAP; unmapping an address that has no mapping is a no-operation and never faults.

PROTECT.description: PROTECT - Protect Page - Rewrites only the permission and key bits of the translation covering SR1 from SR2, keeping the physical base and the size class selected by MO, then invalidates the cached translations.
PROTECT.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. Only the rights field is rewritten, so the physical base and the size class of an existing mapping are preserved; MO uses the MAP size-class table.

PGWALK.description: PGWALK - Page Walk - Walks the three-level page table for linear address SR1 in software and writes the resulting page-table entry into DRG, setting the accessed bit on the way.
PGWALK.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. PGWALK is the software escape hatch used by page-fault handlers and by the MAP micro-code to find the entry a mapping must overwrite.

SETPGT.description: SETPGT - Set Page Table - Loads SR1 as the physical base of the top-level page table, serializes the pipeline and flushes every non-global translation.
SETPGT.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. SETPGT is the cr3-equivalent install: the base must be aligned to 4 KiB and all non-global translations are dropped.

GETPGT.description: GETPGT - Get Page Table - Writes the physical base of the currently active top-level page table into DRG; no flags change and no translation is invalidated.
GETPGT.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. GETPGT reads the value installed by SETPGT or by the last task switch, not the raw cr3 alias.

MKEYALLOC.description: MKEYALLOC - Memory Key Allocate - Allocates the lowest protection key that is still free, writes its index into DRG and sets PKE; #GP when all 16 keys are already allocated.
MKEYALLOC.pseudo_semantics: if free_key == none then #GP; DRG <- free_key; key_bitmap[free_key] <- 1; PKE <- 1
MKEYALLOC.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. Keys 0-15 are the PKEY field values that MAP and PROTECT can attach to a mapping; the allocation bitmap lives in cr6.

MKEYFREE.description: MKEYFREE - Memory Key Free - Releases the protection key whose index is in DRG and leaves mappings that still reference it inaccessible until they are re-keyed.
MKEYFREE.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MKEYFREE makes accesses through any mapping that still carries the key fail with #PGF until those mappings are re-keyed.

EPTMAP.description: EPTMAP - Extended Page Map - Installs an extended-page-table entry mapping the guest-physical page containing SR1 to host-physical SR2 with the size class and rights from MO; requires VME=0.
EPTMAP.pseudo_semantics: if VME == 1 then #GP; ept(SR1) <- {hpa = SR2 & size_mask(MO), rights = MO[7:4], present = 1}; flush_combined(SR1)
EPTMAP.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO uses the MAP size-class and rights tables; the guest-physical base in SR1 and the host-physical base in SR2 must both be aligned to the size class.

EPTUNMAP.description: EPTUNMAP - Extended Page Unmap - Clears the extended-page-table entry covering the guest-physical page containing SR1 and drops the cached combined translations of that page, with the size class taken from MO.
EPTUNMAP.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero.EPTUNMAP drops combined translations as well as the extended entry, because a cached guest mapping survives an entry clear otherwise.

DBGON.description: DBGON - Debug On - Enables the debug facility selected by MO and sets DTE so the selected events become observable; MO 5..15 raise #UDI and cr10 gates the whole instruction.
DBGON.encoding_notes: MO: 0=all 1=breakpoints 2=watchpoints 3=trace 4=single-step; MO 5..15 raise #UDI. Enabling a facility requires the debug-enable bit in cr10.

DBGOFF.description: DBGOFF - Debug Off - Disables the debug facility selected by MO, flushes the trace record when the trace facility is the one disabled, and clears DTE once no facility stays enabled; MO 5..15 raise #UDI.
DBGOFF.encoding_notes: MO uses the same facility table as DBGON; disabling the trace facility also flushes the partially filled record.

BPSET.description: BPSET - Breakpoint Set - Programs execution breakpoint dbg[DRG] with the address SR1 and the control word SR2 so that fetching from SR1 produces a debug break; DRG values above 7 raise #GP.
BPSET.pseudo_semantics: if DRG > 7 then #GP; dbg[DRG] <- {address = SR1, control = SR2, armed = 1}
BPSET.encoding_notes: DRG selects dbg0-dbg7; SR2 is the control word: bit1=global bit2=break before execute bits 7:4=hit count. A fetch at an armed address raises #BP (vector 11).

BPCLR.description: BPCLR - Breakpoint Clear - Disarms the execution breakpoint dbg[DRG] and resets its hit counter, so a following fetch at that address no longer breaks.
BPCLR.encoding_notes: Clearing a breakpoint also clears its hit counter, so a later BPSET starts from zero.

WCHSET.description: WCHSET - Watchpoint Set - Programs data watchpoint wch[DRG] over the address SR1 with the access type and length encoded in SR2; a matching data access produces a debug break.
WCHSET.pseudo_semantics: if DRG > 7 then #GP; wch[DRG] <- {address = SR1, access = SR2[1:0], length = 1 << SR2[7:4]}
WCHSET.encoding_notes: SR2 bits 1:0 are the access type (0=read 1=write 2=read or write) and bits 7:4 the watched length as 1<<n bytes; DRG selects wch0-wch7.

WCHCLR.description: WCHCLR - Watchpoint Clear - Disarms the data watchpoint wch[DRG], so accesses inside its range no longer break; the address and control words are left unchanged.
WCHCLR.encoding_notes: Watchpoints and breakpoints are independent: clearing one never clears the other.

STEP.description: STEP - Single Step - Sets TF so that completion of the instruction selected by MO produces a debug break and returns control to the debugger; MO 3..15 raise #UDI.
STEP.pseudo_semantics: if MO > 2 then #UDI; TF <- 1; step_mode <- MO
STEP.encoding_notes: MO: 0=one instruction 1=to the next branch 2=until the matching return; MO 3..15 raise #UDI. The same effect is reachable in software by setting TF through WRFLAGS.

TRACEON.description: TRACEON - Trace On - Points the trace buffer at SR1 with the control word SR2, then sets DTE so branch and memory records are written to the buffer until TRACEOFF.
TRACEON.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SR2 is the trace control word: bit0 branch records bit1 memory records bits 15:8 the buffer size code; the buffer base must be 64-byte aligned.

TRACEOFF.description: TRACEOFF - Trace Off - Stops trace recording, writes a final end-of-trace record and clears DTE while leaving the buffer contents intact for inspection.
TRACEOFF.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. TRACEOFF does not clear the buffer, so a debugger can still read the recorded window through DBGREAD after tracing stopped.

DBGREAD.description: DBGREAD - Debug Read - Copies the debug state register selected by SR1 into DRG, which exposes breakpoint control words, trace pointers and counters without a memory access.
DBGREAD.pseudo_semantics: case SR1 of 0..7: DRG <- dbg[SR1]; 8..15: DRG <- trace[SR1-8]; 16..23: DRG <- PMC[SR1-16]; else #GP
DBGREAD.encoding_notes: 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SR1 selects the state register: 0-7 debug control dbg0-dbg7, 8-15 trace state, 16-23 performance counters; unimplemented selectors raise #GP.

SLEEP.description: SLEEP - Sleep - Enters the sleep state selected by MO with the IM8 residency hint and resumes at the wake event; a non-maskable interrupt wakes the core even in the deepest state.
SLEEP.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=C1 clock stop 1=C2 2=C3 3=deepest implemented state; IM8 is a residency hint in 100 microsecond units.

STANDBY.description: STANDBY - Standby - Places the core in standby for an expected residency of IM8 milliseconds; all architectural state is retained and any interrupt resumes at the next instruction.
STANDBY.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. IM8 is the expected residency in milliseconds.

CLKGATE.description: CLKGATE - Clock Gate - Gates the clock of the unit selected by MO so it stops drawing dynamic power; the unit keeps all state and wakes on its next use.
CLKGATE.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=all units 1=vector 2=FPU 3=crypto 4=BMU; a gated unit keeps its state and stalls the first instruction that needs it again.

MONITOR.description: MONITOR - Monitor Address - Arms the address monitor over the 32-byte line containing SR1 so a following MWAIT can sleep until that line is written.
MONITOR.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. One monitor address exists per thread; a second MONITOR replaces the first without an error.

MWAIT.description: MWAIT - Monitor Wait - Waits until the line armed by MONITOR is written, a wake event of class MO arrives or the IM8 timeout expires, then continues at the next instruction.
MWAIT.pseudo_semantics: if monitor_unarmed then no_wait; else stall_until(write(monitor_line) OR event(MO) OR timeout(IM8))
MWAIT.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO selects the wake class (0=any event 1=interrupt only 2=event only); the wait ends after IM8 x 100 microsecond units even without a wake event.

WFI.description: WFI - Wait For Interrupt - Suspends execution until an interrupt is pending; when IF is 0 the wait ends immediately because no interrupt can be taken.
WFI.pseudo_semantics: if IF == 1 then stall_until(interrupt_pending) else no_wait
WFI.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. WFI is a hint: an implementation may treat it as a no-operation when the wake latency would exceed the remaining time budget.

WFE.description: WFE - Wait For Event - Suspends execution until the event register is set and then clears it; when the register is already set the instruction is a no-operation.
WFE.pseudo_semantics: if event_register == 1 then event_register <- 0 else stall_until(event_register == 1); event_register <- 0
WFE.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. The event register is set by another processor, by an exception entry and by the wake logic, which makes WFE the natural primitive of spin-then-sleep locks.

DVFSHINT.description: DVFSHINT - Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Hint - Advises the power controller to steer toward the operating point selected by MO and IM8; the hint is advisory and may be ignored.
DVFSHINT.pseudo_semantics: hint(MO, target = IM8); no architectural state change
DVFSHINT.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=frequency ceiling 1=voltage floor 2=latency budget; IM8 is the target level in percent of maximum. Hints are advisory and never fault on an unachievable level.

RESET.description: RESET - Reset - Requests the reset scope selected by MO with the reason code IM8, after draining outstanding stores; RESET is only legal at platform-secure level L7.
RESET.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=warm reset 1=cold reset 2=this core only 3=full power cycle; IM8 is a platform reason code recorded in the reset reason register.

INX.description: INX - Input from Extended Port - Reads a 32-bit port word from the 16-bit port number PRT16 into DRG; ports above 0xFF additionally require I/O privilege level 3 and raise #GP otherwise.
INX.pseudo_semantics: if io_privilege < required(PRT16) then #GP; DRG <- port_in(PRT16, 4 bytes)
INX.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. INX is the 16-bit-port companion of the v1 IN at 0x0D, which carries an 8-bit PRT port number and puts the data in ri.

OUTX.description: OUTX - Output to Extended Port - Writes the low 32 bits of SR1 to the 16-bit port number PRT16; ports above 0xFF require I/O privilege level 3 and the write is posted until IOSYNC.
OUTX.pseudo_semantics: if io_privilege < required(PRT16) then #GP; port_out(PRT16, SR1[31:0])
OUTX.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. OUTX completes in the posted-write queue; use IOSYNC when the device must have observed the write before the next instruction executes.

INS.description: INS - Input String - Copies rc elements of 1<<ESZ bytes from port PRT16 to the memory addressed by ri, advancing ri per element in the direction of DF; REP is legal and repeats rc times.
INS.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..rc-1: [ri] <- port_in(PRT16, 1<<ESZ); ri <- ri + dir(DF)*(1<<ESZ)
INS.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. The address register is ri and the repeat count is rc, exactly as for the v1 string instructions; ESZ selects the element width and DF selects the direction.

OUTS.description: OUTS - Output String - Sends rc elements of 1<<ESZ bytes from the memory addressed by ri to port PRT16, advancing ri per element in the direction of DF; REP is legal.
OUTS.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..rc-1: port_out(PRT16, [ri], 1<<ESZ); ri <- ri + dir(DF)*(1<<ESZ)
OUTS.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. OUTS reads from the memory addressed by ri and posts each element to the port; the port number stays constant while ri advances.

IODELAY.description: IODELAY - Input Output Delay - Stalls for IM8 units of the kind selected by MO (core cycles, microseconds or milliseconds) so a slow device can settle between port accesses.
IODELAY.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=core cycles 1=microseconds 2=milliseconds; IODELAY replaces the calibration loops that portable drivers otherwise need between two port writes.

IOSYNC.description: IOSYNC - Input Output Synchronize - Waits until every posted write in the domain selected by MO (all, port I/O only, or memory-mapped I/O only) is complete and visible to the device.
IOSYNC.encoding_notes: escape1 decode space: the mandatory DBI prefix byte 0xF0 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=all posted writes 1=port I/O only 2=MMIO only; IOSYNC is the I/O analogue of SFENCE and never orders ordinary cacheable memory.

SHSTKPUSH.description: SHSTKPUSH - Shadow Stack Push - Pushes SR1 onto the shadow stack managed through cr11, decrementing the shadow stack pointer by four; #SEC when SSE=0 or the shadow stack is full.
SHSTKPUSH.pseudo_semantics: if SSE == 0 then #SEC; ssp <- ssp - 4; [ssp] <- SR1
SHSTKPUSH.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. The shadow stack base lives in cr11 and must be set before SSE is enabled; every push is four bytes wide regardless of the value pushed.

SHSTKPOP.description: SHSTKPOP - Shadow Stack Pop - Pops the top shadow-stack entry into DRG without comparing it and advances the shadow stack pointer by four; #SEC when SSE=0 or the stack is empty.
SHSTKPOP.pseudo_semantics: if SSE == 0 or ssp == shstk_top then #SEC; DRG <- [ssp]; ssp <- ssp + 4
SHSTKPOP.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. Unlike SHSTKRET, SHSTKPOP does not compare the popped value, which makes it the primitive for unwind and exception paths that already validated the return address.

SHSTKRET.description: SHSTKRET - Shadow Stack Return - Pops the shadow-stack entry and the normal return address, compares them and branches only when they match; a mismatch raises #SEC and the branch does not happen.
SHSTKRET.pseudo_semantics: ret_shadow <- [ssp]; ssp <- ssp + 4; ret_norm <- [sp]; sp <- sp + 4; if ret_shadow != ret_norm then #SEC else IP <- ret_norm
SHSTKRET.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. SHSTKRET is the shadow-stack-checked counterpart of the v1 RET and the return form the compiler emits when SSE=1.

ENDBR.description: ENDBR - End Branch - Marks the instruction as a legal indirect-branch target of the type selected by MO so hardware CFI accepts indirect control transfers that land here and raises #SEC everywhere else.
ENDBR.pseudo_semantics: landing_pad[IP] <- MO; no register or flag change
ENDBR.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. MO: 0=indirect jump target 1=indirect call target 2=return target 3=any indirect target. ENDBR is a legal landing pad only when the branch type matches the recorded marker.

SSBB.description: SSBB - Shadow Stack Branch Barrier - Records the current shadow-stack pointer as a control-flow-integrity barrier that permits at most IM8 further popped entries; exceeding the allowance raises #SEC.
SSBB.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero.SSBB gives coarse-grained CFI over long-lived frames without a shadow-stack entry per call: a barrier records the allowed pop depth and later returns are checked against it.

SPECBAR.description: SPECBAR - Speculation Barrier - Discards speculative state up to the strength in SPB so that no later speculative path can observe state created before the barrier; architecture state is unchanged.
SPECBAR.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. SPB: 0=light 1=standard 2=strong 3=full serializing; SPB 4..15 raise #UDI. SPECBAR stops speculative execution but unlike MFENCE it does not order architectural memory operations.

IBPB.description: IBPB - Indirect Branch Predictor Barrier - Invalidates the branch-prediction state of the current address space so that code entered afterwards cannot reuse predictions trained by the previous one.
IBPB.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. IBPB is issued on a context switch into a less trusted address space; it is expensive, so the OS should batch it with the switch itself.

STIBP.description: STIBP - Single Thread Indirect Branch Predictors - Switches the current hardware thread to single-thread branch prediction so its history is no longer shared with the sibling thread of an SMT core.
STIBP.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. STIBP stays in force until the thread is rescheduled into a context that shares its address space with the sibling thread.

ENCLS.description: ENCLS - Enclave Supervisor Leaf - Executes the enclave management leaf selected by DRG with arguments in SR1 and SR2, reporting success in CF and the leaf error code in ZF; requires level L7.
ENCLS.pseudo_semantics: if level != L7 then #GP; CF <- exec_leaf(DRG, args = (SR1, SR2)); ZF <- leaf_error
ENCLS.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. DRG selects the leaf: 0=create 1=add page 2=initialize 3=remove 4=resume; arguments follow the leaf table in SR1 and SR2 and errors are reported in CF and ZF, not by fault.

ENCLU.description: ENCLU - Enclave User Leaf - Executes the enclave leaf selected by DRG inside an initialized enclave and returns success in CF with the leaf error in ZF; outside an enclave it raises #SEC.
ENCLU.pseudo_semantics: if !in_enclave then #SEC; CF <- exec_leaf(DRG, args = (SR1, SR2)); ZF <- leaf_error
ENCLU.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. DRG selects the leaf: 0=enter 1=exit 2=read report 3=verify report; ENCLU is the only enclave instruction that runs inside an enclave, and it still requires the platform-secure level number.

ENCLV.description: ENCLV - Enclave Virtualization Leaf - Executes the enclave virtualization leaf selected by DRG so a hypervisor can back enclaves with virtual memory; requires level L7 and a hypervisor context.
ENCLV.pseudo_semantics: if level != L7 or VME == 1 then #GP; CF <- exec_vleaf(DRG, args = (SR1, SR2))
ENCLV.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. DRG selects the leaf: 0=virtualize 1=resume 2=migrate; ENCLV must run with VME=0 so an enclave cannot virtualize itself.

ATTEST.description: ATTEST - Attestation Report - Builds the attestation report of type DRG over the enclave measurement into the buffer at SR1 and signs it with the platform attestation key; CF reports success.
ATTEST.pseudo_semantics: report <- build_report(type = DRG, measurement = enclave_state); sign(report, platform_key); [SR1] <- report; CF <- valid(report)
ATTEST.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. 0x0 is a reserved nibble; it must decode as zero. DRG is the report type (0=local 1=remote 2=quote) and SR1 the 64-byte aligned output buffer; the signing key never leaves the platform key store.

ZEROIZE.description: ZEROIZE - Zeroize - Overwrites SR2 elements of 1<<ESZ bytes starting at [SR1] with zeros using non-allocating stores that cannot be reordered or elided, then invalidates those lines from the caches.
ZEROIZE.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..SR2-1: [(SR1 + i*(1<<ESZ))] <- 0; invalidate_lines(SR1, SR2*(1<<ESZ))
ZEROIZE.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. ESZ selects the element width as 1<<ESZ bytes; the stores are non-allocating, cannot be elided by the optimiser and are followed by a cache invalidate of the same range.

CTCOPY.description: CTCOPY - Constant Time Copy - Copies DRG bytes from [SR2] to [SR1] with a data-independent access sequence, no early exit and no branch on the values, which makes it safe for secret material.
CTCOPY.pseudo_semantics: for i in 0..DRG-1: [(SR1+i)] <- [(SR2+i)]; timing <- f(DRG) only
CTCOPY.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. DRG is the byte count, SR1 the destination and SR2 the source; the timing depends only on DRG, never on the copied values.

RDPKRU.description: RDPKRU - Read Protection Key Rights - Writes the current protection-key rights word into DRG with two permission bits per key and sets PKE so that key checking is enabled.
RDPKRU.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. Two bits per key: 00=no access 01=read and write 10=read only 11=no access, for keys 0-15 in the low 32 bits of the rights word.

WRPKRU.description: WRPKRU - Write Protection Key Rights - Replaces the protection-key rights word from SR1, sets PKE and serializes the pipeline so later accesses use the new rights.
WRPKRU.pseudo_semantics: if rights_target_unallocated_key(SR1) then #SEC; PKRU <- SR1; PKE <- 1; serialize()
WRPKRU.encoding_notes: xtu decode space: the mandatory XTU enable prefix byte 0xF5 precedes OPC and the declared length counts OPC plus operands only, so the encoded size is length+1 bytes. WRPKRU is serializing because the new rights apply to every load and store after it; assigning rights to a key that MKEYALLOC never handed out raises #SEC.

PUSH ra.description: Push ra - Pushes the value of the ra register onto the stack

POP ra.description: Pop ra - Pops the top value from the stack into the ra register

PUSH rb.description: Push rb - Pushes the value of the rb register onto the stack

POP rb.description: Pop rb - Pops the top value from the stack into the rb register

PUSH rc.description: Push rc - Pushes the value of the rc register onto the stack

POP rc.description: Pop rc - Pops the top value from the stack into the rc register

PUSH rd.description: Push rd - Pushes the value of the rd register onto the stack

POP rd.description: Pop rd - Pops the top value from the stack into the rd register

PUSH ri.description: Push ri - Pushes the value of the ri register onto the stack

POP ri.description: Pop ri - Pops the top value from the stack into the ri register

PUSH bp.description: Push bp - Pushes the value of the bp register onto the stack

POP bp.description: Pop bp - Pops the top value from the stack into the bp register

ENTR.description: Enter Routine - Sets up a new stack frame by moving the current stack pointer (sp) into the base pointer (bp) register.

LEAV.description: Leave Routine - Restores the stack pointer (sp) to the value stored in the base pointer (bp) register.

LOOP.description: LOOP - Loop - Micro-coded as a decrement of the counter register followed by a conditional branch taken while the internal zero result is clear; the micro-sequencer writes the arithmetic flags only to its internal copy so the architectural flags are preserved.

LOOPZ.description: LOOPZ - Loop While Zero - The micro-sequence saves the architectural flags, decrements the counter into the temporary t0 and writes it back, skips out when the counter reached zero, restores the flags and then branches on the restored ZF, so LOOPZ decrements without disturbing the comparison that set ZF.

LOOPNZ.description: LOOPNZ - Loop While Not Zero - Same micro-sequence as LOOPZ but the final conditional branch tests the restored ZF for clear, so the loop continues while the counter is nonzero and ZF is zero.

MOVS.description: MOVS - Move String - The micro-sequence shown is the dword implementation: load from the source pointer, store through the destination pointer, advance both pointers and, under a REP prefix, decrement rc and loop; the decrement and branch steps run only when a REP prefix is present and byte or word element sizes use the LSU sized-access micro-operations instead of LD and ST.

CMPS.description: CMPS - Compare String - The micro-sequence loads both elements into temporaries, compares them to set ZF, CF, OF and NF, advances both pointers and repeats while rc is nonzero; with REP the loop also exits as soon as the comparison reports equality, and byte or word sizes use the LSU sized-access micro-operations.

SCAS.description: SCAS - Compare String Accumulator - The micro-sequence loads the destination element, compares the accumulator ra against it and advances rd; with REP the loop exits as soon as the comparison reports equality, which is the length-of-string idiom.

STOS.description: STOS - Store String - The micro-sequence stores the accumulator through the destination pointer, advances rd and repeats while rc is nonzero; the block-fill idiom is a REP-prefixed STOS of an immediate count.

LODS.description: LODS - Load String - The micro-sequence loads from the source pointer into the accumulator ra, advances ri and repeats while rc is nonzero.

DIVMOD.description: DIVMOD - Divide With Remainder - The micro-sequence is the restoring form for a core without a divide unit: it clears the quotient, subtracts the divisor from the running remainder until it is smaller, then writes the quotient to DRG and the remainder back to SR1; the hardware divide unit performs the same function in a single pass.

MULH.description: MULH - Multiply High Unsigned - The micro-sequence is a single v1 MUL with the low half aimed at the temporary t0 and the high half aimed at DRG, which shows that MULH is the same multiplier datapath with the high half as the architectural destination.

ISQRT.description: ISQRT - Integer Square Root - The micro-sequence uses the classic odd-number subtraction loop: starting from the odd series 1, 3, 5 and so on it subtracts each odd number from a working copy of the source while that remains possible and counts the iterations, which is exactly the floor of the square root.

RETFAR.description: RETFAR - Return Far - The micro-sequence loads the return address from the top of the stack, advances the stack pointer past it, adds the MO argument words and jumps through the return register, which is the same sequence the hardware performs without the temporary.

SATADD.description: SATADD - Saturating Add Signed - The micro-sequence adds into a temporary, and when the addition overflowed it selects 0x80000000 for a negative overflow or 0x7FFFFFFF for a positive overflow instead of the wrapped sum; VF records that the clamp happened.

GRAYD.description: GRAYD - Gray Decode - The micro-sequence applies the five shift and exclusive-or steps with shifts of one, two, four, eight and sixteen, which converts a reflected Gray code word back to binary; the field width comes from ESZ.

IRET.description: Interrupt Return - Micro-coded as POP rd, POPF, JMPR rd: the interrupt frame holds the return IP at [sp] and the saved flags at [sp+4], so the sequencer pops the return address into rd first, restores the flags second and then jumps through rd. Popping the flags first would load the return address into the flag register and return to the flags word, which is why the order is fixed by the frame layout.

MAP.description: Map Page - Micro-coded as PGWALK, IMM, OR, ST, INVLPG: the walk locates the page-table entry, the immediate supplies PRESENT plus the rights nibble decoded from MO, the OR merges the aligned physical base, the store writes the entry and INVLPG drops the cached translation of that one page. INVTLB would over-flush the whole address space for a single mapping.

SHSTKPUSH.description: Shadow Stack Push - Micro-coded as RDCR, IMM, SUB, ST, WRCR: reads the shadow stack pointer from cr11, decrements it by four, stores the link and writes the pointer back, so the push never touches the normal stack.

LDM.description: Load Multiple - Micro-coded as a thirteen-byte loop body (LD, ADD, CMP, INC, JNZ) executed SR2+1 times with r0 holding the element width 1<<ESZ: load DRG, advance the address, compare the register just loaded against the last register SR2, and only then increment and branch. Comparing after the increment would run one register past SR2.

VMEXIT.description: Virtual Machine Exit - Micro-coded as RDCR, LD, VMSTORE, IMM, AND, WRCR: read the control block from cr8, take the exit reason from its +12 field into DRG, save the guest register block over offsets 0..11 so the two never overlap, then clear VME in cr8 before control returns to L5.

SAL.description: Shift Arithmetic Left - Alias for SHL instruction.

LI.description: LI - Load Immediate - Loads the full 32-bit immediate I32 into DRG by emitting the single 6-byte IMM instruction.

MOVI.description: MOVI - Move Immediate Byte - Loads the 8-bit immediate IM8 into DRG with zero extension, which is the 3-byte IMMB form.

CMPI.description: CMPI - Compare Immediate - Reloads IM8 into the temporary t0 and compares it with SR1, setting ZF, CF, OF and NF from SR1 minus IM8; t0 is clobbered.

TST.description: TST - Test - Ands DRG with SR1 into the temporary t0 only to produce ZF, CF, OF and NF, leaving DRG unchanged; t0 is clobbered.

BEQ.description: BEQ - Branch If Equal - Alias for JCND with CC=0, so it jumps when ZF is set; the encoding is the 4-byte conditional relative jump.

BNE.description: BNE - Branch If Not Equal - Alias for JCND with CC=1, so it jumps when ZF is clear.

BGT.description: BGT - Branch If Greater Signed - Alias for JCND with CC=11, so it jumps when ZF is clear and NF equals OF.

BLT.description: BLT - Branch If Less Signed - Alias for JCND with CC=8, so it jumps when NF differs from OF.

BGE.description: BGE - Branch If Greater Or Equal Signed - Alias for JCND with CC=9, so it jumps when NF equals OF.

BLE.description: BLE - Branch If Less Or Equal Signed - Alias for JCND with CC=10, so it jumps when ZF is set or NF differs from OF.

JMP32.description: JMP32 - Jump 32 - Alias for the 5-byte JMPRELL 32-bit relative jump; the assembler resolves a full 32-bit target symbol into the O32 displacement.

CALL32.description: CALL32 - Call 32 - Alias for the 5-byte CALLREL 32-bit relative call; the assembler resolves a full 32-bit target symbol into the O32 displacement and the return address is the following instruction.

PUSHA.description: PUSHA - Push All Registers - Pushes ra, rb, rc, rd, ri and bp in that order using six 2-byte PUSH instructions; sp is not saved because the pushes themselves define the frame.

POPA.description: POPA - Pop All Registers - Pops bp, ri, rd, rc, rb and ra in that order, which is the exact reverse of PUSHA so a save and restore pair rebuilds the register file.

PUSHR.description: PUSHR - Push Register List - Pushes every general register whose bit is set in the 32-bit mask I32, lowest register number first; each selected register costs one 2-byte PUSH, so the expansion length is two bytes times the number of selected registers.

operands: {rn} for every n where I32[n] == 1, highest first

POPR.description: POPR - Pop Register List - Pops every general register whose bit is set in the 32-bit mask I32, highest register number first so it undoes the matching PUSHR; each selected register costs one 2-byte POP.

MEMCPY.description: MEMCPY - Memory Copy - Copies SR2 dwords from address SR1 to address DRG by loading rd, ri and rc and running a REP-prefixed dword MOVS; rd, ri and rc are clobbered and the total is three 2-byte moves plus a 2-byte REP prefix and a 2-byte MOVS.

MEMSET.description: MEMSET - Memory Set - Fills SR2 bytes starting at address DRG with the low byte of SR1 by loading rd, ra and rc and running a REP-prefixed byte STOS; rd, ra and rc are clobbered.

ZEXT8.description: ZEXT8 - Zero Extend Byte - Alias for ZEXT with ESZ=0, zero-extending the low byte of SR1 into DRG.

ZEXT16.description: ZEXT16 - Zero Extend Word - Alias for ZEXT with ESZ=1, zero-extending the low halfword of SR1 into DRG.

SEXT8.description: SEXT8 - Sign Extend Byte - Alias for SEXT with ESZ=0, sign-extending the low byte of SR1 into DRG.

SEXT16.description: SEXT16 - Sign Extend Word - Alias for SEXT with ESZ=1, sign-extending the low halfword of SR1 into DRG.

NOT32.description: NOT32 - Not 32-bit - Alias for the 2-byte NOT instruction, which complements all 32 bits of SR1 into DRG.

SWAP16.description: SWAP16 - Swap Halfword Bytes - Alias for BSWAP with ESZ=1, exchanging the two bytes of the low halfword of SR1 into DRG, which is the 16-bit network order conversion.

NOPN.description: NOPN - No Operation N Bytes - Emits exactly IM8 bytes of padding by picking one NOP or a combination of NOP2 through NOP15; the entry records the single byte NOP case and the emitted size always equals IM8.

ADD3.description: ADD3 - Three Operand Add - Alias for the 3-byte ADD, which already writes SR1 plus SR2 into a distinct destination register without destroying either source.

MULADD.description: MULADD - Multiply Accumulate - Alias for the 3-byte MADD, which adds the signed product of SR1 and SR2 into DRG.

MOD.description: MOD - Modulus - Alias for the 3-byte REM, which writes the unsigned remainder of SR1 divided by SR2 into DRG.

DIVU.description: DIVU - Divide Unsigned - Copies SR1 into the temporary t0 and divides it by SR2 with DIVMOD so that only the quotient in DRG is kept and SR1 survives; t0 is clobbered.

MIN.description: MIN - Minimum Signed - Alias for the 3-byte MINS signed minimum of SR1 and SR2.

MAX.description: MAX - Maximum Signed - Alias for the 3-byte MAXS signed maximum of SR1 and SR2.

LSHIFT.description: LSHIFT - Variable Left Shift - Alias for the 3-byte SHLX, which shifts SR1 left by the register count SR2 without touching any flag.

RSHIFT.description: RSHIFT - Variable Right Shift - Alias for the 3-byte SHRX, which shifts SR1 right logically by the register count SR2 without touching any flag.

CLZ32.description: CLZ32 - Count Leading Zeros 32 - Alias for CLZ with ESZ=2, counting the leading zero bits of the full 32-bit SR1.

POPC.description: POPC - Population Count - Alias for POPCNT with ESZ=2, counting the one bits of the full 32-bit SR1.

LEA32.description: LEA32 - Load Effective Address 32 - Emits LEASC with a scale of one and a zero displacement, so DRG receives SR1 plus SR2 without any memory access.

ADDR.description: ADDR - Scaled Address - Emits LEASC with an explicit scale and a zero displacement, so DRG receives SR1 plus SR2 times SCL; the scale is a multiplier exactly as the v1 LEASC implementation defines it.

LOG2.description: LOG2 - Logarithm Base Two - Alias for BSR with ESZ=2, writing the index of the highest set bit, that is the floor of log2, of SR1 into DRG.

BITREV.description: BITREV - Bit Reverse 32 - Alias for BREV with ESZ=2, reversing the bit order of the full 32-bit SR1 into DRG.

SETIF.description: SETIF - Set If Condition - Alias for SETCC with a full dword destination, writing 1 into DRG when the condition CC holds and 0 otherwise.

BRKIF.description: BRKIF - Break If Condition - Jumps over the following BRK with a two-byte conditional skip when the condition is false, so BRK executes only when CC holds; the 4-byte JCND plus the 1-byte BRK make the 5-byte expansion.

LOADI.description: LOADI - Load Indirect - Emits LD with a zero displacement, loading the 32-bit word at address SR1 into DRG.

STOREI.description: STOREI - Store Indirect - Emits ST with a zero displacement, storing the 32-bit DRG at address SR1; note the v1 ST operand order of value then base.

XCHG8.description: XCHG8 - Exchange Low Bytes - Swaps the low byte of DRG with the low byte of SR1 and leaves every other bit of both registers unchanged, using two BEXT field extractions into t0 and t1 followed by two BINS insertions.

XCHG16.description: XCHG16 - Exchange Low Halfwords - Swaps the low halfword of DRG with the low halfword of SR1 and leaves every other bit of both registers unchanged, using two 16-bit BEXT extractions and two BINS insertions.

REX.description: Register Extension Prefix - if any bits in the REX prefix are set, the instruction extends that register fields to allow access 0-15 -> 16-31 of the 32-bit general-purpose registers, or f0-f15 -> d0-d15 of the

BRH_H.description: Branch Hint Prefix - provides a hint to the processor about the likely direction of a branch instruction to optimize instruction pipelining. Must be used before a branch instruction, or the hint is ignored. It modifies the BH bit in the instruction to indicate whether the branch is likely to be taken or not taken.

LOCK.description: Lock Prefix - ensures exclusive access to shared memory in multi-processor environments by preventing other processors from accessing the memory location being modified until the operation is complete.

ISL.description: Instruction Specific Length Prefix - specifies the length of the instruction in bytes, from 4 to 16 bytes. Values 0-3 are invalid. This prefix may improve performance by allowing the processor to decode the instruction faster.

XTU.description: Extended Instruction Unit Prefix - the following instruction is executed in XTU.

BMU.description: Big Math Unit Prefix - the following instruction is executed in BMU.

DBI.description: Double Byte Instruction Prefix - escape byte to allow the use of 2-byte instructions.

TBI.description: Triple Byte Instruction Prefix - escape byte to allow the use of 3-byte instructions.

EVX.description: Extended Vector Prefix - supplies the destination mask register (KDG) and the vector-length code (VL) for the next vector instruction. A mask-cleared lane is zeroed by default; the PRED prefix selects the merging form. Legal only on an instruction whose can_use_with_prefixes lists EVX.

OPSZ.description: Operand Size Override Prefix - the first payload nibble is the source element size and the second the destination element size, both from the ESZ code table. Used by the block transfers of the bmu space and by LDM, STM, LDP, STP, LDX, STX, LDSX and LDZX of the memory family.

MEMO.description: Memory Ordering Prefix - the first payload nibble is the ordering class (0 RLX, 1 ACQ, 2 REL, 3 ACQ_REL, 4 SEQ_CST) and the second a cache hint from the CH table. A prefix may strengthen but never weaken the ordering class encoded in the instruction.

REP.description: Repeat Prefix - repeats the following string or block instruction. The first payload nibble is the repeat mode (0 count in rc, 1 until ZF, 2 until ZF clear, 3 fixed count) and the second the counter width and direction. Legal only on the string family (MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, LODS, MOVSN, STOSN) and on INS and OUTS.

PRED.description: Predication Prefix - names the predicate register and the merge/zero/disable mode for an instruction that has no EVX form. MO bit 0 = 0 zeroes a mask-cleared lane and MO bit 0 = 1 merges the old destination value; MO bit 1 = 1 suppresses the whole operation when the mask is empty.

SEC.description: Security Prefix - the first payload nibble is the speculation-barrier strength (SPB) that applies to the following instruction and the second the protection-key index the access is checked against. A key denial raises #SEC at the memory access.

CIU.description: Enable Complex Instruction Unit Prefix - the following instruction is executed by the CIU. The byte carries no payload and is both the enable prefix and the mandatory escape byte of the ciu decode space; the CIE status flag mirrors the enable state.

FMT.description: Floating-Point Format Prefix - overrides the FPF format and the RM rounding mode of the following floating-point instruction. It exists for the forms that carry no FPF or RM nibble of their own (the fused multiply-add family and every BMU transcendental form), where the prefix override wins over the in-instruction default.

ILL.description: Illegal byte, not a prefix - 0xFF is permanently illegal in every decode space and at every privilege level and always raises #UDI. It exists so that a fill pattern, a wiped key or a corrupted opcode stream traps deterministically instead of decoding as a valid opcode, and a v2 CPU must never assign it a meaning.

order_notes.canonical_order: ISL, BRH_H, LOCK, REP, SEC, PRED, EVX, OPSZ, FMT, MEMO, REX, exactly one space escape (XTU, BMU, CIU, DBI or TBI), OPC
order_notes.v1_compatibility: The v1 relative order is preserved verbatim: ISL before BRH_H before LOCK before REX before the space escape before OPC. Every v1 prefix sequence therefore keeps its meaning and its byte order; the seven new two-byte prefixes take their places inside the existing groups.
order_notes.rationale: ISL comes first so the length hint reaches the IGL stage before anything else; BRH_H stays next because the branch predictor consumes it at decode; LOCK, REP and SEC order the semantic modifiers; PRED and EVX bind the mask before the vector operands are read; OPSZ, FMT and MEMO carry element type and cache policy; REX is honoured last so that register-extension bits are known only after every other modifier has been decoded; the space escape selects the opcode table and must be the last byte before OPC.
order_notes.decoder_rule: A decoder accepts any subset of declared, individually legal prefixes in any physical order, but the canonical order above is what the assembler emits and what the encoding examples show. Only the space escape has a hard position: it must be the last byte before OPC, because the opcode table is chosen from it.

space_escape_group.note: Exactly one space-selecting escape byte may appear per instruction.
members: TBI (0xF1) selects escape2, which is reserved and holds no instruction

prefixes.max_size_unit: bytes of prefix total, not prefix count
prefixes.max_size_notes: At most four prefix bytes may precede an opcode: one four-byte combination such as ISL+BRH_H+LOCK+REX, or two two-byte prefixes, or one two-byte prefix plus two one-byte prefixes. A fifth prefix byte raises #UDI. A space escape counted in the prefix stream consumes the same budget.

illegal_combinations.combination: REX twice: two register-extension prefixes in one instruction
illegal_combinations.reason: Two REX bytes are ambiguous because the field extension would be applied twice.

illegal_combinations.combination: LOCK without a memory destination: LOCK on a register-only instruction, on a branch, or on an FPU or vector op
illegal_combinations.reason: LOCK only orders an atomic read-modify-write of one memory location.
A repeated string instruction is not a single atomic memory operation.

illegal_combinations.combination: LOCK on a multi-element transfer (LDM, STM, LDP, STP) or on any block transfer that can touch more than one cache line
illegal_combinations.reason: LOCK is defined only for one aligned atomic location of at most 8 bytes; XBEGIN covers the multi-element case.

illegal_combinations.combination: EVX or PRED on an instruction that is not a vector or mask operation
illegal_combinations.reason: Both prefixes only name predicate registers and vector length, which an integer, FPU or system instruction cannot consume.

illegal_combinations.combination: FMT on an integer, memory, system or vector instruction
