illegal_combinations.reason: FMT carries FPF and RM, which only a floating-point or BMU form consumes.

illegal_combinations.combination: ILL (0xFF) anywhere: before an opcode, inside an operand stream, or as the only byte of a stream
Two space-selecting escapes in one instruction (for example XTU with BMU, or DBI with CIU)
illegal_combinations.reason: The opcode table is selected by exactly one escape byte, and two escapes name two tables for one opcode.
The escape2 space is reserved and holds no instruction in v2.0.
The prefix budget of max_size is four bytes.

illegal_combinations.combination: A prefix that the instruction does not list in can_use_with_prefixes, for example MEMO on a branch or REP on an ALU op
illegal_combinations.reason: The prefix has no meaning for that instruction, and accepting it would silently do nothing while suggesting otherwise.
Two length hints for one instruction are contradictory.

illegal_combinations.combination: SEC whose PKEY names a key outside the current rights word
illegal_combinations.reason: The encoding is legal; the access it guards is not.
illegal_combinations.behaviour: #SEC at the memory access, not at decode

legal_on.REX: every base-space instruction and every escaped-space instruction that names a register field (all three parts list it)
legal_on.BRH_H: the branch family: v1 JZ, JC, JO, JN, JNZ, JNC, JNO, JNN, JL, JGE, JA, JBE, JLE, JAG and A_core JCND, JCNDL, LOOP, LOOPZ, LOOPNZ, LOOPL, LOOPZL, LOOPNZL
legal_on.LOCK: the atomic family (LDLK, STLK, CAS, AMOSWAP, AMOADD, AMOSUB, AMOAND, AMOOR, AMOXOR, AMOMIN, AMOMAX, AMOMINU, AMOMAXU, AMOFADD, AMOFAND, AMOFOR, AMOFXOR, AMOFSWAP) and LDSTVAL/STSTVAL
legal_on.ISL: any instruction of 4 to 15 bytes; it is a length hint with no architectural effect
legal_on.XTU: every instruction in the xtu decode space (SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP, SHSTKRET, ENDBR, SSBB, SPECBAR, IBPB, STIBP, ENCLS, ENCLU, ENCLV, ATTEST, ZEROIZE, CTCOPY, RDPKRU, WRPKRU); it is that space's mandatory escape byte
legal_on.BMU: every instruction in the bmu decode space; it is that space's mandatory escape byte
legal_on.DBI: every instruction in the escape1 decode space (power 0x00-0x03, memory_management 0x10, io_ext 0x20); it is that space's mandatory escape byte
legal_on.TBI: nothing in v2.0, because the escape2 space is reserved
legal_on.EVX: the vector and mask instructions that list it: VLDR, VSTR, VLDRS, VSTRS, VLDRX, VSTRX, VLDREP, VLOADM, VSTOREM and the vector arithmetic, logic, shift, compare and conversion families
legal_on.OPSZ: the block and pair transfers that list it: LDM, STM, LDP, STP, LDX, STX, LDSX, LDZX, LDNT, STNT, and the bmu big-integer forms
legal_on.MEMO: every memory-touching instruction that lists it: the memory and atomic family, the fences, the FPU loads and stores, the vector memory family, the string family and the power family
legal_on.REP: the string family (MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, LODS, MOVSN, STOSN) and INS/OUTS
legal_on.PRED: the vector instructions that list PRED and the masked memory forms VLOADM and VSTOREM
legal_on.SEC: the security family, the shadow-stack calls, the fences and any memory access that must be checked against a protection key
legal_on.CIU: every crypto instruction; it is both the enable prefix and the ciu space escape byte
legal_on.FMT: the floating-point instructions that list it (the fused forms and every BMU transcendental form)

OPC.description: Opcode field, specifies the operation to be performed by the processor.

SOP.description: Sub-Opcode field, specifies a variant of the main opcode operation.

ISL.description: Instruction Size Length field, specifies the length of the instruction in bytes.

GB1.description: General encode bit, used for instructions that have a 1-bit immediate value.

GB2.description: General encode bit, used for instructions that have a 2-bit immediate value.

DRG.description: Destination Register field, specifies the register where the result of the operation is stored.

SR1.description: Source Register 1 field, specifies the first source register for the operation.

SR2.description: Source Register 2 field, specifies the second source register for the operation.

SR3.description: Source Register 3 field, specifies the third source register for the operation.

DRC.description: Destination Control Register field, specifies the control register where the result of the operation is stored.

SRC.description: Source Control Register field, specifies the source control register for the operation.

DFR.description: Destination Floating-point Register field, specifies the floating-point register where the result of the operation is stored.

SF1.description: Source Floating-point Register 1 field, specifies the first source floating-point register for the operation.

SF2.description: Source Floating-point Register 2 field, specifies the second source floating-point register for the operation.

SF3.description: Source Floating-point Register 3 field, specifies the third source floating-point register for the operation.

IM8.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

I16.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

I32.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

OF8.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

O16.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

O32.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

AD8.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

A16.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

A32.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

SCL.description: Scale field, specifies the scaling factor for indexed addressing.

PRT.description: Port field, specifies the I/O port to be accessed.

CR.description: Control Register field, specifies the system control register to be accessed.

CC.description: Condition-code selector: one of the 16 codes of the conditions table (0 EQ, 1 NE, 2 CS/LO, 3 CC/HS, 4 MI, 5 PL, 6 VS, 7 VC, 8 LT, 9 GE, 10 LE, 11 GT, 12 HI, 13 LS, 14 AL, 15 NV). Consumed by JCND, JCNDL, SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC, TSTCC, VCMP and FSEL.

ESZ.description: Element/operand size code: 0 BYTE, 1 WORD, 2 DWORD, 3 QWORD; 4-15 reserved and raise #UDI. An instruction that cannot operate on 64-bit elements (every integer-core user) reserves code 3 and raises #UDI for it, while the vector unit uses all four codes.

MO.description: Modifier code, instruction specific: ordering class for the atomics and fences, saturation class for arithmetic, destination width for CVTSZ, accuracy class for the BMU transcendentals, size class for MAP and PROTECT. Every instruction that carries MO documents its own code table in its description or encoding_notes, and a code it does not define raises #UDI.

CH.description: Cache and eviction hint code: 0 T0, 1 T1, 2 T2, 3 non-temporal, 4 last-level-only, 5-15 reserved and ignored. Used by PREFETCH, PREFETCHW and CLZERO, and as the second payload nibble of the MEMO prefix.

RP.description: Repeat/pattern mode code: the first REP payload nibble is the repeat mode (0 count in rc, 1 until ZF, 2 until ZF clear, 3 fixed count) and the second is the counter width and direction. v2.0 carries RP only inside the REP prefix (0xFA); no instruction format contains RP as an operand field.

SPB.description: Speculation-barrier strength code: 0 light, 1 standard, 2 strong, 3 sequentially consistent for MFENCE, LFENCE and SFENCE, or fully serializing for SPECBAR; 4-15 raise #UDI. Also the first payload nibble of the SEC prefix.

PKEY.description: Protection-key index 0-15. MKEYALLOC hands out indices 0-15, MAP and PROTECT attach one to a mapping, RDPKRU and WRPKRU read and write the rights word, and the SEC prefix carries a key index so a memory access can be checked against it. No instruction format in v2.0 uses PKEY as a standalone operand field.

FPF.description: Floating-point format code: 0 F16, 1 BF16, 2 F32, 3 F64; 4-15 reserved and raise #UDI. Used by every FPU instruction and by the BMU transcendental forms; the FMT prefix carries the same code as an override.

RM.description: Rounding mode: 0 round to nearest even (RN), 1 round toward zero (RZ), 2 round toward +infinity (RP), 3 round toward -infinity (RM); 4-15 reserved and raise #UDI. The FPU forms carry RM in the instruction and the fused forms take it from the FMT prefix.

VL.description: Vector length code: 0 128 bits, 1 256 bits, 2 512 bits, 3 1024 bits; 4-15 reserved. In v2.0 the register file is 256 bits wide, so code 1 is the only value the core accepts and codes 0, 2 and 3 raise #UDI. The active element count of a vector instruction is architectural state set by VSETVL and reported through the VLE status flag, not a per-instruction operand, so VL appears only in the EVX prefix payload (0xF7) and no v2.0 instruction format contains VL.

VDG.description: Destination vector register, v0-v31. The REX bit for VDG extends the 4-bit index by 16.

VF3.description: Source vector register 3, v0-v31. A form with three vector sources needs three distinct tokens, so VF1, VF2 and VF3 never repeat inside one format.

KDG.description: Destination mask (predicate) register. Codes 0-7 name k0-k7, the implemented predicate file; codes 8-15 are reserved and raise #UDI. KDG may name k0, but k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask, so a write to it through KDG is discarded and only k1-k7 change.

KM1.description: Source mask register 1: a 32-bit predicate register, one bit per lane. Codes 0-7 name k0-k7 and codes 8-15 are reserved and raise #UDI. k0 named here reads all ones for the active mask length, which is no masking; k1-k7 read their stored bits. KM1 is the first of at most two mask sources, and a second mask source must use KM2.

KM2.description: Source mask register 2, a token distinct from KM1 so that a three-operand mask instruction such as KAND or KTEST never repeats a field token. Codes 0-7 name k0-k7; 8-15 are reserved and raise #UDI. k0 named here reads all ones for the active mask length, exactly as in KM1.

MSI.description: Model-specific register index: 0x00-0x3F implemented (64 MSRs), 0x40-0xFF reserved and raising #GP. Used by RDMSR and WRMSR.

SOP8.description: 8-bit sub-opcode for a decode space, reserved for an escape-space family whose variants outgrow the 16 values of SOP. No v2.0 instruction uses SOP8: the escape1 and xtu spaces group their variants in the 4-bit SOP nibble, and the bmu and ciu spaces give every mnemonic its own opcode byte.

SEG.description: Selector or segment-like space identifier: the 16-bit address-space identifier that INVTLB matches, and the translation context that INVEPT names.

PRT16.description: Extended I/O port number, 0x0000-0xFFFF, used by INX, OUTX, INS and OUTS. The v1 PRT field stays the 8-bit port number of IN and OUT.

#SYS.description: System call gate trap interrupt vector.

~IOMMU.description: IOMMU translation and fault-report interrupt vector.

~DMA.description: DMA completion and error interrupt vector.

#SI0.description: Software interrupt vector #SI0, raised by INT 48 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI1.description: Software interrupt vector #SI1, raised by INT 49 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI2.description: Software interrupt vector #SI2, raised by INT 50 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI3.description: Software interrupt vector #SI3, raised by INT 51 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI4.description: Software interrupt vector #SI4, raised by INT 52 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI5.description: Software interrupt vector #SI5, raised by INT 53 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI6.description: Software interrupt vector #SI6, raised by INT 54 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI7.description: Software interrupt vector #SI7, raised by INT 55 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI8.description: Software interrupt vector #SI8, raised by INT 56 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI9.description: Software interrupt vector #SI9, raised by INT 57 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI10.description: Software interrupt vector #SI10, raised by INT 58 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI11.description: Software interrupt vector #SI11, raised by INT 59 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI12.description: Software interrupt vector #SI12, raised by INT 60 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI13.description: Software interrupt vector #SI13, raised by INT 61 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI14.description: Software interrupt vector #SI14, raised by INT 62 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

#SI15.description: Software interrupt vector #SI15, raised by INT 63 or by a device driver that multiplexes its own work onto this vector.

ZF.description: Zero Flag - Set if the result of an operation is zero.

CF.description: Carry Flag - Set if an arithmetic operation generates a carry out or borrow into the most significant bit.

OF.description: Overflow Flag - Set if an arithmetic operation results in a signed overflow.

NF.description: Negative Flag - Set if the result of an operation is negative.

DF.description: Direction Flag - Controls the direction of string operations (0 = increment, 1 = decrement).

FLZ.description: Floating-Point Divide-by-Zero Flag - Set if a floating-point division by zero occurs.

FLO.description: Floating-Point Overflow Flag - Set if a floating-point operation results in an overflow.

FLV.description: Floating-Point Result Inaccurate Flag - Set if a floating-point operation results in an inaccurate result.

IF.description: Interrupt Flag - Controls the enabling and disabling of maskable interrupts.

AF.description: Auxiliary Flag - Set if a BCD or nibble operation generated a carry out of, or a borrow into, bit 3 of the byte (the carry between the two packed BCD digits). Read by ADDBCD, SUBBCD, CMPBCD and NEGBCD.

PF.description: Parity Flag - Set if the low 8 bits of the result contain an even number of one bits. Written by the parity forms; PARCNT reports the count itself in a register.

VF.description: Saturation/Valid Flag - Set when the written result is not the exact mathematical result: a saturating or clamping operation hit its bound, a narrowing conversion lost bits, a packed BCD digit was invalid, or a vector lane clamped. VF is the single loss-of-information flag of the integer and vector units.

BE.description: Big Endian Flag - Set if the processor is using a big-endian byte order.

AC.description: Alignment Check Flag - Enables alignment checking for memory accesses.

TF.description: Trap/Step Flag - When set, the core raises a debug trap after every instruction (single step). STEP sets TF, DTE governs tracing, and the trap runs at L3 or above.

RF.description: Resume Flag - Suppresses the instruction breakpoint for exactly one instruction so that a resume from a debug exception does not re-trigger the breakpoint that caused it. Managed by the debugger, not by ordinary code.

XTE.description: XTU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Extension Unit (XTU) is enabled.

BME.description: BMU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Big Math Unit (BMU) is enabled.

CIE.description: CIU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Complex Instrucion Extension Unit (CIU) is enabled.

VME.description: Virtual Machine Enable Flag - Set while the core executes guest context (L6) and cleared in host context. VMENTER and VMRUN require VME=0 and set it; VMEXIT and VMCALL require VME=1 and clear it, so the flag is the host/guest selector of the virtualization extension.

TXE.description: Transaction Execution Flag - Set while a transaction started by XBEGIN is active and cleared by XEND, XABORT or an abort. A guest or an interrupt handler can test XTEST instead of reading the flag directly.

SSE.description: Shadow Stack Enable Flag - Enables the shadow stack. SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP and SHSTKRET raise #SEC when SSE=0, and a return whose shadow entry does not match the architectural one raises #SEC when SSE=1.

PKE.description: Protection Key Enable Flag - Enables protection-key checking. RDPKRU sets PKE; MAP, PROTECT and MKEYALLOC attach keys; a write to a page whose key denies write raises #SEC.

DTE.description: Debug Trace Enable Flag - Set by DBGON and TRACEON while the debug or trace facility is active, so that a handler can tell whether DTE-driven events are being recorded. The last eight branches and the last eight data accesses land in the trace buffer.

VIE.description: Virtual mode Interrupt Enable Flag - Indicates whether virtual mode interrupts are enabled.

SXE.description: Supervisor Access Exclusion Flag - The SMEP/SMAP analogue: when set, supervisor code cannot fetch and cannot (unless the access sets an explicit override) read or write a page that is marked user-accessible at L0, and such an attempt raises #SEC.

MCE.description: Machine Check Enable Flag - Enables the machine-check path. When MCE=0 a machine check is reported as #MCC; when MCE=1 the core takes the machine-check abort with the banked status recorded in the MSR space.

VLE.description: Vector Length Extension Flag - Set by VSETVL when the accepted active length exceeds the 256-bit baseline, so software can see that the running length is only representable by zeroing the tail. Cleared when a length of 256 bits or less is installed.

PROT.description: Protected mode Flag - If flag enabled, the processor will abort when operating a invalid memory address or other operations.

architecture.name: Hayneko_Arch32S.v2
architecture.description: Hayneko_Arch32S.v2 is the second revision of the Hayneko_Arch32S 32-bit CISC/RISC-hybrid architecture: a variable-length (1 to 16 byte) instruction format with an 8-bit opcode, a 32-entry 32-bit general register file, a 32-entry floating-point register file whose upper 16 physical slots are shared with the 256-bit vector file, eight predicate registers, six decode spaces (the base space plus five escape prefixes), and a coprocessor model (XTU, BMU, MMU, KCU, CIU). v2 is a strict backward-compatible superset of v1: every v1 encoding keeps its meaning, its operands and its length, and the v1 defect list of SPEC section 12 is repaired in place. v2 adds bit manipulation, integer math, string and packed-BCD families, a unified condition-code field, a scalar FPU, a 256-bit vector unit, a crypto unit, a big-math unit, atomics with transactional memory, a three-level MMU with protection keys, virtualization, debug and trace, power management and a security extension (shadow stack, speculation barriers, enclaves, key isolation). The instruction set is 555 instructions: the 156 v1 instructions carried forward unchanged plus 399 new v2 instructions delivered by the three instruction parts (A_core 104, B_fpvec 173, C_sys 122), on top of 46 assembler pseudo instructions and 33 micro-coded expansions (14 carried from v1 and 19 delivered by the parts).

instruction_counts.note: The three part counts are the delivered category totals; escaped-space entries declare length without the mandatory escape byte, so their on-wire size is length+1.

extensions.description: The v1 instruction set carried forward verbatim (156: control 32, stack 28, logic 32, arithmetic 17, branch 14, condition_move 14, system 11, load_store 4, data_transfer 2, io 2) plus the 17 non-PMU system_ext instructions kept in the base space (RDCR, WRCR, RDMSR, WRMSR, INVLPG, INVTLB, INVEPT, ICACHEINV, CLWBI, SYSENT, SYSEXI, CPUID, READREV, SETMODE, GETMODE, WRFLAGS, RDFLAGS).

Bit test and modify (BT, BTS, BTR, BTC and the immediate forms BTI, BTSI, BTRI, BTCI), scans and counts (BSF, BSR, POPCNT, CLZ, CTZ, PARCNT, BREV), double-width shifts (SHLD, SHRD), flag-free shifts and rotates (SHLX, SHRX, SARX, ROLX, RORX), parallel bit extract and deposit (PEXT, PDEP), low-mask generation (BZHI, MASKLSB), bit fields (BEXT, BINS, BEXTS, BEXTD, BINSD) and Gray code (GRAYE, GRAYD) over base 0x81-0x87.

Widening multiply and divide (MULH, MULHS, MULX, MULI, DIVMOD, REM, REMS, DIVI), multiply-accumulate (MADD, MSUB, MADDU, MSUBU), two independent carry chains (ADDC and SUBC on CF, ADCX on CF, ADOX on OF), min/max and saturation (MAXS, MINS, MAXU, MINU, ABSDIFF, AVG, SATADD, SATSUB, SATADDU, SATSUBU, CLAMP, CLAMPU, ISQRT) and width conversion (SEXT, ZEXT, TRUNC, BSWAP, CVTSZ, SATCAST, PACK) over integer_math 0x88-0x8B and convert 0x12-0x16.

String primitives that address memory through ri (source), rd (destination) and ra (accumulator), with rc as the explicit repeat counter, DF as the direction and ESZ as the element size: MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, LODS plus the non-temporal MOVSN and STOSN at base 0x8C. The REP prefix supplies the repetition mode.

Packed BCD arithmetic with two digits per byte: ADDBCD, SUBBCD, CMPBCD, NEGBCD, BCDSHL, BCDSHR, MULBCD, DIVBCD, BCD2BIN, BIN2BCD at base 0x8D-0x8E. VF records an invalid digit or a lost result and AF carries the nibble carry between digits.

A unified 4-bit condition-code field (CC) over the 16 condition codes of the conditions table, plus the transfers that consume it: JCND, JCNDL, JMPREL, JMPRELL, CALLREL, the LOOP family (LOOP, LOOPZ, LOOPNZ, LOOPL, LOOPZL, LOOPNZL), JTABLE, CALLTAB, RETFAR and the materialisation forms SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC, TSTCC at base 0x78-0x7E and 0x8F.

A complete scalar FPU over F16, BF16, F32 and F64 (FPF) with in-instruction rounding (RM): FADD, FSUB, FMUL, FDIV, FSQRT, FRECIP, FRECIPSQRT, FROUND, the fused FMADD, FMSUB, FNMADD, FNMSUB, sign and select (FABS, FNEG, FCOPYSIG, FSEL), compare and classify (FCMP, FCMPU, FCLASS), conversion (FTOSI, FTOUI, SITOF, UITOF, FCVT), moves (FMOV, FMOVG), memory (FLOAD, FSTORE) and exponent control (FLDEXP, FSCALE, FRMSTATE) at base 0xB0-0xB9.

A 256-bit SIMD unit with 32 vector registers v0-v31 and eight predicate registers k0-k7: configuration (VSETVL, VGETVL, VZERO, VCLEAR), memory (VLDR, VSTR, VLDRS, VSTRS, VLDRX, VSTRX, VLDREP, VLOADM, VSTOREM), arithmetic and FMA (VADD, VSUB, VMUL, VDIV, VMIN, VMAX, VABSD, VNEG, VMADD, VMSUB, VFMA, VFMS, VADDSAT, VSUBSAT, VAVG, VDOT), logic and shifts, compare, mask ALU (VCMP, VTEST, VFIND, KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT, KMOV, KMOVG, KTEST, KUNPCK, VPOPC), permute (VSHUF, VSWIZ, VPERM, VSLIDE, VBLEND, VTBL), reduce and scan, lane insert/extract/broadcast, conversion (VCVT, VZEXT, VSEXT, VTRUNC, VSAT, VROUND, VCNT, VCLZ, VBYTEREV, VCOMPRESS, VEXPAND) and state save/restore (VSTATE) at base 0xA0-0xAF.

AES rounds and key schedule (AESENC, AESDEC, AESENCLAST, AESDECLAST, AESIMC, AESKEYGEN), SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 message schedules and rounds, carry-less multiply and GF(2^8) (CLMUL, GF2P8MUL, GF2P8AFFINE), CRC32 and CRC32C, entropy (RDRAND, RDSEED), secure compare (SECCMP), key management (KEYGEN, KEYLOAD, KEYZERO, MONT) at base 0xC0-0xC5 and the ciu-space sponge and stream primitives (SHA3ABS, SHA3FIN, KECCAKF, POLY1305, CHACHA).

The big-math unit behind the BMU.EN prefix (0xF6): transcendental functions (FSIN, FCOS, FTAN, FASIN, FACOS, FATAN, FATAN2, FEXP, FLN, FLOG2, FLOG10, FPOW, FSINH, FCOSH, FTANH, FHYPOT) on FPR operands, arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic on GPR blocks (BMUL, BADD, BSUB, BDIV, BMOD, BSHL, BSHR, BAND, BOR, BXOR, BNOT, BCMP, B2D, D2B) and matrix operations on vector blocks (MMUL, MVEC, MTRANS), space bmu opcodes 0x00-0x0F, 0x20-0x2D and 0x40-0x42.

Load-linked and store-conditional (LDLK, STLK, CLREX), compare-and-swap (CAS), store-form atomic memory operations (AMOSWAP, AMOADD, AMOSUB, AMOAND, AMOOR, AMOXOR, AMOMIN, AMOMAX, AMOMINU, AMOMAXU), fetch-returning forms (AMOFADD, AMOFAND, AMOFOR, AMOFXOR, AMOFSWAP) and the fence family (MFENCE, LFENCE, SFENCE) whose strength comes from the SPB field, at base 0xC8-0xCB.

Transactional memory at base 0xCC-0xCD: XBEGIN (checkpoint plus a signed fallback offset), XEND, XABORT with an abort code in IM8, XTEST and XSUSPEND. Conflicts are detected at cache-line granularity and the nesting state lives in the txs kernel register and cr13.

The v2 memory system: paired and list transfers (LDP, STP, LDM, STM), sized and extending accesses (LDX, STX, LDSX, LDZX), streaming and cache control (LDNT, STNT, PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, CACHECTL) at base 0x1A-0x1C, and the explicit MMU operations of escape1 0x10 (MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC, MKEYFREE, EPTMAP, EPTUNMAP) plus TLB and cache invalidation (INVLPG, INVTLB, INVEPT, ICACHEINV, CLWBI) at 0x9A. Three-level paging with 4 KiB, 2 MiB and 1 GiB pages replaces the v1 two-level model.

Hypervisor and guest entry and exit at base 0x9C: VMENTER, VMEXIT, VMRUN, VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMCALL, VMFUNC, VMLOAD, VMSTORE. VM state lives behind cr8 and the VME status flag distinguishes host context (VME=0) from guest context (VME=1).

Shadow stack (SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP, SHSTKRET), control-flow integrity (ENDBR, SSBB), speculation barriers (SPECBAR, IBPB, STIBP), enclave lifecycle (ENCLS, ENCLU, ENCLV, ATTEST), zeroization and constant-time copy (ZEROIZE, CTCOPY) and protection-key access (RDPKRU, WRPKRU) in the xtu decode space 0x00-0x05. Key isolation lives in the CIU (KEYGEN, KEYLOAD, KEYZERO).

Hardware debug and trace at base 0x9D: DBGON, DBGOFF, BPSET, BPCLR, WCHSET, WCHCLR over eight dbg0-dbg7 registers, STEP, DBGREAD, TRACEON, TRACEOFF. The TF flag drives single step and the DTE status flag records that tracing is enabled.

Power management, timestamps and performance monitoring: the counter instructions RDTSC, RDTSCP, RDPMU and PMUCTL over eight 32-bit counters pmc0-pmc7 with cr7 as the performance-control register and the cr14 TSD bit gating L0 reads, plus the power family of escape1 0x00-0x03 (SLEEP, STANDBY, CLKGATE, MONITOR, MWAIT, WFI, WFE, DVFSHINT, RESET). v2.0 has no separate POWER extension id, so the nine power instructions are counted here.
The 16-bit port space and block I/O in escape1 0x20: INX, OUTX (PRT16), INS, OUTS (string forms under REP), IODELAY and IOSYNC, complementing the v1 8-bit IN and OUT.

coprocessor.name: XTU
coprocessor.description: Extension Unit for handling additional and complex instructions.
coprocessor.v2_role: Executes every vector instruction of 0xA0-0xAF and every security instruction of the xtu decode space, so needs_coprocessor is XTU for all 77 vector and 16 security entries.

coprocessor.name: BMU
coprocessor.description: Big Math Unit for handling complex mathematical operations.
coprocessor.v2_role: Owns the bmu decode space (BMU.EN 0xF6) and therefore the transcendental, big-integer and matrix instructions; the BMU prefix is that space's mandatory escape byte.

coprocessor.name: MMU
coprocessor.description: Memory Management Unit for handling memory management operations.
coprocessor.v2_role: Executes the explicit MMU operations of escape1 0x10 and the invalidation forms INVTLB and INVEPT; needs_coprocessor is MMU for MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC, MKEYFREE, EPTMAP, EPTUNMAP, INVTLB and INVEPT.

coprocessor.name: KCU
coprocessor.description: Kernel Control Unit for handling kernel and system-level operations.
coprocessor.v2_role: Kernel control path: modes, IDT and flags (SETMODE, GETMODE, WRFLAGS, RDFLAGS, SYSENT, SYSEXI, LDIDT, MODIDT, SETIDT). No v2 instruction declares needs_coprocessor KCU because the kernel path executes in-line at L3 and above.

coprocessor.name: CIU
coprocessor.description: Complex Instrucion Extension Unit for handling complex instructions and operations.
coprocessor.v2_role: Owns the ciu decode space and executes all 30 crypto instructions; the CIU prefix (0xFD) is both the enable prefix and the space escape byte.

pipelining.description: The v2 core is the v1 7-stage pipeline plus a register-rename stage (REN) that maps the 32 architectural general registers onto a larger physical file, and a retire stage (RET) that frees reorder-buffer entries in order. IF and IGL are split because an instruction is 1 to 16 bytes long: IGL reads the prefix stream and the opcode, computes the total encoded length (see instruction_length_rules), and IF then fetches the remaining operand bytes. Up to four prefix bytes may precede the opcode and they are consumed by IGL.

structures: direction predictor: 4096-entry PHT indexed by 16 bits of global history (gshare)
branch_prediction.hint_input: BRH_H (0xF2 not taken, 0xF3 taken) is a static hint that overrides the dynamic predictor for the next branch
branch_prediction.resolution_stage: EX, one stage after AC, because a relative branch target is the address of the branch instruction plus the sign-extended offset

speculative_execution.description: Loads and stores may execute speculatively after rename; retirement is in order and no architectural state is visible before RET. Speculation barriers (SPECBAR with its SPB strength, LFENCE, IBPB) stop speculation, and a speculatively executed store never reaches the cache before it is known non-faulting.

out_of_order_execution.description: v2 adds out-of-order execution behind an in-order front end: dispatch and rename are in order, EX and MEM may reorder, and RET retires strictly in order. v1 declared out-of-order execution unsupported. The v1 instruction set is unaffected because every new ordering guarantee is opt-in through the MO field and the fence family (MFENCE, LFENCE, SFENCE); a program that never uses them keeps the v1 weak ordering.

virtual_memory.address_translation: three-level paging with 4 KiB, 2 MiB and 1 GiB pages
virtual_memory.description: v2 replaces the v1 two-level paging model with three levels plus 2 MiB and 1 GiB huge pages. The page-table root is named by the pgt kernel register (KR 5) and by cr1 (memory management and protection). Translation is explicit for the privileged MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT and PGWALK instructions and implicit for ordinary loads and stores. A translation miss is #PGF; a missing right or a supervisor-only page taken at L0 is #GP, and a protection-key denial or a shadow-stack mismatch is #SEC.
virtual_memory.asid: 16-bit address-space identifier supplied in SEG and matched by INVTLB
virtual_memory.protection_keys: 16 keys (PKEY 0-15) with a two-bit rights field per key; the allocation bitmap lives in cr6

L0.description: User mode for executing user applications with restricted access to system resources. No privileged register, MSR, port, key or translation operation is reachable; the only privileged touch point is RDPKRU (floor L0), which reads the key rights word and sets PKE.
allowed_operations: CIU crypto instructions that are not key management
LDLK, STLK, CAS and the AMO forms
LDP, STP, LDM, STM, LDX, STX, LDSX, LDZX, PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, LDNT, STNT
SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP, SHSTKRET, ENCLU, SPECBAR, SSBB, IBPB, STIBP, RDPKRU

L1.description: Trusted mode for executing trusted applications, providing elevated privileges compared to user mode. Architecturally L1 adds no capability bit; it marks a trust domain, and the only instruction whose floor is exactly L1 is JMPFAR.

L2.description: Restricted mode for virtualization and sandboxed environments, providing limited access to system resources. Adds the control-register capability through MOVCTRL, plus flag and IDT control: CLI, STI, POPF and the INT/IRET pair floor here.

L3.description: Kernel mode for host operating system execution and management, allowing privileged code execution and access to system resources. This is the floor for every control-register, MSR, TLB, cache-maintenance, port, key, debug, power, shadow-stack and speculation-barrier instruction.
allowed_operations: MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC, MKEYFREE
IN, OUT, INX, OUTX, INS, OUTS, IODELAY, IOSYNC
DBGON, DBGOFF, BPSET, BPCLR, WCHSET, WCHCLR, STEP, DBGREAD
SLEEP, STANDBY, MONITOR, MWAIT, WFI, WFE
SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP, SHSTKRET, SPECBAR, IBPB, STIBP, SSBB, ZEROIZE, RDPKRU, WRPKRU
SYSENT, SYSEXI, SETMODE, GETMODE, WRFLAGS, RDFLAGS

L4.description: Hardware mode for direct hardware access and control, typically used for firmware and low-level system tasks. No v2 instruction floors at L4: hardware mode reaches the same architectural surfaces as L3 and is entered through SETMODE from L3 or from reset.

L5.description: Hypervisor mode for managing virtual machines and providing virtualization services. Adds the virtualization capability (VMENTER, VMRUN, VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMFUNC, VMLOAD, VMSTORE, INVEPT, EPTMAP, EPTUNMAP) and the trace capability (TRACEON, TRACEOFF). VMENTER requires VME=0 and sets VME.
allowed_operations: VMENTER, VMRUN, VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMFUNC, VMLOAD, VMSTORE

L6.description: Virtual Machine mode for executing guest operating systems within a virtualized environment. The mask is numerically nested above L5, but a guest runs with VME=1, which blocks the entry instructions (VMENTER requires VME=0) and admits only the guest-side exits VMCALL and VMEXIT, both of which floor at L6.
allowed_operations: everything allowed at L5 except the entry paths blocked by VME=1
guest kernel instructions with floor L0 to L3

L7.description: Platform Secure mode for handling secure operations and sensitive data, providing an additional layer of security. It has individual instruction and hardware support for sensitive data: enclave lifecycle and attestation (ENCLS, ENCLU, ENCLV, ATTEST), platform key generation (KEYGEN) and platform reset (RESET).

mask_rules.description: A higher level number admits every capability of every lower level, so capability_mask is monotone non-decreasing from L0 to L7. The L5 to L6 step is intentionally flat in bits: the host and guest split is enforced by the VME flag, which gates the entry instructions on VME=0 and the exits on VME=1, not by the mask.
mask_rules.capability_note: A capability bit authorises a family, not a specific instruction: the per-instruction mode field is the authoritative floor and the validator enforces it against L0..L7.

L1_cache.description: Level 1 Cache (L1 Cache) is a small, fast memory located close to the CPU cores, designed to store frequently accessed data and instructions to reduce latency and improve overall performance.

L2_cache.description: Level 2 Cache (L2 Cache) is a larger, slightly slower memory located between the L1 Cache and main memory, designed to store data and instructions that are less frequently accessed than those in the L1 Cache. It is used to reduce the impact of cache misses on overall performance.

L1I_cache.policy: read-only, LRU replacement, virtually indexed and physically tagged, two fetch ports
L1I_cache.description: Level 1 instruction cache. It caches the instruction stream after the IGL stage has computed the encoded length, so a fetch never crosses a page boundary without a second IGL pass on the new page.

L1D_cache.policy: write-back, write-allocate, LRU replacement, eight line-fill buffers, MESI
L1D_cache.description: Level 1 data cache. LDNT, STNT and the CH non-temporal hint bypass it for streaming data, CLZERO allocates a zeroed line, and CACHECTL, ICACHEINV and CLWBI maintain it.

L3_cache.policy: write-back, inclusive of L2, RRIP replacement, shared by the cores of a socket
L3_cache.description: Level 3 cache, shared and inclusive of L2, so an L2 eviction is mirrored by an L3 invalidate. EPT translations and I/O traffic also allocate here.

rex_byte_layout.meaning: The high nibble of a REX byte is 1110 (0xE0-0xEF); the low nibble holds one extension bit per register field. The v1 prefixes table declares that nibble as the ordered list [DRG, SR1, SR2, SR3] read most significant bit first, so DRG is bit 3 and SR3 is bit 0.
rex_byte_layout.evidence: v1 prefixes.types.REX format is [1,1,1,0,[DRG,SR1,SR2,SR3]] and the v1 reference implementation applies the mapping DRG 0x8, SR1 0x4, SR2 0x2, SR3 0x1 in _apply_rex. Both agree; a table that names the payload bits in the order the v1 format lists them is the same statement read left to right.

extension_rule.description: A 4-bit register field encodes indices 0-15. When the REX bit that belongs to that field is zero the instruction addresses register field_value; when the bit is one the instruction addresses register field_value + 16. The addition is masked to 31, so the reachable set is exactly 0-31. A field whose REX bit is set and whose value is 15 addresses register 31, which is reachable and legal.
extension_rule.general_register_effect: A REX bit extends the general register file to all 32 entries: with no bit set DRG/SR1/SR2/SR3 name r0-r15 (x0, ra, rb, rc, rd, ri, bp, sp, r8-r15), and with the bit set they name r16-r31 (r16-r23, t0-t7).
extension_rule.floating_point_effect: For the FPU fields DFR, SF1, SF2 and SF3 the same rule names the two v1 views: bit clear addresses f0-f15 (single precision), bit set addresses d0-d15, which are the same physical slots numbered 16-31.
extension_rule.vector_effect: For the vector fields VDG, VF1, VF2 and VF3 the rule addresses v0-v31, so a vector instruction reaches the upper half of the vector file only through a REX bit.

architectural_aliases.rule: Register 0 is a constant zero. Reads return 0 and every write is discarded. No instruction can change it; a write-only use such as the destination of a computed discard is legal and has no effect.
architectural_aliases.evidence: v1 registers.interger.x0 and the v1 reference implementation, which never writes index 0.

architectural_aliases.rule: The 16 physical slots numbered 16-31 are the double-precision registers d0-d15 and, under the second spelling, f16-f31. c is not a separate register: writing dN changes f(16+N) and vice versa, and a double-precision operation may name either spelling.
architectural_aliases.evidence: v1 registers.floating_point.double numbers d0-d15 as 16-31 and the v1 REX description says the extension renames f0-f15 to d0-d15.

architectural_aliases.rule: The floating-point file and the vector file share the top 16 physical 256-bit slots. v16-v31 are those slots in full; d0-d15 (alias f16-f31) are their low 64 bits. Writing a vector register therefore changes the corresponding double register and vice versa. v0-v15 occupy the remaining 16 slots and their low 64 bits are the f0-f15 view.
architectural_aliases.evidence: B_fpvec states the sharing normatively: f16-f31 alias v16-v31, and the crypto instructions keep their 128-bit state in the low half of a vector register, which is the same unification.

architectural_aliases.rule: A lane view is a spelling of the same 256-bit register at a narrower element size: .b is 32 lanes of 8 bits, .w 16 lanes of 16 bits, .d 8 lanes of 32 bits and .q 4 lanes of 64 bits. The view is what the ESZ field selects; the register number does not change.
architectural_aliases.evidence: The vector model of B_fpvec (ESZ 0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD, VLMAX = 256/(8<<ESZ)) makes the lane views a function of ESZ, not a second register file.

architectural_aliases.rule: k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask. Named as any mask operand - through the EVX or PRED prefix, or directly in the KM1 or KM2 fields of an instruction such as VLOADM, VSTOREM, KAND or KTEST - it reads all ones for the active mask length, which is exactly no masking. A write to k0 through KDG is discarded, so k0 never changes and VCLEAR affects k1-k7 only. k1-k7 are ordinary read/write 32-bit mask registers, and a mask with no enabled bits is built by clearing one of them (KMOVG with MO=0 stores a zero general register into a mask, and VCLEAR with MO bit 1 clears k1-k7).
architectural_aliases.evidence: B_fpvec notes (k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask), KMOV (naming k0 as KM1 reads all ones and a write to k0 through KDG is discarded), KAND (k0 as a source reads all ones, so KAND with k0 leaves the other operand unchanged), VLOADM and VSTOREM (a masked transfer through k0 is exactly the unit-stride form), VCLEAR (k0 is not affected because it is hardwired) and VSTATE (the k0 word of the mask area reads as all ones on save and is ignored on restore).

architectural_aliases.alias: ip and the KR ip register
architectural_aliases.rule: ip is the architectural program counter (registers.interger.ip, number null) and is also visible as kernel register ip (KR 2), which privileged code can write. It is not a general register and no DRG/SR1/SR2/SR3 encoding names it.
architectural_aliases.evidence: v1 registers lists ip with number null in the integer section and again as KR 2 in the kernel section.

register_renaming.notes: v1 left register_renaming as an empty object. v2 fills it with the byte layout, the extension formula, the field lists that REX does and does not extend, and the six architectural alias rules. The extension is applied after operand decoding and before any register read or write, exactly as the v1 reference implementation does it.

x0.description: Zero register, always holds the value 0.

ra.description: Return Address register, holds the return address for function calls.

rb.description: Base register, used for base addressing.

rc.description: Counter register, used for loop counting.

rd.description: Data register, used for general data storage.

ri.description: Index register, used for indexed addressing.

bp.description: Base Pointer register, used for stack frame management.

sp.description: Stack Pointer register, points to the top of the stack.

ip.description: Instruction Pointer register, holds the address of the next instruction to be executed.

cr0.description: Control Register 0 - Used for system control and configuration.

cr1.description: Control Register 1 - Used for memory management and protection.

cr2.description: Control Register 2 - Used for interrupt handling and status.

cr3.description: Control Register 3 - Used for system performance monitoring.

cr4.description: Control Register 4 - Vector control: VLEN encoding, the default VL, the default mask policy (zeroing or merging) and the default ESZ for the vector unit.

cr5.description: Control Register 5 - Security control: enables the shadow stack (SSE), sets the speculation-barrier default (SPB) and holds the supervisor-access-exclusion bits behind the SXE status flag.

cr6.description: Control Register 6 - Protection keys base: the 16-key allocation bitmap used by MKEYALLOC and MKEYFREE plus the two-bit rights field per key that RDPKRU and WRPKRU read and write.

cr7.description: Control Register 7 - Performance control: event selection, counter gating and the hypervisor-only bits that turn an L0 RDPMU into #GP.

cr8.description: Control Register 8 - Virtualization control: points at the VM control block that VMSTORE writes guest state into and VMLOAD restores from.

cr9.description: Control Register 9 - TLB control: global-entry flush policy, ASID width and the invalidation filters used by INVLPG and INVTLB.

cr10.description: Control Register 10 - Debug control: master enable for DBGON and TRACEON, the trace buffer base and the watchpoint gating bits.

cr11.description: Control Register 11 - Shadow stack register: holds the shadow stack pointer that SHSTKPUSH decrements and SHSTKPOP advances; the kernel loads the shadow stack base here before the first push.

cr12.description: Control Register 12 - Cache control: default cache hints (CH), whether CLZERO and the non-temporal forms are permitted at L0, and the L3 partition selector.

cr13.description: Control Register 13 - Transaction control: nesting limit, default XBEGIN attributes and the retry policy after an abort.

cr14.description: Control Register 14 - Feature control: per-extension enable bits for BIT, MATH, VEC, CIU, BMU, ATOM and TX, plus the TSD bit that turns an L0 RDTSC into #GP.

cr15.description: Control Register 15 - Architecture revision: read-only revision and extension bitmap reported by READREV and CPUID.

mode.description: Kernel Mode Register - Indicates the current operating mode.

status.description: Kernel Status Register - Holds status flags and information.

ip.description: Program Counter Register - Holds the address of the next instruction to be executed. Can be modified in kernel mode or hardware mode.

idt.description: Interrupt Descriptor Table Register - Points to the interrupt descriptor table used for handling interrupts.

tlb.description: TLB Control Register - base and geometry of the translation cache plus the current address-space identifier.

pgt.description: Page Table Register - physical address of the level-0 page table root used by the three-level walk.

shstk.description: Shadow Stack Limit Register - base and limit of the shadow stack region that cr11 walks; SHSTKRET compares the popped entry against it.

pmu.description: PMU Control Register - global counter enable, freeze and overflow aggregation for pmc0-pmc7.

txs.description: Transaction State Register - nesting depth, checkpoint identifier and the last abort code reported by XTEST.

reserved.description: Kernel registers 9-15 are reserved in v2.0, read as zero, and a write to them raises #GP.

lane_views.description: A vector register is one 256-bit storage and the lane view selects how an instruction interprets it. The view is chosen by the ESZ field (0 BYTE, 1 WORD, 2 DWORD, 3 QWORD); the assembler spelling vN.b, vN.w, vN.d or vN.q is an explicit alias for the same register at that element size.

mask_registers.index_field: KDG, KM1, KM2 (4 bits each; codes 0-7 name k0-k7, codes 8-15 are reserved in v2.0 and raise #UDI)
mask_registers.description: Predicate registers hold one bit per lane of a 256-bit vector operation, so a predicate register is 32 bits wide: 32 lanes at 8-bit elements, 16 at 16-bit, 8 at 32-bit and 4 at 64-bit. Bits above the active mask length read as zero. k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask; k1-k7 are ordinary read/write registers of the mask file.

k0.description: Predicate Register 0 - the hardwired all-ones mask register. It reads all ones for the active mask length in every mask-operand position and a KDG write to it is discarded, so it never changes; the full rule is registers.mask_notes.k0_rule.

model_specific_registers.description: The MSR space is model specific and has no architectural names in v2.0; only the index range is architectural. An unimplemented index raises #GP.

control_notes.container: registers.control is flat, exactly as in v1: minimum_privileged_level followed by cr0-cr15 and nothing else (seventeen keys), so a v1 consumer that reads registers.control.cr0 keeps working unchanged. An additive name-to-number index sat here during review only because the gate then required a nested member; the gate now accepts the flat shape, so the index is gone.
control_notes.index_field: CR (4 bits: 0x0-0xF selects cr0-cr15). A decoder that carries a narrower CR width masks the index into the implemented range.
control_notes.access_instructions: RDCR and WRCR (mode L3) move a control register through a general register; MOVCTRL (mode L2) copies between two control registers.
control_notes.v1_shape: cr0-cr3 keep v1's exact number, type and description values; cr4-cr15 are the v2 extension of the same 4-bit CR field.
control_notes.wrapper_note: cr0-cr3 are the four v1 control registers carried forward verbatim; cr4-cr15 are the v2 extension of the same 4-bit CR field. The v1 reference implementation decoded the field with a 2-bit mask, so a v1 loader sees only cr0-cr3.
control_notes.hardware_info_cr: architecture.hardware_info.CR is 16 in v2 because the CR field is four bits and all sixteen values are implemented; v1 declared CR 4 because only cr0-cr3 existed. It is the only v1 hardware_info value that changed, and registers.control keeps cr0-cr3 byte-for-byte identical to v1 underneath the wider count.

mask_notes.width_and_lanes: A predicate register is 32 bits because the widest element granularity of a 256-bit operation is 8 bits, which gives 32 lanes. B_fpvec's VSTATE record confirms the width arithmetically: 32 vector registers x 32 bytes = 1024, 8 mask registers x 4 bytes = 32, plus 8 bytes for VL and VLE, total 1064 bytes.
mask_notes.bits_above_active_mask: Bits above the active mask length read as zero and are written as zero by the mask ALU (KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT, KUNPCK, KMOV).
mask_notes.k0_rule: k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask. Named as any mask operand - through the EVX or PRED prefix, or directly in the KM1 or KM2 fields of an instruction such as VLOADM, VSTOREM, KAND or KTEST - it reads all ones for the active mask length, which is exactly no masking. A write to k0 through KDG is discarded, so k0 never changes and VCLEAR affects k1-k7 only. k1-k7 are ordinary read/write 32-bit mask registers, and a mask with no enabled bits is built by clearing one of them (KMOVG with MO=0 stores a zero general register into a mask, and VCLEAR with MO bit 1 clears k1-k7).
mask_notes.reset_state: k0 is hardwired and needs no initialisation. No delivered instruction states the architectural reset value of k1-k7; a program that needs a known mask must set it explicitly, and VCLEAR with MO bit 1 clears k1-k7 to zero when an empty mask is wanted.
mask_notes.register_count: k0-k7 are implemented; KDG, KM1 and KM2 codes 8-15 are reserved and raise #UDI.

ABI.stack_alignment_notes: sp is 16-byte aligned at the point of the call, so a callee sees sp+4 aligned to 16 after the 4-byte return address is pushed and sp+8 aligned to 16 after the saved bp is pushed.

high_to_low: outgoing arguments beyond the eight register parameters
return address (pushed by CALL, four bytes)
saved bp (pushed by the callee prologue)
stack_frame_layout.description: CALL pushes the address of the following instruction (four bytes). The callee prologue is PUSH bp followed by ENTR, which copies sp into bp, so [bp] holds the saved caller bp, [bp+4] holds the return address and [bp+8] holds the first incoming stack argument. LEAV restores sp from bp, POP bp restores the frame pointer and RET pops the return address. Local storage lives below the saved bp, and the 128 bytes below sp are a red zone a leaf function may use without adjusting sp.
stack_frame_layout.interrupt_frame: An interrupt pushes the flags word and then the return address (the address of the following instruction, including any prefix bytes), and IRET pops the address before the flags, so the interrupt frame is the reverse of the call frame.

ABI.callee_saved_notes: bp and sp are callee-saved by construction; r16-r22 are the seven allocatable callee-saved registers. r23 is the thread pointer and is neither callee-saved nor allocatable (see tls_register).
ABI.caller_saved_notes: The return address register ra, the five named working registers (rb, rc, rd, ri), the eight argument registers r8-r15 and the eight temporaries t0-t7 are volatile. The whole floating-point file (f0-f15, d0-d15), the whole vector file (v0-v31) and the whole predicate file (k0-k7) are volatile as well, because d0-d15 alias v16-v31 and the v1 ABI already passes floating-point arguments in d1-d8; no FP or vector register survives a call except through the stack.
ABI.tls_register_notes: r23 is the thread pointer: it holds the base of the thread-local storage block, is set by the runtime at thread creation, is preserved across calls and is never used by the parameter-passing convention.
ABI.red_zone_notes: The 128 bytes below sp may be used by a leaf function without adjusting sp; a signal, an interrupt or a call from that function destroys them.

syscall_convention.notes: The v1 system_call_parameters list is kept verbatim and is read with ra as the first argument and rc as the system call number, which is why rc appears in both roles in the v1 list. The v2 kernel entry points SYSENT and SYSENT-family gates do not change the convention; SYSEXI returns through ra as well. A call that needs more than five scalar arguments passes the rest on the stack above the return address.

variadic.notes: v2 defines no vector-argument count register in the v1 format, so a variadic routine receives the number of vector arguments in t0, which is never a parameter register. A callee that calls va_start spills v0-v31 and k0-k7 into a 1056-byte save area (32 vector registers x 32 bytes plus 8 predicate registers x 4 bytes); VSTATE writes the same record plus the 8-byte VL/VLE word as 1064 bytes. The whole FP and vector file is volatile, which is why the spill is mandatory.
variadic.floating_point_notes: Floating-point variadic arguments follow the v1 rule: the first eight go in f1-f8 for single precision and d1-d8 for double precision, and everything beyond goes on the stack.

ABI.register_passing_notes: The v1 lists are kept verbatim: eight integer parameters in rb, rd, ri, r8, r9, r10, r11 and r12; eight single-precision parameters in f1-f8; eight double-precision parameters in d1-d8. v2 adds the vector parameters v1-v8 with the mask parameter k1 and the vector return register v0; v0-v15 are volatile, so v1-v8 are safe only until the next call.

3.name: CC
3.meaning: carry clear (unsigned higher or same: HS)

register_direct.syntax: DRG, SR1, SR2, SR3 (general) and DFR, SF1, SF2, SF3 (floating point) and VDG, VF1, VF2, VF3 (vector)
register_direct.encoding: one 4-bit field per operand; a REX bit for that field adds 16 to the index (see register_renaming.extension_rule)
register_direct.allowed_instructions: every register form of the ALU, SHIFT, MUL, DIV, logic, branch, FPU, vector and crypto families; the majority of the 555 instructions
register_direct.notes: Register 0 is the constant zero and discards writes. Register-direct is the only mode that needs no address calculation, so it retires in EX with no AC stage use.

displacement_8.syntax: [SR1 + disp8]  (LD, ST, LDSTVAL, STSTVAL, PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, INVLPG and every other base+disp8 form)
displacement_8.encoding: OF8, an 8-bit signed displacement sign-extended to 32 bits before the addition
displacement_8.allowed_instructions: v1 LD, ST, LDSTVAL, STSTVAL; C_sys PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, INVLPG and the memory family; A_core JMPREL and the LOOP family use the same OF8 token as a signed rel8 branch offset
displacement_8.notes: Address = (SR1 + sign_extend(OF8,8)) mod 2^32. The same token serves a memory displacement and a rel8 branch offset; which one it is follows from the instruction, never from the bits.

displacement_16.syntax: [SR1 + disp16]  (VLDR, VSTR); [ip + disp16] for LDOFIP and STOFIP
displacement_16.encoding: O16, a 16-bit signed offset (the token corrected from the v1 spelling OF16 by SPEC section 12 item 5)
displacement_16.allowed_instructions: B_fpvec VLDR, VSTR; v1 LDOFIP, STOFIP; A_core JCND uses O16 as a signed rel16 branch offset
displacement_16.notes: Base plus disp16 covers a 64 KiB window either side of the base register or of the instruction pointer. LDOFIP and STOFIP measure from the address of the instruction itself (see ip_relative_16).

displacement_32.syntax: [SR1 + disp32] is the defined pattern; no v2.0 instruction encodes it
displacement_32.allowed_instructions: none as a memory displacement: O32 appears only as a signed rel32 branch or call offset in JCNDL, JMPRELL, CALLREL, LOOPL, LOOPZL and LOOPNZL
displacement_32.notes: The field exists, is 32 bits wide and sign-extended, and a future memory family can use it without changing the token set; v2.0 has no encoder that emits a memory form with O32, which is why the opcode map lists the remaining primaries of the memory range as reserved.

base_index_scale_displacement.syntax: [SR1 + SR2*SCL + disp8] for LEASC; [SR1 + (SR2 << SCL)] for LDX, STX, LDSX and LDZX
base_index_scale_displacement.encoding: SR1 base, SR2 index, SCL scale (4 bits), OF8 signed displacement
base_index_scale_displacement.allowed_instructions: v1 LEASC; C_sys LDX, STX, LDSX, LDZX
base_index_scale_displacement.notes: The scale means two different things and an implementer must not unify them: LEASC (and the v1 reference implementation) treats SCL as a numeric multiplier, so SCL=3 multiplies the index by 3, while LDX and STX treat SCL as a shift count restricted to 0-3 bits and raise #UDI for SCL 4-15. LEASC writes no memory, it computes the address into DRG.

ip_relative_8.allowed_instructions: none: no v2.0 instruction combines the instruction pointer with an 8-bit displacement
ip_relative_8.notes: Listed for completeness of the mode list. Software that needs PC-relative data at rel8 reach uses LEA on the instruction pointer or a 16-bit form.

ip_relative_16.encoding: O16 with the base fixed to the instruction pointer
ip_relative_16.notes: The base is the address of the LDOFIP or STOFIP instruction itself, not the address of the following instruction: the v1 reference implementation computes dec.start_ip + sign_extend(O16) before the operands are read. This is the same base rule the relative branches use.

ip_relative_32.syntax: [ip + disp32] is the defined pattern; no v2.0 instruction encodes it
ip_relative_32.encoding: O32 with a fixed instruction-pointer base
ip_relative_32.notes: A rel32 branch (JCNDL, JMPRELL, CALLREL) is not an ip-relative memory operand: it computes a transfer target. The distinction matters because a branch target is computed in EX while an ip-relative load is computed in AC.

absolute_16.notes: The address is taken as an unsigned 16-bit value and zero-extended to 32 bits; it names a location in the low 64 KiB of the address space.

absolute_32.allowed_instructions: v1 JMPFAR, MODIDT, SETIDT; NOP15 also carries an A32 operand to reach its 15-byte encoding
absolute_32.notes: Absolute 32-bit addressing is the only way to reach the whole 4 GiB space without a base register. AD8 (8-bit absolute) is declared in the encode section for completeness but no v1 or v2 instruction uses it.

absolute_8.allowed_instructions: none: AD8 is declared in the encode section of v1 and is carried into v2, but no instruction in v1 or in the three parts uses it
absolute_8.notes: Recorded so that a decoder implementer knows the token exists and why nothing emits it; it is not a reserved hole in any instruction format.

string_pre_post_increment.syntax: MOVS / CMPS / SCAS / STOS / LODS with implicit operands: [ri] and [rd] walk by 1, 2 or 4 bytes
string_pre_post_increment.encoding: no address operand is encoded: SOP selects the operation, ESZ selects the element size, DF selects the step direction, rc is the counter, ri the source pointer, rd the destination pointer and ra the accumulator
string_pre_post_increment.allowed_instructions: A_core MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, LODS, MOVSN, STOSN; C_sys INS, OUTS
string_pre_post_increment.notes: The pointers step after each element: +-(1<<ESZ) bytes, upward when DF=0 and downward when DF=1. A REP prefix supplies the count and the termination test, so a REP-prefixed block move names three registers (ri, rd, rc) and hides nothing.

vector_unit_stride.syntax: VLDR vD, [SR1 + disp16] and VSTR [SR1 + disp16], vS
vector_unit_stride.encoding: VDG or VF1, SR1, O16 and ESZ; lane i comes from base + i*sizeof(ESZ)
vector_unit_stride.notes: Unit stride is the contiguous case. Lanes past VL are zeroed and a mask-cleared lane is never touched in memory, so a masked load cannot fault.

vector_strided.encoding: VDG or VF1, SR1 (base), SR2 (stride register), MO (scale applied to the stride), ESZ
vector_strided.notes: Element i lives at base + i*(SR2 << MO). A zero stride is allowed and reads the same element into every lane.

vector_indexed_gather_scatter.syntax: VLDRX vD, [SR1 + VF1], VSTRX [SR1 + VF1], vS
vector_indexed_gather_scatter.encoding: VDG or VF2, SR1 base, VF1 index vector, MO (32-bit or 64-bit offsets), ESZ
vector_indexed_gather_scatter.notes: Gather and scatter use per-lane offsets held in a vector register instead of a constant stride. A masked-off lane is neither loaded nor stored, and a faulting lane suppresses the whole instruction so VDG is unchanged (#PGF or #AC).

vector_broadcast.syntax: VLDREP vD, [SR1] and VBROADCAST vD, SR1 / VEXTRACT
vector_broadcast.notes: Broadcast reads one memory element (or one scalar register) and replicates it into every active lane, so it is a load with lane fan-out rather than a distinct addressing mode.

vector_masked_block.syntax: VLOADM vD, [SR1], kM and VSTOREM [SR1], vS, kM
vector_masked_block.encoding: VDG or VF1, SR1, OF8 or O16 displacement, KM1 naming the mask directly
vector_masked_block.notes: The mask register is named in the instruction (KM1) rather than in the EVX prefix because fault suppression is part of the semantics: only enabled lanes touch memory.

stack_push_pop.syntax: PUSH src / POP dst, plus the implicit frames of CALL, RET, INT, IRET and the PUSH/POP families
stack_push_pop.encoding: DRG and SOP for the register forms, IM8 for PUSHIMMB, I32 for PUSHIMMDW, I16 for PUSHIMMW; no address operand
stack_push_pop.allowed_instructions: v1 PUSH, POP, PUSHIMMB, PUSHIMMW, PUSHIMMDW, PUSHF, POPF, PUSHIP, PUSHTR, POPTR, ADDSP, SUBSP, CALL, RET, INT, IRET; ENTR and LEAV move bp and sp
stack_push_pop.notes: The stack is full-descending and 32-bit wide: a push stores sp-4 and then sets sp = sp-4, a pop reads at sp and then sets sp = sp+4 (the v1 reference implementation does exactly this). The stack pointer is sp (register 7).

port_io.syntax: IN dst, port / OUT port, src (8-bit PRT) and INX dst, port16 / OUTX port16, src / INS / OUTS (16-bit PRT16)
port_io.encoding: PRT (8-bit port number) or PRT16 (16-bit port number), with the data in a general register; INS and OUTS address memory through ri or rd under REP
port_io.allowed_instructions: v1 IN, OUT; C_sys INX, OUTX, INS, OUTS, IODELAY, IOSYNC
port_io.notes: Port I/O is a separate address space, not a memory address: PRT names one of 256 ports and PRT16 one of 65536. Everything with a port operand floors at L3 except IODELAY and IOSYNC, which are also L3 in v2.0.

mode_summary.notes: Nineteen addressing modes are defined. Fifteen are instantiated by at least one instruction of v1 or of the three parts (register direct, displacement 8, displacement 16, base+index*scale+displacement, ip-relative 16, absolute 16, absolute 32, string pre/post-increment, vector unit stride, vector strided, vector indexed gather/scatter, vector broadcast, vector masked block, stack push/pop, port I/O). Four are pattern definitions with no encoder user in v2.0: displacement 32, ip-relative 8, ip-relative 32 and absolute 8 (AD8).

instruction_length_rules.length_identity: length = 1 + (sum of 4-bit units of every format token after OPC) / 2
instruction_length_rules.byte_alignment_invariant: The number of 4-bit units after OPC must be even, so every instruction is a whole number of bytes. A format that would leave an odd nibble count is fixed by adding an explicit reserved 0x0 nibble, never by shortening a field.
instruction_length_rules.encoded_size_rule: encoded_size = number of prefix bytes + length. Length counts the opcode byte and the operand fields only; every prefix byte before the opcode is outside it, which is why a REX-prefixed LD is reported as length 3 but occupies 4 bytes on the wire.
instruction_length_rules.escaped_space_length: An instruction in an escaped decode space declares length as OPC plus its operand fields exactly like a base-space instruction. The mandatory escape prefix byte (DBI 0xF0 for escape1, XTU 0xF5 for xtu, BMU 0xF6 for bmu, CIU 0xFD for ciu) is a prefix like REX and is not counted, so the encoded size on the wire is length+1: a 3-byte escape1 MAP occupies 4 bytes and a 4-byte bmu FSIN occupies 5.
instruction_length_rules.prefix_budget: At most four prefix bytes may precede the opcode (prefixes.max_size). A prefix byte never changes length and never counts toward the 16-byte maximum.

isl_prefix.nibble: 0xD0 + a 4-bit value that declares the total encoded length of the instruction
isl_prefix.valid_values: 4 to 15 per the v1 definition (values 0-3 are invalid because no instruction is shorter than 4 bytes when ISL is present); a 16-byte instruction cannot be annotated because 16 does not fit in four bits
isl_prefix.decoder_behaviour: The decoder may use the nibble to fetch the whole instruction in one cycle, but the architectural length always comes from the format. The v1 reference implementation decodes the nibble and then ignores it, using the format-derived length, and v2 keeps that behaviour: a mismatching ISL is not a fault in v2.0 and never changes the meaning of the instruction.

reserved_nibble.rule: A literal 0x0 nibble is a reserved pad that must be encoded as zero and ignored on read. It is the only token allowed to repeat inside one format, and it exists only to keep the nibble count after OPC even.

steps: read prefix bytes until a byte that is not a prefix, applying the four-byte budget
decode the opcode byte and, when the format of the selected entry contains SOP or SOP8, the sub-opcode nibble
look up the format of the selected instruction and sum its nibble units after OPC
length = 1 + units/2; fetch that many operand bytes
apply any register-extension prefix to the register fields before the operand read
decoder_length_computation.reference_implementation: The v1 reference implementation computes format_length as 8 bits plus FIELD_SIZES of every non-OPC token divided by 8, which is the same identity, and it takes the on-wire size as start_ip + len(raw) where raw includes every prefix byte.
decoder_length_computation.sub_opcode_rule: sub_opcode is decoded exactly when SOP or SOP8 appears in the format, and never otherwise. The 0x5B opcode needs a special rule in a v1 loader because v1 booked COPYIP and SAR on the same byte without a sub-opcode field; v2 removes that collision by moving SAR to 0x5D, so a v2 decoder needs no special case.

instructions: NOP2 through NOP15 (2 to 15 bytes, opcode 0x80 with sub_opcode 0x2 to 0xF: the sub-opcode equals the padding length, so NOP2 carries 0x2 and NOP15 carries 0xF. Sub-opcodes 0x0 and 0x1 of 0x80 are undefined and raise #UDI; the one-byte pad is NOP at opcode 0x00, which has no sub-opcode.)
padding.rule: Padding uses the NOP family: NOP for one byte, NOPn for n bytes. A 16-byte pad is a NOP15 plus a NOP because no 16-byte NOP exists, and the padding bytes must still respect the format of the instruction used, so the disassembler never loses alignment.

relative_branch_base.rule: A relative transfer computes its target as the address of the branch instruction itself plus the sign-extended offset: target = start_ip + sign_extend(offset). The instruction pointer has already been advanced past the whole instruction stream when the branch executes, so the base must be the saved start address, not the current ip.
applies_to: v1 JZ, JC, JO, JN, JNZ, JNC, JNO, JNN, JL, JGE, JA, JBE, JLE, JAG
A_core JCND, JCNDL, JMPREL, JMPRELL, CALLREL, LOOP, LOOPZ, LOOPNZ, LOOPL, LOOPZL, LOOPNZL
relative_branch_base.evidence: The v1 reference implementation calls _jump(self.ip + offset) while self.ip still holds the address of the branch (ip is advanced after the handler returns), and the v1 description of JZ says the target is the current address plus the signed offset. The three parts state the same rule in every relative-transfer description.
relative_branch_base.documented_exception: XBEGIN measures its fallback offset from the end of the instruction (IP + length + sign_extend(O16)) as its encoding_notes state, because the fallback is the point a transaction resumes at, not a branch target. CALLREL pushes start_ip + 5 (the address of the following instruction) and branches to start_ip + sign_extend(O32).

length_classes.1 byte: 28 v1 control, stack and system instructions (NOP, ENTR, LEAV, RET, CLI, STI, PUSH/POP of the six named registers, INC rc, DEC rc, RANDOM, CLR ra, SYSCALL, SYSRET, HALT, LDIDT, BRK, IRET). v2 adds none: every v2 instruction is 2 to 5 bytes.
length_classes.2 bytes: v1 two-byte forms (PUSH/POP with DRG and SOP, IMMB, the shift forms) and the v2 short forms (string MOVS at 2 bytes, escape1 MKEYALLOC and xtu security forms at length 2 plus the escape byte).
length_classes.3 bytes: The modal v2 length: most register forms of the integer, crypto and system families.
length_classes.4 bytes: Vector arithmetic, FPU arithmetic and the bmu forms, all of which carry four to six nibble fields.
length_classes.5 bytes: 11 instructions: the memory forms VLDR, VSTR, FLOAD and FSTORE, the transfer forms CALLREL, JMPRELL and JMPFAR, the v1 far-pointer stores PUSHIMMDW and SETIDT, the atomic CAS and the padding NOP5.
length_classes.6 bytes: 15 instructions: the v1 dword-immediate ALU forms (IMM, ADDIDW, SUBIDW, XORIDW, ANDIDW, ORIDW, XNORIDW, NANDIDW, NORIDW), the long loop forms LOOPL, LOOPZL and LOOPNZL, MODIDT and NOP6, plus JCNDL, which combines a condition code with a 32-bit relative offset and is the longest instruction v2 adds.
length_classes.7 to 15 bytes: The v1 padding family only: NOP7 through NOP15 occupy one instruction at each length and nothing else in v1 or v2 is longer than 6 bytes.
length_classes.16 bytes: No instruction uses the architectural maximum; the largest in v1 is NOP15 at 15 bytes and the largest v2 addition is 6 bytes.

base.reserved_opcode_space: 0xD0-0xFF is not opcode space: 0xD0-0xDF ISL, 0xE0-0xEF REX and the 0xF0-0xFF prefix block are prefix bytes only
base.owning_unit: the core pipeline and its coprocessors: CTRL, ALU, SHIFT, MUL, DIV, LSU, FPU, VEC, SYS, IO, MMU, CIU
base.sub_opcode_usage: optional and per primary: a v2 primary either uses SOP for all of its instructions or for none (base family rule)
base.notes: The base space holds all 156 v1 instructions and 320 of the 399 v2 instructions. It is the only space whose opcode byte is limited to 0x00-0xCF.
base.opcode_count_note: 190 opcodes carry an instruction delivered by v1 or by one of the three parts; 0x5D is in use as the post-fix home of the v1 SAR, which no part file carries, so 191 of the 208 base opcodes are assigned and 17 are reserved.
base.exec_unit_note: v1 instructions declare no exec_unit field, so a map entry whose owner is v1 alone shows an empty exec_units array. The unit is implied by the v1 category: ALU for arithmetic, logic and condition_move, SHIFT for the shift and rotate forms, LSU for load_store and stack, CTRL for control and branch, SYS for system and IO for io. Every v2 part entry names its unit explicitly.

escape1.owning_unit: C_sys: SYS for power, MMU for memory management, IO for the extended port family
escape1.needs_coprocessor: MMU for MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC, MKEYFREE, EPTMAP, EPTUNMAP; none for the power and io_ext families
escape1.sub_opcode_usage: SOP is used inside every used opcode byte to group the family variants (3 variants for power 0x00, 2 for 0x01, 2 for 0x02, 2 for 0x03, 10 for 0x10, 6 for 0x20)
escape1.length_note: An escape1 entry declares length without the DBI byte, so the encoded size is length+1
escape1.notes: The escape1 space is reached only through DBI (0xF0), the v1 double-byte instruction prefix. Opcode bytes 0x04-0x0F, 0x11-0x1F and 0x21-0xFF are reserved: 250 of the 256 bytes are unused and raise #UDI on decode.

escape2.notes: The escape2 space is reserved in its entirety: TBI (0xF1) followed by any byte raises #UDI. The space is documented so that a future triple-byte family has a home and so that a decoder assigns it a distinct trap rather than aliasing it to escape1.

xtu.owning_unit: XTU, executing the SYS-visible security family of C_sys
xtu.sub_opcode_usage: SOP groups the variants: 3 for 0x00 (shadow stack push, pop, ret), 2 for 0x01, 3 for 0x02, 4 for 0x03 (enclave leaves), 2 for 0x04, 2 for 0x05
xtu.length_note: An xtu entry declares length without the XTU byte, so the encoded size is length+1
xtu.notes: The XTU prefix doubles as the enable prefix for the vector unit, which is why the 77 vector instructions in the base space declare needs_coprocessor XTU while living in the base decode space.

bmu.sub_opcode_usage: none: the bmu space gives every mnemonic its own opcode byte and no format contains SOP or SOP8
bmu.length_note: A bmu entry declares length without the BMU byte, so the encoded size is length+1
bmu.notes: Three ranges are used: 0x00-0x0F transcendental functions, 0x20-0x2D big-integer arithmetic, 0x40-0x42 matrix operations. The remaining 223 bytes are reserved and raise #UDI.

ciu.sub_opcode_usage: none: the ciu space gives every mnemonic its own opcode byte and no format contains SOP or SOP8
ciu.length_note: A ciu entry declares length without the CIU byte, so the encoded size is length+1
ciu.notes: Used bytes are 0x00-0x02 (SHA-3 sponge: absorb, finalize, raw Keccak-f) and 0x10-0x11 (Poly1305 MAC and ChaCha block). The remaining 251 bytes are reserved and raise #UDI. The crypto family also owns base 0xC0-0xC5, so the CIU executes instructions in two spaces.

summary.breakdown: base 191 of 208 in use (17 reserved), escape1 6 of 256, escape2 0 of 256, xtu 6 of 256, bmu 33 of 256, ciu 5 of 256
summary.note: Six decode spaces exist and each has its own opcode universe, so encoding identity is the triple (decode_space, opcode, sub_opcode). Five spaces carry instructions; escape2 is reserved in its entirety. The 241 in-use opcode bytes carry the 555 instructions because a base-space primary can group up to 16 SOP variants under one byte, with 0x5D counted as in use for the relocated v1 SAR.

0x17.note: reserved by A_core so the convert family can grow a 64-bit register-pair converter without disturbing the layout; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x1D.note: reserved inside the C_sys memory range (0x1A-0x1F); the delivered memory family uses 0x1A-0x1C; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x1E.note: reserved inside the C_sys memory range (0x1A-0x1F); the delivered memory family uses 0x1A-0x1C; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x1F.note: reserved inside the C_sys memory range (0x1A-0x1F); the delivered memory family uses 0x1A-0x1C; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x3F.note: unallocated: no owner claims 0x3F in allocation.json, v1 left it free and no v2 part uses it; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x50.note: one primary shared by several v1 categories; the v1 layout groups them here and v2 keeps every encoding

0x5B.note: v1 booked COPYIP and SAR on 0x5B without a sub-opcode field; allocation.v1_fixes relocates SAR to 0x5D, so 0x5B holds COPYIP alone in v2 (v1 defect fix 4)

0x5D.note: v1 defect fix 4: logic.SAR is relocated here from 0x5B by allocation.v1_fixes. The entry is part of the v1 instruction set and is carried by the integrator, not authored by any of the three parts, so it is in use even though no part file defines it.

0x67.note: reserved by A_core because multi-word 64-bit shifts are already expressible with SHLD, SHRD and the ADDC/SUBC carry chains; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0x7F.note: reserved by A_core as the home for a future conditional indirect transfer family, keeping SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC and TSTCC together in 0x8F; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBA.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBB.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBC.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBD.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBE.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xBF.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec floating-point range (0xB0-0xBF) for a future FP extension; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xC6.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec crypto range (0xC0-0xC7); a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xC7.note: reserved inside the B_fpvec crypto range (0xC0-0xC7); a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xCE.note: reserved inside the C_sys range (0xC8-0xCF); the delivered atomic and transaction families use 0xC8-0xCD; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

0xCF.note: reserved inside the C_sys range (0xC8-0xCF); the delivered atomic and transaction families use 0xC8-0xCD; a decode of this opcode raises #UDI

fault.description: A fault is reported before the faulting instruction has changed architectural state. The return address on the interrupt frame is the address of the faulting instruction itself, so the handler either repairs the cause and re-executes it or abandons it. Every fault in this architecture is precise: all results older than the faulting instruction are visible, the faulting instruction has no visible result, and no younger instruction has a result.

trap.description: A trap is reported after the trapping instruction has completed. The return address on the interrupt frame is the address of the next instruction, so re-executing from the return address does not repeat the trapped event. Software interrupts (INT, BRK, SYSENT/SYSCALL) are traps by construction: v1 INT already pushes the following instruction, and v2 keeps that rule for every gate that is entered from software.
trap.return_address: address of the instruction after the trapped instruction

abort.description: An abort reports a condition that prevents the core from knowing which instruction was executing, so the saved state is not resumable and the handler must rebuild the context or reset the machine. #DF is the only abort in v2; #MCC and #NMI use interrupt-style delivery with the next-instruction return address because a machine check may happen between instructions.
abort.return_address: not resumable; the frame is recorded for diagnosis only

#BRK.note: BRK is a one-byte v1 instruction and keeps its behaviour: enter vector 0 and resume after BRK.

#DIV.retry: yes, after fixing the divisor or replaying with a different register value
raised_by: v1 MUL and SDIV divide-by-zero paths
#DIV.note: The divisor is unchanged and the dividend register is unchanged, so the fault is restartable.

raised_by: debug trigger with the NMI bit set in the BPSET control word
#NMI.note: NMI ignores IF and is delivered even inside a transaction, which aborts the transaction.

#HLT.note: HALT stops the core; vector 3 is the notification path to a monitor that wants to observe the halt.

#MCC.note: Highest priority; when the MCE status flag is clear a machine check is reported but execution may continue.

#MAV.retry: yes for a protection fault, no for a hardware violation
#MAV.note: v1 already defines this vector for an invalid access; v2 adds the error code described below and a precise restart.

#UDI.retry: no, unless the handler emulates the instruction
raised_by: a reserved ESZ, MO, SPB or RM code
an escaped-space instruction with its escape prefix missing
#UDI.note: The instruction must not have changed state. #UDI is declared on 233 of the 399 v2 entries (every entry whose encoding leaves a reserved code field) and on the v1 control ops that decode reserved fields, so an emulator hook works: the return address still names the undecoded instruction.

#PGF.retry: yes, after the handler installs or repairs the mapping
#PGF.note: PREFETCH and PREFETCHW never raise #PGF and never fault: a hint that misses, or that names an unmapped address, simply does nothing.

raised_by: an instruction executed below its mode floor
a write to a reserved bit of a control register, an MSR or an IDT gate
a selector that is not a valid table index
VMENTER or VMRUN executed with VME=1
VMEXIT or VMCALL executed with VME=0
