XEND, XABORT or XSUSPEND executed with TXE=0
a debug register index above 7 in BPSET, BPCLR, WCHSET, WCHCLR or DBGREAD
a protection-key operation on an unallocated key in WRPKRU
#GP.note: v2 turns every one of these into a #GP fault so that a privilege violation is always reported: an instruction that a lower level may not execute fails at the decode stage instead of leaving the failure for the kernel to discover later.

raised_by: a second exception during delivery of a first exception
a gate with the present bit clear, or with a reserved bit set, while delivering any exception
#DF.note: Always pushes error code 0. A fault during #DF delivery is a shutdown: the core stops and waits for RESET.

#AC.retry: yes, if the handler emulates the unaligned access
#AC.note: Raised only when the AC flag in the flags register is set; with AC=0 an unaligned access is performed by the LSU as two accesses and is not single-copy atomic.

#BP.retry: no; resume after the breakpointing instruction when the handler clears TF or the breakpoint
raised_by: BPSET-programmed execution breakpoint on an instruction fetch
STEP with TF=1 at the end of each instruction
#BP.note: Debug traps are delivered only when the DTE or TF enable conditions described in debugging_model hold.

raised_by: a trap-on-overflow request armed through the debug control word
#OF.note: The OF flag is read, not modified, by the delivery.

#SYS.note: The fast system-entry path SYSENT uses SYSENT_BASE rather than the IDT, so vector 13 is the gate used when a program deliberately goes through the IDT.

#VC.retry: yes; the handler is the hypervisor and re-enters the guest when the condition is resolved
raised_by: VMFUNC when the service is not available
an EPT violation or an EPT misconfiguration during guest execution
an invalid guest-state load in VMENTER or VMRUN
#VC.note: The error code REASON field carries the virtualization exit reason defined in virtualization_model.

raised_by: SHSTKRET with a shadow stack that does not match the return address
SHSTKPUSH or SHSTKPOP with SSE=0 or a shadow-stack overflow
KEYGEN or KEYLOAD on a slot the caller may not use
an SXE violation (supervisor access to a user page)
ENDBR at a target that was not reached by an indirect branch
a RESET or ATTEST attempt without platform authority
#SEC.note: Raised instead of #GP whenever the violation is a security-policy violation rather than a privilege-level or encoding error.

#SI0.note: #SI1..#SI15 are identical in shape at vectors 49..63 and exist so a driver can multiplex sub-devices without consuming a hardware vector.

vector_assignment.0-7: v1 exceptions, unchanged in number and in meaning: #BRK 0, #DIV 1, #NMI 2, #HLT 3, #MCC 4, #MAV 5, #UDI 6, #PGF 7.
vector_assignment.40-47: RESERVED. A gate installed at any of these vectors is accepted but no source in v2 raises it; a spurious interrupt there is a no-op that returns.
vector_assignment.48-63: software vectors #SI0..#SI15, reachable only through INT with an immediate vector operand.
vector_assignment.64-255: RESERVED for future expansion; INT with an immediate above 63 does not fault and is delivered to the gate at that index, so an operating system may use the space freely.

error_code_layout.delivered_when: the gate descriptor has the EC bit set (bit 12 of the attribute word); the code is pushed last, so it lies below the return address

bits.name: EXT
bits.meaning: 1 when the exception came from an external source (device, another core, hypervisor) and 0 when it is synchronous with the instruction named by the return address.

bits.name: W
bits.meaning: 1 when the faulting memory access was a write, 0 for a read or an instruction fetch.

bits.name: U
bits.meaning: 1 when the access came from L0, L1 or L2, 0 when it came from L3 and above.

bits.name: X
bits.meaning: 1 when the fault was raised on an instruction fetch, 0 for a data access or for a cause that involves no memory access.

bits.name: SZ
bits.meaning: Access size code: 0 = byte, 1 = word, 2 = dword, 3 = qword, 7 = no memory access. Codes 4..6 are reserved and read as 7.

bits.name: PKEY
bits.meaning: The protection key of the access when the fault is a key violation, otherwise 0.

bits.name: REASON
bits.meaning: Vector-specific reason. For #VC this is the 16-bit virtualization exit reason of virtualization_model.vmexit_reasons. For #GP it is the selector or table index involved, or 0. For #PGF raised by an explicit MMU instruction it is the ASID. For #AC it is the low 16 bits of the address that was not aligned.

error_code_layout.df_error_code: #DF always pushes the value 0x00000000 so a double-fault handler can use the same frame shape as an error-code gate without inspecting a code that carries no information.

exception_model.priority_rule: When two sources are pending at the same instruction boundary the one earlier in the list is delivered first. The order is fixed by the architecture, and a gate descriptor may only raise a pending source above a lower-priority one by using its PRIORITY field within one class (device IRQs are ordered by PRIORITY, then by vector number). An instruction raises at most one of #PGF, #MAV, #AC, #UDI or #DIV, so the relative order among those is unobservable from software, but the model fixes it so that a fault-injection test is deterministic.

legacy_layout.selected_when: bit 2 of cr0 (IDTG) is 0, which is the reset value
legacy_layout.behaviour: exactly the v1 reference implementation layout: MODIDT writes the 4-byte handler address at IDT_BASE + sign_extend(OF8) and INT/IRET use it unchanged. No error code is ever pushed and no attribute is checked, so every v1 program keeps its meaning.

extended_layout.selected_when: bit 2 of cr0 (IDTG) is 1; only L3 and above may set it, and clearing it restores the legacy layout
extended_layout.word0: bits 31:0 handler linear address; identical in meaning and position to the legacy word0, so a table built by v1 code remains readable at every even vector and the first dword of every gate is still the address

word1_bits.name: TARGET_MODE
word1_bits.meaning: The L level the handler runs at (0..7). A value lower than the current level is allowed; a value that the current level may not reach is a #GP at dispatch.

word1_bits.name: STACK_SEL
word1_bits.meaning: 0 = build the frame on the current stack; 1..7 = switch to the stack recorded for that privilege level before pushing, which is how an L0-to-L3 transition gets a kernel stack.

word1_bits.name: P
word1_bits.meaning: Present. A clear present bit turns the delivery into #DF.

word1_bits.name: GATE_TYPE
word1_bits.meaning: 0 = interrupt gate (IF is cleared on entry), 1 = trap gate (IF unchanged), 2 = call gate (no flags word is pushed), 3..7 reserved and turn the delivery into #DF.

word1_bits.name: EC
word1_bits.meaning: The gate expects an error code; the core pushes the 4-byte code described in error_code_layout below the return address.

word1_bits.name: RESERVED
word1_bits.meaning: Must be zero; a set bit turns the delivery into #DF.

word1_bits.name: PRIORITY
word1_bits.meaning: Selection priority among pending sources of the same class (0 = lowest). Device IRQ gates normally use 1..15.

word1_bits.name: PKEY
word1_bits.meaning: The protection key applied while the handler runs; 0 means the default key of the target mode.

word1_bits.name: RESERVED
word1_bits.meaning: Must be zero; a set bit turns the delivery into #DF.

gate_descriptor.idt_instructions: SETIDT sets IDT_BASE, LDIDT reads it into rb, MODIDT writes a handler address at IDT_BASE + sign_extend(OF8). All three are v1 instructions with unchanged encodings; MODIDT addresses the legacy 4-byte slot, and code that runs with IDTG=1 must build gates with ordinary stores (ST) so that the attribute word is written explicitly.

stack_frame.growth: The stack grows downward: each pushed word decrements sp by 4 and is stored little-endian at the new sp.
push_order: error code (4 bytes, only when gate EC = 1)
stack_frame.layout_with_error_code: [sp+0] error code, [sp+4] return address, [sp+8] flags register
stack_frame.return_address_rule: fault delivery pushes the address of the faulting instruction; trap and software delivery pushes the address of the next instruction. This is exactly the v1 reference rule (INT, BRK and SYSCALL push the next instruction, _fault pushes the faulting one), so no v1 handler changes behaviour.
stack_frame.iret_rule: IRET pops the return address and then the flags register. It never pops an error code, so a handler for an EC gate must discard the code itself, for example with ADDSP 4 or by loading sp from a saved value before IRET.
stack_frame.alignment: sp is 4-byte aligned at every gate entry; the frame of a byte-sized faulting access is still made of 4-byte words.
stack_frame.nested_frames: Delivery does not save general registers, segment-like state or floating-point state. A handler that needs them uses v1 PUSHTR/POPTR or v2 VSTATE for the vector file.

double_fault_escalation.rule: Any exception that is raised while the core is delivering another exception is escalated to #DF, except #MCC and #NMI which are escalated to shutdown directly.
double_fault_escalation.delivery_failures: A gate with P=0, a reserved attribute bit set, a reserved GATE_TYPE, an unreachable TARGET_MODE, or a stack push that itself faults all turn into #DF.
double_fault_escalation.df_priority: #DF outranks every exception except #MCC and #NMI, so it is delivered even when the original condition was a #GP.
double_fault_escalation.df_reentry: An exception raised while delivering #DF is a shutdown: the core stops fetching, records the shutdown cause in the machine-check state and waits for RESET. v2 does not define a triple-fault vector because there is nothing left to deliver to.
double_fault_escalation.recovery: A #DF handler must not rely on the saved context. It either rebuilds the task from kernel state or calls RESET.

delivery_sequence: 1. Select the highest-priority pending source at an instruction boundary (or, for a fault, at the point the fault is detected).
2. Read the gate at IDT_BASE + vector * (4 or 8) according to cr0.IDTG.
3. In the legacy layout: push flags, push the return address, set ip to the gate word, leave the mode unchanged, and continue.
4. In the extended layout: check the present bit, the reserved bits, the GATE_TYPE and the TARGET_MODE; any failure is #DF.
5. If STACK_SEL is nonzero, switch to the stack recorded for that level before pushing anything.
6. Push flags, then the return address, then the error code when EC=1.
7. For GATE_TYPE 0 clear IF; for GATE_TYPE 1 leave IF unchanged; for GATE_TYPE 2 do not push flags at all.
8. Apply the gate protection key and switch to TARGET_MODE.
9. Set ip to the handler address and resume fetching at the new mode.

masking_and_nesting.IF: A maskable interrupt (vectors 16-63 through a device source, and the software vectors) is delivered only when IF=1. CLI clears IF and STI sets it; both are v1 one-byte instructions with unchanged encodings.
masking_and_nesting.nmi: #NMI ignores IF, is delivered once per edge and cannot be masked by a handler; a second edge while the first is being handled is latched and delivered after the first completes.
masking_and_nesting.interrupt_gate_effect: GATE_TYPE 0 clears IF so the handler runs to its own IRET without re-entering; GATE_TYPE 1 leaves IF set, which is the correct choice for handlers that can tolerate nesting.
masking_and_nesting.exceptions_below_if0: Faults and traps are delivered regardless of IF; only the flag-register snapshot differs.
masking_and_nesting.txe_interaction: An interrupt delivered while TXE=1 aborts the transaction: buffered writes are discarded, the abort code is recorded as external, and control passes to the XBEGIN fallback address. The interrupt is then delivered normally.
masking_and_nesting.vme_interaction: When VME=1 the core delivers the interrupt to the guest unless the host has configured interrupt exiting, in which case the event becomes a #VC with reason 'external interrupt'.

v1_compatibility.vectors: Vectors 0-33 keep their numbers and their names, and the v1 descriptions are reproduced verbatim in interrupt_vectors.
v1_compatibility.layout: With cr0.IDTG=0 the IDT is the v1 4-byte handler array, the frame is flags plus return address, and IRET pops exactly those two words. A v1 program that calls SETIDT, fills handlers with MODIDT and uses INT/IRET executes unchanged.
v1_compatibility.new_vectors: Vectors 8-15 were unassigned in v1, so assigning #GP there changes no v1 behaviour: a v1 program never triggers one of the new conditions because every new instruction is decoded as an unallocated opcode in v1.
v1_compatibility.error_codes: Error codes exist only under the extended layout. Because cr0.IDTG is 0 at reset, a v1 binary never sees a 12-byte frame.

memory_model.overview: Hayneko_Arch32S v2 has a weak (relaxed) memory model with explicit fences. A single core always observes its own accesses in program order, and every access to one address is observed in one order by all agents, but two accesses to different addresses may become visible in an order different from program order unless a fence or an ordering annotation forbids it. This is the same model v1 had implicitly, now written down so that an operating system, an SMP implementation and a device driver can rely on it.
ordering_rules: Load -> load: two loads may complete out of order and may be observed out of order by another agent.
Store -> store: two stores to different addresses may become visible out of order; two stores to the same address are always observed in program order.
Load -> store: a younger store may become visible before an older load has completed.
Store -> load: a younger load may be satisfied before an older store to a different address has become visible (store-to-load forwarding is allowed only when the addresses match).
Load/store -> fence: a fence orders every access before it against every access after it, within the domains selected by its IM8 operand.
Same address: all agents agree on one modification order per address, and a load returns the value of the latest store in that order.
Instruction fetch is ordered by SFENCE and LFENCE but not by MEMO hints; code patched by a store becomes visible after SFENCE followed by ICACHEINV on the affected line.

WB.name: Write-back
WB.description: Default for ordinary memory. Cached in L1D, L2 and L3, allocated on a read miss, written back when evicted, and snooped for coherence. Speculative and out-of-order accesses are allowed.

WT.name: Write-through
WT.description: Cached for reads but every store goes to memory and to L2 immediately. Ordered like WB for reads; a store is not reordered before an older load.

WC.name: Write-combining
WC.description: Used for frame buffers. Stores are collected in the eight write-combining buffers and merged into full 32-byte sectors; reads from WC memory are uncached and strongly ordered against the buffers, and SFENCE drains the buffers.

UC.name: Uncacheable
UC.description: No caching, no speculation, no reordering: every access goes to the device in program order. Used for memory-mapped control registers.

UC-.name: Uncacheable, write-combining allowed
UC-.description: Reads are uncached and ordered; writes may coalesce in the write-combining buffers. SFENCE drains.

reserved.description: A memory-type code of 5, 6 or 7 in a present page-table entry is a page-structure error and raises #GP with the linear address in the error-code REASON field.

LFENCE.semantics: No load issued after the fence may be observed before a load issued before it, and no later load may bypass the fence speculatively. It does not order stores.
LFENCE.im8_domain: bit 0 loads, bit 1 stores, bit 2 I/O, bit 3 instruction fetch; selected domains are also ordered, bits 7:4 must be zero and a nonzero value in them raises #UDI.

SFENCE.semantics: Every store issued before the fence is globally visible before any store issued after it. It drains write-combining buffers and non-temporal stores and is the publishing barrier for a producer that already made its data stores to WB memory.

MFENCE.semantics: Full barrier: orders all loads and all stores before it against all accesses after it, drains the write-combining buffers and waits for outstanding snoops.

barriers.strength: The SPB nibble keeps its speculation-barrier meaning on the fence instructions as well: SPB 0 leaves speculation alone and only enforces execution ordering, SPB 2 additionally kills dependent speculative loads, SPB 3 serializes the pipeline. The encodings declared by C_sys are unchanged; the barrier strength codes themselves are defined in security_model.speculation_barrier_codes.
barriers.atomic_ordering: LDLK, STLK, CAS and every AMO carry an MO nibble that gives them an acquire/release class without a separate fence. See atomic_model.ordering_codes.
barriers.prefix_form: The MEMO prefix (0xF9, payload MO,CH) may attach an ordering class to an ordinary load or store. It can only strengthen: a MEMO prefix asking for a weaker class than the instruction already has is #UDI.

atomicity_and_alignment.single_copy: A naturally aligned access of 1, 2 or 4 bytes is single-copy atomic: every other agent observes the whole value or none of it. No scalar v2 instruction performs an 8-byte data access, because a general register is 32 bits wide and nothing in the ISA names a pair of them as one operand; the QWORD element size exists only inside the vector unit, where a vector load touches up to 32 bytes and single-copy atomicity is per element rather than per instruction.
atomicity_and_alignment.alignment_requirement: Natural alignment means the address is a multiple of the access size. With the AC flag set, a misaligned access raises #AC and performs no memory reference. With AC clear, the LSU splits the access into byte-enables and the operation is not single-copy atomic.
atomicity_and_alignment.atomics_are_strict: Every atomic instruction (LDLK, STLK, CAS, the AMO family) requires natural alignment unconditionally: a misaligned atomic raises #AC even when the AC flag is clear, because there is no split-lock emulation in v2.
atomicity_and_alignment.sizes: The atomic family is defined for ESZ 0, 1 and 2 (byte, word, dword). ESZ 3 would need an 8-byte atom built from a 32-bit general register pair with no encoding for the second register, so it is reserved and raises #UDI. Vector and FP families use ESZ 3 as QWORD because their registers are wide enough.
atomicity_and_alignment.cross_cacheline: An access that crosses a 32-byte sector boundary is performed as two accesses and is not single-copy atomic; an access that crosses a page boundary with one half unmapped raises #PGF and performs no part of the access.

endianness.default: Little-endian. Multi-byte values are stored least significant byte first, and instruction encodings are always little-endian.
endianness.be_flag: The BE flag (bit 12 of the flags register) switches data accesses to big-endian for loads, stores, string operations, vector memory operations and atomics. Instruction fetch, page tables, descriptor tables and the interrupt frame are unaffected by BE.
endianness.mixed_access: Changing BE requires a serialize (WRFLAGS or SETMODE already serializes). A store performed with BE=0 and a load performed with BE=1 to the same address return byte-swapped values, and no hardware conversion is provided: that is the programmer's contract.
endianness.device_registers: Device MMIO pages are defined little-endian; a driver must clear BE before touching them.

linear_address_split.31:30: L2 index, 4 entries, table page 4 KiB with entries 0..3 meaningful
linear_address_split.29:21: L1 index, 512 entries, 2 MiB span per entry
linear_address_split.20:12: L0 index, 512 entries, 4 KiB span per entry

virtual_memory.walk: The walker reads three tables. At L2 a present entry with PS=1 maps a 1 GiB page and the walk stops; at L1 a present entry with PS=1 maps a 2 MiB page and the walk stops; at L0 the entry maps a 4 KiB page. The physical base of a large page is taken from the bits above the page size and the low bits of the base field are ignored.
virtual_memory.v1_extension: v1 defined two-level paging with 4 KiB pages. v2 keeps the low half of every entry bit-compatible with the v1 32-bit entry and adds a second word for keys, memory type and execute permission, so a v1-era table read through a v2 walker still yields the present, writable, accessed and dirty bits where v1 put them, and remains usable with the default memory type and no execute-disable.
virtual_memory.table_page_faults: A not-present entry, a rights violation or a protection-key violation raises #PGF with the error code of exception_model.error_code_layout. A present entry with a reserved field set, a reserved memory type, or PS=1 at L0 raises #GP as a page-structure error.

word0.name: P
word0.meaning: Present. When clear the walk stops and #PGF is raised.

word0.name: W
word0.meaning: Writable. A store through a read-only entry raises #PGF with the W bit set in the error code.

word0.name: U
word0.meaning: User. When clear only L3 and above may access the page, and an access from L0..L2 raises #PGF.

word0.name: PWT
word0.meaning: Write-through memory type for this page (overrides the default WB).

word0.name: PCD
word0.meaning: Cache disable for this page: the page is treated as UC.

word0.name: A
word0.meaning: Accessed. Set by hardware on the first access, and by PGWALK in software walks.

word0.name: D
word0.meaning: Dirty. Set by hardware on the first store. UNMAP clears it, which is why an unmap also drops a dirty line.

word0.name: PS
word0.meaning: Page size: 0 = 4 KiB at L0, 1 = a large page at L1 (2 MiB) or L2 (1 GiB). PS=1 at L0 is a page-structure error (#GP).

word0.name: G
word0.meaning: Global. The translation survives an INVTLB that keeps global entries.

word0.name: RESERVED
word0.meaning: Must be zero; a set bit is a page-structure error (#GP).

word0.name: BASE
word0.meaning: Physical frame number of the 4 KiB page, or the high bits of the base of a large page.

word1.name: KEY
word1.meaning: Protection key of the page, 0..15. Checked when PKE=1 against the rights word in cr6.

word1.name: MEMTYPE
word1.meaning: Memory type code from memory_types (0 WB, 1 WT, 2 WC, 3 UC, 4 UC-). PWT/PCD in word0 take precedence when set.

word1.name: NXE
word1.meaning: No-execute. When set an instruction fetch from the page raises #PGF with the X bit set in the error code. v1 has no execute permission and every v1 page is executable because NXE resets to 0.

word1.name: RESERVED
word1.meaning: Must be zero; a set bit is a page-structure error (#GP).

word1.name: SW
word1.meaning: Available to software. The MMU never reads it and MAP/UNMAP never write it.

pte_layout.asid_tagging: A cached translation is tagged with the ASID of the address space that installed it, so a context switch does not need a flush; ASID 0 is reserved for the global/hypervisor context and is never assigned to a process.

structures.name: L2 unified TLB
structures.associativity: 8-way, shared by instruction and data, per-ASID

tlb.miss_path: A miss allocates in the L2 TLB and, for a normal access, in the L1 TLB; a large-page entry may be replicated into 512 4 KiB slots or kept as one entry with a range tag, and both behaviours are architecturally identical because software only observes the invalidation instructions.

invalidation.INVLPG: Invalidates the entry that translates SR1 + sign_extend(OF8), keeping global entries unless the global-flush bit (bit 0 of cr9) is set. Latency 30 cycles, defined for one address only.
invalidation.INVTLB: MO 0 flushes every non-global entry of every ASID, MO 1 flushes the ASID in SEG, MO 2 flushes only global entries, MO 3 flushes everything including global entries; MO 4..15 raise #UDI. Requires L3.
invalidation.INVEPT: Flushes EPT-derived translations, including nested combinations, and is only legal with VME=0; a descriptor that is not a valid EPT root raises #VC.

tlb.cost: A TLB shootdown to another core is expressed as an inter-processor interrupt on a #SI vector; v2 defines no implicit shootdown, so the operating system must issue it and wait before reusing the page.

protection_keys.rights_word: cr6 bits 31:0 hold PKRU: for key k, bit 2k is AD (access disable) and bit 2k+1 is WD (write disable). cr6 bits 47:32 hold the 16-bit allocation bitmap, and bits above 47 are reserved.
protection_keys.checking: When the PKE status flag is 1, every data access is checked against the rights of the page key and the current key. AD raises #SEC on read or write, WD raises #SEC on write only, and an access to an unallocated key raises #SEC. When PKE is 0 no check happens.
protection_keys.selecting_a_key: The SEC prefix (0xFC, payload SPB,PKEY) applies a key to the next instruction; PKEY 0 means the default key of the current mode.
protection_keys.management: MKEYALLOC reserves a key and returns its index in DRG, MKEYFREE returns it, RDPKRU reads PKRU into DRG and sets PKE, WRPKRU writes PKRU from SR1, sets PKE and serializes. WRPKRU also raises #SEC when SR1 grants a right on an unallocated key.
protection_keys.interaction: Keys are orthogonal to the U bit: the key check happens after the present and rights checks, so an access to a not-present page raises #PGF and only a mapped, permitted page can raise #SEC for its key.

mmu_instruction_interaction.explicit_operations: MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC and MKEYFREE are explicit MMU operations in the escape1 space. A kernel installs a mapping without storing to the page table itself, and can walk a table without faulting.
mmu_instruction_interaction.ordering: MAP and EPTMAP write the leaf entry and then invalidate the cached translations of the page before the next instruction retires, so the mapping is visible to the very next access. PROTECT rewrites only the rights field. UNMAP clears present, clears dirty and drops any dirty line of the page.
mmu_instruction_interaction.page_directory_base: cr3 holds the physical base of the L2 table, exactly as in v1 where MOVCTRL moved cr3. SETPGT writes it with the walk-inhibit and global-enable bits in the low four bits of the argument, and GETPGT reads it back.
mmu_instruction_interaction.walk_inhibit: While page walking is inhibited every linear address is physical, which is the state a boot loader runs in and the state the v1 reference implementation always used.
mmu_instruction_interaction.fault_precedence: During one access the MMU reports the first failure in this order: page-structure error (#GP), not present (#PGF), write to a read-only page (#PGF), user/supervisor violation (#PGF), NXE on a fetch (#PGF), protection key (#SEC), alignment (#AC). The order matters because only one exception is delivered per access.

coherence_and_snooping.protocol: A write-invalidate MESI protocol runs on L1D and is extended to L2 with a directory at L3. Snoops are never reordered against a fence.
coherence_and_snooping.state_transitions: A load miss allocates Shared unless a write is imminent; an AMO or STLK takes the line Exclusive before performing the operation; a store to a Shared line invalidates the other copies before the store becomes visible.
coherence_and_snooping.single_core_note: The v2 reference implementation is single-core, so every rule above degenerates to program order; the protocol is specified so that a multi-core implementation has one legal behaviour instead of many.

L2.write_policy: write-back, write-allocate, non-inclusive of L1D (victim cache)
L2.note: The 32 KiB 4-way 64-byte L1 and the 1 MiB 8-way 256-byte L2 are the v1 parameters, unchanged; v2 splits L1 into an instruction and a data cache of the same size and adds L3.

L3.note: Shared by all cores. Because it is inclusive of L2, evicting a line from L3 back-invalidates it in L2, which lets the directory serve as the snoop filter.

sector_granularity.rule: The architectural granularity of a cache operation is the 32-byte sector, not the line.
sector_granularity.why: CLZERO zeroes the 32-byte sector containing its operand, MONITOR watches the 32-byte sector containing its operand and ZEROIZE invalidates the sectors it overwrote. A 64-byte L1 line is two sectors and a 256-byte L2 line is eight, so all three instructions are expressible without forcing one line size on every level.
sector_granularity.fill: A sector fill transfers 32 bytes; a full-line fill is eight sector fills at L2 and L3 and two at L1.

replacement.L1: Tree pseudo-LRU over the 4 ways, updated on allocation and on a hit.
replacement.L2: Two-bit RRIP with a 1/32 set-dueling counter that switches between SRRIP and BRRIP.
replacement.L3: Two-bit RRIP with way prediction; the predicted way is tried first, and a misprediction costs no extra latency because both ways are read in parallel.
replacement.victim_path: An L1D eviction is inserted into L2 because L2 is a victim cache; an L2 eviction is inserted into L3 and, being inclusive, back-invalidates the L2 copy.

hint_codes.field: CH (4 bits). Used by PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, LDNT, STNT and by the CH half of the MEMO prefix payload.

codes.name: NTA
codes.meaning: Non-temporal: allocate in the smallest level that can hold the line and mark it as the next eviction candidate.

codes.name: T0
codes.meaning: Temporal, all levels: fetch into L1, L2 and L3. This is the default when a program supplies no hint.

codes.name: T1
codes.meaning: Fetch into L2 and L3 but not L1, so the prefetch does not displace L1 contents.

codes.name: T2
codes.meaning: Fetch into L3 only.

codes.name: W
codes.meaning: Prepare for a write: fetch the line and take it Exclusive (read-for-ownership).

codes.name: EVICT_FIRST
codes.meaning: Mark the line as the next victim in its set.

codes.name: EVICT_LAST
codes.meaning: Protect the line from replacement until the hint is superseded.

codes.name: DEMOTE
codes.meaning: Write back a modified line and keep it clean and Shared.

codes.name: ZERO
codes.meaning: Allocate the sector in the zero state without a memory read; this is what CLZERO uses.

codes.name: RESERVED
codes.meaning: Ignored by every instruction that only hints (PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, LDNT, STNT). CACHECTL selects its operation with MO, not CH, and raises #UDI for the codes it reserves.

codes.name: BYPASS
codes.meaning: Do not allocate in any level; the access goes straight through.

prefetch.instructions: PREFETCH (read, opcode 0x1C sub_opcode 0x0) and PREFETCHW (write-intent, opcode 0x1C sub_opcode 0x1), both format OPC,SOP,0x0,SR1,OF8,CH and 4 bytes.
prefetch.never_faults: A prefetch of an unmapped, unaligned or protected address does nothing and raises no exception, which is why neither instruction declares a fault.
prefetch.hardware_prefetcher: Sixteen independent stride streams per core feed the L2, one stream is dedicated to the instruction stream, and the prefetcher is inhibited for UC and UC- pages and while a transaction is open.

nontemporal_and_streaming.stores: STNT, MOVSN and STOSN store through the write-combining path without allocating a line, using CH to select the eviction class. Eight write-combining buffers of 32 bytes are drained by SFENCE, MFENCE, a serializing instruction or a buffer-full condition.
nontemporal_and_streaming.loads: LDNT fetches without allocating for reuse and marks the sector as the first eviction candidate.
nontemporal_and_streaming.guarantee: A non-temporal store is still coherent: a later load from the same address forwards the buffered data or waits for the buffer to drain. The hint changes performance, never the memory model.

CACHECTL.encoding: opcode 0x1C, sub_opcode 0x3, format OPC,SOP,0x0,SR1,OF8,MO, mode L3

mo_codes.0: INVD - invalidate the line, discarding a dirty copy
mo_codes.1: CLWB - write back the line and keep it clean and resident
mo_codes.2: CLFLUSH - write back and invalidate the line
mo_codes.3: CLEAN - write back if modified and keep it resident
mo_codes.4: WBINVD - write back and invalidate the whole data cache
mo_codes.5: INVD-ALL - invalidate the whole data cache without write-back

CLWBI.encoding: opcode 0x9A, sub_opcode 0x4, format OPC,SOP,SR1,OF8, mode L3
CLWBI.semantics: Fixed-purpose write-back and invalidate of the line containing SR1 + sign_extend(OF8). It is the same operation as CACHECTL MO 2; it exists as its own opcode because a device driver uses it far more often than the generic form.

ICACHEINV.semantics: Invalidates the instruction cache lines of the addressed range and refetches; it must follow SFENCE after a code patch.

CLZERO.semantics: Zeroes the 32-byte sector containing SR1 + sign_extend(OF8) with non-allocating stores and the CH hint.

ZEROIZE.semantics: Zeroes a buffer that cannot be reordered or elided and then invalidates the sectors, which is the only architecturally guaranteed way to erase a secret from the cache hierarchy.

cache_model.coherence_note: All hint and maintenance instructions are local to the issuing core except CACHECTL MO 4 and 5, which flush only that core's cache; a multi-core flush requires an inter-processor interrupt so that each core executes its own flush.

atomic_model.overview: Atomicity is provided at three levels: load-linked/store-conditional for arbitrary read-modify-write sequences, compare-and-swap and a family of AMOs for the common updates, and best-effort transactional memory for whole regions. All three are single-copy atomic per naturally aligned element, all three take an ordering class from an MO nibble instead of requiring a separate fence, and none of them is emulated.

LDLK.semantics: Loads 1<<ESZ bytes from [SR1], zero-extends into DRG and arms the exclusive monitor for that address and size.

STLK.semantics: Stores the low 1<<ESZ bytes of DRG to [SR1] and sets ZF when the monitor still covers the address; clears ZF and stores nothing otherwise. The monitor is always invalidated afterwards.

CLREX.semantics: Invalidates the local exclusive monitor without storing. A context switch or an exception delivery clears it anyway, so CLREX only matters inside hand-written code.

llsc.monitor_granularity: One 32-byte sector per core, tracked by address plus size. Any store from the same core to that sector, any snoop that invalidates it, any exception delivery, any VMENTER or VMEXIT and any XBEGIN/XEND clears the monitor.
llsc.retry_pattern: LDLK, compute, STLK, branch back on ZF=0. Because the monitor is invalidated by every conflicting store, a retry loop makes progress: STLK cannot fail spuriously more than once per intervening store, and the hardware guarantees a successful STLK for a thread that is the only writer (see forward_progress).

cas.semantics: Reads the ESZ-sized value at [SR1]; when it equals the low ESZ bytes of DRG it stores the low ESZ bytes of SR2 and sets ZF, otherwise it zero-extends the observed value into DRG and clears ZF. CAS is a full RMW: it needs no LDLK and survives a context switch in the middle.
cas.use: CAS is the primitive for lock-free stacks, treaps and reference counting; LDLK/STLK is cheaper for a simple counter because it needs no compare value.

ordering_codes.field: The 4-bit MO nibble carried by every atomic instruction, and the MO half of the MEMO prefix payload.

codes.name: RLX
codes.meaning: Relaxed: atomicity without ordering. Any other access may be reordered around it.

codes.name: ACQ
codes.meaning: Acquire: no later load or store may be observed before the atomic operation.

codes.name: REL
codes.meaning: Release: no earlier load or store may be observed after the atomic operation.

codes.name: ACQ_REL
codes.meaning: Both directions.

codes.name: SEQ_CST
codes.meaning: A single total order over all SEQ_CST atomics in the system, on top of ACQ_REL.

codes.name: RESERVED
codes.meaning: Reserved. Because every atomic entry that carries an MO nibble declares #UDI, a reserved class is a #UDI rather than a silent relaxation to RLX.

ordering_codes.prefix_interaction: A MEMO prefix may only strengthen: MEMO MO=SEQ_CST on an RLX AMOADD is legal, while MEMO MO=RLX on an instruction whose own MO is ACQ_REL is #UDI.
ordering_codes.default: The family default is RLX; software that needs ordering must say so in-band or add a fence.

store_form.semantics: Fetch the operand at [SR1], apply the operation with DRG, store the result; the fetched value is discarded and DRG keeps its old value. The operation wraps at the access width; the MIN/MAX forms interpret the value as signed and the U forms as unsigned.

fetch_form.semantics: Identical, except that DRG receives the value that was in memory before the operation. This is the form a lock-free algorithm needs for fetch-and-add on a ticket lock.

amo_classes.timing: All AMOs are latency 12, throughput 8: an AMO takes the line Exclusive, so it costs a snoop round trip and cannot be pipelined with another AMO to the same sector.
amo_classes.no_flags: No AMO modifies a flag. A caller that needs a condition reads the fetch-form result and compares it.

alignment_and_size.rule: Every atomic requires natural alignment and raises #AC when it is not aligned, regardless of the AC flag. The family is defined for ESZ 0..2 (byte, word, dword); ESZ 3 is reserved and raises #UDI because an 8-byte atom cannot be expressed from 32-bit general registers.
alignment_and_size.cacheline: An atomic that would cross a 32-byte sector boundary is impossible because natural alignment of a 4-byte object cannot cross a 4-byte boundary, so no atomic is ever split.
alignment_and_size.lock_prefix: The LOCK prefix on an ordinary load or store promotes it to an atomic RMW for the same size and alignment rules; it is redundant on an instruction that is already atomic and it is illegal on an instruction without a memory operand, where it raises #UDI.

forward_progress.guarantee: A thread that executes LDLK and then STLK with no intervening conflicting access from another thread always succeeds. A conflicting store from another core invalidates the first monitor, which turns into a failed STLK, a retry, and then success because the conflicting store has completed.
forward_progress.bounded_retry: The hardware retries nothing on behalf of software: a failed STLK returns ZF=0 immediately (6 cycles) so a software loop cannot be starved by a hidden hardware retry.
forward_progress.starvation: The architecture does not guarantee lock freedom. It guarantees that between two successful STLKs of an address the monitor was invalidated by a real conflict, so a fairness policy in the firmware can bound the number of retries a thread performs.

transactional_memory.overview: XBEGIN, XEND, XABORT, XTEST and XSUSPEND (opcodes 0xCC and 0xCD) form a best-effort transactional memory. A transaction is a region of code whose stores are buffered and whose reads are tracked; XEND commits all buffered stores atomically, an abort discards them and transfers control to the fallback address that XBEGIN recorded.

xbegin.fallback_address: IP + 4 + sign_extend(O16), that is relative to the END of the XBEGIN instruction and not to its start. This is the one relative transfer in v2 that does not use the address of the instruction itself as its base, and the difference is deliberate: the fallback path is the alternative to entering the transaction, so it must be the instruction after XBEGIN.
xbegin.txe: Sets TXE=1 and takes a checkpoint of the architectural state. Executing XBEGIN while TXE=1 is an abort with code 1, which keeps the nesting depth at one for XBEGIN-initiated nesting.
xbegin.mo_attributes: MO is a transaction attribute nibble: MO[0] = write the 16-bit abort code into ra when the transaction aborts, MO[1] = retry the transaction once automatically after a capacity abort, MO[2] = retry once after a conflict abort, MO[3] reserved and must be written as zero. An implementation that does not support an attribute ignores it; no attribute changes the memory model.

xend.semantics: Commits the buffered stores atomically: every store becomes visible at once to every other agent, then TXE is cleared and the checkpoint is released. XEND with TXE=0 raises #GP. Timing: latency 12.

xabort.semantics: Discards the buffered stores, records the software abort code IM8, clears TXE and jumps to the fallback address. XABORT with TXE=0 raises #GP. The code is a software choice and should be checked by the fallback path.

xtest.semantics: Sets ZF=1 when the thread is inside a transaction and ZF=0 otherwise, and changes no other flag. A retry loop uses XTEST to distinguish an abort from a normal return of the fallback path.

xsuspend.semantics: Suspends speculative execution of the transaction for up to O16 cycles so a conflicting writer can make progress and the transaction can commit instead of aborting. ZF reports whether the suspension completed. XSUSPEND with TXE=0 raises #GP. Timing: latency 30.

conflict_detection.read_set: Every load inside a transaction records the 32-byte sector it touched, so a later store from another agent to that sector aborts the transaction with reason 256 (read-set conflict).
conflict_detection.write_set: Every store inside a transaction is buffered in the L1D and its sector is recorded; a snoop that would take the sector Exclusive or Invalid from another agent aborts with reason 257 (write-set conflict).
conflict_detection.granularity: Conflict detection is at sector granularity, which means false sharing inside a 32-byte sector causes aborts. This is a documented performance property, not a correctness hazard: a false conflict only makes the fallback path run.
conflict_detection.depth: The architectural nesting depth limit is 8. The ninth XBEGIN aborts with code 259. In v2 a nested transaction commits only when its outermost XEND executes; an abort of any level discards the whole nest.
conflict_detection.capacity: A transaction aborts with code 258 when its write set exceeds the 32 KiB L1D, when it executes more than 4096 instructions, or when it performs an I/O access, an MMU operation, or a serializing instruction.
conflict_detection.prohibited_operations: Inside a transaction, INX/OUTX/INS/OUTS, MAP/UNMAP/PROTECT/SETPGT, INVLPG/INVTLB/INVEPT, VMENTER/VMRUN/VMEXIT, SLEEP/MWAIT/WFI/WFE, CACHECTL MO 4..5 and CLZERO force an abort. XSUSPEND is the only instruction that lets a transaction wait.

abort_codes.name: read-set conflict
abort_codes.meaning: Another agent stored to a sector the transaction had read.

abort_codes.name: write-set conflict
abort_codes.meaning: Another agent wrote a sector that the transaction had buffered.

abort_codes.name: capacity
abort_codes.meaning: Write set or instruction count exceeded the implementation limits.

abort_codes.name: external event
abort_codes.meaning: A maskable interrupt or #SI vector arrived and interrupt exiting was not suppressed.

abort_codes.name: prohibited instruction
abort_codes.meaning: A serializing, I/O or MMU instruction executed inside the transaction.

abort_codes.name: fault inside transaction
abort_codes.meaning: A #PGF, #AC or #SEC occurred; the fault itself is delivered after the abort.

abort_codes.name: virtualization event
abort_codes.meaning: A VM exit or #VC was taken while TXE=1.

abort_codes.name: XSUSPEND timeout
abort_codes.meaning: The suspension expired without the conflicting writer making the transaction committable.

abort_codes.name: NMI or machine check
abort_codes.meaning: A non-maskable event aborted the transaction.

abort_codes.name: software
abort_codes.meaning: The IM8 operand of XABORT, chosen by software.

fallback_rules: The fallback address is computed once, at XBEGIN, from the encoding of XBEGIN itself; it is not affected by the length of anything executed inside the transaction.

On abort, TXE is cleared, the buffered stores are discarded, the abort code is recorded in cr13 and, when MO[0] of XBEGIN requested it, the 16-bit code is written into ra before control passes to the fallback address.
A fault that aborts a transaction is delivered to its own vector after the abort, with the return address of the faulting instruction, so the handler sees ordinary fault semantics.

Software must treat a transaction as best effort: a correct program has a non-transactional path that produces the same result, and the fallback path is entered both by an abort and, on an implementation without transactional memory, immediately by XBEGIN itself.

fences_relationship.atomic_sufficiency: An ACQ or REL class on an atomic instruction removes the need for a separate fence around it; an RLX atomic plus MFENCE is equivalent in effect and more expensive.
fences_relationship.publishing: Publishing a non-atomic result to another thread requires SFENCE (or an atomic with REL class) after the result and LFENCE (or an ACQ class) before the consumer reads it.
fences_relationship.transaction_end: XEND has release ordering for the whole write set. A consumer that acquires the same atomic that guarded the transaction sees every buffered store.

atomic_model.v1_compatibility: v1 has no atomic instruction: a v1 program that used a plain LD/ST read-modify-write was never atomic and can be recompiled onto LDLK/STLK or CAS without changing the data layout. The new instructions occupy opcodes that v1 decodes as #UDI, so a v1 binary is unaffected.

vector_extension.overview: The v2 vector unit is a 256-bit (VLEN=256) SIMD file of 32 registers with byte, half-word, word and double-word lanes, eight predicate registers, and a single set of names for masked forms supplied by two prefixes rather than by extra mnemonics. Every vector instruction is length-selected by ESZ, lane-masked by EVX or PRED, and reported through the VF, FLZ, FLO and FLV flags.

register_file.names: v0-v31, addressable directly for the first 16 registers and through the REX prefix for v16-v31, exactly like the general registers.
register_file.lane_views: vN.b (32 byte lanes), vN.w (16 half-word lanes), vN.d (8 word lanes), vN.q (4 double-word lanes). A write to a lane view zeroes the lanes it does not write unless a masked form with the merging policy is used.
register_file.aliases: d0-d15 alias v16-v31, so the v1 floating-point register file d0-d15 is the upper half of the vector file and no state is duplicated. f0-f15 are register indices 0-15 and d0-d15 are indices 16-31, so the floating-point file and the vector file share one physical register file: a write to fN touches the low 32 bits of vN, and a write to dN touches the low 64 bits of v(16+N).
register_file.reset: All vector registers are zeroed at RESET and the vector state is not saved by an interrupt frame; software uses VSTATE when it needs a context switch.
register_file.sharing_with_crypto: AES, SHA and the other crypto instructions operate on the low 128 bits of a vector register and zero the upper half, so the CIU needs no private data registers.

mask_registers.rationale: The widest mask that any form can need is one bit per lane of a byte vector: 256 bits divided by 8 is 32 lanes, so a predicate register is 32 bits. The v2 pieces agree on this figure: the VSTATE save record is 1064 bytes, which is 32 vector registers of 32 bytes (1024) plus eight predicates of 4 bytes (32) plus the VL word (4) plus the VLE status word (4), and nothing else.
mask_registers.general_register_view: KMOVG moves one 8-bit slice of a predicate to or from a general register, selected by its MO operand, which is why an 8-bit predicate word is the natural thing to see in a general register even though the register itself is 32 bits.
mask_registers.k0_policy: k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask, in the x86 APX/AVX-512 sense. Named as any mask operand, whether it comes from the EVX or PRED prefix or from the KM1 or KM2 field of the instruction itself, k0 reads as all ones for the active mask length, that is no masking at all. A write to k0 as the destination mask field KDG is discarded, so k0 never changes. k1-k7 are ordinary read-write mask registers, and a mask with no enabled bits is built by zeroing k1-k7 rather than by naming k0.

element_formats.integer_types: Signedness is not encoded in the lane type; it is selected per instruction by the MO[1:0] field: 0 signed, 1 unsigned, 2 logical, 3 reserved.
element_formats.fp_types: VFMA, VFMS, VCVT, VROUND and the other floating forms take their format from FPF, either in-band or through the FMT prefix: 0 F16, 1 BF16, 2 F32, 3 F64.
element_formats.vlmax: VLMAX = 256 / (8 << ESZ), that is 32 byte lanes, 16 word lanes, 8 dword lanes and 4 qword lanes.

vsetvl.semantics: DRG receives the previous VL in elements; VL becomes SR1 interpreted through MO (0 = element count, 1 = byte count, 2 = vtype bitfield) clamped to VLMAX for the current ESZ; VLE is set when the accepted length exceeds 256 bits.
vsetvl.vltype: With MO=2 the argument is a vtype word whose low 8 bits are the element count or byte count, bit 8 selects byte units, and bits 15:9 are reserved and must be zero.

vgetvl.semantics: Writes the current VL in elements into DRG.

length_control.vle_flag: The VLE status flag (bit 27) records that the last VSETVL accepted a length that the baseline 256-bit datapath could not hold. On the v2 baseline VLEN=256 so VLE is always 0; an implementation with a wider datapath sets it so that software that must stay portable can clamp its own loops.
length_control.default: VL after RESET is VLMAX for the largest element size, 4 elements, so a program that never calls VSETVL sees a defined behaviour.

tail_and_mask_policy.written_lanes: Only lanes 0..VL-1 that the mask enables are written.
tail_and_mask_policy.mask_policy: ZEROING is the default: a lane that the mask clears is written with zero. PRED MO=1 selects MERGING: a cleared lane keeps the previous destination value. There is no per-instruction choice; it is a property of the prefix.
tail_and_mask_policy.tail_policy: Lanes VL..VLMAX-1, the tail, are always ZEROED. Tail-undisturbed behaviour has no encoding in v2, so a compiler that wants to preserve a tail uses MERGING with an explicitly constructed mask.
tail_and_mask_policy.no_lane_no_flag: An instruction that writes no destination lane never modifies a flag, so a fully masked-off vector operation cannot change VF. Fully masking-off means every enabled lane bit of a k1-k7 mask is clear; k0 never masks anything off, so a program that wants an empty mask must build it in k1-k7.
tail_and_mask_policy.fault_suppression: A masked-off lane never accesses memory and never faults, which makes VLOADM/VSTOREM the way to probe a page without a fault.

masking_forms.prefix_masking: EVX (0xF7, payload KDG,VL) supplies a mask register and an explicit vector length for one instruction; PRED (0xFB, payload KDG,MO) supplies a mask register and the merge/zero mode. These two prefixes are the whole of the masked syntax: there is no separate masked mnemonic for each vector operation.
masking_forms.in_instruction_masking: Instructions whose memory access must be suppressed per lane name the mask as KM1 in their own encoding: VLOADM, VSTOREM, VCOMPRESS, VEXPAND, VFIND, VPOPC, KMOV, KTEST, KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT, KUNPCK, KMOVG, VCMP (KDG destination), VTEST (KDG destination).
masking_forms.mask_algebra: KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT and KUNPCK operate on whole mask registers (KUNPCK concatenates two 8-bit slices into one register); KTEST sets ZF when the AND of its two masks is zero and CF when they are equal; VPOPC counts the set bits into a general register. Every one of these operations follows the k0 rule: k0 as a source reads all ones, and a KDG of 0 discards the result.
masking_forms.compare: VCMP writes a mask register, not a vector register: the CC nibble selects one of the 16 condition codes of the ISA and KDG receives one bit per participating lane. A compare with KDG=0 computes its condition and discards the mask, because k0 is the hardwired all-ones sentinel and cannot be written; use k1-k7 for a mask that must be consumed.

saturation_and_flags.vf: VF means the written value is not the exact mathematical result: it is set by VADDSAT, VSUBSAT, VNARROW, VTRUNC, VSAT, VDOT, VREDSUM, VAVG, VMADD, VMSUB, VSHL and VABSD when a lane saturates, wraps or loses bits, and it is sticky until an instruction that clears flags runs.
saturation_and_flags.fp_flags: The floating forms use FLZ, FLO and FLV with exactly the meaning the FPU gives them: FLZ = the result is a zero or a comparison found equality, FLO = the result is inexact, overflowed or lost a denormal, FLV = invalid operation or indefinite conversion.
saturation_and_flags.mo_overflow_modes: MO[3:2] selects the overflow behaviour for the arithmetic forms: 0 wrap, 1 signed saturation, 2 unsigned saturation, 3 flags only (the lane keeps its low bits and VF is the only record).
saturation_and_flags.conversion: VCVT, VZEXT, VSEXT, VTRUNC and VSAT take their source and destination widths from ESZ and MO, and VTRUNC reports the lost bits through VF exactly as the scalar TRUNC does.

memory_forms.unit_stride: VLDR and VSTR use base plus displacement (O16) and touch VL consecutive elements.
memory_forms.strided: VLDRS and VSTRS add SR2 as a stride register scaled by MO, for the columns of a matrix.
memory_forms.indexed: VLDRX and VSTRX take their per-lane offsets from the vector register VF1, with 32-bit or 64-bit offsets selected by MO.
memory_forms.broadcast: VLDREP fetches one element and replicates it across the destination.
memory_forms.masked_block: VLOADM and VSTOREM name their mask explicitly and suppress both the access and the fault of a disabled lane.
memory_forms.alignment: A unit-stride or strided access must be naturally aligned for its element size or it raises #AC; an indexed gather is checked per lane and the first failing lane reports #AC or #PGF.
memory_forms.precise_faults: A faulting vector load or store leaves the destination register unchanged, so the instruction is restartable after the handler repairs the mapping. A gather does not partially write on a fault.

exception_behaviour.udi: A reserved ESZ (there is none for a vector form, all four codes are legal), a reserved MO code, or a reserved VL code raises #UDI before any lane is written.
exception_behaviour.faults: The vector memory forms declare only #UDI, #AC and #PGF, and which of them appear depends on the form: VLDR and VSTR declare all three, VLDRS and VSTRS declare #UDI and #PGF because a strided access is element-aligned by construction, and the masked forms VLOADM and VSTOREM declare #UDI and #PGF because fault suppression makes #AC unreachable. No vector instruction raises #DIV, and VSTATE is the only vector instruction that raises #GP (a restore record shorter than 1064 bytes).
exception_behaviour.interrupts: A vector instruction is interruptible only at its boundaries; a partially executed masked store is never visible, because the LSU retires the whole instruction or none of it.

vstate.record_layout: v0..v31 as 32 bytes each (1024 bytes), then k0..k7 as 4 bytes each (32 bytes), then the VL word (4 bytes), then the VLE status word (4 bytes, zero-extended, bits above 0 reserved)
vstate.save: MO=0 writes the record to [SR1] and returns the byte count in DRG.
vstate.restore: MO=1 reloads from [SR1] with SR2 giving the record length; a length below 1064 raises #GP before any register is written, which makes the restore atomic.

state_save_restore.lazy_switch: An operating system may keep the vector state resident instead of lazy, because VSTATE is a single instruction of latency 6 for the save direction and the restore prefetches the record.

naming_grammar.vector_ops: V<OP>[.<esize>] - the mnemonic starts with V, the operation name is upper case ASCII, and an optional dot suffix selects the element size: .b, .w, .d, .q for ESZ 0..3. Examples: VADD.b, VMUL.w, VFMA.d, VLDR.q.
naming_grammar.mask_ops: K<OP> for the mask ALU: KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT, KMOV, KTEST, KUNPCK, KMOVG. Mask mnemonics never take a size suffix.
naming_grammar.no_suffix: A vector mnemonic written without a size suffix takes ESZ from the first explicit size operand, or, when there is none, defaults to ESZ=2 (DWORD) for integer operations and FPF=2 (F32) for floating-point operations.
naming_grammar.fp_forms: VFMA and VFMS are the only vector mnemonics whose source is floating-point; they take FPF from the FMT prefix, defaulting to F32.
naming_grammar.register_syntax: v0-v31 for vector registers, k0-k7 for masks, both with the lane view written as v3.b or v3.w when a fragment of one register is meant.

instruction_groups.0xA2: strided and indexed memory: VLDRS, VSTRS, VLDRX, VSTRX (4)
instruction_groups.0xA3: broadcast and masked block memory: VLDREP, VLOADM, VSTOREM (3)
instruction_groups.0xA4: lane arithmetic: VADD, VSUB, VMUL, VDIV, VMIN, VMAX, VAVG, VADDSAT, VSUBSAT, VDOT (10)
instruction_groups.0xA5: fused and unary: VMADD, VMSUB, VFMA, VFMS, VABSD, VNEG (6)
instruction_groups.0xA6: logic: VAND, VOR, VXOR, VXNOR, VNOT (5)
instruction_groups.0xA7: shifts: VSHL, VSHR, VSAR, VSHLV, VNARROW (5)
instruction_groups.0xA8: compare and search: VCMP, VTEST, VFIND (3)
instruction_groups.0xA9: mask ALU: KAND, KOR, KXOR, KNOT (4)
instruction_groups.0xAA: mask move and count: KMOV, KTEST, KUNPCK, VPOPC, KMOVG (5)
instruction_groups.0xAB: permute: VSHUF, VSWIZ, VPERM, VSLIDE, VBLEND, VTBL (6)
instruction_groups.0xAC: reduce and scan: VREDSUM, VREDMIN, VREDMAX, VREDAND, VSCAN (5)
instruction_groups.0xAD: lane and convert: VEXTRACT, VINSERT, VBROADCAST, VCVT, VZEXT, VSEXT, VTRUNC, VSAT (8)
instruction_groups.0xAE: round, count and compress: VROUND, VCNT, VCLZ, VBYTEREV, VCOMPRESS, VEXPAND (6)

fpu_interaction.aliasing: v16-v31 alias d0-d15, so an FPU instruction that writes d0 writes the low 64 bits of v16 and leaves the upper 192 bits unchanged.
fpu_interaction.lane_extract: VEXTRACT reads one lane into a general register and VINSERT writes one lane from a general register, which is the sanctioned bridge between the integer and vector worlds; there is no implicit cross-domain move.
fpu_interaction.synchronization: The vector and FPU pipelines share one physical register file, so a read of a vector register after an FPU write of an aliasing register needs no explicit fence: the scoreboard stalls the dependent read.

vector_extension.v1_compatibility: v1 has no vector state. A v1 program that uses f0-f15 and d0-d15 sees its registers unchanged because d0-d15 are the upper half of v16-v31 and nothing in v1 addresses v0-v15 as vectors. The ten vector primaries 0xA0-0xAF were unassigned in v1, where each of those bytes decoded as #UDI.

privilege_model.levels: L0 user, L1 trusted, L2 restricted/sandbox, L3 kernel, L4 hardware, L5 hypervisor, L6 virtual machine, L7 platform secure. An instruction's mode field is the lowest level that may execute it, so L0 instructions are available at every level and an L7 instruction only at L7.
privilege_model.capability_mask: Each level has a capability mask in the mode descriptor; SETMODE checks it, and a request that the mask forbids raises #GP rather than silently lowering the level.
privilege_model.state_protection: Anything that touches a control register, an MSR, the TLB, the IDT, the protection keys or the power state is at least L3; the virtualization family is L5 except the guest-side exits at L6; enclave and attestation instructions are L7.
privilege_model.independent_gates: The mode field is a numeric floor only. Finer gates are the status flags: VME for virtualization, SSE for the shadow stack, PKE for keys, DTE for tracing, TXE for transactions, MCE for machine-check reporting, VIE for virtual interrupts. An instruction whose flag gate is closed raises #GP, not #UDI, because the encoding is valid and the privilege is not.
privilege_model.no_implicit_escalation: No instruction raises the privilege level except SETMODE, SYSENT, an interrupt gate with a higher TARGET_MODE, VMENTER and VMEXIT; each of those is a point where the architecture re-checks the mode descriptor and can raise #GP.

shadow_stack.base_and_pointer: cr11 holds the shadow stack base and length; the shadow stack pointer is a separate register managed only by the SHSTK instructions. The shadow stack is not writable through ordinary stores: a store into the shadow-stack range from any instruction other than SHSTKPUSH raises #SEC.

SHSTKPUSH.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x00 sub_opcode 0x0, format OPC,SOP,SR1, length 2
SHSTKPUSH.semantics: Pushes SR1 (the return address) and decrements the shadow stack pointer by four. #SEC when SSE=0 or the stack is full.

SHSTKPOP.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x00 sub_opcode 0x1, format OPC,SOP,DRG, length 2
SHSTKPOP.semantics: Pops one shadow entry into DRG.

SHSTKRET.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x00 sub_opcode 0x2, format OPC,SOP,0x0, length 2
SHSTKRET.semantics: Compares the shadow entry with the return address at [sp]; on a mismatch it raises #SEC and does not branch, so a corrupted return address cannot redirect control.

shadow_stack.pairing: The call sequence is SHSTKPUSH at the call site and SHSTKRET at the return. A longjmp or a signal return must call SHSTKPOP the right number of times; the unwinder does so explicitly rather than by relaxing the check.
shadow_stack.privilege: The three instructions are L3, and SSE is set by the kernel when it enables the feature for a thread.

speculation_barrier_codes.field: SPB (4 bits), used by SPECBAR (xtu space 0x02/0x0) and by the fence instructions MFENCE, LFENCE and SFENCE (opcode 0xCB).

codes.name: NONE
codes.meaning: No speculation barrier; only the execution ordering of the fence itself.

codes.name: LIGHT
codes.meaning: Later speculative loads may not bypass the barrier, but already-issued speculative loads complete.

codes.name: ADDR
codes.meaning: Address-dependency barrier: speculative loads that depend on an address computed before the barrier are killed, which closes the load-to-address pattern used by Spectre variant 1.

codes.name: FULL
codes.meaning: Drain every speculative path and serialize. This is the strength a context switch or an indirect-branch target load uses.

codes.name: RESERVED
codes.meaning: Reserved. SPECBAR, MFENCE, LFENCE and SFENCE all declare #UDI, so a reserved strength is a #UDI rather than an implicit FULL.

companions.IBPB: Invalidates the branch-predictor state of the current address space so code entered afterwards cannot reuse predictions trained by the previous one. Latency 300.
companions.STIBP: Switches the current hardware thread to single-thread prediction so a sibling SMT thread cannot train the same predictor entries. Latency 5.
companions.SSBB: Speculation-stop for the current indirect branch only; the cheap form used at the head of a sensitive indirect target.
companions.SPECBAR: The general barrier whose strength is the SPB code above. Latency 25.

speculation_barrier_codes.rule: A barrier is never weaker than the code says and never stronger than FULL; software must not rely on a barrier stronger than it asked for.

supervisor_access_exclusion.semantics: When SXE=1 the core may not fetch or read a page whose PTE has the U bit set while running at L3 or above: an instruction fetch raises #SEC with X=1 and a read raises #SEC. A write to a user page remains allowed because the legitimate use of the mechanism is to copy a result into a user buffer.
supervisor_access_exclusion.purpose: The SMEP/SMAP analogue: it prevents a kernel from being tricked into executing or reading data from a user mapping.
supervisor_access_exclusion.control: Set by WRCR on cr5 during boot; per-instruction opt-out is not provided, so a needed user copy uses the v1 store path or a temporary mapping.

endbr.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x01 sub_opcode 0x0, format OPC,SOP,MO, length 2
endbr.semantics: Marks a legal indirect-branch target. When the feature is enabled an indirect CALL/JMP/return that lands on an instruction other than ENDBR raises #SEC; MO selects the allowed branch class (0 call/jump, 1 call only, 2 jump only).

ssbb.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x01 sub_opcode 0x1, format OPC,SOP,0x0,IM8, length 3
ssbb.semantics: Speculation-stop for the following indirect branch; the IM8 operand names the branch class so a call site does not double-count.

control_flow_integrity.shadow_stack: Returns are additionally protected by the shadow stack, so an attacker who can write the normal stack still cannot redirect a return without breaking the shadow copy.
control_flow_integrity.combination: ENDBR plus the shadow stack covers both the forward and the backward edge; IBPB and STIBP cover the predictor-training channel between address spaces and between SMT threads.

enclaves.lifecycle: ENCLS (L7) creates, adds pages to, initializes, measures and removes an enclave; ENCLU (L7) runs a leaf inside an initialized enclave and raises #SEC outside one; ENCLV (L7) is the virtualization-side leaf used by a hypervisor to schedule enclave state.
enclaves.isolation: Enclave pages are mapped only while the core is inside the enclave; leaving the enclave through an asynchronous exit unmaps them and the state is encrypted in memory. No instruction other than ENCLU can read an enclave page, and an access attempt from outside raises #SEC.

attestation.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x03 sub_opcode 0x3, format OPC,SOP,DRG,0x0,SR1, length 3
attestation.semantics: Produces a signed quote over the enclave measurement into the buffer at SR1; CF reports success. The signing key never leaves the platform, so ATTEST cannot be used to exfiltrate it.
attestation.timing: latency 500, the single most expensive instruction in the ISA

enclaves.leaf_results: Every enclave leaf reports success in CF and an error code in ZF, which is why ENCLS, ENCLU and ENCLV declare both flags.

key_isolation.slots: The CIU keeps key slots addressed by a handle in DRG. A generated key never appears in a general register, a vector register or memory that software can read: the only operations that consume a key slot are the crypto instructions that name a handle.

instructions.KEYGEN: L7 only. Derives a key from the platform root secret into the slot named by DRG, with SR1 as the derivation context and SR2 as the caller nonce, ESZ selecting 1, 2, 4 or 8 blocks of 128 bits. Raises #SEC when the slot is occupied or the caller lacks platform authority.
instructions.KEYLOAD: L3. Loads key material supplied by the kernel into a slot for use by an enclave.
instructions.KEYZERO: L3. Overwrites a slot with zeros through a path that cannot be optimized away, and returns the slot to the free list.

key_isolation.zeroization: KEYZERO is the only architecturally guaranteed way to erase a key; a store of zeros to a buffer is not sufficient because the cache may retain the line, which is what ZEROIZE exists for.

ctcopy.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x04 sub_opcode 0x1, format OPC,SOP,DRG,SR1,SR2, length 3
ctcopy.semantics: Copies DRG bytes from [SR2] to [SR1] with a data-independent access sequence and no early exit, so the timing depends only on the length.
ctcopy.timing: latency 12, throughput 10, independent of the values

seccmp.semantics: Compares ESZ-sized operands in constant time and reports the result in ZF only; no intermediate result that depends on the data is architecturally visible.

constant_time_primitives.crypto: Every AES, SHA, CLMUL, GF(2) and CIU instruction is constant-time with respect to data and key operands: no table lookup indexed by a secret and no data-dependent branch. Instructions of this family modify no flag except the ones their own definition names.
constant_time_primitives.entropy: RDRAND and RDSEED read the hardware generator, set CF on success and clear it when the generator is not ready, with no timing dependence on the requested value.

zeroize.encoding: xtu space opcode 0x04 sub_opcode 0x0, format OPC,SOP,SR1,SR2,ESZ, length 3
zeroize.semantics: Overwrites SR2 elements of 1<<ESZ bytes at [SR1] with zeros using non-allocating stores that cannot be reordered or elided, then invalidates those sectors.

zeroization.clzero: CLZERO zeroes a whole 32-byte sector, which is the right granularity for scrubbing a stack frame.
zeroization.guarantees: ZEROIZE plus CLZERO is the only combination that the architecture guarantees against a cold-boot or cache-remanence attack; ZEROIZE alone is enough when the line is also invalidated by the following CLWBI or CACHECTL.

residual_risks: The architecture does not protect against a physical attacker who can probe the memory bus; enclave memory is encrypted but the bus protocol itself is outside the ISA.
Speculation barriers reduce but do not eliminate covert channels; a kernel that runs untrusted speculative code on a sibling SMT thread must use STIBP and accept a throughput cost.
A protection key protects against a stray pointer inside one privilege level, not against a kernel that rewrites cr6; PKE is a fault-isolation tool, not an isolation boundary.

The mode model is numeric, so a bug in the mode descriptor check is a total compromise; the v2 design therefore keeps every privileged operation behind a named instruction instead of a general write to a machine register.

modes_and_flags.hypervisor: L5. The hypervisor owns the control block, the EPT and the guest state; VMENTER and VMRUN, VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMFUNC, VMLOAD and VMSTORE are L5.
modes_and_flags.guest: L6. A guest runs with VME=1 and may reach only the instructions whose mode floor is at most L6; VMEXIT and VMCALL are the guest-side exits and are L6.
modes_and_flags.vme: The VME status flag (bit 19) is the virtualization-enable latch. VMENTER and VMRUN require VME=0 and set it; VMEXIT requires VME=1 and clears it. Every other virtualization instruction is gated on VME in the direction its description states, so a guest cannot re-enter or a host cannot exit twice.
modes_and_flags.vie: The VIE status flag (bit 24) enables virtual interrupts: when VIE=1 a pending device interrupt is delivered to the guest through the guest IDT instead of the host, unless interrupt exiting is configured.

control_block.location: cr8 holds the physical address of the active control block; the block is 4 KiB and its field offsets are fixed by the architecture, so a hypervisor can build it with ordinary stores and a guest cannot see it because cr8 is L5.

fields.name: GUEST_IP
fields.meaning: Guest instruction pointer, loaded by VMENTER and saved by a hardware exit.

fields.name: GUEST_SP
fields.meaning: Guest stack pointer for the current guest privilege level.

fields.name: GUEST_LEVEL
fields.meaning: Guest privilege level, which must be L0..L2 for VMENTER to succeed; any other value is an invalid guest state.

fields.name: GUEST_CR3
fields.meaning: Guest page-directory base for the stage-1 walk.

fields.name: GUEST_CR0
fields.meaning: Guest control word 0, including its IDTG gate-layout bit.

fields.name: GUEST_IDT
fields.meaning: Guest IDT base used for virtual interrupt delivery.

fields.name: GUEST_ASID
fields.meaning: ASID the guest translations are tagged with.

fields.name: EPT_ROOT
fields.meaning: Physical address of the stage-2 translation root.

fields.name: EXIT_REASON
fields.meaning: 16-bit reason code, written on every exit and mirrored into the #VC error code.

fields.name: EXIT_QUALIFICATION
fields.meaning: Reason-specific data: the faulting address for an EPT violation, the port for an I/O exit, the vector for an interrupt exit.

fields.name: EXIT_INSTRUCTION_LENGTH
fields.meaning: Length in bytes of the instruction that caused the exit, so the hypervisor can emulate it and skip it.

fields.name: CONTROLS
fields.meaning: Exit-control word: external-interrupt exiting, I/O exiting, EPT-enable, NMI exiting, plus the MSR-load and store count.

fields.name: MSR_BITMAP
fields.meaning: Physical address of the MSR-access bitmap used by the exit-on-MSR mechanism.

fields.name: GUEST_VECTOR_STATE
fields.meaning: Physical address where VSTATE saves the guest vector file.

fields.name: HOST_STATE
fields.meaning: Hypervisor segment-like state restored by a hardware exit.

control_block.access: VMREAD and VMWRITE address one field at a time by index in SR2/SR1 with the value in a register; VMLOAD and VMSTORE move the guest state between the block and the machine registers in bulk, which is what a context switch uses.

VMENTER.semantics: Loads the guest state from the control block addressed by DRG, sets VME and switches to L6. With VME=1 it raises #GP. An invalid guest state raises #VC with the invalid-state reason and does not switch.

VMRUN.semantics: Enters the guest and stays in it until an exit occurs, then writes the exit reason into DRG. This is the long-running form that a hypervisor loop uses.

VMEXIT.semantics: Saves the guest state to the active control block, writes the exit reason into DRG, sets VME=0 and returns to L5. With VME=0 it raises #GP.

entry_and_exit.hardware_exit: A hardware exit is the same save sequence triggered by an event rather than by an instruction: the reason code goes into the control block and into DRG when the exit was caused by a guest instruction that the hypervisor then reads.

VMCALL.semantics: Raises #VC with the reason hypercall and the hypercall number IM8, leaving guest mode as a side effect of the exception. Arguments ride in SR1, SR2, SR3 and r0.

VMFUNC.semantics: Runs a hypervisor service identified by MO (class) and IM8 (function) without a world switch and reports completion in CF. An unavailable service raises #VC.

vmexit_reasons.name: hypercall
vmexit_reasons.meaning: VMCALL raised #VC with a hypercall number.

vmexit_reasons.name: ept violation
vmexit_reasons.meaning: The stage-2 walk found no mapping, or the mapping denied the access.

vmexit_reasons.name: ept misconfiguration
vmexit_reasons.meaning: An EPT entry had a reserved field set.

vmexit_reasons.name: external interrupt
vmexit_reasons.meaning: A device interrupt arrived while external-interrupt exiting was enabled.

vmexit_reasons.name: nmi
vmexit_reasons.meaning: A non-maskable interrupt arrived while NMI exiting was enabled.

vmexit_reasons.name: io instruction
vmexit_reasons.meaning: INX/OUTX/INS/OUTS executed while I/O exiting was enabled; the port is in EXIT_QUALIFICATION.

vmexit_reasons.name: cpuid
vmexit_reasons.meaning: CPUID executed; the hypervisor may present a different feature set per guest.

vmexit_reasons.name: invalid guest state
vmexit_reasons.meaning: VMENTER or VMRUN found a control-block field the architecture does not permit.

vmexit_reasons.name: vmenter with vme set
vmexit_reasons.meaning: A nested entry was attempted inside a guest.

vmexit_reasons.name: vmexit with vme clear
vmexit_reasons.meaning: An exit was attempted outside a guest.

vmexit_reasons.name: invvpid equivalent
vmexit_reasons.meaning: An INVEPT descriptor did not name a valid EPT root.

vmexit_reasons.name: transaction conflict
vmexit_reasons.meaning: A transaction was open and the guest had to be exited; abort code 263.

vmexit_reasons.name: triple fault in guest
vmexit_reasons.meaning: The guest would have shut down; the exit reason lets the hypervisor reset only the guest.

vmexit_reasons.name: enclave event
vmexit_reasons.meaning: ENCLV took an asynchronous exit while the guest owned the enclave.

vmexit_reasons.name: mode change
vmexit_reasons.meaning: SETMODE asked to leave the guest level, which is not permitted from L6.

ept.structure: The stage-2 translation is a three-level table identical in shape to the stage-1 table, rooted at EPT_ROOT in the control block, mapping guest-physical to host-physical addresses.

EPTMAP.encoding: escape1 opcode 0x10 sub_opcode 0x8, format OPC,SOP,SR1,SR2,MO, mode L5
EPTMAP.semantics: Installs a stage-2 mapping of the guest page containing SR1 to host base SR2, with the size class and rights in MO, then drops the cached translations.

EPTUNMAP.encoding: escape1 opcode 0x10 sub_opcode 0x9, format OPC,SOP,SR1,0x0,MO, mode L5
EPTUNMAP.semantics: Clears the stage-2 mapping of the page containing SR1.

INVEPT.encoding: opcode 0x9A sub_opcode 0x2, format OPC,SOP,MO,SEG, mode L5
INVEPT.semantics: Invalidates cached stage-2 translations; a descriptor that does not name a valid root raises #VC.

ept.rights: MO bits 7:4 are write/user/execute/global for the stage-2 mapping, so a guest can be given a page that is readable but not executable without the guest kernel cooperating.

nested_paging.walk: A guest linear address is translated by the stage-1 walk rooted at GUEST_CR3 to a guest-physical address, which is then translated by the stage-2 walk rooted at EPT_ROOT to a host-physical address. Both walks use the same 8-byte entry format, so the walker is one piece of hardware.
nested_paging.faults: A stage-1 failure raises the guest's own #PGF; a stage-2 failure raises #VC to the hypervisor with reason 1, so a hypervisor can implement memory ballooning without the guest noticing anything but a normal exit.
nested_paging.caching: A cached translation is tagged with (GUEST_ASID, stage-2 root) so a switch of either invalidates exactly the affected entries; INVTLB MO 1 flushes by ASID and INVEPT flushes by root.

interrupt_virtualization.delivery: With VIE=1 and external-interrupt exiting disabled, a device interrupt is delivered to the guest through the guest IDT while the host keeps control of the vector mapping; the guest sees a normal interrupt vector and an ordinary frame.
interrupt_virtualization.injection: A hypervisor can synthesise a virtual interrupt by writing the vector into the control block before VMENTER; the entry code then delivers it before the first guest instruction.
interrupt_virtualization.exiting: With external-interrupt exiting enabled every device interrupt becomes exit reason 3 and the hypervisor decides whether to inject it, which is how a device can be assigned to one guest.
interrupt_virtualization.nmi: NMI exiting is independent of VIE and is controlled by its own bit in CONTROLS; an NMI that the host does not claim is delivered to the guest unchanged.

state_save.what_is_saved: Guest-visible state saved by an exit: IP, flags, SP, level, CR0, CR3, IDT, ASID, plus the general registers through VMLOAD/VMSTORE when the hypervisor enables the MSR-load list. Vector state is saved through the GUEST_VECTOR_STATE pointer using VSTATE.
state_save.what_is_not_saved: The hypervisor's own vector and floating-point state is not touched; a hypervisor that uses vector code must save it itself, exactly as a process would.
state_save.cost: A hardware exit costs 120 cycles, dominated by the serialization of the guest store buffer; VMFUNC exists so that a service that does not need a world switch can avoid that cost.

virtualization_model.v1_compatibility: v1 has no virtualization state at all: the VME and VIE status flags existed as defined bits that no v1 instruction modified, and L5/L6 existed as descriptors. A v1 program runs unchanged in a guest because the hypervisor enters the guest with VME=1 and the guest's view of every v1 instruction is identical.

debugging_model.overview: v2 adds an in-ISA debug layer: eight execution breakpoints, eight data watchpoints, single stepping through TF, a branch-and-memory trace buffer, eight performance counters and a register read path. Everything is instruction-driven, so a debugger does not need a special bus or a halt line.

breakpoints.registers: dbg0-dbg7, each holding an address, a control word and an armed bit.

BPSET.semantics: Programs dbg[DRG] with address SR1 and control word SR2. DRG above 7 raises #GP, as does a reserved bit in SR2.

control_word.name: G
control_word.meaning: Keep the breakpoint armed across VMENTER, so it also fires inside a guest.

control_word.name: MINLVL
control_word.meaning: 0 = fire at every level, 1 = L3 and above, 2 = L5 and above, 3 = L7 only.

control_word.name: TRAP
