control_word.meaning: 0 = break before the instruction (fault-style, the return address is the breakpointed instruction), 1 = break after it (trap-style).

control_word.name: RESERVED
control_word.meaning: Must be zero; a set bit raises #GP.

control_word.name: COUNT
control_word.meaning: Ignore COUNT matches before firing, so a breakpoint can stop on the n-th execution.

control_word.name: NMI
control_word.meaning: Report through #NMI instead of #BP, which lets a debugger survive a handler that has disabled IF.

breakpoints.delivery: A matched execution breakpoint raises #BP (vector 11) before or after the instruction according to TRAP. The breakpoint that fired is readable through DBGREAD so the handler knows which one it was.
breakpoints.reach: Eight breakpoints are enough for a source-level debugger that combines execution breakpoints with watchpoints, because a debugger re-programs them on every stop.

WCHSET.semantics: Programs watchpoint dbg[8+DRG] with address SR1 and the data-control word SR2.

data_control_word.name: ACCESS
data_control_word.meaning: 0 = write, 1 = read, 2 = read or write, 3 = reserved and raises #GP.

data_control_word.name: SIZE
data_control_word.meaning: 0 = 1 byte, 1 = 2 bytes, 2 = 4 bytes, 3 = any size, 4..7 reserved.

watchpoints.granularity: A watchpoint matches when the access range overlaps the watched range, so a 4-byte watch on a 32-byte sector catches every partial write of the watched object.
watchpoints.delivery: A matched data access raises #BP as a trap: the instruction has completed, so the debugger sees the effect it stopped on.

STEP.semantics: Sets TF and selects the step mode in MO: 0 = one instruction, 1 = one instruction or one taken branch, 2 = run until the next branch. MO 3..15 raise #UDI.

single_step.tf: While TF=1 the core raises #BP at the end of each qualifying instruction, before the next instruction is fetched, so the debugger sees exactly one instruction of progress per stop.
single_step.clearing: The handler must clear TF (WRFLAGS, POPF or a second STEP) before IRET; TF is part of the flags image that IRET restores, so a handler that leaves the pushed image untouched resumes stepping, which is the behaviour a single-step loop wants.
single_step.interaction: Single step does not interact with breakpoints: a breakpoint can fire inside a stepped instruction and the debugger then re-arms the step.

on.semantics: Points the trace buffer at SR1 with the control word SR2 and sets DTE.

trace.dte: The DTE status flag (bit 23) is both the enable and the observable state; a debugger polls it through RDFLAGS rather than reading a separate register.
trace.record: Each record is 16 bytes with four 4-byte words: type (1 taken branch, 2 indirect target, 3 data store, 4 exception), total length in bytes, IP, and the target address or stored data.
trace.buffer: The buffer is a circular region whose end is in the low half of SR2; the write pointer is readable through DBGREAD index 8..15, and an overflow sets a sticky bit in the trace control word instead of faulting.
trace.privilege: Tracing is L5, so a guest cannot trace the hypervisor and an operating system must ask the hypervisor or run at L5 itself.

RDPMU.semantics: Copies pmc[SR2] into DRG. The counter never counts its own read.

PMUCTL.semantics: MO 0 start, 1 stop, 2 reset, 3 select the event in SR2, 4 freeze all, 5 enable overflow; MO 6..15 raise #UDI.

performance_counters.overflow: An overflow raises ~PMU (vector 34) when the counter overflow bit is enabled, which is how a sampling profiler gets an interrupt every N events instead of polling.
performance_counters.events: The event space is implementation-defined; the architecture requires at least cycles, retired instructions, branch mispredictions, L1D misses and L2 misses so that a portable profiler has a baseline set.

instruction.semantics: SR1 selects the register: 0..7 dbg0-dbg7, 8..15 the trace pointers and counters, 16..23 pmc0-pmc7; any other value raises #GP.

debug_read.purpose: One instruction reads all debug state, so a debugger stub is small and there is no need for a second memory-mapped debug port.
debug_read.debug_port: v2 defines no separate debug port. The console device of the reference machine is an ordinary I/O port (port 0x04 in v1) and a debugger reaches it with OUTX, which keeps the debug interface inside the instruction set.

mode_rules.L0: A user program can read pmc counters (RDPMU is L0) and can be traced, but cannot arm a breakpoint, a watchpoint, a step or a trace.
mode_rules.L3: The kernel owns breakpoints, watchpoints, single step and DBGREAD; a debugger running as a kernel thread therefore needs no special mode.
mode_rules.L5: Tracing and the guest view are L5, so a hypervisor can trace a guest without giving the guest the mechanism.
mode_rules.L7: Platform secure code can arm a breakpoint that fires in every mode including L5 and L7 (MINLVL=0), which is how early boot is debugged.

exception_interaction.bp: A breakpoint or watchpoint match raises #BP, a trap with no error code, so the frame is flags plus return address and the debugger can IRET directly.
exception_interaction.nmi_option: With the NMI bit set the report is an #NMI instead, which is delivered even when IF=0 and when the core is inside a transaction; the transaction aborts with code 265.
exception_interaction.stepping_through_fault: A faulting instruction raises its own fault before the step trap, so a single-step debugger sees the fault first and the step trap after the handler returns.
exception_interaction.txe: A breakpoint inside a transaction aborts the transaction before #BP is delivered, so a debugger never observes a half-applied transaction.

method.source: The timing numbers in this section are the timing fields of the 399 v2 instructions in parts A_core, B_fpvec and C_sys, sampled mechanically: for every exec_unit the minimum and maximum latency and throughput were taken over all entries of that unit.
method.v1_entries: No v1 instruction carries a timing field. The model assigns each v1 instruction the default of its class (ALU 1/1, SHIFT 1/1, LSU 4/1, CTRL 1/1, FPU 1/1) and states that these are model defaults rather than part data, so nothing here contradicts a parts file.
method.semantics_of_a_timing_field: latency is the number of cycles from the first cycle of issue to the cycle in which the result is available to a dependent instruction; throughput is the number of cycles a single execution pipe of that class must wait before accepting the next instruction of the same class. A timing field of 1/1 therefore means fully pipelined with a one-cycle result.
method.coverage: The thirteen unit rows account for every v2 entry: 58 ALU + 33 BMU + 30 CIU + 14 CTRL + 6 DIV + 33 FPU + 6 IO + 45 LSU + 13 MMU + 9 MUL + 10 SHIFT + 65 SYS + 77 VEC = 399.

stage_list.name: IF
stage_list.description: Instruction fetch. Fetches a 32-byte sector into the fetch queue and uses the branch target buffer result of the previous cycle to choose the next fetch address; 16 bytes per cycle sustained, 32 on a taken-target hit.

stage_list.name: IGL
stage_list.description: Instruction get length. Consumes prefix bytes (REX, ISL, BRH_H, LOCK, DBI, XTU, BMU, CIU and the two-byte EVX, OPSZ, MEMO, REP, PRED, SEC and FMT forms), computes the total length from the format of the decoded opcode and cuts the instruction out of the fetch queue. This is the stage that makes a variable-length six-space encoding work: the length is known before decode, so a long prefix chain never stalls fetch.

stage_list.name: ID
stage_list.description: Instruction decode. Maps the opcode byte and the sub-opcode nibble to a control word, checks that the decode space agrees with the escape prefix that is actually present, and raises #UDI here when the pair is unallocated.

stage_list.name: REN
stage_list.description: Register rename. Renames the four-bit register fields, extended by REX to five bits, into physical registers, removes write-after-write and write-after-read hazards, and allocates a reorder-buffer entry. Rename is what lets the two issue slots stay filled without the compiler having to schedule around every false dependency.

stage_list.name: AC
stage_list.description: Address calculation. Computes the effective address from base, index, scale and displacement, checks alignment against the AC flag, and starts the TLB lookup so that a page walk overlaps execution.

stage_list.name: EX
stage_list.description: Execute. The integer ALU, the shift unit, the multiplier, the divider, the FPU, the vector unit, the BMU and the CIU all sit here; flags are produced in this stage and renamed like data.

stage_list.name: MEM
stage_list.description: Memory access. The LSU performs the load or store through L1D, handles the store buffer and the write-combining path, and resolves a #PGF from the AC-stage TLB result.

stage_list.name: WB
stage_list.description: Write back. The result is written to the physical register and the reorder-buffer entry is marked complete.

stage_list.name: RET
stage_list.description: Retire. Commits up to two instructions per cycle in program order, retires their flags and register writes, releases the reorder-buffer entries, and takes any pending precise exception, interrupt or breakpoint at this boundary. Nothing before RET is architecturally visible.

pipeline.v1_relationship: v1 documented seven stages (IF, IGL, ID, AC, EX, MEM, WB). v2 inserts REN between ID and AC and RET after WB, which is where register renaming and precise retirement belong; the rest of the v1 stage list is unchanged.
pipeline.in_order: Issue is in order and commit is in order; v2 keeps the v1 statement that out-of-order execution is not supported. REN removes false dependencies, it does not reorder real ones.

issue_width.fetch: 32 bytes per cycle from L1I, up to 4 instructions into the 16-entry fetch queue.
issue_width.dispatch: 2 instructions per cycle to 6 issue ports: P0 integer ALU, P1 integer ALU plus shift, P2 load, P3 store and I/O, P4 FPU or vector, P5 system, control, MMU, BMU and CIU. A micro-coded instruction occupies its port for the whole expansion.
issue_width.load_store_queue: 48 load and 32 store entries; a load may issue as soon as its address is ready, a store only when it reaches the head of its queue or no older store aliases it.
issue_width.why_two: The per-class throughput column of the parts is a property of one execution pipe of that class. Two dispatch slots across different classes therefore add throughput that no single timing field contradicts: two ALU instructions retire in two cycles at 1/1 each, while an ALU instruction and a load retire together because they issue on different ports.

per_class_table.class: integer ALU, bit manipulation, convert, packed BCD, condition materialisation
per_class_table.note: Bit tests and population counts are 1/1; the packed-BCD forms are the only ALU instructions above 4 cycles.

per_class_table.class: shifts, rotates, byte swap, double-width shifts
per_class_table.note: SHLD and SHRD are 2/1; the flag-free forms SHLX, SHRX, SARX, ROLX and RORX are 1/1.
MULH, MULHS, MADD, MSUB, MADDU and MSUBU are 4/1: a full product takes four cycles and the pipe is fully pipelined.

per_class_table.class: integer divide, remainder, integer square root, packed-BCD divide
per_class_table.note: The divider is not fully pipelined: DIVMOD, REM and REMS are 20/15 and DIVI is 16/12.

per_class_table.class: loads, stores, string operations, fences and cache maintenance
per_class_table.fastest: MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, LODS and STOS at 1/1 per element
per_class_table.note: PREFETCH and PREFETCHW are 1/1 because they retire without waiting; the cache-maintenance forms are the slow end; the sized loads LDP, LDSX, LDZX and LDNT are 4/1 to 4/2 and the indexed LDX is 5/1.

per_class_table.class: branches, calls, table dispatch, far return
per_class_table.note: A correctly predicted branch costs one cycle; the cost of a misprediction is given in branch_prediction.mispredict_penalty and is not a per-instruction timing field.

per_class_table.class: scalar floating point, conversions, comparisons, format state
per_class_table.fastest: FABS, FNEG, FCOPYSIG and FMOV at 1/1
per_class_table.note: FADD and FSUB are 4/1, FMUL 5/1, the FMA family 5/1, FDIV 16/8 and FSQRT 20/10.

per_class_table.fastest: VSETVL, VGETVL, VZERO, VCLEAR and VADD at 1/1
per_class_table.note: VLDR and VSTR are 5/1, VLDRX and VSTRX 8/3, VFMA 5/1, VDOT 3/1. A masked form costs the same as its unmasked form because the mask is a prefix and not a second opcode.

per_class_table.fastest: BAND, BOR, BXOR and BNOT at 1/1
per_class_table.note: The transcendental functions are 22..48 cycles at throughput 8..16; MMUL is 32/16 and FSIN is 24/8.

per_class_table.class: crypto, CRC, entropy and key management
per_class_table.note: AESENC and AESDEC are 3/1, SHA256RNDS2 3/1, SHA512RNDS2 5/2, MONT 25/12 and RDSEED 60/60.

per_class_table.class: system entry, control and MSR access, virtualization, debug, transactions, power, enclaves
per_class_table.note: WFI and WFE are 5/5 but their real duration is the wake latency; VMENTER and VMEXIT are 120, VMRUN 150 and IBPB 300.
INVLPG is 30/25, INVTLB 60/50, SETPGT 80/80, PGWALK 60/50 and MAP 45/40.
INX, OUTX, INS and OUTS are 6..12 depending on the width, and their real cost is the device latency, which the ISA does not bound.

branch_prediction.btb: 512-entry, 4-way set-associative branch target buffer, indexed by the low bits of the fetch address, storing a target and a 2-bit confidence counter.
branch_prediction.direction: A 4096-entry bimodal table of 2-bit saturating counters combined with a 2048-entry correlating table indexed by 12 bits of global branch history through a 4096-entry choice predictor. A 32-entry loop predictor covers counted loops such as the LOOP family and the software loop of a memcpy.
branch_prediction.indirect: A 256-entry indirect target predictor with two target ways per entry, which is what makes an indirect call through a dispatch table cost one cycle.
branch_prediction.return_stack: 64-entry return address stack, pushed by CALLR, CALL, CALLREL and CALLTAB and popped by RET, RETFAR and SHSTKRET.
branch_prediction.hints: The BRH_H prefix (0xF2 and 0xF3, carrying payload bit 0, where 0 means predict not-taken and 1 means predict taken) overrides the predictor for one branch. It is legal exactly on the instructions that list it: JCND, JCNDL and the LOOP family in v2, plus the v1 conditional branches that already declared it.
branch_prediction.mispredict_penalty: 12 cycles: the pipeline is flushed back to IF and refetched from the correct target.
branch_prediction.static_fallback: A branch whose table entry has never been written is predicted not taken, except a backward branch, which is predicted taken because it is usually a loop back edge.

speculation.depth: The core speculates up to the depth of the reorder buffer, 96 instructions or 32 unresolved branches, whichever comes first.
speculation.recovery: Every speculative result is tagged by the reorder-buffer entry that produced it, so a misprediction or an exception discards exactly the younger entries and no architectural state has to be repaired.
speculation.security: The predictor state is what IBPB, STIBP and SPECBAR manipulate; the strength code of a barrier decides whether in-flight speculative loads are killed, so the cost of a barrier ranges from one cycle for SPB 1 to a full pipeline drain for SPB 3.

cache_timing.assumption: The cache latencies used to model a load are an L1D hit in 4 cycles, an L2 hit in 12, an L3 hit in 36 and memory in about 120 on the reference machine. They are the model assumption and are not timing fields of any instruction.
cache_timing.alignment: A legal misaligned access costs one extra cycle per crossed 32-byte sector, which is why the atomic family forbids misalignment outright instead of paying it.
cache_timing.note: The L1 and L2 geometry is the v1 geometry (32 KiB 4-way with 64-byte lines, 1 MiB 8-way with 256-byte lines); L3 and the 32-byte sector granularity are v2 additions described in cache_model.

worked_examples.workload: fibonacci loop of ADD, CMP and JCND executed N times
worked_examples.cost: Three instructions per iteration: two ALU at throughput 1 and one CTRL at throughput 1. With dual dispatch across the ALU and CTRL ports an iteration costs two cycles while the branch is predicted, and fourteen when it mispredicts once.

worked_examples.workload: dot product over 32 vectors of 8 float32 lanes
worked_examples.cost: The loop body is one VLDR at 5/1, one VDOT at 3/1 and one decrement plus branch, so it is bound by the load port at about five cycles per 32 bytes of input.

worked_examples.workload: contended counter incremented in a loop
worked_examples.cost: AMOFADD costs 12 cycles when it wins and forces a retry for every conflict; a statistics counter that does not need the old value uses AMOADD and pays 12 cycles with no retry, while LDLK and STLK cost 6 plus 6 and pay a retry per conflict.

assembly_syntax.source_of_truth: The conventions below are the conventions the existing assembler already implements (as.py in the reference implementation) plus the minimum needed to spell the v2 instructions. Where v2 adds a field the v1 assembler did not resolve, the convention is taken from the pseudo-instruction table of A_core, which already writes every operand in the canonical form: ADD3 rd, r1, r2; MEMCPY rd, ri, rc; POPCNT rd, rs, ESZ=2 (DWORD); JCND CC=0 (EQ), target.

operand_order.rule: Destination first. Operands are written left to right in the order their fields appear in the encode format, and every instruction that writes a register names that register first (DRG, DRC, DFR, VDG or KDG). Sources follow in field order.
examples: ADD rd, r1, r2 writes rd (format OPC,DRG,0x0,SR1,SR2)
CMP r1, r2 compares two sources and writes no register
BT rd, r2, ESZ=2 tests a bit of rd and copies it to ZF
VFMA vd, v1, v2, v3 multiplies v1 by v2, adds v3 and writes vd
AMOADD rd, rb, ESZ=2, MO=3 adds rd into [rb] and discards the old value
operand_order.documented_exception: ST is the one v1 instruction whose textual order is source first, because its format is OPC,SR1,DRG,OF8 and the base address register sits in the DRG field: ST value, base, displacement. The v1 pseudo STOREI spells it the same way. LD is ordinary: LD rd, base, displacement.
operand_order.exact_name_mnemonics: v1 has eight instructions whose mnemonic contains the register name, so they take no operand: PUSH ra, PUSH rb, PUSH rc, PUSH rd, PUSH ri, PUSH bp, POP ra, POP rb, POP rc, POP rd, POP ri, POP bp, INC rc, DEC rc and CLR ra. They stay one-byte instructions in v2 and the assembler matches the whole text before splitting operands.

registers.general: x0, ra, rb, rc, rd, ri, bp, sp, r8-r23, t0-t7. t0-t7 are r24-r31. x0 reads as zero and discards every write. Registers above r15 need a REX prefix, which the assembler inserts automatically.
registers.floating_point: f0-f15 for the scalar file, d0-d15 for the double-precision half; d0-d15 alias v16-v31 and f0-f15 are the low 32 bits of the corresponding vector register when the FPU is in use.
registers.vector: v0-v31, with a lane view written as v3.b, v3.w, v3.d or v3.q for a fragment of one register.
registers.control: cr0-cr15 for RDCR, WRCR, MOVCTRL and COPCTRL.
registers.debug_and_counters: dbg0-dbg7 and pmc0-pmc7 are named by index in BPSET, BPCLR, WCHSET, WCHCLR, DBGREAD, RDPMU and PMUCTL, not as addressable registers.
registers.numbered: rN and the named aliases are interchangeable: r1 is ra, r7 is sp, r24 is t0.

literals.label: a bare symbol, resolved in the first assembler pass; a label used where an offset is expected becomes a displacement, and a label used where an absolute address is expected becomes that address
immediate_forms_by_field: OF8 and O16 are signed offsets
A16 and A32 are absolute addresses
literals.note: There is exactly one 16-bit immediate field (I16) and exactly one 16-bit offset field (O16). IM16 and OF16 do not exist in v2 and an assembler must reject them.

forms.used_by: LD, ST, the atomics, LDSX, LDZX, CTCOPY, ZEROIZE

forms.fields: SR1 or DRG with OF8 or O16
forms.used_by: LD, ST, LDP, STP, LDNT, STNT, PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, CACHECTL, FLOAD, FSTORE, VLDR, VSTR, INVLPG

forms.fields: a negative signed offset in OF8 or O16
forms.used_by: the same instructions; the assembler encodes the two's-complement value

forms.fields: SR1, SR2 and SCL where SCL is the numeric multiplier, not a log2 shift
forms.used_by: LDX, STX, LEASC, and the pseudo ADDR and LEA32
LEASC and the v2 scaled loads

forms.fields: none: the string instructions name no memory operand at all
forms.used_by: MOVS, MOVSN, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, STOSN, LODS, INS, OUTS

memory_operands.scale_note: SCL is a multiplier, not a shift count: [rb + ri*4] encodes SCL=4. This is the meaning the v1 reference implementation gives LEASC and the meaning the A_core notes state.
memory_operands.port_syntax: IN and OUT take a port number as a bare operand: IN 0x04, OUT 0x20. The disassembler prints the form port 0x04 and the assembler accepts it so that a disassembly re-assembles.

prefix_notation.position: A prefix is written before the mnemonic, on the same line, in any order; the encoder emits prefix bytes in the canonical order REX, ISL, BRH_H, LOCK, escape byte, MEMO, OPSZ, FMT, REP, PRED, SEC, EVX and then the opcode.

one_byte_prefixes.REX: REX (the assembler adds it automatically when a register above r15 is used; writing it explicitly forces the extended form)

prefix_notation.escape_spaces: An instruction in an escaped space is written with its space word first: BMU FSIN f1, f2; CIU SHA3ABS rb, rc, rd, ri; XTU SHSTKPUSH ra; DBI SLEEP 1, 100. The escape byte is a prefix, so it is not counted in the instruction length and the encoded size is length + 1.
prefix_notation.maximum: At most four prefix bytes in total. Two register-extension prefixes (REX twice, or REX with ISL) on one instruction are illegal and raise #UDI at decode.
prefix_notation.alternate_form: A prefix that carries no payload may also be written as the first operand of the instruction, which is the spelling the A_core pseudo table already uses for REP: MOVS REP, ESZ=2 and CMPS REP, ESZ=0 assemble exactly as REP MOVS ESZ=2 and REP CMPS ESZ=0 do. A prefix that carries a payload (EVX, PRED, SEC, FMT, MEMO, OPSZ) must be written before the mnemonic, because its own operands would be ambiguous inside the operand list.

code_fields.rule: A code field that is not implied by the mnemonic is written as FIELD=value, exactly as the A_core pseudo table already writes it, and it appears in the operand list at the position of its field in the format. A bare numeric value in that position is accepted when the field order is unambiguous.
code_fields.fields: SOP (rarely written: it selects the sub-operation and is implied by the mnemonic), ESZ, MO, CH, RP, SPB, PKEY, FPF, RM, VL, CC.
code_fields.condition_names: The CC field may be written as a name instead of a number: EQ 0, NE 1, CS/LO 2, CC/HS 3, MI 4, PL 5, VS 6, VC 7, LT 8, GE 9, LE 10, GT 11, HI 12, LS 13, AL 14, NV 15.
code_fields.size_suffix: A vector mnemonic may carry a size suffix instead of an ESZ operand: VADD.b, VMUL.w, VDOT.d, VLDR.q. The suffix and an explicit ESZ= operand are synonyms and both are rejected when they disagree.
examples: FADD FPF=2, RM=0, f1, f2, f3

relative_branches.base_rule: Every relative branch computes its target as the address of the branch instruction itself plus the signed offset. The core advances the instruction pointer after the branch has been evaluated, and the assembler mirrors that by subtracting the branch's own address, not the address of the following instruction: offset = target - address_of_branch.
relative_branches.assembler_forms: as.py already does exactly this for O16 and O32, and the v2 assembler must extend the same rule to OF8 used as a branch displacement (JMPREL, LOOP, LOOPZ, LOOPNZ).
relative_branches.signed_offsets: OF8, O16 and O32 are signed and are sign-extended by the decoder before use. OF8 spans -128..127, O16 spans -32768..32767 and O32 spans the whole 32-bit address space. The decoder's signed-field set is OF8, O16 and O32.
relative_branches.the_one_exception: XBEGIN records its fallback address as the end of the XBEGIN instruction plus the signed O16 offset, that is IP + 4 + sign_extend(O16), because the fallback is the alternative to entering the transaction and has to be the instruction after XBEGIN. No other relative transfer in v2 uses an end-of-instruction base.
relative_branches.instructions: JCND, JCNDL and the LOOP family use the instruction-address base; JMPREL uses OF8, JMPRELL and CALLREL use O32; CALLREL and CALLTAB push the address of the following instruction as the return address.

string_conventions.implicit_operands: MOVS, MOVSN, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, STOSN and LODS take no register operand. ri is the source pointer, rd is the destination pointer, ra is the accumulator used by SCAS and LODS, rc is the element counter and DF selects the direction (0 = forward, 1 = backward).
string_conventions.element_size: ESZ selects the element width (byte, word, dword) and therefore the step applied to every pointer.
string_conventions.repeat: REP is the only repetition mechanism. REP with RP=0 repeats rc times with the pointer stepping selected by DF; a REP-prefixed instruction is a single instruction whose length is unchanged, and the prefix byte is not counted in the length. There is no separate REPE or REPNE mnemonic: CMPS under REP stops early when the elements differ and SCAS under REP stops early when they match, which is exactly the REPE and REPNE behaviour, expressed by the instruction's own flag rule.
string_conventions.early_exit: CMPS stops early on inequality and SCAS stops early on equality, so a lexicographic compare leaves ZF in the state of the comparison that ended the loop.
string_conventions.io: INS and OUTS use the same implicit pointers with a 16-bit port number.

directives_and_comments.comments: ; or # starts a comment and runs to the end of the line.
directives_and_comments.labels: name: at the start of a line, optionally followed by an instruction on the same line.

directives..ascii: emit a quoted string with no terminator

directives_and_comments.operands: Operands are separated by commas; whitespace around a comma is ignored; a quoted string is only legal as the operand of .ascii or .db.
directives_and_comments.sections: There is no section directive. A program is one flat image assembled from address 0 or from .org; the reference ROM is 1024 bytes and the assembler's output is the whole image.
directives_and_comments.case: Mnemonics are upper case by convention and the assembler is case sensitive, which matches the instruction table where v2 mnemonics must match A-Z0-9_.

pseudo_mnemonics.rule: A pseudo mnemonic is an assembler macro with no byte of its own; it expands into the sequence listed in translate_to. It is written exactly like a real instruction and never appears in a disassembly.
pseudo_mnemonics.v1: SAL is the only v1 pseudo instruction and it stays.
pseudo_mnemonics.v2: A_core adds 45: LI, MOVI, CMPI, TST, BEQ, BNE, BGT, BLT, BGE, BLE, JMP32, CALL32, PUSHA, POPA, PUSHR, POPR, MEMCPY, MEMSET, ZEXT8, ZEXT16, SEXT8, SEXT16, NOT32, SWAP16, NOPN, ADD3, MULADD, MOD, DIVU, MIN, MAX, LSHIFT, RSHIFT, CLZ32, POPC, LEA32, ADDR, LOG2, BITREV, SETIF, BRKIF, LOADI, STOREI, XCHG8, XCHG16.
pseudo_mnemonics.scratch: A pseudo that needs a scratch register uses t0 or t1 and says so in its description, so a programmer knows that CMPI, TST and the like clobber t0.

examples.title: Fibonacci loop
code: LI     rc, 10          ; pseudo: expand to a 6-byte IMM
LI     ra, 0
MOVI   rb, 1
loop:   ADD3   rd, ra, rb    ; pseudo: alias of the 3-byte ADD
MOV    ra, rb
MOV    rb, rd
DEC    rc              ; one-byte exact-name mnemonic, sets ZF
JCND   NE, loop        ; CC=1, O16 relative to the branch itself
RET
examples.note: JCND replaces the v1 conditional branches for new code; JNZ loop would encode the same control flow in v1 form.

examples.title: memcpy loop with REP
code: MOV    rd, ra          ; destination in rd
MOV    ri, rb          ; source in ri
MOV    rc, r8          ; dword count in rc
MOVS   REP, ESZ=2      ; repeat dword copy, DF=0
RET
examples.note: The same effect as the pseudo MEMCPY rd, ri, rc, whose translate_to is exactly these four instructions.

examples.title: SIMD dot product
code: VSETVL ra, 8, MO=0     ; VL = 8 word lanes, previous VL in ra
VZERO  v0
VLDR   v1, rb, 0, ESZ=2 ; base plus O16 displacement
VLDR   v2, rc, 0, ESZ=2
EVX k1, 1 VFMA v0, v1, v2, v0 ; masked fused multiply-add, v0 = v1 * v2 + v0
FMT F32, RN VREDSUM v3, v0, v0 ; horizontal sum with explicit F32 rounding
VEXTRACT ra, v3, 0     ; lane 0 of v3 into ra
examples.note: EVX and PRED are the only masked forms: no separate masked mnemonic exists. A prefix is written before its instruction on the same line, as in the EVX and FMT lines above.

examples.title: atomic increment, two ways
code: AMOADD rd, rb, ESZ=2, MO=3 ; atomically add rd to [rb], acquire-release
retry:  LDLK   r8, rb, ESZ=2, MO=1
ADD    r8, r8, rd
STLK   r8, rb, ESZ=2, MO=2
JNZ    retry               ; ZF=0 means the monitor was lost
examples.note: AMOADD needs no retry loop because it is a single atomic operation; LDLK and STLK are the form to use when the update is not one arithmetic operation.

examples.title: system call stub
code: MOVI   ra, 1           ; syscall number 1 = write (pseudo: 3-byte IMMB)
MOV    rc, rd          ; argument 1 in rc
SYSCALL                ; v1 trap into the #SYS gate
RET                    ; result in ra
;; fast path equivalent
SYSENT 0               ; push IP and flags, enter SYSENT_BASE
SYSEXI                 ; restore flags and IP, return to L0
examples.note: SYSCALL goes through the IDT; SYSENT and SYSEXI are the fast gate pair that does not.

examples.title: string compare
code: MOV    ri, ra
MOV    rd, rb
MOV    rc, r8
CMPS   REP, ESZ=0      ; stops early when the bytes differ
JCND   NE, differ      ; ZF=0 means the strings differ
examples.note: CMPS under REP already implements the early-exit behaviour, so no explicit loop is needed.

examples.title: bit scan
code: BSF    ra, rb, ESZ=2   ; index of the lowest set bit
JCND   EQ, all_zero    ; ZF=1 means the source was zero
examples.note: BSF and BSR write zero into the destination when the source is zero, so the destination is always defined.

examples.title: floating-point accumulate
code: FLOAD  f1, rb, 0, FPF=2, RM=0
FLOAD  f2, rb, 4, FPF=2, RM=0
FADD   f3, f1, f2, FPF=2, RM=0
FSTORE f3, rb, 8, FPF=2, RM=0
examples.note: FLZ, FLO and FLV summarise the result of every arithmetic form; FCLASS or FCMPU is the way to test for NaN.

examples.title: transaction
code: XBEGIN MO=1, fallback  ; MO[0]=1 writes the abort code into ra
LD     rd, rb, 8
ADD    rd, rd, 1
ST     rd, rb, 8
XEND
fallback: MOV r9, ra           ; the abort code is in ra when MO[0] was set
JNZ    retry_path
examples.note: The fallback label is encoded as an offset from the end of XBEGIN, not from its address.

examples.title: shadow-stack protected call
code: caller: SHSTKPUSH after          ; shadow copy of the return address
CALLREL target           ; normal call, return address on the stack
after:  RET
target: ENDBR  MO=0              ; legal indirect target marker
SHSTKRET                 ; pops both, compares, branches only on a match
examples.note: A mismatch raises #SEC and the branch does not happen, so a corrupted return address cannot redirect control.

assembler_extension_notes: as.py resolves DRG, SR1-SR3, DRC, SRC, CR, DFR, SF1-SF3, SCL, PRT, O16, O32, OF8, OF16, A16, A32, AD8, IM8, IM16, I16 and I32. A v2 assembler must add the new tokens: CC, ESZ, MO, CH, RP, SPB, PKEY, FPF, RM, VL, VDG, VF1, VF2, VF3, KDG, KM1, KM2, MSI, SOP8, SEG and PRT16.

as.py treats O16 and O32 as a target address and subtracts the current instruction address; OF8 and OF16 are taken verbatim as register-relative offsets. That rule is correct for v2 as long as the assembler keeps applying it to branch mnemonics only, and applies the end-of-instruction rule to XBEGIN alone.

as.py rejects d0-d15 operands in DFR, SF1-SF3 because a REX prefix only extends DRG, SR1, SR2 and SR3. In v2 a vector register is named v0-v31 directly, so the vector forms do not need that restriction; the floating forms keep it because the ISA extends only the four general fields.
as.py's NIBBLE_LITERALS set covers 0x0-0xF, which is exactly what a reserved pad nibble needs; no change is required for those.
The lexical layer needs no change: labels, .org, .equ, .db, .dw, .dd, .ascii, ; and # comments are unchanged.
assembly_syntax.v1_syntax_compatibility: Every v1 source line assembles to the same bytes as before, with two exceptions that are the documented defect fixes: a relative branch is still target - branch address, and no v1 mnemonic changed spelling. Code that used the v1 0x5B byte for SAR must be re-assembled, because SAR now encodes as 0x5D and 0x5B is COPYIP only.

encoding_examples.source: v1 instructions.control.CMP, opcode 0x07, decode space base
encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 bits + SR1 4 + SR2 4 = 16 bits, 2 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 2/2 = 2 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: No prefix. The opcode byte 0x07 is followed by one byte whose high nibble is SR1=1 (ra) and whose low nibble is SR2=2 (rb), giving 0x12: the instruction is 07 12, two bytes. v1 declared length 3 for this 16-bit format; v2 declares 2 as required by allocation.json v1_entry_corrections, and because the reference decoder derives the length from the format the bytes a v1 assembler actually emitted were already two, so no v1 binary changes.
encoding_examples.note: The shortest complete register-form v2 example and the demonstration of the CMP defect fix.

encoding_examples.source: v1 instructions.arithmetic.ADD, opcode 0x70, decode space base

fields.meaning: 0xE0 | 0x8: the 0x8 bit extends the DRG field
4 + 16 = 20 = r20 because the REX bit is set
r2 (ra is r1, so r2 is the plain index 2)

encoding_examples.arithmetic: Body is OPC 8 + DRG 4 + pad 4 + SR1 4 + SR2 4 = 24 bits = 3 bytes; the REX prefix adds one byte on the wire, so the encoded size is 4.
encoding_examples.encoding: The REX prefix byte is 0xE0 | payload, and payload bit 3 (0x8) extends DRG. DRG encodes 4 and becomes 4 + 16 = 20, which is r20. The body is 70 | 40 | 23: byte 1 packs DRG=4 in the high nibble and the reserved 0x0 nibble in the low nibble, byte 2 packs SR1=2 and SR2=3. Total on the wire: 4 bytes, of which 3 are the instruction length and 1 is the prefix. REX payload bits are 0x8 for DRG, 0x4 for SR1, 0x2 for SR2 and 0x1 for SR3, and a set bit means add 16 to the four-bit index.
encoding_examples.note: The same instruction with three registers below r16 assembles to three bytes with no prefix.

encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + SOP 4 + DRG 4 + SR2 4 + ESZ 4 = 24 bits, 4 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 4/2 = 3 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: The sub-opcode nibble travels in the high nibble of the first byte after the opcode, so byte 1 is (SOP 0 << 4) | DRG 2 = 0x02 and byte 2 is (SR2 3 << 4) | ESZ 2 = 0x32. The whole instruction is 81 02 32.
encoding_examples.note: Shows how a primary opcode with SOP variants spends its sub-opcode nibble, and how a reserved-code field (ESZ=3) is what makes BT declare #UDI.

encoding_examples.assembly: JCND NE, 0x0180 (the branch itself at address 0x0100)
encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + SOP 4 + CC 4 + O16 16 = 32 bits, 6 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 6/2 = 4 bytes. Target arithmetic: 0x0100 + 0x0080 = 0x0180.
encoding_examples.encoding: Byte 1 is (SOP 0 << 4) | CC 1 = 0x01. The signed 16-bit offset 0x0080 occupies bytes 2 and 3 most-significant nibble first, so 00 80. The assembler computes the offset as target minus the address of the branch instruction itself, not the following instruction, so a backward branch encodes a negative value such as 0xFFF0 and the decoder sign-extends it.
encoding_examples.note: Demonstrates the relative-branch base rule and a multi-byte field that crosses a byte boundary.

fields.meaning: RP=0 mode, RP=0 counter width and direction

encoding_examples.arithmetic: Body is OPC 8 + SOP 4 + ESZ 4 = 16 bits = 2 bytes; the two-byte REP prefix is not part of the length, so the encoded size is 4.
encoding_examples.encoding: A two-byte prefix 0xFA plus one payload byte, then the two-byte body 8C 02. The whole operand state of a string instruction is architectural (ri, rd, rc and DF), so the body needs no register fields and every string instruction is exactly two bytes. REP is the only repetition mechanism in the ISA.
encoding_examples.note: Shows a two-byte prefix and the implicit-operand string form.

encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + SOP 4 + VDG 4 + VF1 4 + VF2 4 = 24 bits, 4 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 4/2 = 3 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: Byte 1 packs the sub-opcode in the high nibble and the destination vector register in the low nibble: (1 << 4) | 5 = 0x15. Byte 2 packs the two sources: (6 << 4) | 7 = 0x67. Every crypto instruction that reads the vector file follows this three-byte shape.
encoding_examples.note: Shows a 3-byte crypto form and the sub-opcode nibble again, this time with a vector destination.

encoding_examples.assembly: EVX k1, 1 VADD.b v3, v1, v2

fields.meaning: KDG=1 (k1 mask), VL=1 (vector length code 1 = 256 bit)
signed operand interpretation, wrap on overflow

encoding_examples.arithmetic: Body is OPC 8 + SOP 4 + ESZ 4 + MO 4 + VDG 4 + VF1 4 + VF2 4 = 32 bits, 6 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 6/2 = 4 bytes; the two-byte EVX prefix brings the encoded size to 6.
encoding_examples.encoding: EVX is 0xF7 followed by one payload byte holding KDG in the high nibble and the vector-length code in the low nibble, so k1 with VL=1 is 0x11. The body is A4 | 00 | 03 | 12: byte 1 carries SOP and ESZ, byte 2 carries MO and VDG, byte 3 carries the two sources. Masking is a prefix property, never a second opcode, which is why there is no masked VADD mnemonic.
encoding_examples.note: Shows EVX, the only way a vector operation is masked aside from the in-instruction KM1 forms.

encoding_examples.assembly: BMU FSIN f1, f2, FPF=2, RM=0
encoding_examples.source: B_fpvec instructions.bmu.FSIN, opcode 0x00 in decode space bmu, no sub_opcode

fields.meaning: mandatory escape byte that selects the bmu space
FSIN inside the bmu space; there is no sub-opcode here
reserved pad nibble that keeps the format even

encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + FPF 4 + RM 4 + MO 4 + DFR 4 + SF1 4 + pad 4 = 32 bits, 6 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 6/2 = 4 bytes declared; the BMU escape byte is a prefix and is not part of the length, so the encoded size is 4 + 1 = 5 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: The escape byte 0xF6 is followed by the opcode byte 0x00, which is meaningful only inside the bmu space, then three body bytes 20 | 01 | 20. A decoder that sees an opcode inside an escaped space must never compare it against base-space opcodes: 0x00 in the bmu space is FSIN, while 0x00 in the base space is the v1 NOP.
encoding_examples.note: The escaped-space example: length 4 plus one escape byte equals 5 bytes on the wire, which is the rule for the escape1, escape2, xtu, bmu and ciu spaces.

encoding_examples.assembly: CIU SHA3ABS rb, rc, rd, ri
encoding_examples.source: B_fpvec instructions.crypto.SHA3ABS, opcode 0x00 in decode space ciu, no sub_opcode

fields.meaning: mandatory escape byte that selects the ciu space

encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + ESZ 4 + MO 4 + DRG 4 + SR1 4 + SR2 4 + SR3 4 = 32 bits, 6 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 6/2 = 4 bytes declared; the CIU escape byte 0xFD is a one-byte prefix, so the encoded size is 5 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: CIU.EN is a single byte, unlike the two-byte v2 prefixes, so the space selector costs one byte. The body packs ESZ and MO in byte 1 and three register pairs in bytes 2 and 3. As in the bmu space, opcode 0x00 here is a ciu-space opcode and has nothing to do with base-space NOP.
encoding_examples.note: A second escaped-space example with a one-byte escape, on a different space, to show the rule is a space property and not a bmu quirk.

fields.meaning: ra, the first destination; the second is ra+1, which is rb
signed displacement, two nibbles across the byte boundary

encoding_examples.arithmetic: OPC 8 + SOP 4 + DRG 4 + SR1 4 + OF8 8 + ESZ 4 = 36 bits, 6 nibbles after OPC, 1 + 6/2 = 4 bytes.
encoding_examples.encoding: The 8-bit offset starts in the low nibble of byte 2 and ends in the high nibble of byte 3, so byte 2 is (SR1 2 << 4) | 0x0 = 0x20 and byte 3 is (0x8 << 4) | ESZ 2 = 0x82. OF8 is signed: +8 encodes as 0x08 and -8 encodes as 0xF8, which the decoder sign-extends before adding to the base.
encoding_examples.note: Shows a field wider than one nibble that crosses a byte boundary, and the signed-offset rule for the OF family.

v1_subset_guarantee.statement: Hayneko_Arch32S v2 is a strict superset of v1: every v1 mnemonic keeps its name, its opcode byte, its sub-opcode, its format (after the documented corrections) and its length, so every v1 program that assembles against the v1 table assembles against the v2 table to the same bytes, and the v1 reference interpreter executes it with the same effect.
v1_subset_guarantee.what_is_preserved: 156 v1 instructions in 10 categories, their descriptions, their flag effects, their mode, their can_use_with_prefixes lists and their reserved nibbles. The v1 top-level keys are preserved too, including the misspelled psuedo_instructions key, which v2 keeps for loader compatibility and does not fix.
v1_subset_guarantee.what_is_added: 399 v2 instructions in 20 categories, 21 new field tokens, 8 new prefixes, 8 new flags, 9 new status flags, 8 new exceptions, 6 new device IRQs and 16 software vectors. None of them takes an encoding that v1 already used: the v2 authoring ranges are disjoint from every v1 primary opcode, and three parts were cross-checked for encoding uniqueness.
v1_subset_guarantee.numeric_identity: 156 v1 instructions plus 399 v2 instructions is 555 instruction entries, which is exactly the mnemonic count the validator derives from v1 plus the three parts.

v1_fixes.reason: The format OPC,SR1,SR2 is 16 bits, which is 2 bytes, so the declared 3 was a metadata error.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: None. The v1 decoder derives its length from the format, so v1 already consumed two bytes; only the declared number changes.

v1_fixes.reason: The v1 layout is 72 bits after OPC, which is 10 bytes, but the mnemonic declares 13. The corrected layout is 96 bits after OPC, which is exactly 13 bytes.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: A v1 assembler emitted ten bytes for NOP13 and a v2 assembler emits thirteen. Code that used NOP13 as a thirteen-byte pad must be re-assembled; code that used it as a ten-byte pad should use NOP10.

v1_fixes.reason: The format OPC,0x0,SOP,I16 is 32 bits, which is 4 bytes.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: None: the format already produced four bytes, so only the declared number changes.

v1_fixes.reason: IM16 was never a field of the encode section; the single 16-bit immediate field is I16.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: None: 16 bits either way, so the bytes are unchanged and only the token name changes.

v1_fixes.reason: OF16 was never a field of the encode section; the single 16-bit offset field is O16.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: None: both are 16-bit signed offsets, so the bytes and the sign extension are identical.

v1_fixes.reason: A JSON null inside a prefix list is meaningless; an empty list is the correct way to say that no prefix is allowed.
v1 declared sub_opcode 0x0 but the format never encoded SOP, so BTLE and BTBE produced the same bytes and one of them was unreachable.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: A v1 two-byte BTLE becomes a three-byte v2 BTLE. This is one of the two binary-incompatible fixes and it cannot be avoided: the v1 encodings of BTLE and BTBE were literally identical.

v1_fixes.reason: The corrected SOP layout is 24 bits.
Same defect as FIX-11 with sub_opcode 0x4.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: A v1 two-byte BTBE becomes a three-byte v2 BTBE.

v1_fixes.reason: The corrected SOP layout is 24 bits.

SAR and COPYIP both claimed primary opcode 0x5B with no sub-opcode, so the two instructions were distinguished only by a heuristic on the low nibble of the second byte. 0x5D was unallocated in v1, so SAR moves there and 0x5B becomes COPYIP alone.
v1_fixes.binary_effect: A v1 artifact that encodes SAR as 0x5B must be re-assembled; the byte 0x5B now always means COPYIP. Because 0x5B had two meanings in v1, no rewriting of an existing image can be correct in general, so a loader must re-assemble rather than patch.

compatibility.v1_fix_summary: Fifteen corrections in three groups. Metadata only, because the v1 decoder derives its length from the format and never read the declared number: CMP length 3 to 2, PUSHIMMW length 3 to 4, and the IM16 to I16 and OF16 to O16 respellings in PUSHIMMW, LDSTVALOW, STSTVALOW, LDOFIP and STOFIP, which are 16-bit fields either way. Cosmetic: the two meaningless null entries in the prefix lists of NOP and CLR ra become empty lists. Binary visible, and therefore re-assembly items: NOP13's format now really produces thirteen bytes, BTLE and BTBE gain the SOP nibble they always declared and become three bytes, and SAR moves from the double-booked 0x5B to 0x5D so that 0x5B means COPYIP alone. Provenance lists seventeen items because the OF16-to-O16 respelling class is applied to the four instruction formats and to the two v1 descriptions that repeated the old spelling, and because the SAR relocation is counted separately.

what_a_v1_only_tool_sees.instruction_table: A v1 loader reads the 156 v1 entries unchanged and finds 399 unknown mnemonics. Because every v2 entry lies outside the v1 opcode ranges and outside the v1 sub-opcode assignments, a v1 decoder that looks up (opcode, sub_opcode) simply fails to find them and raises its undefined-instruction exception, which is exactly #UDI.
what_a_v1_only_tool_sees.prefix_bytes: v1 treats 0xE0-0xEF as REX, 0xD0-0xDF as ISL, 0xF0 as DBI, 0xF1 as TBI, 0xF2 and 0xF3 as BRH_H, 0xF4 as LOCK, 0xF5 as XTU and 0xF6 as BMU. The v2 bytes 0xF7 (EVX), 0xF8 (OPSZ), 0xF9 (MEMO), 0xFA (REP), 0xFB (PRED), 0xFC (SEC), 0xFD (CIU), 0xFE (FMT) and 0xFF are not prefixes in v1, so a v1 decoder treats each as an opcode byte and raises #UDI at that address, before it can misinterpret the rest of the stream.
what_a_v1_only_tool_sees.flags: The eight new flags occupy bits that v1 already declared reserved inside the same 32-bit flags word, so a v1 tool that saves and restores flags keeps them intact as long as it treats the word as opaque. A v1 tool that reconstructs the word from its 16 known bits would clear the new flags, which is a real, documented hazard of a 16-bit-flag-shim.
what_a_v1_only_tool_sees.interrupts: Vectors 0-33 keep their numbers and meanings. A v2 machine never raises a v2-only exception into a v1 handler unless the program executes a v2 instruction, so a v1 handler table stays correct.
what_a_v1_only_tool_sees.safe_statement: A v1-only tool can run v1 binaries unchanged, can assemble v1 sources unchanged, and cannot silently mis-execute a v2 instruction: it fails closed with #UDI at the first byte it does not know.

loader_notes.FIELD_SIZES: Add the 21 new tokens with their widths: CC 4, ESZ 4, MO 4, CH 4, RP 4, SPB 4, PKEY 4, FPF 4, RM 4, VL 4, VDG 4, VF1 4, VF2 4, VF3 4, KDG 4, KM1 4, KM2 4, MSI 8, SOP8 8, SEG 16, PRT16 16. The 27 existing entries stay as they are.
loader_notes.NIBBLE_LITERALS: No change is required. The set 0x0-0xF already covers every reserved pad nibble the v2 formats use.
loader_notes.FOUR_BIT_FIELDS: Add every new 4-bit token so that two of them pack into one byte in format order: CC, ESZ, MO, CH, RP, SPB, PKEY, FPF, RM, VL, VDG, VF1, VF2, VF3, KDG, KM1 and KM2. SOP is already present. MSI, SOP8, SEG and PRT16 are byte or half-word fields and must not be added.
loader_notes.SIGNED_FIELDS: No new member is needed: the offset family is closed at OF8, O16 and O32, and every new token is either unsigned or a code field. Keep OF16 in the set only so that a v1 artifact still parses; a v2 instruction never uses it.
loader_notes.legacy_spellings: The v1 reference implementation's FIELD_SIZES still carries IM16 and OF16 spellings for v1 source compatibility. That is correct and must stay, because a v1 image may reference them, but the v2 instruction set uses I16 and O16 exclusively: no v2 entry may contain either legacy spelling, and the v2 encode section declares neither.
loader_notes.the_0x5B_workaround: The explicit special case in fetch_decode that inspects the low nibble of the second byte when the opcode is 0x5B, choosing COPYIP when it is zero and SAR otherwise, becomes unnecessary the moment SAR moves to 0x5D. It must be deleted rather than left in place, because after the move 0x5B has exactly one meaning and the heuristic would silently accept a malformed COPYIP whose reserved nibble is not zero.
loader_notes.decode_spaces: A v2 loader must key its table on the triple (decode_space, opcode, sub_opcode). For the base space the space key is the string base; for an escaped space it is the space name that the escape prefix selected, and the opcode is compared inside that space, where 0x00 is a legal opcode.
loader_notes.unknown_space_instructions: Any (space, opcode, sub_opcode) triple that is not in the table must decode as #UDI until it is implemented. That includes every reserved opcode, every reserved sub-opcode, every reserved ESZ, MO, CH, SPB and RM code, and every byte of the escape2 space, which is reserved for a future unit. The illegal byte 0xFF is always #UDI even before any lookup.
loader_notes.prefix_length: The loader must decode 0xF7-0xFC and 0xFE as two-byte prefixes, 0xFD as a one-byte prefix, 0xF0-0xF6 as the v1 prefixes with their v1 lengths, 0xFF as a permanently illegal byte, and must count a maximum of four prefix bytes.
loader_notes.length_and_escapes: length counts OPC plus the operand fields. The encoded size is length plus one byte for every escape prefix, zero for a base-space instruction and for a base-space instruction carrying REX, LOCK, BRH_H, ISL, MEMO, OPSZ, REP, PRED, SEC, FMT or EVX. A loader that advances the instruction pointer by length alone will desynchronize on every escaped-space instruction.
loader_notes.flags_word: The flags word widens by eight bits of meaning, not in width. A loader that models flags as individual booleans must add AF, PF, VF, TF and RF, and the status flags VME, TXE, SSE, PKE, DTE, SXE, MCE and VLE, at the bit positions that the v2 flags and status_flags sections declare.
loader_notes.vector_state: A loader that supports the vector file must allocate 32 registers of 256 bits and eight predicate registers of 32 bits, and must keep the v1 alias rule that d0-d15 are v16-v31.

interrupt_and_fault_compatibility.existing_vectors: Vectors 0-33 keep their numbers and their names, and the v1 descriptions are reproduced verbatim in interrupt_vectors.
interrupt_and_fault_compatibility.new_vectors: Vectors 8-15 were unassigned in v1, so v2 can use them without moving anything; a v1 program never triggers them because every instruction that can raise them is new.
interrupt_and_fault_compatibility.fault_names: The nine fault names that appear in instruction fault lists across v1 and the three parts are #UDI, #GP, #PGF, #AC, #SEC, #MAV, #DIV, #VC and #NMI, and all nine are defined in interrupt_vectors together with the seven v1 exceptions and the new software and device vectors.

compatibility.source_compatibility: v1 assembly source is accepted unchanged by the v2 assembler with two exceptions that follow from the fixes: a SAR mnemonic now encodes as 0x5D, and the padding NOP13 now really is thirteen bytes. Both are re-assemblies, not source edits.

changelog.summary: v1 contributes 156 instructions, 1 pseudo instruction and 14 micro-coded expansions and keeps every encoding it had, with the fifteen documented corrections. v2 adds 399 instructions, 45 pseudo instructions and 19 micro-coded expansions across seventeen named extensions, and takes the total to 555 instruction entries.

by_extension.note: The v1 instruction set itself, preserved mnemonic for mnemonic and encoding for encoding, with the fifteen corrections of compatibility.v1_fixes applied, plus the seventeen system-control and identity instructions that extend the v1 system group rather than belonging to a new extension: RDCR, WRCR, RDMSR, WRMSR, INVLPG, INVTLB, INVEPT, ICACHEINV, CLWBI, SYSENT, SYSEXI, CPUID, READREV, SETMODE, GETMODE, WRFLAGS and RDFLAGS. BASE also carries the container-level changes: six decode spaces instead of one, the prefix space extended from 0xF0-0xF6 to 0xF0-0xFF, and the 21 field tokens of the v2 encode section. 173 = 156 preserved + 17 added.

Bit test and modify (BT, BTS, BTR, BTC and the immediate forms), bit scan and count (BSF, BSR, POPCNT, CLZ, CTZ, PARCNT, BREV), double-width and flag-free shifts (SHLD, SHRD, SHLX, SHRX, SARX, ROLX, RORX), bit gather and scatter (PEXT, PDEP, BZHI, MASKLSB), field extract and insert (BEXT, BINS, BEXTS, BEXTD, BINSD) and Gray code (GRAYE, GRAYD). Primary opcodes 0x81-0x87.

Width conversion (SEXT, ZEXT, TRUNC, BSWAP, CVTSZ, SATCAST, PACK) and integer arithmetic: high halves and multiply-accumulate (MULH, MULHS, MULX, MULI, MADD, MSUB, MADDU, MSUBU), divide and remainder (DIVMOD, REM, REMS, DIVI), independent carry chains (ADDC, SUBC, ADCX, ADOX), min and max (MAXS, MINS, MAXU, MINU, ABSDIFF, AVG) and saturation (SATADD, SATSUB, SATADDU, SATSUBU, CLAMP, CLAMPU, ISQRT). Primaries 0x12-0x16 and 0x88-0x8B.

MOVS, CMPS, SCAS, STOS, LODS and their non-temporal forms MOVSN and STOSN, all two bytes, all on implicit ri, rd, ra and rc with DF as the direction and REP as the only repetition mechanism. Primary 0x8C.

Packed BCD arithmetic and conversion: ADDBCD, SUBBCD, CMPBCD, NEGBCD, BCDSHL, BCDSHR, MULBCD, DIVBCD, BCD2BIN and BIN2BCD, with AF and VF reporting digit carry and invalid digits. Primaries 0x8D and 0x8E.

Unified conditional execution and extended branches: JCND and JCNDL on a CC nibble, JMPREL, JMPRELL, CALLREL, the LOOP family, JTABLE, CALLTAB, RETFAR, and the condition materialisation set SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC, TSTCC. Primaries 0x78-0x7E and 0x8F.

A complete scalar floating-point unit: the four arithmetic operations, SQRT, reciprocals, the fused multiply-add family, sign and select, compare and classify, the sixteen conversion forms, moves, load and store, exponent manipulation and the format-state instruction. FPF selects F16, BF16, F32 or F64 and RM selects the rounding mode; FLZ, FLO and FLV summarise a result. Primaries 0xB0-0xB9.

A 256-bit vector unit with 32 registers, eight predicate registers, configuration, unit-stride, strided, indexed, broadcast and masked memory forms, lane arithmetic, fused forms, logic, shifts, compare and mask algebra, permutes, reductions, lane and conversion forms, and vector state save and restore. Masking lives in the EVX and PRED prefixes. Primaries 0xA0-0xAF.

AES, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 rounds, carry-less and GF(2^8) multiply, CRC32 and CRC32C, the entropy instructions RDRAND and RDSEED, constant-time compare, key management (KEYGEN, KEYLOAD, KEYZERO), Montgomery multiply, and the ciu-space sponge and stream primitives SHA3ABS, SHA3FIN, KECCAKF, POLY1305 and CHACHA. Primaries 0xC0-0xC5 plus the ciu space.

The whole bmu decode space: sixteen transcendental functions, big-integer arithmetic on register blocks (BMUL, BADD, BSUB, BDIV, BMOD, BSHL, BSHR, BAND, BOR, BXOR, BNOT, BCMP), float and big-integer conversion (B2D, D2B), and matrix operations (MMUL, MVEC, MTRANS).

Load-linked and store-conditional (LDLK, STLK, CLREX), compare-and-swap (CAS), ten store-form and five fetch-form AMOs, and the three fences MFENCE, LFENCE and SFENCE that the v2 ordering model names. Primaries 0xC8-0xCB.

Best-effort transactional memory: XBEGIN, XEND, XABORT, XTEST and XSUSPEND, with sector-granularity conflict detection, an architectural nesting depth of eight and a documented abort-code table. Primaries 0xCC and 0xCD.

Sized and paired memory access (LDP, STP, LDM, STM, LDX, STX, LDSX, LDZX), cache hints and maintenance (PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, CACHECTL, LDNT, STNT), and explicit memory management in the escape1 space (MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT, GETPGT, MKEYALLOC, MKEYFREE, EPTMAP, EPTUNMAP) plus the TLB maintenance instructions INVLPG, INVTLB, INVEPT, ICACHEINV and CLWBI. Primaries 0x1A-0x1C, 0x9A and the escape1 space.
VMENTER, VMEXIT, VMRUN, VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMCALL, VMFUNC, VMLOAD and VMSTORE, with a 4 KiB control block addressed by cr8, a fifteen-entry exit-reason table, EPT and nested paging. Primary 0x9C.

The whole xtu decode space: shadow stack (SHSTKPUSH, SHSTKPOP, SHSTKRET), control-flow integrity (ENDBR, SSBB), speculation barriers (SPECBAR, IBPB, STIBP), enclaves (ENCLS, ENCLU, ENCLV, ATTEST), data hygiene (ZEROIZE, CTCOPY) and protection keys (RDPKRU, WRPKRU).

DBGON, DBGOFF, BPSET, BPCLR, WCHSET, WCHCLR, STEP, TRACEON, TRACEOFF and DBGREAD: eight execution breakpoints, eight watchpoints, single step through TF, a 16-byte-record trace buffer and a single instruction that reads every debug register. Primary 0x9D.

Time and performance counters (RDTSC, RDTSCP, RDPMU, PMUCTL) and power management in the escape1 space (SLEEP, STANDBY, CLKGATE, MONITOR, MWAIT, WFI, WFE, DVFSHINT, RESET). Primaries 0x97 and escape1 0x00-0x03. The seventeen system-control instructions of C_sys.system_ext are counted under BASE instead, which is the partition D1_meta publishes; together the two rows cover all 21 system_ext instructions plus the 9 power instructions, so nothing is counted twice and nothing is dropped.
16-bit port I/O and its ordering controls: INX, OUTX, INS, OUTS, IODELAY and IOSYNC, extending the v1 8-bit IN and OUT. Escape1 opcode 0x20.

changelog.totals_check: 17 + 33 + 36 + 7 + 10 + 18 + 33 + 77 + 30 + 33 + 22 + 5 + 24 + 9 + 16 + 10 + 13 + 6 = 399, and 173 + 382 = 555 for the full instruction set, exactly as D1_meta's extension partition counts it.
non_instruction_changes: Six decode spaces replace the single v1 space: base, escape1 (DBI 0xF0), escape2 (TBI 0xF1, reserved), xtu (XTU.EN 0xF5), bmu (BMU.EN 0xF6) and ciu (CIU.EN 0xFD).
Eight new prefixes: EVX 0xF7, OPSZ 0xF8, MEMO 0xF9, REP 0xFA, PRED 0xFB, SEC 0xFC, FMT 0xFE, plus CIU 0xFD which doubles as a space selector; 0xFF becomes permanently illegal.
Five new flags (AF, PF, VF, TF, RF) and eight new status flags (VME, TXE, SSE, PKE, DTE, SXE, MCE, VLE), which together widen the flags word from 16 to 24 defined bits.
Eight new exceptions at vectors 8-15, six new device IRQs at 34-39 and sixteen software vectors at 48-63.
A nine-stage pipeline replaces the seven-stage pipeline, and the memory model becomes a written weak model with three named fences.
A three-level page table with 2 MiB and 1 GiB large pages and 8-byte entries replaces the two-level 32-bit table; the v1 layout stays readable through the low half of every entry.
changelog.extension_partition_agreement: The eighteen extension ids and their instruction counts are the partition D1_meta publishes (BASE 173, BIT 33, MATH 36, STR 7, BCD 10, COND 18, FPU 33, VEC 77, CIU 30, BMU 33, ATOM 22, TX 5, MMU 24, VIRT 9, SEC 16, DBG 10, PMU 13, IO2 6). Two fragments of one deliverable must not disagree about how the same 555 instructions are grouped, so this file follows D1's partition rather than inventing a second one; the per-entry detail below is unchanged and the sum is identical either way.

isa_invariants.name: byte alignment
isa_invariants.rule: The number of 4-bit units after OPC in a format must be even.
isa_invariants.check: For every instruction entry, count 4-bit units of every token after the first and assert (sum mod 2) == 0, counting a 0xN literal as one unit, SOP as one, IM8 as two, I16 and O16 as four, I32 and O32 as eight.

isa_invariants.name: length identity
isa_invariants.rule: length == 1 + (units after OPC) / 2 for every entry.
isa_invariants.check: Recompute from the format and compare with the declared length; the validator does exactly this and reports any mismatch.

isa_invariants.name: escaped-space size
isa_invariants.rule: The encoded size of an instruction in an escaped space is length + 1, because the escape byte (DBI, XTU, BMU or CIU) is a prefix. For a base-space instruction the encoded size is length plus one byte for each prefix present.
isa_invariants.check: For every entry with decode_space other than base, assert that the assembler emits declared length + 1 bytes and that the first emitted byte is 0xF0, 0xF5, 0xF6 or 0xFD; for every base-space entry, assert that the emitted size equals length + number of prefix bytes and that at most four prefix bytes are present.

isa_invariants.name: encoding uniqueness
isa_invariants.rule: The triple (decode_space, opcode, sub_opcode) is globally unique across v1 and all v2 parts.
isa_invariants.check: Build a dictionary keyed by the triple over the whole instruction set and assert no key is inserted twice and that no base-space primary above 0xCF exists.

isa_invariants.name: sub-opcode presence
isa_invariants.rule: An entry carries sub_opcode exactly when its format contains SOP or SOP8, and a primary opcode either uses SOP for all of its instructions or for none of them.
isa_invariants.check: For every entry, assert (SOP in format or SOP8 in format) == (sub_opcode present); then group entries by (space, opcode) and assert the group is uniform.

isa_invariants.name: distinct operands
isa_invariants.rule: No field token appears twice inside one format; the 0x0 pad nibble is the only repetition allowed.
isa_invariants.check: Count token occurrences per format and assert every count is at most one apart from 0x0.

isa_invariants.name: field-token licence
isa_invariants.rule: Every format token is declared in the encode section, and neither IM16 nor OF16 is ever declared or referenced by a v2 entry.
isa_invariants.check: Assert every token is a key of the encode table; assert IM16 and OF16 are absent from the encode table and from every v2 format, and that I16 and O16 are present.

isa_invariants.name: prefix legality
isa_invariants.rule: Every prefix name in can_use_with_prefixes is one of the sixteen declared prefixes, an escaped-space entry lists its own escape prefix, and LOCK appears only on an instruction with a memory operand.
isa_invariants.check: Assert the prefix list is a subset of the declared names; assert every non-base entry lists DBI, XTU, BMU or CIU; assert any entry listing LOCK has a memory reference in its semantics.

isa_invariants.name: mode floor
isa_invariants.rule: Every mode is one of L0..L7; an instruction that touches a control register, an MSR, the TLB, the IDT, a key, the debug layer, the power state or an enclave is at least L2, virtualization is L5 or L6 and enclave and attestation instructions are L7.
isa_invariants.check: Assert the mode is in the enumeration and applies the floor table mechanically to the mnemonic's family: any entry whose description mentions a control register, an MSR, a TLB, an IDT or a key must have mode L2 or above.

isa_invariants.name: space ownership
isa_invariants.rule: An instruction's opcode lies inside the range that allocation.json assigns to its owner in that space.
isa_invariants.check: For every entry, look up the owner's space_ranges and assert the opcode value is inside one of the closed intervals; assert no v2 entry reuses a v1 (space, opcode, sub_opcode).

isa_invariants.name: flag naming
isa_invariants.rule: Every name in modify_flags and flags_read comes from the v2 flags or status_flags table, and a status flag may only be written by the instruction that owns it (VLE by VSETVL, VME by VMENTER and VMEXIT, PKE by RDPKRU and WRPKRU, DTE by DBGON, DBGOFF, TRACEON and TRACEOFF, TF by STEP).
isa_invariants.check: Assert the flag set is a subset of the declared names; assert every status flag written by an entry appears in the owner list of that flag.

isa_invariants.name: length bounds
isa_invariants.rule: Every v2 instruction is 2..16 bytes and every v1 control instruction may be 1 byte; the encoded size including prefixes never exceeds 16 bytes.
isa_invariants.check: Assert 2 <= length <= 16 for every v2 entry, and assert length + prefix bytes <= 16 for every entry.

isa_invariants.name: v1 preservation
isa_invariants.rule: Every v1 mnemonic survives with its opcode, sub_opcode, format and semantics, allowing only the fifteen entries of compatibility.v1_fixes to differ.
isa_invariants.check: Diff the v1 table against the v2 table mnemonic by mnemonic; assert every difference is one of the fifteen recorded corrections and that no v1 mnemonic is missing.

isa_invariants.name: no placeholder semantics
isa_invariants.rule: Every instruction has a description of at least 40 ASCII characters that starts with its own mnemonic and a pseudo-semantics expression of at least 8 characters, and no text says TBD, TODO or placeholder.
isa_invariants.check: Scan every description and pseudo_semantics string for the required prefix, the minimum length, ASCII-only content and the forbidden placeholder words.

notes.architecture:
OWNER SCOPE. This fragment is the architectural metadata of Hayneko_Arch32S v2.0 (owner D1_meta). It authors no instruction: every instruction-level fact below was read out of the v1 ISA file and the three delivered parts A_core (104 instructions, 45 pseudo, 14 micro_rom), B_fpvec (173) and C_sys (122, plus 5 micro_rom), and every count, token, flag, prefix, fault and opcode in this file was computed from those files rather than assumed.
CORPUS. 555 instructions in total: 156 carried from v1 unchanged and 399 new (320 in the base space, 25 in escape1, 16 in xtu, 33 in bmu, 5 in ciu, 0 in escape2). 48 field tokens are declared (the 27 v1 tokens verbatim plus the 21 new tokens of SPEC section 4), 29 flag bits (16 flags plus 13 status flags), 17 prefix bytes, 16 condition codes, 6 decode spaces and 208 base-space primaries. Only the exact token and flag sets actually used by the corpus are endorsed below as in-use; the rest are declared and marked as such in their descriptions.
WHY THE FULL SPEC SECTION 4 TOKEN SET IS DECLARED. The gate only requires the tokens the corpus uses, but the encode section is the architecture document a decoder is built from, so all 21 new tokens are declared with their widths and code tables. Five of them are not used as operand fields by any instruction in v2.0 and each says so in its own description: RP and PKEY exist only inside the REP and SEC prefix payloads, SOP8 is the reserved 8-bit escape-space sub-opcode (the delivered escape spaces group their variants in the 4-bit SOP nibble or give each mnemonic its own opcode byte), and VL is the vector-length code carried only in the EVX prefix payload (0xF7) because the active element count of a vector instruction is architectural state installed by VSETVL, not a per-instruction operand. I16 and O16 are declared as required and IM16 and OF16 are not declared anywhere: the five v1 instructions that wrote those spellings (PUSHIMMW, LDSTVALOW, STSTVALOW, LDOFIP, STOFIP) are repaired by allocation.v1_entry_corrections to I16 and O16, which is SPEC section 12 item 5.
DECLARED BUT UNUSED TOKENS. AD8 is declared (v1 declared it too) and no instruction in v1 or in the three parts uses it; the absolute-8 addressing mode says the same thing. GB1 and GB2 are the v1 bit fields and are also unused by any instruction. ISL is the length-hint prefix field and is unused as an operand field. These are listed so that a decoder implementer does not hunt for an emitter that does not exist.
REX BIT ORDER - DECISION AND DEVIATION. The task brief describes the REX payload as bit0 DRG, bit1 SR1, bit2 SR2, bit3 SR3. Both authoritative sources disagree with that numbering: the v1 prefixes table declares the REX byte as 1110 followed by the ordered list [DRG, SR1, SR2, SR3] read most significant bit first (so DRG is bit 3 and SR3 is bit 0), and the v1 reference implementation applies exactly that mapping (DRG 0x8, SR1 0x4, SR2 0x2, SR3 0x1) in _apply_rex. This file follows the implementation, because an implementer who follows the brief wording instead would silently swap destination and immediate-source extension bits for every REX-prefixed instruction. register_renaming.rex_byte_layout records both statements side by side so the reviewer can see the discrepancy, and the extension formula (physical = (field + 16*bit) & 31) is unaffected by which numbering is used.
MASK FILE - DECISION. The 4-bit KDG, KM1 and KM2 fields can name k0-k15, but the delivered vector unit implements eight predicate registers k0-k7 (B_fpvec states this normatively and SPEC 9-D1 asks for k0-k7), so codes 8-15 are declared reserved with #UDI. A predicate register is 32 bits, not 8: at VLEN 256 the finest element is 8 bits, which is 32 lanes, and B_fpvec's VSTATE record fixes the layout arithmetically (32 x 32 bytes of vector state plus 8 x 4 bytes of mask state plus 8 bytes of VL/VLE = 1064 bytes, with the k0 word saved as all ones and ignored on restore). Bits above the active mask length read as zero. The k0 rule is single, and the parts and this document agree on it: k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask, it reads all ones for the active mask length in every mask-operand position (EVX/PRED prefix or KM1/KM2), a KDG write to it is discarded, VCLEAR leaves it alone, and k1-k7 are ordinary read/write registers (registers.mask_notes.k0_rule).
REGISTER SHAPES. The v1 keys are preserved verbatim, including the misspelling interger (the validator and the v1 loaders index that spelling) and the nested float/double shape of floating_point. kernel and control keep v1's flat shape: registers.control is minimum_privileged_level followed by cr0-cr15 and nothing else, seventeen keys, with cr0-cr3 byte-for-byte identical to v1, so a v1 consumer that reads registers.control.cr0 keeps working. The narrative that used to live in a wrapper now lives in registers.control_notes, which is a sibling of the control section and not part of it. vector keeps a vector_registers wrapper because v1 has no vector section at all; lane_views and element_formats sit beside it as descriptive keys.
FLAGS - WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRITTEN. 29 flag bits are declared. The delivered corpus writes or reads 19 of them (ZF, CF, OF, NF, DF, FLZ, FLO, FLV, IF, AC, AF, PF, VF, TF, RF, PKE, DTE, VME, VLE). The other ten (BE, XTE, BME, CIE, VIE, PROT, SSE, SXE, MCE, TXE) are architectural state that no delivered instruction writes: SSE and SXE are tested by the shadow-stack and supervisor-access descriptions but no entry lists them in flags_read or modify_flags, and BE, XTE, BME, CIE, VIE, PROT and MCE are v1 status bits or machine-level enables. They are declared because the v1 contract declares them and because an implementer must implement the bits even where no v2 instruction writes them.
PREFIXES. Seventeen prefix bytes exist: the eight v1 prefixes verbatim plus the eight new modifiers of SPEC section 5 plus ILL. ILL is the name this fragment gives the permanently illegal 0xFF byte; SPEC section 5 lists that byte without a name and asks D1 to document it, and it is not a prefix, it is a trap. The prefix order is the v1 order with the new modifiers inserted: ISL, BRH_H, LOCK, REP, SEC, PRED, EVX, OPSZ, FMT, MEMO, REX, one space escape, OPC. REX stays last so that register extension is applied after every other modifier is decoded, and the space escape stays last before OPC because it selects the opcode table. max_size stays 4, and it counts bytes rather than prefixes, so a single two-byte prefix plus two one-byte prefixes is the practical maximum; 13 illegal combinations are enumerated, including the five the brief requires (two register-extension prefixes, LOCK without a memory operand, EVX on a non-vector op, FMT on an integer op, ILL anywhere).
ESCAPED-SPACE SIZE - STATED ONCE, AS REQUIRED. An escaped-space instruction declares length as OPC plus its operand fields, exactly like a base-space instruction, so its encoded size is length+1: the mandatory escape byte (DBI 0xF0, XTU 0xF5, BMU 0xF6, CIU 0xFD) is a prefix like REX and is outside length. All 79 escaped-space entries in the three parts say this in their own encoding_notes and instruction_length_rules.escaped_space_length restates it. A 3-byte escape1 MAP therefore occupies 4 bytes and a 4-byte bmu FSIN occupies 5.
RELATIVE BRANCH BASE. v1 and v2 relative transfers are relative to the address of the branch instruction itself with a signed offset: target = start_ip + sign_extend(offset). The v1 reference implementation keeps ip on the branch address while the handler runs and branches with ip + offset, and every relative-transfer description in A_core restates the rule. CALLREL additionally pushes start_ip + 5, the address of the following instruction. One documented exception exists and is not a branch: XBEGIN measures its fallback offset from the end of the instruction, because the fallback is where a transaction resumes.
ISL. The ISL prefix is a length hint (0xD0 + 4-bit total length, valid 4-15). It cannot annotate a 16-byte instruction because 16 does not fit in four bits, and it never changes the architectural length, which always comes from the format. The v1 reference implementation decodes the nibble and ignores it; v2.0 keeps that behaviour, so a mismatching ISL is not a fault.
REPORTED CAVEATS RATHER THAN SILENT FIXES. (a) v1 booked COPYIP and SAR on 0x5B; the map records 0x5B as COPYIP and 0x5D as the SAR relocation target that allocation.v1_fixes mandates, and notes that no part file carries SAR because it is a v1 entry the integrator moves. (b) 0x3F is unallocated: no owner claims it in allocation.json and no v1 or v2 instruction uses it, so the map marks it reserved with owner none. (c) Sixteen primaries are reserved (0x17, 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F, 0x3F, 0x67, 0x7F, 0xBA-0xBF, 0xC6, 0xC7, 0xCE, 0xCF); 0x17, 0x67 and 0x7F are A_core reserved by explicit decision, 0x1D-0x1F, 0xBA-0xBF, 0xC6-0xC7 and 0xCE-0xCF are unused tails of an owner range, and 0x3F is unowned. (d) LEASC treats SCL as a numeric multiplier while LDX and STX treat it as a shift count of 0-3 bits; the v1 reference implementation confirms the multiplier reading for LEASC, so the addressing-mode table documents both meanings instead of unifying them. (e) The v1 SHLR, SHRR, SARR, ROLR and RORR forms live at 0x50 with SOP 0x8-0xF while the plain SHL/SHR/SAR/ROL/ROR live at 0x58/0x59/0x5D/0x5E/0x5F; both families are listed in the map. (f) No primary in the whole corpus mixes bare instructions with SOP variants, so the v2 grouping rule holds everywhere without a grandfather clause.
PRIORITY/FLOOR. Instruction modes were read, not invented: L0 463 instructions, L1 1 (JMPFAR), L2 11, L3 58, L4 0, L5 14, L6 2 (VMEXIT, VMCALL), L7 6. No instruction floors at L4. The mode capability masks are monotone from L0 to L7 and the L5/L6 step is flat in bits on purpose: the hypervisor/guest split is enforced by the VME flag (VM entry requires VME=0, guest exits require VME=1), not by the mask.
ABI DECISIONS. v1 ABI.format is kept verbatim and extended with v0, v1-v8 and k1. callee_saved is bp, sp and r16-r22; r23 is the thread pointer and is deliberately neither callee-saved nor allocatable. The entire floating-point, vector and predicate files are volatile because d0-d15 alias v16-v31 and the v1 ABI already passes floating-point arguments in d1-d8, so making any vector register callee-saved would contradict the v1 argument convention. A variadic routine receives the number of vector arguments in t0 (r24), which is never a parameter register. The frame layout follows the v1 ENTR/LEAV and CALL/push32 mechanics: [bp] saved bp, [bp+4] return address, [bp+8] first stack argument. The red zone is 128 bytes and the stack alignment is 16, which means a callee sees sp+4 16-byte aligned.
LENGTH FACTS. 1 byte: 28 v1 instructions, none in v2. 2 bytes: 91. 3 bytes: 210. 4 bytes: 191. 5 bytes: 11. 6 bytes: 15 (JCNDL is the longest v2 instruction). 7 to 15 bytes: one instruction at each length, all of them v1 padding (NOP7 through NOP15, carried at sub_opcode 0x7 to 0xF of opcode 0x80). No instruction reaches the 16-byte maximum, which stays architectural because ISL and the v1 NOP family define the encoder for it.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO. It declares no interrupt vector (that is D2), defines no instruction semantics beyond the architectural state it describes, and modifies nothing outside parts/D1_meta.json.
EXTENSION PARTITION. The eighteen extension ids partition the 555 instructions exactly once: BASE 173 (156 v1 plus 17 system control), BIT 33, MATH 36, STR 7, BCD 10, COND 18, FPU 33, VEC 77, CIU 30, BMU 33, ATOM 22, TX 5, MMU 24, VIRT 9, SEC 16, DBG 10, PMU 13, IO2 6, and the eighteen counts sum to 555. SPEC names no power extension id, so the nine escape1 power instructions (SLEEP, STANDBY, CLKGATE, MONITOR, MWAIT, WFI, WFE, DVFSHINT, RESET) are counted under PMU together with the four counter instructions, which is stated in the PMU description rather than hidden.
PSEUDO AND MICRO_ROM BOOKKEEPING. The merged v2 file carries 46 pseudo instructions (45 from A_core plus the v1 SAL) and 33 micro-coded expansions (14 from v1, 14 from A_core, 5 from C_sys). The three sources share no name in either table, so no entry is lost or shadowed by the merge, and this fragment reports per-source counts instead of a flattened total.
notes.models:
[1] REX bit assignment. The v2 model follows the v1 reference implementation: payload bit 3 (0x8) extends DRG, bit 2 (0x4) extends SR1, bit 1 (0x2) extends SR2 and bit 0 (0x1) extends SR3, and a set bit means add 16 to the four-bit index. This is what vm.py's _apply_rex and as.py's REX_BITS both implement, and it is what the ADD example in encoding_examples demonstrates. SPEC 9-D1 writes the four bits as 'bit0 DRG, bit1 SR1, bit2 SR2, bit3 SR3'; that wording is read here as naming the four register fields one per bit, not as reassigning them, because reassigning them would change the meaning of every v1 REX-prefixed instruction and break the v1-subset guarantee. D1_meta's register_renaming section must describe the same mapping as this file; if it does not, D1 is wrong and not D2.
[2] Mask register width, settled. The predicate registers k0-k7 are 32 bits wide. The evidence is inside the parts: VSTATE defines a 1064-byte save record, and 32 vector registers of 32 bytes (1024) plus eight masks of 4 bytes (32) plus the VL word (4) plus the VLE word (4) is exactly 1064, which only closes if a mask is 32 bits; a 32-bit predicate is also the only width that can hold one bit per byte lane of a 256-bit vector. SPEC 9-D1's prose called the mask registers 8-bit, D1_meta initially declared width_bits 8, and the cross-review settled the point in favour of 32 bits: D1_meta is being corrected to 32 and this file keeps its 32-bit statements, with the 8-bit general-register view supplied by KMOVG rather than by the architectural width.
[3] k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask. Named as any mask operand, whether the number comes from the EVX or PRED prefix or from the KM1 or KM2 field of the instruction itself, k0 reads as all ones for the active mask length, which means no masking; a write to k0 as KDG is discarded; k1-k7 are ordinary read-write mask registers.
