This single rule replaces an earlier two-case reading of k0 in this file, which had followed B_fpvec's split wording: its notes gave k0 the all-ones meaning in a prefix mask, while the VLOADM description gave it the opposite meaning for the mask it names in its own encoding. The cross-review resolved that contradiction in favour of the x86-style sentinel, so B_fpvec is being patched to remove that exception from VLOADM and the KMOV wording that treated k0 as an ordinary writable register, and this file follows the single rule: k0 always reads as all ones for the active mask length and can never be written, so there is no instruction for which k0 means an empty mask.
[4] Cache line versus sector. CLZERO and MONITOR say 32-byte line and v1's architecture says a 64-byte L1 line, so the model defines an architectural sector of 32 bytes and keeps the v1 line geometry: an L1 line is two sectors and an L2 or L3 line is eight. Nothing in the parts contradicts a 32-byte sector, and every maintenance instruction becomes expressible without forcing one line size on every level.
[5] CH, SPB and the CACHECTL operation codes are defined here because no part defines them. CH is the cache and eviction hint used by PREFETCH, PREFETCHW, CLZERO, LDNT, STNT and the MEMO prefix; SPB is the speculation-barrier strength used by SPECBAR and the three fences; CACHECTL's MO codes 0..5 are named in cache_model.maintenance because the part says only that MO 6..15 raise #UDI. Reserved CH codes are ignored by every hint-only instruction (none of them declares #UDI) and CACHECTL raises #UDI for its own reserved MO codes, which is exactly what each entry's fault list permits.
[6] Two IDT layouts. v1's IDT is a flat array of 4-byte handler addresses and a v1 binary must keep working, so the v1 layout is the reset state, selected by cr0 bit 2 (IDTG) being 0. The v2 gate is 8 bytes: the first dword is the same handler address in the same position, and the second dword carries TARGET_MODE, STACK_SEL, P, GATE_TYPE, EC, PRIORITY and PKEY. Error codes exist only under the extended layout, so a v1 program never sees a 12-byte frame. MODIDT keeps writing the legacy slot; code that needs gates writes them with ordinary stores.
[7] The error-code layout, the priority order, the double-fault escalation rule, the per-vector class table and the vector assignment ranges are all v2 material: v1 defines no error code and no gate attributes. Where the parts already imply a rule, this file repeats their rule rather than inventing a competing one (for example that VMCALL raises #VC with reason 'hypercall', and that atomics are gated on natural alignment).
[8] Atomic size and alignment. The atomic family is defined for ESZ 0..2. ESZ 3 is reserved there and raises #UDI, because an 8-byte atom would need a second register that no atomic encoding has, and because every atomic entry that carries an MO nibble already declares #UDI. For the same reason a misaligned atomic raises #AC regardless of the AC flag: split-lock emulation would break the single-copy guarantee, and a fault is the only honest answer. This is the one place where #AC is not gated by the AC flag, and it is stated in memory_model.atomicity_and_alignment.
[9] XBEGIN is the only relative transfer whose base is the end of the instruction. The parts fix this: XBEGIN's own pseudo-semantics computes the fallback as IP + 4 + sign_extend(O16), and a fallback must be the instruction after XBEGIN. Every branch, call and loop in v2 and v1 uses the address of the instruction itself as its base. Both rules are stated in assembly_syntax.relative_branches so that no assembler implements the wrong one, and the reference assembler already subtracts the branch's own address for O16 and O32.
[10] XBEGIN's MO nibble is the transaction attribute field, and the parts give it no code table, so this file assigns one: MO[0] writes the 16-bit abort code into ra (the ABI return register), MO[1] retries once after a capacity abort, MO[2] retries once after a conflict abort, MO[3] is reserved and must be written as zero. cr13 always records the abort code, the reason and the nesting depth for a privileged reader. XBEGIN declares no fault in its part entry, so an implementation must ignore an attribute it does not support rather than fault on it.
[11] Page tables are 8 bytes per entry and three levels, with a 4-entry top level that maps the 32-bit address space as 1 GiB large pages, 2 MiB large pages at the middle level and 4 KiB pages at the leaf. The v1 bits keep their positions in the low dword (present, writable, user, write-through, cache-disable, accessed, dirty, page-size, global, base), so a v1 table is still readable. A present entry with a reserved bit set, a reserved memory type, or page-size at the leaf is a page-structure error and raises #GP, while a not-present, rights, execute or key failure raises #PGF or #SEC; the fault precedence order is written out in memory_model.mmu_instruction_interaction.
[12] Vector state. VSTATE's 1064-byte record is fixed by the part, and this file publishes the layout so that an operating system can size a context: 1024 bytes of vector registers, 32 bytes of predicates, the VL word and the VLE word. The default VL after reset is 4 elements, the tail is always zeroed, and the merge/zero choice is a property of the PRED prefix, not of the instruction.
[13] The v1 instruction entries carry no faults field at all, so the nine fault names that the validator collects from the corpus come from the 399 v2 entries. Where this file says a v1 instruction can raise #MAV or #PGF (for example LDOFIP and STOFIP), that is a statement of the v1 reference implementation's behaviour, not a field of a v1 entry, and no v1 entry is edited to add one.
[14] Numbers in this file were checked mechanically rather than estimated. The v2 instruction total is 399 by category (104 + 173 + 122), the complete instruction set is 555 mnemonics (156 v1 plus 399), the per-unit timing rows sum to 399 (58 + 33 + 30 + 14 + 6 + 33 + 6 + 45 + 13 + 9 + 10 + 65 + 77), and the extension rows of the changelog sum to 399. Every latency and throughput quoted in performance_model is a minimum or a maximum taken over the timing fields of the entries of that unit, and the instruction named at each end is the entry that carries that number.
[15] Every mnemonic quoted anywhere in this file exists: it is a v1 mnemonic, a v2 mnemonic from one of the three parts, or a pseudo mnemonic from A_core's pseudo table (LI, MOVI, CMPI, TST, BEQ, BNE, BGT, BLT, BGE, BLE, JMP32, CALL32, PUSHA, POPA, PUSHR, POPR, MEMCPY, MEMSET, ZEXT8, ZEXT16, SEXT8, SEXT16, NOT32, SWAP16, NOPN, ADD3, MULADD, MOD, DIVU, MIN, MAX, LSHIFT, RSHIFT, CLZ32, POPC, LEA32, ADDR, LOG2, BITREV, SETIF, BRKIF, LOADI, STOREI, XCHG8, XCHG16). No mnemonic was invented for this document, and the four encoding_examples entries that are not base-space talk about real bmu and ciu opcodes.
[16] Three v1 fixes are binary visible and are called out as re-assembly items rather than migrations: NOP13 now really is thirteen bytes, BTLE and BTBE gain the SOP nibble they always declared (and become three bytes, because their v1 encodings were literally identical and one of them was unreachable), and SAR moves from 0x5B to 0x5D so that 0x5B means COPYIP alone. The other twelve corrections change metadata only, because the v1 decoder derives its length from the format and both IM16 and OF16 were 16 bits wide.
[17] The 0x5B workaround in the reference decoder must be deleted, not kept. After the move to 0x5D, 0x5B has exactly one meaning, and keeping a heuristic that inspects the low nibble of the second byte would silently accept a malformed COPYIP whose reserved nibble is not zero. compatibility.loader_notes states this as an instruction to the integrator.
[18] The v2 assembler surface is the v1 surface plus three conventions: a size suffix (or an explicit ESZ= operand) for the element size, FIELD=value for every other code field, and a space word (DBI, XTU, BMU, CIU) before an escaped-space instruction. The FIELD=value form is not invented here: A_core's pseudo table already writes ESZ=2 (DWORD) and CC=0 (EQ) in its translate_to operands, so the convention is taken from the delivered parts.
[19] Vector registers are named v0-v31 and are extended by REX like the general registers, so the v1 assembler rule that a DFR operand cannot name d0-d15 stays true for floating forms and is irrelevant for vector forms. This is noted in assembly_syntax.assembler_extension_notes so that an implementer does not attempt to rename vector registers through the float path.
[20] Reservations were kept explicit rather than filled. Vectors 40-47 stay reserved with no source. In the base space exactly eighteen primaries are unallocated across v1 and the three parts as delivered: 0x17, 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F, 0x3F, 0x5D, 0x67, 0x7F, 0xBA-0xBF, 0xC6, 0xC7, 0xCE and 0xCF. Of those, 0x17, 0x67 and 0x7F are reserved on purpose in the design (a future 64-bit converter, a future multi-word shift pair family and a future conditional indirect transfer), 0x1D-0x1F are the memory family's reserve, 0xBA-0xBF and 0xC6-0xC7 are the FPU and crypto reserves, and 0x3F, 0xCE and 0xCF are filler that no owner claimed. 0x5D appears in that list only because v1 left it free, which is exactly why SAR could move there: D1_meta's opcode map lists seventeen reserved primaries rather than eighteen because it already places SAR at 0x5D, while this list is computed over the parts as delivered. The escape2 space is reserved for a future unit and every byte of it must decode as #UDI. Nothing in this file depends on an unallocated encoding.
[21] Cross-check that was found here and has been resolved: C_sys's micro_rom entry for IRET expanded it as POPF followed by RET, which pops the frame backwards. The v1 reference implementation is the authority: vm.py's _i_IRET pops the instruction pointer and then the flags word, so the frame is [sp] = return address and [sp+4] = flags, and a POPF first would have consumed the return address as the flags word and then returned to the saved flags. The review confirmed the finding against vm.py and C_sys is being patched, so the micro-coded expansion and this document will agree. exception_model.stack_frame.iret_rule already states the v1-compatible order and therefore needs no change: IRET pops the return address first, then the flags, and never pops an error code. Everything else checked against the reference implementation was already consistent: v1 ST really does take its base register in the DRG field, LD and ST really do sign-extend OF8, and the relative-branch base really is the address of the branch itself.
[22] Second cross-check, also resolved: D1_meta's instruction_length_rules.padding described the NOP family as NOP2 to NOP15 with sub_opcode 0x0 to 0xD, while the v1 table assigns NOP2 to 0x2 and NOP15 to 0xF. The review confirmed it and D1_meta is being patched, so the padding range is 0x2..0xF and pads of 2 to 15 bytes remain available; NOP13 is the one padding entry whose format changed under v1 fix FIX-2, so a 13-byte pad is still expressible and now really occupies thirteen bytes.
notes.core:
Owner A_core. Base decode space only; no escaped decode space is used, so every length below is the full on-wire size.
Primary opcode map: 0x12 SEXT/ZEXT/TRUNC, 0x13 BSWAP, 0x14 CVTSZ, 0x15 SATCAST, 0x16 PACK, 0x17 RESERVED.
0x78 JCND/JCNDL, 0x79 JMPREL, 0x7A JMPRELL, 0x7B CALLREL, 0x7C LOOP family, 0x7D JTABLE/CALLTAB, 0x7E RETFAR.
0x81 bit test family, 0x82 bit scan and count family, 0x83 SHLD/SHRD, 0x84 flag-free shifts and rotates, 0x85 PEXT/PDEP/BZHI/MASKLSB, 0x86 immediate bit fields, 0x87 register bit fields and Gray, 0x88 multiply family, 0x89 divide family, 0x8A carry chains, 0x8B min/max/saturation, 0x8C string, 0x8D and 0x8E packed BCD, 0x8F condition materialisation.
ESZ code (all instructions that use it): 0 = BYTE (8 bits), 1 = WORD (16 bits), 2 = DWORD (32 bits), 3 = reserved and raises #UDI. Instructions that use ESZ: SEXT, ZEXT, TRUNC, BSWAP, CVTSZ, SATCAST, BT/BTS/BTR/BTC, BSF, BSR, POPCNT, CLZ, CTZ, PARCNT, BREV, MASKLSB, GRAYE, GRAYD, MULX, ADCX, ADOX, ISQRT, string MOVS/CMPS/SCAS/STOS/LODS/MOVSN/STOSN, SETCC, CMPCC, TSTCC.
MO code fields, instruction by instruction. CVTSZ: MO[1:0] destination width 0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD, MO[2] signed source, MO[3] saturate instead of wrap. SATCAST: MO[0] unsigned clamp, MO[1] merge into DRG instead of zeroing. PACK: MO[1:0] lane width 0=BYTE 1=WORD, MO[3:2] mode 0=signed saturate 1=unsigned saturate 2=truncate. BEXT/BINS/BEXTS: MO = field width minus one, so 1 to 16 bits. MULI, DIVI: MO[0] zero-extend the immediate instead of sign-extending it. BCDSHL/BCDSHR: MO[2:0] digit shift count. NEGBCD: MO[0] nine's complement instead of ten's complement. BCD2BIN: MO[0] lenient invalid digits. BIN2BCD: MO[0] wrap modulo 10^8 instead of saturating. JTABLE/CALLTAB: MO[0] 32-bit table entries instead of 16-bit. RETFAR: MO = number of additional 32-bit argument words to discard.
Condition codes are the SPEC 7.2 table verbatim: 0 EQ, 1 NE, 2 CS/LO, 3 CC/HS, 4 MI, 5 PL, 6 VS, 7 VC, 8 LT, 9 GE, 10 LE, 11 GT, 12 HI, 13 LS, 14 AL, 15 NV. SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC, TSTCC, JCND and JCNDL all consume it.
Relative branch base: every relative transfer (JCND, JCNDL, JMPREL, JMPRELL, CALLREL, LOOP family) computes its target as the address of the branch instruction itself plus the sign-extended offset, matching the v1 reference implementation of JZ and JMP rather than a next-instruction base. CALLREL and CALLTAB push the address of the following instruction.
Register roles that are implicit in the string instructions: ri is the source pointer, rd is the destination pointer, ra is the accumulator and rc is the repeat counter; DF selects the step direction and a REP prefix supplies the count. The counter register was chosen explicitly (rc) instead of being hard wired, so a REP-prefixed block move reads three named registers and nothing hidden.
Relation to v1 arithmetic: v1 MUL already produces the full 64-bit product with the high half in SR3 and v1 DIV already produces quotient in DRG and remainder in SR3. MULH/MULHS are the single-destination high-half forms that waste no third register, and DIVMOD/REM/REMS put the remainder in the dividend register so the operation needs only the three registers named in the instruction.
Relation to v1 LEASC: the v1 implementation multiplies the index register by SCL, so SCL is a numeric multiplier and the pseudo ADDR/LEA32 inherit exactly that meaning.
v1 LD and ST are fixed 32-bit accesses; the string instructions therefore implement byte and word element sizes with LSU sized-access micro-operations that are not architecturally visible, and the micro_rom expansions show the dword form.
Pseudo conventions: length is the number of bytes the macro expands to, length_after is the same figure after full expansion, and format records the operand layout of the source form. translate_to entries name real v1 or v2 instructions; a field assignment such as CC=0 or ESZ=1 names the value placed in that field. Macros that need a scratch register use t0 and t1 (r24 and r25) and say so in their description.
micro_rom conventions: every entry here is a micro-coded expansion of an instruction that owns an opcode byte, which is why PUSHA, POPA, PUSHR and POPR appear only in the pseudo table: they are assembler macros with no byte of their own, and their expansion is fully listed there.
Fault policy: #UDI is declared only where a reserved code field can be decoded (ESZ 3 and the reserved MO codes), #DIV only on zero or invalid divisors, and #MAV or #PGF only where the instruction performs a memory access. No data value other than a zero divisor can fault.
Flags policy: instructions that only move or reshape bits (SEXT, ZEXT, BSWAP, BREV, GRAYE, GRAYD, ROLX, RORX, SHLX, SHRX, SARX, PACK, CMOVCC, SETCC) write no flags; the VF flag is reserved for loss of information (TRUNC, CVTSZ, SATCAST, PACK, saturation and clamp operations, invalid BCD digits) so that VF always means the result is not exact.
No instruction in this fragment uses the IM16 or OF16 tokens: only I16 and O16 exist, and this fragment uses O16 and O32 for every relative offset.
Helper vocabulary used by pseudo_semantics, all operating on 32-bit integers unless stated: lowmask(n) is 0xFFFFFFFF when n >= 32 and (1 << n) - 1 otherwise; sign_extend(x,n) and zext(x,n) widen the low n bits of x to 32 bits; wrap32(x) is x mod 2^32; bitlen(x) is 32 - clz32(x), that is floor(log2(x)) + 1 for nonzero x; ctz(x) counts the trailing zero bits of a nonzero x; popcount(x) counts the one bits; reverse_bytes(x,n) reverses the low 8*n bits in byte units and bitreverse(x) reverses the low 32 bits; pext(src,mask) and pdep(src,mask) are exactly the operations defined by PEXT and PDEP; gray_to_binary(g,w) is the iterative Gray decode over a w bit field; isqrt(v) is the floor integer square root; sdiv and srem are truncated signed division and the matching remainder; clamp_signed(x,w) and clamp_unsigned(x,w) return the w bit pattern of x clamped into the signed or unsigned range of a w bit field; clamp_to(x,d) and wrap_to(x,d) return the 32-bit value of x clamped into or wrapped to d bits; pack_lane(x,w,md) returns the w bit lane pattern for signed saturation (md 0), unsigned saturation (md 1) or truncation (md 2); pack_lost(x,w,md) returns 1 when that lane conversion changed the value, tested as sign_extend(pack_lane(x,w,md),w) != sign_extend(x,32) for md 0, zext(pack_lane(x,w,md),w) != x for md 1 and (x & ~lowmask(w)) != 0 for md 2; mem16[a] and mem32[a] are little-endian 16-bit and 32-bit loads at address a; nontemporal_store is a non-allocating streaming store; cond(CC) evaluates the SPEC 7.2 table against the current flags; bcd_value, bcd_add, bcd_sub, bcd_neg, bcd_nines, bcd_invalid, bcd_to_bin_masked and bin_to_bcd are the eight digit packed BCD helpers.
Three primaries of this owner are deliberately left reserved and must be marked RESERVED in the final opcode map: 0x17, 0x67 and 0x7F. 0x17 is kept free so the convert family can grow a 64-bit register-pair converter later without disturbing the layout; 0x67 is kept free because multi-word 64-bit shifts are already expressible with SHLD and SHRD plus the ADDC/SUBC carry chains, so no pair opcodes were spent; 0x7F is kept free so a future conditional indirect transfer family has a home next to the conditional branches, and so that SETCC, CMOVCC, CMPCC and TSTCC stay together in the single primary 0x8F that the contract suggests.
Why three separate bare primaries for the 32-bit transfers: JMPREL is a two-byte O8 branch and JMPRELL and CALLREL are O32 branches. SOP plus O32 is nine nibbles and SOP plus OF8 is three nibbles, both odd, so giving each transfer its own primary is what keeps them at their minimum sizes instead of forcing a pad nibble into every branch.
Why PACK is one MO-driven instruction instead of three SOP variants: three register operands plus SOP plus a size field is five nibbles and breaks the even-nibble rule, so the lane width and the pack mode were folded into MO and the primary stayed a single 3-byte instruction. The same reasoning is why SETCC and CMOVCC are 3 bytes and only the conditional compare forms that also produce a predicate carry a sixth nibble.
String instructions are 2 bytes because their whole operand state is architectural: SOP selects the operation and ESZ the element width, and the pointers, counter and direction come from ri, rd, rc and DF.
notes.fpvec:
B_fpvec owns the floating-point unit, the 256-bit vector/SIMD unit, the CIU crypto unit and the BMU big-math unit of Hayneko_Arch32S v2.0.

Counts: floating_point 33, vector 77, crypto 30 (25 base + 5 ciu), bmu 33; total 173 v2 instructions.

OPCODE MAP (base space). 0xB0 FP add/sub/mul/div/min/max; 0xB1 sqrt/recip/rsqrt/round; 0xB2 FMA family; 0xB3 sign and select; 0xB4 compare and classify; 0xB5 int<->float conversion; 0xB6 moves; 0xB7 float load/store; 0xB8 ldexp/scale; 0xB9 precision convert and rounding-mode state; 0xBA-0xBF reserved for a future FP extension. 0xA0 vector configuration; 0xA1 unit-stride load/store; 0xA2 strided and indexed memory; 0xA3 broadcast and masked block memory; 0xA4 lane arithmetic; 0xA5 fused multiply-add plus lane abs/negate; 0xA6 logic; 0xA7 shifts; 0xA8 compare/test/find; 0xA9 mask ALU; 0xAA mask move/test/unpack/popcount; 0xAB permute; 0xAC reduce; 0xAD lane extract/insert/broadcast and conversion; 0xAE round/popcount/clz/byterev/compress/expand; 0xAF vector state save/restore. 0xC0 AES; 0xC1 SHA-1; 0xC2 SHA-256; 0xC3 SHA-512 plus carry-less and GF(2^8); 0xC4 CRC, entropy and secure compare; 0xC5 key management and Montgomery; 0xC6-0xC7 reserved.

ESCAPED SPACES. bmu space (prefix BMU.EN 0xF6): 0x00-0x0F transcendental functions, 0x20-0x2D big-integer arithmetic, 0x40-0x42 matrix operations. ciu space (prefix CIU.EN 0xFD): 0x00-0x02 SHA-3 sponge (absorb, finalize, raw Keccak-f), 0x10-0x11 MAC and stream cipher blocks. Bytes in these spaces do not use SOP: each mnemonic has its own opcode byte.

FIXED LENGTH RULE. Every instruction in this part is 4 bytes except: FMOV (3), VLDR/VSTR (5), FLOAD/FSTORE (5), VSETVL/VGETVL/VZERO/VCLEAR (2 or 3), the vector memory family (3 to 5 as per format), AES/SHA/CLMUL/GF2P8MUL/CRC32/RDRAND (3), mask ALU and KUNPCK/KTEST/VPOPC/KMOVG/VBROADCAST (3). All FP register forms are 4 bytes, so the FPU decodes one length; all bmu forms are 4 bytes with six nibble fields after the opcode.

ESCAPED SPACES AND LENGTH. A bmu or ciu entry declares length as OPC plus its operand fields only; the mandatory escape prefix byte (BMU.EN 0xF6, CIU.EN 0xFD) is a prefix like REX, so the on-wire size is length+1 bytes and every escaped-space entry states this once in encoding_notes. sub_opcode is present exactly when SOP appears in the format: the base-space groups carry SOP, while the bmu and ciu spaces use one opcode byte per mnemonic and carry no sub_opcode.

RESERVED NIBBLE. A trailing 0x0 token in a format is a reserved nibble that must be encoded as zero and ignored on read. It exists only to keep the byte-alignment invariant (an even number of nibbles after OPC). It appears in the unary FP forms, FLOAD/FSTORE do not use it, and in the bmu space the rule is uniform: families needing only five fields carry one trailing reserved nibble.

FP FLAGS. FLZ/FLO/FLV condense IEEE-754 status into three architectural flags and are set by every arithmetic FP instruction. FLZ means the written result is +0 or -0 (or that a comparison found equality). FLO means the result was inexact, overflowed or lost a denormal: the rounded result differs from the exact one. FLV means the operation was invalid and produced a default quiet NaN, or that a conversion produced its indefinite integer. Testing an operand for NaN is FCLASS or FCMPU, not FLV.

FP FORMATS AND ROUNDING. FPF selects F16/BF16/F32/F64 (0..3) on every FP instruction; F32 is the default when a program relies on v1 FRMSTATE defaults. RM selects RN/RZ/RP/RM (0..3) in the instruction, so a well-formed FP instruction is self-describing and the FMT prefix (0xFE: FPF,RM) is only an override for vector and BMU forms that have no FPF/RM nibbles of their own. The fused forms FMADD/FMSUB/FNMADD/FNMSUB carry no RM nibble: they always round to nearest even and the FMT prefix overrides them. NaN handling: an arithmetic instruction quiets a signalling NaN and propagates the payload of the first NaN source operand; FMIN/FMAX use minNum/maxNum so a single NaN yields the other operand. Signed zero: x + (-x) is +0 in RN/RZ/RP and -0 in RM; FABS and FNEG are pure bit operations; FROUND keeps the sign of the operand so FROUND(-0.4) is -0.

VECTOR MODEL. VLEN is 256 bits with 32 vector registers v0-v31, addressable through REX; f16-f31 alias v16-v31. Eight 32-bit predicate registers k0-k7 hold masks, one bit per 8-bit lane at VLEN=256, so bits above the active mask length read as zero. ESZ selects the element size 0=BYTE 1=WORD 2=DWORD 3=QWORD. VL (the active element count) is set by VSETVL and reported with the VLE status flag; VLMAX is 256/(8<<ESZ). VL, the mask register and merge/zero mode are supplied by the EVX prefix (0xF7: KDG,VL) and the PRED prefix (0xFB: KDG,MO), so predication is a prefix bit and never a second opcode.

MASK AND TAIL POLICY (normative for every vector instruction). Written lanes are 0..VL-1 that are enabled by the mask register named in EVX/PRED; the default mask policy is ZEROING (a mask-cleared lane becomes zero) and PRED MO=1 selects MERGING (a mask-cleared lane keeps the old destination value). Tail elements, that is lanes VL..VLMAX-1, are always ZEROED (tail-undisturbed has no encoding in v2). k0 is the hardwired all-ones mask: named as a mask operand it reads all ones for the active mask length, and a write to it through KDG is discarded, which is exactly no masking; k1-k7 are ordinary read/write registers of the mask file. Because k0 reads all ones, a masked load, store, compress, expand, find or popcount through k0 behaves as the unmasked form. Vector loads and stores touch memory only for written or read lanes, and a masked-off lane can never fault. Instructions that write no destination lane never modify flags.

VECTOR MO CODES. MO[1:0] selects operand interpretation: 0 = signed, 1 = unsigned, 2 = logical, 3 = reserved. MO[3:2] selects overflow behaviour: 0 = wrap, 1 = signed saturation, 2 = unsigned saturation, 3 = flags only. Instructions that need different modifiers document their own table in their description (VSHLV, VBYTEREV, VSAT, VTRUNC, VCMP-free compare forms, VLDREP, VSTRX/VLDRX, KMOVG).

PREFIX LEGALITY. EVX/PRED appear only on instructions that produce vector or predicate register results from vector operands; instructions that only move or clear state, write a general register (VSETVL, VGETVL, VEXTRACT, VFIND, VPOPC, VSTATE) or name their mask explicitly in KM1 (VLOADM, VSTOREM, VCOMPRESS, VEXPAND) list REX only. MEMO appears only where the instruction touches memory. FMT appears on floating-point forms and OPSZ on the block forms of the bmu space.

MASK REGISTER OPERANDS. The encode section declares one destination mask field KDG and two source mask fields KM1 and KM2, so a three-operand mask instruction such as KAND names KM1 and KM2 and no token ever repeats inside one format. KTEST names KM1 and KM2 with no destination because it writes flags only. pseudo_semantics uses the field names verbatim; no positional reading or invented suffix exists.

VECTOR MEMORY. VLDR/VSTR use base+displacement (O16). VLDRS/VSTRS use a stride register with an MO scale. VLDRX/VSTRX use an index vector in the vector file with 32- or 64-bit offsets selected by MO. VLDREP broadcasts one memory element. VLOADM/VSTOREM name their mask register directly in KM1 instead of through the EVX prefix because fault suppression is part of the semantics.

CRYPTO. AES and SHA instructions keep their 128-bit state in the low half of a vector register and zero the upper half, so the crypto unit shares the vector register file and needs no private data registers; the CIU keeps only key slots and sponge/MAC contexts, addressed by handle. Key-management instructions are privileged: KEYGEN is mode L7 (platform secure), KEYLOAD and KEYZERO are mode L3 (kernel). All crypto instructions are constant-time with respect to data and key operands and modify no flag except SECCMP (ZF), RDRAND/RDSEED (CF) and the explicitly listed ones.

BMU REGISTER CONVENTIONS. Transcendental functions take FPR operands in FPF format with RM rounding and expose an accuracy class in MO: 0 = default 1 ulp, 1 = high accuracy 0.5 ulp, 2 = fast 8 ulp; results are deterministic for a given class and the three FP flags summarise the whole operation. Big-integer operands are GPR blocks named by their base register: 2 << ESZ words (2, 4, 8, 16 words for ESZ = 0..3), least significant word in the base register, word k in register base+k, and a block that would contain r0 raises #UDI because r0 discards writes. BMUL and BDIV consume or produce double-width blocks. Matrix operands are vector-register blocks of order N (ESZ 0 = 2, 1 = 4, 2 = 8), one 256-bit row per register, with the element width taken from the OPSZ prefix.

ENCODING IDENTITY. Every (decode_space, opcode, sub_opcode) triple in this fragment is unique; base-space opcodes stay inside 0xA0-0xC7 and no prefix byte is used as an opcode.
notes.system: C_sys authors 122 v2 instructions covering memory, atomics, transactional memory, system and MMU control, virtualization, debug, power management, memory management, security and 16-bit I/O. Base primaries: memory 0x1A-0x1C (0x1D-0x1F reserved), atomics 0xC8-0xCB, transactions 0xCC-0xCD, system 0x96/0x97/0x9A/0x9B/0x9E, virtualization 0x9C, debug 0x9D. Escaped spaces: escape1 opcodes 0x00-0x03 power, 0x10 memory management, 0x20 I/O extensions (the rest of escape1 is reserved); xtu opcodes 0x00-0x05 security. Two local conventions do not contradict the SPEC but must be read with it: escaped-space entries declare length as OPC plus operands, so the encoded size is length+1 because the mandatory DBI or XTU prefix byte precedes OPC; and every 0x0 format token is a reserved nibble that must decode as zero. The design_decisions array below records the ordering, MMU, virtualization, mode and compatibility rationale that the per-entry descriptions refer to.
system_design_decisions: C_sys owns base 0x1A-0x1F (memory), 0x96/0x97/0x9A-0x9E (system_ext, virtualization, debug), 0xC8-0xCD (atomic, transaction) and the whole escape1 (0x00-0x2F used) and xtu (0x00-0x05 used) decode spaces.

Primary opcode to family map: 0x1A pair/block transfers, 0x1B indexed and extending loads, 0x1C cache hints and maintenance, 0x1D-0x1F left RESERVED for a future memory family; 0xC8 exclusives and CAS, 0xC9 store-form AMOs, 0xCA fetch-form AMOs, 0xCB fences; 0xCC transaction begin/end/abort, 0xCD transaction test/suspend; 0x96 control and MSR access, 0x97 counters, 0x9A TLB and cache maintenance, 0x9B system entry/exit and identity, 0x9C virtualization, 0x9D debug and trace, 0x9E mode and flags; escape1 0x00-0x03 power, 0x10 memory management, 0x20 I/O extensions (0x04-0x0F, 0x11-0x1F and 0x21-0xFF stay RESERVED); xtu 0x00 shadow stack, 0x01 control-flow integrity, 0x02 speculation barriers, 0x03 enclaves, 0x04 data hygiene, 0x05 protection keys.
Grouping rule: every primary in this fragment is used either entirely with SOP variants or not at all, and SOP assignments are contiguous inside a primary so the decoder can use a small jump table.

Escaped-space length convention: for escape1 and xtu entries the declared length counts OPC plus operands only; the mandatory escape prefix byte (0xF0 DBI or 0xF5 XTU) is not part of length, so the encoded size is length+1. This keeps the byte-alignment identity of SPEC section 1 true for every entry. Each such entry carries the same statement in encoding_notes.

Reserved nibble convention: any 0x0 token in a format is a reserved nibble that must decode as zero; it exists only to reach an even nibble count after OPC (the v1 ADD entry uses the same trick). CAS needs two of them because it carries three registers.

Atomic ordering model: the atomic family defaults to relaxed ordering and takes its acquire/release class from the in-band MO nibble (0=RLX 1=ACQ 2=REL 3=ACQ_REL 4=SEQ_CST). The MEMO prefix (0xF9, payload MO,CH) may strengthen the class but never weaken it, so a MEMO-prefixed AMOADD with MO=SEQ_CST is legal and a MEMO prefix trying to relax an in-band ACQ_REL is a #UDI. The fetch forms AMOF* return the pre-operation value in DRG; the plain forms discard it. All atomics address exactly [SR1] with no displacement, must be naturally aligned, and are single-copy atomic for their width; SFENCE or MFENCE is still required to publish a non-atomic result.

MMU and PTE interaction: MAP, UNMAP, PROTECT, PGWALK, SETPGT and GETPGT are explicit MMU operations rather than implicit page-walk side effects, so a kernel can install a mapping without executing a store to the page table and can walk a table without faulting. MAP and EPTMAP write the leaf entry and then invalidate the cached translations of the page; PROTECT rewrites only the rights field and never the physical base; UNMAP clears present and therefore also drops the write-back of a dirty line. MO bits 3:0 are the size class (4 KiB, 64 KiB, 2 MiB, 1 GiB) and bits 7:4 the write/user/execute/global rights, matching the three-level page table with two large-page sizes required by the v2 memory model. Protection keys ride on the PKEY nibble of the SEC prefix and on the rights field, and MKEYALLOC/MKEYFREE manage the 16-key allocation bitmap in cr6.

VM exit model: VMENTER and VMRUN are the entry paths at L5, VMEXIT and VMCALL the guest-side exit paths at L6. VMENTER is gated on VME=0 and sets VME; VMEXIT requires VME=1, performs the same save sequence as a hardware exit, writes the exit reason into DRG, clears VME and returns to L5. VMRUN is the long-running form that returns only after an exit. Hardware exits re-use the VMEXIT save sequence internally and fill the exit-reason table in the control block addressed by cr8. VMCALL raises virtualization exception #VC with a hypercall number instead of leaving guest mode directly; VMFUNC runs a hypervisor service without a world switch. Nested paging is expressed by EPTMAP/EPTUNMAP/INVEPT, which are only legal with VME=0.

Mode assignment: memory, atomic and transaction instructions are L0 because they only need the current privilege; anything touching CR, MSR, TLB, IDT equivalents, keys, debug or power state is L3 or above; EPT and the whole virtualization family is L5 except the guest-side exits which sit at L6; RESET, enclave and attestation instructions are L7; shadow-stack and protection-key instructions are L3 as required by the brief. The mode field is the numeric floor only: the finer gates (VME, SSE, PKE, DTE, TXE, cr10/cr14 enable bits) are named in each description, because a linear L0-L7 model cannot express them.

Deviation from the brief worth recording: MFENCE, LFENCE, SFENCE and CLREX are not in the section 9-C list but are required by the ordering model the same section asks for (the D2 memory model refers to LFENCE/SFENCE/MFENCE) and by any LDLK/STLK usage pattern, so they were added inside the allocated 0xCB primary and 0xC8 group rather than left to another owner. No instruction from the section 9-C list was dropped.

needs_coprocessor choice: every xtu-space entry names XTU, because SPEC section 3 requires escaped-space instructions to name the matching unit; KCU is not used anywhere in this fragment since no key unit other than XTU is defined by the contract. The MMU unit is named on the base-space TLB operations (INVLPG, INVTLB, INVEPT) and on the whole escape1 memory-management group.

v1 complementarity: this fragment adds no duplicate of LD/ST (base+disp8), LDOFIP/STOFIP, IN/OUT (8-bit PRT, data in ri), INT/IRET/BRK/SYSCALL/SYSRET/HALT, LDIDT/MODIDT/SETIDT, MOVCTRL/COPCTRL, CLI/STI or PUSHF/POPF. LDSX/LDZX give the signed and zero-extending sized loads that v1 LD lacks, LDX/STX add register-indexed addressing, INS/OUTS extend the v1 string and port mechanisms to 16-bit ports, SYSENT/SYSEXI are the fast system gate while IRET stays the interrupt-frame return, and RDFLAGS/WRFLAGS complement PUSHF/POPF without using the stack.

No instruction in this fragment is one byte long: every new entry is 2..5 bytes, as required for v2 instructions. The longest are CAS at 5 bytes and the 4-byte LDP/STP/LDM/STM/LDX/STX, PREFETCH family, XBEGIN, XSUSPEND, INVTLB, INVEPT and INX/OUTX/INS/OUTS forms.

micro_rom: IRET, MAP, SHSTKPUSH, LDM and VMEXIT are the five micro-coded expansions. Each translate_to list uses only v1 base instructions plus this fragment's own MMU and virtualization instructions, and length_after is the sum of the v2 (defect-fixed) lengths of the expanded instructions, with the loop case LDM reporting the per-iteration body.

provenance.merge_rules: v1 entries come first with the documented field corrections and the SAR relocation, then each part's categories, pseudo and micro_rom tables and the D1/D2 metadata sections are appended verbatim, with author notes folded into this one object.
